trajectories.note: ★ACK TWO-SIDED SEMANTICS CLOSED (2026-08-27), and the defect was a SIBLING that never got its brother's fix. alert_dismissals is keyed onConflict 'hive_id,alert_key' - ONE row per alert per hive - so marking handled, snoozing and marking SEEN are all hive state. dismissAlert knows this and says so ('hidden for your whole hive now, recorded under your name'), and its comment names the exact failure it is preventing: 'a plant alert quietly blinded for the whole crew by someone who thought they were tidying their own view.' acknowledgeAlert writes the SAME ROW with the SAME conflict key and said 'Marked seen'. Two words. ★EVERYTHING AROUND IT REINFORCED THE WRONG READING: the local map is `_seen`, the control is an aria-pressed toggle, the copy was a bookmark's worth of text - a surface that says personal over a write that is shared. And the way OUT was worse: un-marking DELETES the hive's row, returning the alert to unseen for everyone, and said NOTHING - so the crew could watch an alert reappear with no idea who or why. Both directions now name the scope and the actor, in EN and FIL. ★GATE alert-scope-is-told holds the rule for every alert_dismissals WRITE (a read owes nothing), matching by MEANING across both languages rather than a fixed sentence, because the copy ships bilingual through _t(en, fil) and a gate that pins wording is a gate that punishes improving it. 3 write paths, 3 announcing. ★THE TEETH ARE THE PRE-FIX WORLD VERBATIM: the selftest's RED cases are literally the old `_t('Marked seen', 'Minarkahang nakita')` and the old silent un-mark, so the resurrection is not simulated - it is the code that shipped. ★AND THE GATE WAS WRONG FIRST, caught by its own selftest asserting the live page passes: a fixed 900-char window ended before both announcements (they sit past a writeAuditLog call and a long explanatory comment) and reported two CORRECT paths as silent. The search is now bounded by the `catch (` that actually ends the success path - a real boundary instead of a guess. Second time today a fixed-size window read correct code as broken; the fix both times was to find the structural edge. REMAINS to LOCKED: the low-stock multi-band handoff, and the SS6j cap decision (Ian's). ★WHY THE LOW-STOCK HANDOFF IS NOT A LINK - MEASURED (2026-08-27). The remaining local item read 'the low-stock multi-band handoff', and the reason it was never a one-line href is now on record. The tile ALREADY carries href:'inventory.html' - the door exists, it just drops the FILTER, so tapping a count lands on the whole catalogue and the supervisor re-derives by hand the filter the tile already applied. ★BUT NO SINGLE BAND MATCHES THE TILE'S NUMBER. inventory's #filter-status offers out / critical / low / ok / surplus, while the tile's _lowStockTotal spans out + critical + low (index computes _lowOnly = _lowStockTotal - _outOfStock, so 'out' is inside its total). Linking to any one band would land on FEWER rows than the number tapped - breaking this trajectory's own tile-count-agreement gate, which exists to assert exactly that the number tapped equals the rows shown. ★AND THE TWO SURFACES DEFINE 'LOW STOCK' DIFFERENTLY, which is the deeper reason: inventory's own lowCount is criticalCount + lowOnlyCount, commented 'at or below min_qty' and EXCLUDING out-of-stock, while the index tile INCLUDES it. Measured on the fixture hive: 0 out-of-stock, 3 at-or-below-min, 3 by the tile's definition - so the two agree TODAY only because nothing is at zero. The divergence is latent and appears the moment one part empties: two windows, one metric name. ★SO THIS IS A DEFINITION DECISION BEFORE IT IS A LINK - which count is canonical for 'low stock' - and it sits beside the SS6j cap decision this trajectory already routes to Ian. A ?status= reader was built and then REVERTED rather than left in: a deep-link parameter with no caller is the declared-but-never-wired class, and shipping one while flagging others all session would not survive its own standard.

trajectories.title: Supervisor clears the approval queue
trajectories.basis: two-sided walk (worker 390 submits -> supervisor 1280 queue): submit toast sets expectations, queue item shows kind/number/name/submitter/qty/category + optimistic-locked approve/reject. FOUND+FIXED the broken feedback loop: queue Reject was one-tap with NO reason (worker card just said REJECTED, notes empty) and the card claimed IN STOCK beside REJECTED. Fixes: whPrompt reason capture in hive rejectItem (writes rejection_reason to BOTH tables - additive migration 20260825000001 + v_inventory_items_truth extended), worker card renders 'Why rejected: ... fix and resubmit via Edit', stock badge suppressed for non-approved. Proven: reason typed at reject -> stored -> rendered on the worker's 390 card. Remaining: submitted-at timestamp + dedup hinting in queue items, bulk actions (wave close). T108 CROSS-RECEIPT (2026-08-25): the two-sided loop closed - approve AND reject now notify the SUBMITTER via the guarded notify_submission_decided RPC (mig 003; the reject push names the way forward, pairing this session's rejection_reason card). ADVANCED 2026-08-26: queue cards now carry SUBMITTED-AT (mig 20260825000006 adds created_at to the RPC's pending_parts - pending_assets already had it; applied locally + pgrst reloaded) and a DEDUP HINT. Check-the-premise finding: same-IDENTIFIER dupes are impossible (unique indexes on (hive,tag) and (hive,part_number) refuse them at submission) - so the hint covers the one REACHABLE collision: the same exact NAME under a different identifier. Live-proven as supervisor: 'submitted Aug 25, 2026' + the name-dup warning rendered on a staged probe part, probe cleaned. Remaining: bulk actions for large queues (scoped product decision). || ★THE TWO-SIDED REJECTION LOOP IS CLOSED ON BOTH TABLES, AND PROVEN IN THE DATA (2026-08-28). This trajectory's sharpest question is whether a rejected submitter LEARNS WHY, or is left to guess. They learn. The supervisor's reject prompts for a reason through whPrompt - 'Tell them why, so they can fix it instead of guessing', labelled 'Reason (the submitter sees this)' - and the reason is written to rejection_reason, capped at 500 chars, behind the same optimistic lock as the approve. ★AND BOTH RETURN PATHS RENDER IT: asset-hub shows 'Why: <reason>' in red on the submitter's own card, and inventory.html shows 'Why rejected: <reason> - fix it and resubmit', which is the better of the two because it names the NEXT ACTION rather than only the verdict. That is the whole loop - refuse, say why, and tell them what to do about it - on a surface where the refused party would otherwise have no channel at all. ★MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: 4 of 4 rejected asset_nodes carry a reason. 100%, not a sample. inventory_items has no rejected rows yet so its half is verified by CODE rather than by data, which is worth stating precisely - the render exists and is correct, but nothing has exercised it. pct -> 86. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate rejection-reaches-the-submitter re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★THE TWO-SIDED REJECT LOOP IS CLOSED AND WAS UNGATED (2026-08-26). This trajectory's sharpest probe - does the submitter LEARN why - is already answered on all three reject paths: hive.html's queue writes a reason for asset_nodes AND inventory_items, asset-hub and project-manager write their own, and the reason is rendered back as 'Why: ...' (asset-hub), 'Why rejected: ... - fix it and resubmit via Edit' (inventory) and 'Rejected: ...' (project-manager), with asset-hub saying 'No reason recorded.' for rows predating the column rather than showing an empty box. Nothing was broken and nothing was protecting it. Gate rejection-reaches-the-submitter asserts BOTH halves - the reason written in the same update, and rendered on the surface the submitter reads - pairing them by TABLE rather than by page, since the reject and the render live apart by design. Its own first run wrongly accused asset-hub by looking for a capitalised caption where the page branches on a status VALUE. Teeth proven on both halves.

trajectories.title: Supervisor sets up PM for a newly registered asset
trajectories.basis: walked 1280 as leandromarquez: the asset 360 KNEW its PM state ('33d overdue' in its own risk factors) but offered NO path to act - schedule-PM meant re-navigating + re-finding in a 91-item list. FIXED: detail-pm-link chip ('Schedule PM') beside the alerts/hail chips, href pm-scheduler.html?tag=<tag> (exact-match key; name fallback). Proven: chip -> lands ON the asset's detail with the first actionable complete-btn FOCUSED (the carry-intent machinery). Remaining: frequency-template defaults (G5c), first-due-date visibility on create, new-asset compliance fairness (wave close). ADVANCED 2026-08-26: (1) G5c frequency templates CONFIRMED already present (PM_TEMPLATES per asset class, per-item freqs) - the remaining line was stale; (2) FIRST-DUE-DATE now NAMED in the save receipt ('First PM due <date>' from the truth view's freshly loaded next_due_date - the old toast promised 'from its first due date' without saying when); (3) FAIRNESS: the truth view is fair for blank anchors (COALESCE last_completed/anchor/created + period - never instantly overdue), but the anchor input's helper claimed the OPPOSITE ('leave blank: all tasks overdue immediately') - a stale claim contradicting the DB rule, REWRITTEN to the truth (blank = clock starts today; a months-old date starts longer cycles overdue). Remaining: asset->PM handoff polish rides the earlier fix; live save-receipt re-proof at close. || ★THE ASSET-TO-PM HANDOFF CARRIES THE ASSET, AND THE FAR END READS IT (2026-08-28). This trajectory's first probe is whether scheduling a PM for a just-approved asset is one tap from that asset or a re-navigation and a re-find. It is one tap with context: asset-hub builds pm-scheduler.html?tag=<tag_id> when the asset has a tag and falls back to ?asset=<name> when it does not - four parameterised links in all - and pm-scheduler READS both, calling get('tag') and get('asset') on adjacent lines. Both halves of the chain agree, which is the part that usually breaks: a link decorated with a parameter the destination never reads looks more specific than a bare link while delivering exactly the same thing, and is worse because it reads as context that was handed over. ★THE tag-BEFORE-name PREFERENCE MATTERS MORE HERE THAN IT LOOKS, given T127: 24 asset names are duplicated within a single hive in this data, so a handoff keyed on NAME would land the supervisor on an ambiguous set. Preferring tag_id - the identifier that is actually unique - is what makes the arrival land on the machine they were looking at rather than on everything sharing its name. ★NOT VERIFIED HERE: whether the newly-created plan shows its first due date immediately, and whether a brand-new asset's compliance denominator treats it fairly on day one rather than tanking the hive's score - both are about what the supervisor sees AFTER the handoff lands. ★UPDATE, same session: the FIRST half is answered and answered well. Creating the plan confirms '<name> added → on your PM schedule now, and it counts toward PM compliance from its first due date', with the computed first due date interpolated into the sentence. The supervisor learns the plan exists, that it affects the compliance number, and exactly when that starts - in one line, at the moment they act. What remains open is only the fairness question: whether a brand-new asset's denominator treats the hive's score gently on day one. pct 75 -> 86. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate asset-pm-handoff-carries-context re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★THE ASSET-TO-PM HANDOFF ALREADY KEEPS ITS CONTEXT AND WAS UNGATED (2026-08-26). This trajectory's core probe - is 'schedule a PM' one tap from the asset, or a re-navigation and a re-find - is answered: asset-hub links to pm-scheduler.html?tag= / ?asset=, and pm-scheduler reads all four of asset_id, asset, pm_id and tag, so BOTH ends of the promise are wired. The two bare links are in genuine empty states ('No approved assets in this hive yet'), where naming an asset would be naming nothing. Gated with both halves asserted, since a carried parameter the receiver ignores is worse than none. The gate's own first run accused a COMMENT that merely mentions pm-scheduler.html; a mention is not a navigation.

trajectories.title: Supervisor drills an analytics KPI to its source and believes it
trajectories.basis: walked 1280: every KPI names its standard (ISO 22400-2, ISO 14224 SS9.2, SMRP), qualifiers sit NEAR figures ('PARTIAL (A x Q) - 30 ASSET(S)', 'calendar days not running hours'), denominators stated, per-machine row table adjacent + expandable = rows reachable within 2 interactions; headline tiles themselves not clickable but the row set is one scroll away. Zero fixes needed on the walked path. Remaining: the drill-path oracle (every headline KPI -> rows <=2 hops, basis carried) + snapshot-vs-recompute honesty probe (wave close). ORACLE SLICE 1 + A REAL FIX 2026-08-26: prove_kpi_parity.mjs (gate kpi-parity) MEASURED the headline PM-compliance KPI telling two stories side-by-side - analytics 78% (orchestrator snapshot's copy) vs pm-scheduler 77% (canonical get_pm_compliance_smrp live), despite pm-scheduler's comment claiming 'the SAME number Analytics shows'. FIXED: the canonical RPC patches the analytics card when it answers; snapshot stays the instant-paint fallback. Re-proven 77==77 with the window named on the glass. Remaining: more headline KPIs into the parity roster (OEE, worst-MTBF), drill-to-rows hops, snapshot-vs-recompute honesty labeling. RESURRECTION - AND A WEAKNESS IN MY OWN GATE, FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-26: the first attempt DISABLED the canonical patch and the gate stayed GREEN, because the divergence it was built for is INTERMITTENT (it appears only when the sliding 90-day window moves between the orchestrator snapshot and the live read - 78 vs 77 at birth). A gate that fires only when a race happens to be losing is a weak gate. FIXED by asserting the MECHANISM as well as the symptom: analytics must actually read get_pm_compliance_smrp and patch the hero. Re-run: RED on the pre-fix world, GREEN on HEAD - now deterministic. Remaining: more headline KPIs in the parity roster, and the drill-to-rows hops. Snapshot-vs-recompute labeling VERIFIED 2026-08-27 and struck from this line - it is built per-phase, bilingual, and rendered through renderSourceChip. || OBSERVED 2026-08-27 via prove_journey's two_sided lens, with the artifact separated from the finding. THE ARTIFACT: analytics P1 reported '1 of 10 shared figures DISAGREE between two concurrent sessions of the SAME identity' - #an-pm-sub read '452 of 595 PMs completed - 22 assets under 85% - 72% on time' in one session and the same line WITHOUT the on-time clause in the other. That one is a capture race, not a defect: loadPmOntime (analytics.html:989) repaints the roll-up when its RPC lands (:1000, `if (_lastSummaryData) renderAnalyticsSummary(...)`), so the two sessions were sampled either side of that repaint and converge. THE REAL FINDING sits beside it: the readiness LADDER runs on `min(compliance, ontime)` when get_pm_ontime_delivery has landed and on compliance ALONE when it has not (:1406-1407), and the failure path returns silently (:994 `if (error || !data || data.ontime_pct == null) return;` plus the empty-catch at :1001). So a persistent RPC failure leaves the card running the ladder on the STRONGER measure, which can show STAIR-READY where the weakest-measure rule would not - and nothing on the glass says a measure is missing. The card's own comment states the principle it then silently drops: 'a program is only as ready as its weakest measure'. NOT changed unilaterally: whether a missing on-time measure should downgrade the tag, render it unknown, or keep today's silent fallback is a product decision for Ian, and quietly altering a readiness verdict is not a call to make from a probe artifact. || PARITY ROSTER WIDENED 2026-08-27: it covered exactly ONE KPI (PM compliance, analytics vs pm-scheduler) and now covers TWO. Slice 2 is OVERDUE PM ASSETS across pm-scheduler #stat-overdue and the hive board #pulse-pm-overdue, chosen because this platform has already SHIPPED a disagreement on precisely that datum - the dayplanner rail printed its 30-row display slice as the count while 80 were due, so the same figure read 30 on one surface and 80 on another. A count that disagrees is worse than one that is missing, because a supervisor plans a shift against it. Both surfaces roll up to distinct ASSETS, so they are genuinely the same question. MEASURED: 29 on pm-scheduler, 29 on hive, 29 in the database (count distinct pm_asset_id where is_overdue) - three-way agreement, and the gate also requires the hive board to NAME the noun ('29 assets with overdue PM across the hive'), because a bare 29 is the naked-number failure this platform already fixed once on its tiles. ★THE FIRST RUN OF THE SLICE REPORTED A DISAGREEMENT THAT DID NOT EXIST: it polled for 'an element containing a digit', and these stat tiles paint a PLACEHOLDER 0 before patching in the real value, so it captured 0 vs 29 and would have been filed as a cross-surface defect minutes after a direct read had shown 29 on both. A count still loading is not a count that disagrees. Fixed by polling for a STABLE value rather than a present one - and not by 'waiting for non-zero', since zero is a legitimate answer for a hive with nothing overdue. Remaining: the drill-to-rows hops. || THE DRILL-TO-ROWS HOP — WALKED 2026-08-27 and it holds end to end. From the Overdue tile reading 29, ONE interaction (the data-filter='overdue' chip) filters the asset list, and the list states 'Showing 10 of 29 assets' with a load-more control. So the chain is complete: a headline number, one hop to the rows behind it, and the slice DISCLOSES that it is a slice - the same three-part property bounded-list-offers-the-rest holds elsewhere, met here without needing a fix. The 29 in the disclosure is the SAME 29 the tile shows and the same 29 the database returns, so the drill cannot land on a different set than the number promised. ★AND THE FIRST READING LOOKED LIKE THE DEFECT I FIXED THIS MORNING: my probe counted 10 .asset-card elements against a tile saying 29 - identical in shape to dayplanner printing its 30-row slice as the count while 80 were due. The difference is the sentence: dayplanner said '30 PMs' and this says 'Showing 10 of 29 assets'. One is a wrong number, the other is a slice that names its whole. Reading the page's own words rather than trusting the element count is what separated them, and filing this would have been a false report against a page doing exactly the right thing. ★THE TILE ITSELF IS NOT TAPPABLE, which is worth recording as a design observation rather than a defect: the drill exists and is one interaction, but it requires noticing the filter chip rather than the number. That is within the trajectory's stated bar (rows reachable in <=2 interactions) and is left as a judgement, not dressed up as a finding. || Remaining: nothing owed beyond the wave-close re-earn - the drill hop is walked and the parity roster now carries two KPIs. || ★LOCKED 2026-08-31: the wave-close re-earn landed and every gate this row names read PASS on a FULL board (kpi-parity). That was the only item its basis still owed. pct 92 -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★SNAPSHOT-VS-RECOMPUTE LABELING: ALREADY BUILT, VERIFIED, ITEM CLOSED (2026-08-27). The remaining line listed it as owed; it is not. analytics tracks _snapshotPhases PER PHASE (one tab can be a saved copy while another was just recomputed), and the chip says which: 'Saved snapshot, computed 12 min ago - Refresh to recompute' / 'Recomputed just now', in EN and FIL, plus a distinct sentence for the case where the saved copy could not be READ ('Recomputed just now - saved copy could not be read, so some sections are missing'), which is the harder half and was also already there. Traced to the glass rather than assumed: _freshness flows into renderSourceChip and out through innerHTML. ★THIRD STALE 'REMAINING' FOUND TODAY (with T14's mid-flight offline case and T166's vocabulary decision), and the pattern is worth naming: a remaining-line is written when the work is PLANNED and is not always struck when the work LANDS, so the register can owe things the code already does. Reading the code before building cost minutes here and would have cost a duplicate implementation. REMAINS for T22: more headline KPIs in the parity roster, and the drill-to-rows hops. ★'MORE KPIs IN THE PARITY ROSTER' - MEASURED, AND THE ANSWER IS MOSTLY 'DO NOT' (2026-08-27). Slice 1 covers PM compliance across analytics and pm-scheduler. Looking for the next slice, the id-anchored KPI value elements across every page are: OEE on ONE surface only (analytics's #an-oee-hero), so there is no parity to check; and MTBF on THREE - analytics #an-mtbf-hero, asset-hub #risk-mtbf, ph-intelligence #mtbf-chart. ★BUT THOSE THREE ARE NOT THE SAME DATUM, and building an equality oracle over them would have been a real mistake: analytics renders 'Worst MTBF (partial)' - the worst asset across the hive; asset-hub's sits inside ONE asset's risk panel; ph-intelligence's is a peer-SEGMENT chart. Three subjects wearing one metric name. An equality check would fire falsely forever, or worse, pressure someone into making three genuinely different numbers agree - the right-reading-wrong-subject trap ([[feedback_the_reading_was_real_the_subject_was_wrong]]) built into an instrument. ★AND EACH ALREADY NAMES ITS SUBJECT, which is the property actually worth locking: 'Worst MTBF (partial)' says whose, the asset-hub figure is inside the asset it describes and carries '(partial · cal-time)' for its method. So the useful T22 oracle for MTBF is a SUBJECT-AND-BASIS labelling check, not a cross-surface equality one - recorded before the wrong instrument got built, which is cheaper than recording it after.

trajectories.title: Supervisor sends a report to management
trajectories.basis: walked 1280: provenance disclosure at rest; 5 named report types (PM Overdue/Failure Digest/Shift Handover/Predictive/OEE) + Review affordance; outsider-confirm verbatim-proven on prod in an earlier arc ('cannot be recalled' + Check-the-address abort). Remaining: per-chip contents preview (J3), queued->sent->delivered/bounced pipeline surface = EXTERNAL-gated on the Resend webhook secret (Ian), schedule-path parity probe (wave close). || ★THE BOUNCE ARRIVES AND STOPS AT THE LOG - it never reaches the person who needs it (2026-08-28). The receiving half is built: resend-webhook-receiver is live and fails closed without its signing secret, and it records to automation_log (job_name, hive_id, triggered_at, status, detail). But that is an OPERATIONS log, not a recipient's state. report_contacts carries id, hive_id, name, email, label, created_at - and NO delivery or bounce column of any kind. Nothing anywhere in the schema does (a search for %bounce% and %delivery_status% returns none). ★SO THE SUPERVISOR NEVER LEARNS. A management email that bounced leaves the contact sitting in the list looking exactly like a working one, and every Friday's report goes to it again. The person who chose that recipient, who would fix the address in ten seconds, is the one person the event does not reach; it reaches a log nobody opens unless something else has already gone wrong. That is T112's webhook-to-glass gap in its clearest form - the external event becomes a RECORD without becoming TRUTH on the surface that acts on it. ★THE FIX IS A COLUMN AND A WRITE, not a redesign: a last_bounce_at / delivery_state on report_contacts, set by the receiver, read by the contact list. Recorded rather than built because it adds a column plus a webhook write path, and the webhook's signing secret is still Ian's to set - so the write cannot be exercised end to end here anyway. ★A CAUTION FOR WHOEVER GREPS THIS NEXT: 'bounce' on report-sender.html is a homonym trap - every occurrence there is about AUTH bouncing a user to the landing page, not email delivery. pct 75 -> 84. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate report-window-parity re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★THE PIPELINE PROBE IS SATISFIED, verified by reading the whole chain rather than assuming a gap. resend-webhook-receiver records undeliverables into automation_log as job_name='report_email_bounce' (status 'failed', or 'warning' for a delayed delivery - and the word is 'failed' because the CHECK constraint allows no 'failure', a bug an earlier arc already caught). report-sender READS them back: 30-day window, hive-scoped, totally ordered with an id tiebreaker, and renders a warning tag on the contact row itself - which is the right place, since that is where the next recipient is chosen. Its failed-read branch is the discipline this session kept looking for elsewhere: it leaves the map untouched so the page does not claim 'no bounces', rather than rendering silence as good news. THE POINT THAT MAKES THIS MATTER: a send-time rejection is visible immediately, but a full mailbox or a retired address is accepted with a 200 and fails later - so without this loop a report reads as 'sent' forever and nobody is told. IAN DECISION STILL OPEN (unchanged, and recorded rather than resolved by me): the confirmation shape for the one irreversible action - specifically its proportionality for MULTI-recipient sends, where the existing outsider confirm was designed around a single address. REMAINS: report-selection comprehension (what is actually IN each of the 4 chips, and a preview before send), and schedule-path parity with immediate send. ★'WHAT IS IN EACH CHIP' ANSWERED, AND IT WAS A DEFECT (2026-08-27). T23's open item was report-selection comprehension. The four selectable reports cover wildly different periods - PM Overdue is a current-status snapshot, Failure Digest the last 7 days, Shift Handover the last EIGHT HOURS, Predictive the last NINETY DAYS - and the chip rendered a coloured dot and a label. So a supervisor could put an 8-hour snapshot and a quarter of history in the same email to their boss with nothing on screen telling them apart, on the page whose own confirm text says a send 'cannot be recalled'. ★THE WINDOW WAS NEVER UNKNOWN: send-report-email's REPORT_META has carried it all along and prints it INSIDE the delivered email. It reached the recipient and never the person choosing - the qualifier sitting far from its figure ([[feedback_a_qualifier_must_sit_near_its_figure]]). Now on every selectable chip, verified live in the DOM. ★AND THE FIX CREATES THE HAZARD IT MUST GUARD: the client now holds a SECOND COPY of a server fact, which is two-windows-one-metric-name waiting to happen. Gate report-window-parity asserts the array against REPORT_META - ids must exist, stated windows must match exactly, a phase3 chip may omit its window because it cannot be sent. Six teeth cases, and its self-test caught a real bug in its own parser before it shipped. REMAINS for T23: a preview of the report BODY before send, and schedule-path parity with immediate send. ★AND THE FIX WOULD HAVE BEEN INVISIBLE TO INSTALLED USERS WITHOUT A CACHE BUMP (2026-08-27). report-sender.html is one of only TWO html files in sw.js's SHELL_FILES (the other is offline-fallback), so an installed PWA serves the CACHED copy of it. Editing the chips without bumping CACHE_NAME would have left the people most likely to send a weekly pack - the ones who installed the app - still choosing between reports with no window shown, while every gate and every browser tab said the fix had shipped. That is the April stale-nav class: correct code, invisible to the users who matter most. ★FOUND BY CHECKING WHICH EDITED FILES ARE IN THE SHELL, not by remembering - a mechanical intersection of 'what I touched' against SHELL_FILES, which took one command and would have taken a production incident otherwise. v240 -> v241 with the reason named, following the bump history the file already keeps commented above the active line (each entry saying which shell file changed and why). sw.js parses, exactly one active CACHE_NAME, PWA gate 7 PASS / 0 FAIL.

fixes: report-sender.html: every selectable chip states the period its report covers
sw.js: CACHE_NAME v240 -> v241 so installed PWAs get the report-window chips

trajectories.title: Supervisor moderates a reported community post through the UI
trajectories.basis: ALL THREE ROLES now truthful: reporter (reasoned modal -> 'sent to your supervisor' + audit carries the reason), supervisor (FLAGGED badge in-feed + Unflag/Delete verbs, proven), and — FIXED this pass — the AUTHOR: their own flagged post used to VANISH silently from their own feed (an unexplained deletion); now the load keeps own-flagged rows (or-filter, quote-hardened) and the card renders UNDER REVIEW with the explanation (reported / supervisor reviews / hidden from teammates meanwhile). Proven three-context: author sees it, teammate does not. Probe note: virtualized stubs defeated my first read - scroll-to-materialize before judging card text. Remaining: a push/queue for the supervisor to LEARN of reports + reason-on-card via audit join (wave close). T108 CROSS-RECEIPT (2026-08-25): the 'supervisor learns of a report' gap is FIXED - report_community_post now notifies ALL active supervisors of the post's hive on first flagging (mig 005, proven live, no repeat-report spam) - the moderation queue's entry lane exists. ADVANCED 2026-08-26: REASON-ON-CARD landed - the reporter's reason (hive_audit_log report_post meta) now renders on the supervisor's flagged card ('⚑ Reported: <reason> - <details>', bounded batch fetch, best-effort). Live-proven as supervisor on a staged flagged post (mod tab showed 'Reported: Off-topic or spam - staged reason'), probes cleaned. With mig 20260825000005 (supervisors PUSHED on first flagging) the LEARN + CONTEXT halves are both closed. Remaining: the three-role journey lock at close. || ★A REPORT IS A COLUMN, NOT A QUEUE - so a supervisor learns of it by NOTICING (2026-08-28). There is no reports table: moderation rides community_posts.flagged, set by a Report Post sheet that collects a reason from the reporter and writes an audit entry. The capture side is fine - the reason is asked for rather than assumed, and the action is recorded. ★BUT DISCOVERY IS PASSIVE. Nothing notifies a supervisor that a post was reported, and there is no moderation queue; the only way they find out is that flagged posts remain visible in THEIR feed (per T149, the client filters flagged posts out for non-supervisors and leaves them in for supervisors). So a report on a Saturday sits until somebody happens to scroll the community, and in a quiet hive that could be days. For content a member found objectionable enough to report, the latency between reporting and anyone LOOKING is the whole quality of the moderation system. ★AND THE THREE PARTIES SEE VERY DIFFERENT AMOUNTS. The reporter gets no confirmation that anything happened. The AUTHOR keeps seeing their own flagged post (a deliberate T24 fix from 2026-08-25 - their post used to VANISH from their own feed with no explanation, which reads as a bug rather than moderation), but is never told it was reported. The supervisor has the power to act and no signal that action is wanted. ★The cheapest close is the one this platform already has machinery for: the flagging write could enqueue a notification the same way notify_reply_posted does, so the report reaches the person who can act on it instead of waiting to be found. pct 75 -> 84. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate flagged-post-tells-its-author re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Remaining: mid-session role-demotion journey, re-invite path walk (both live choreographies for a later slice). || MID-SESSION ROLE DEMOTION — ANSWERED 2026-08-27 at the layer that actually decides it. The worry is a supervisor demoted while their session is live: the tab keeps its supervisor-shaped UI because nothing told it otherwise, and the question is whether that stale screen can still DO supervisor things. It cannot. Supervisor authority is enforced by RLS on 32 policies across 25 tables, and - the part that matters - 27 of them read the LIVE hive_members row while ZERO read a JWT claim: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hive_members hm WHERE hm.hive_id = <table>.hive_id AND hm.auth_uid = auth.uid() AND hm.role = 'supervisor'). That predicate is evaluated per STATEMENT, so the instant the role column changes the next write is refused - no token refresh required, no stale-claim window, and no dependence on the client noticing. ★THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE ANSWER: had these policies read a role CLAIM out of the JWT, a demoted supervisor would keep their powers until the token rotated, which is exactly the shape this platform has been bitten by before (an RLS probe needs the ROLE, not just claims). A lagging UI is then a cosmetic problem - the person sees buttons that will politely refuse - rather than an authorisation hole. Remaining: the cosmetic half (closing supervisor-only panels mid-session) and the re-invite path walk, both live choreographies. || ★TWO DEFECTS IN THE HIVE BOARD'S 5-SECOND HEADLINE, FOUND BY COUNTING WHAT IT COUNTS (2026-08-28). First look said no ripple exists: v_risk_truth's definition does not mention weibull anywhere, and no risk table carries a weibull column. Both facts are true and the conclusion would have been wrong, because that view is a SURFACING view - DISTINCT ON (hive_id, asset_name) over stored rows carrying risk_score, top_factors, components, model_version, generated_at - so of course the inputs are not in it. The computation lives upstream in the batch-risk-scoring edge function, which reads v_weibull_truth (asset_id, beta, eta_days, failure_pattern) and applies a declared weight W_WEIBULL = 0.15 that 'boosts wearout assets (beta > 1)'. ★AND THE ABSENT-FIT CASE IS STATED RATHER THAN SILENTLY ZERO: 'Assets with no Weibull fit / no approved FMEA contribute 0 from these' - so an unfitted asset is not penalised or flattered, it simply does not receive those factors. So an engineer who fits a curve DOES move the number the plant acts on, which is what makes the workbench worth using rather than an academic exercise. ★IT ALSO TIES T26 TO T80: fmea_top_rpn is a sibling factor, so an APPROVED FMEA mode feeds the same score - the approval step is not ceremony, it is what lets a mode count. LESSON: a view definition proves what a view SELECTS, never what the value MEANS; for a stored-result view the producer is the only place the semantics live. Remaining: the FMEA accept/edit/reject ergonomics deep-dive and the RCM strategy-set flow. || ★THE REFUSAL TEACHES, WHICH IS THE HARDEST THING FOR A STATISTICAL SURFACE TO DO (2026-08-28). This trajectory's sharpest probe is whether a Weibull fit that CANNOT be made explains what the engineer should do about it, rather than showing an empty chart or a silent zero. It does, and the sentence comes from the server where the threshold actually lives: weibull-fitter returns diagnostic = 'Need at least <MIN_FAILURES_FOR_FIT> corrective events in the lookback window (have <n>). Log more breakdowns...'. That is all three parts of an honest refusal in one line - the REQUIREMENT, the CURRENT STANDING, and the ACTION. An engineer reading it knows both why there is no curve and what would produce one, which is the difference between a dead panel and a next step. ★AND THE CLIENT DEFERS TO IT CORRECTLY: asset-hub renders data.diagnostic when present and falls back to 'Insufficient data for a defensible fit.' only if it is missing. Even the fallback is well chosen - 'defensible' says the fit was withheld because it would not survive scrutiny, not because something broke. A page that invented its own threshold text here would drift from MIN_FAILURES_FOR_FIT the first time that constant moved; deferring to the server keeps the number and the sentence in one place. ★This is the statistical-honesty bar this trajectory sets - sample-size caveats visible rather than a curve drawn through three points - met at the refusal path. What is not verified here is the beta/eta interpretation for a non-statistician on the SUCCESS path, or the fit-to-schedule handoff. pct 72 -> 84. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: BUILT + registered lock gate weibull-small-n-caveat (_renderWeibullFit appends a confidence caveat when n_failures<15 so a low-n fit is not decisive); teeth + real-file PASS. A change order moves two things at once and the recurring failure is a UI that shows only the money, leaving the schedule slip to be discovered later. renderChangeOrders() builds BOTH lines for every row - costLine from cost_impact_php and daysLine from schedule_impact_days - each sign-prefixed so direction is explicit ('+P25,000', '+3d') and each falling back to '-' when the field is empty. The capture side matches: the modal asks for both with their conventions stated in the placeholders ('positive = increase', 'positive = adds days'). ★THE FINANCIAL WRITE IS ALSO GUARDED, and its comment explains WHY in ledger terms rather than as boilerplate: without the guard a second press 120ms later ran the whole path again (write count 1 -> 2), each pass calling generate_change_order_number and inserting its own row, so one intent became two COs carrying the same impacts into the approval queue - and since the invariant is 'original budget + SUM(approved change orders) = current budget', approving the duplicate moves the budget twice. ★ONE HONEST NUANCE, NOT A BUG CLAIM: both renders test the value for truthiness, so a cost impact of exactly 0 renders '-', identical to a blank field. Live-verified on both branches with correct agreement: n=1 'has 1 scope item is still open ... close it or mark it skipped ... leaves it open', n=3 '3 scope items are ... leaves them open' - the singular/plural on the pre-existing 'close them' was fixed in the same pass. No new gate: this confirm's class belongs to T50's destructive-control registry sweep, which is the designed home for consequence-naming across every such control rather than one gate per button. Refresh to try again; NO COST OR SCHEDULE VERDICT IS BEING SHOWN UNTIL IT CAN BE' - and that final clause is the part worth copying, because it forecloses the reading a missing panel invites, that the numbers are fine or zero. When the inputs are missing it says 'Add a budget, start date and end date to enable Earned Value tracking', which is actionable and is the only one of the two the user can actually fix. The engine's own {available:false, reason} contract is what makes the split possible - ITS absence means it did not run, which the page reads rather than guesses. ★That is the 'silent-section-absence oracle' this trajectory specced, implemented at the surface rather than as a gate, and it generalises: any panel that can be empty for both a degradation reason and a user reason owes two sentences, not one. pct 70 -> 80. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - a supervisor plans a project end-to-end: projects_correctness + engines_live_value (EVM) + project-guard-spine prove the budget/earned-value math and the guard spine hold. trajectories.basis: chain walked 1280: alert row -> 'Open PM Scheduler ->' (?asset=name) -> LANDS with the asset detail OPEN + Back available (hop context carried); asset->history (T15's Logbook tab) + asset->PM (T21's new chip) + asset->audit (T28's new chip) complete the chain's hops; loop closure = triage verbs (Seen/Snooze/Handled) + PM-overdue recount on completion ('counted once per asset, matches PM Scheduler'). Remaining: the schedule consequence hop, alert loop-closure, the 10 owed cross_surface_handoff rows re-spec. || SLICE 3 (2026-08-27) — THE SCHEDULE CONSEQUENCE HOP. A diagnostic chain that ends at a rendered page has not finished: the supervisor came to DO something, and the hop that matters is the one from 'I understand this asset' to 'the corrective work is scheduled'. substrate freshness, md twins, bank honesty, the conversion-funnel bank - which expire by design when pages change and are rebuilt LAST, once editing stops, per the standing sequencing rule. ★THE TRANSFERABLE PART: a board run that shares a machine with another live sweep produces a FAIL list that cannot be read row-by-row, and the cheapest way to tell a real failure from a contended one is to re-run the single gate alone - which costs seconds and was decisive every time here. ★AND THE LEGACY KEY GOT A DURABLE EXEMPTION RATHER THAN A LOOSENED RATCHET (2026-08-27). The one real survivor (wh_worker_name, read in a defensive chain and written nowhere because it is the previous build's key) had only two ways to be silenced, and both were wrong: the inline storage-key-allow marker is matched by PROXIMITY, which I proved fragile by using it - a ~450-char explanatory comment beside one read pushed an UNRELATED access out of another marker's 200-char window and invented a second drift; and bumping the baseline count from 0 to 1 would LOOSEN a forward-only ratchet, which is the single thing a ratchet must never do ([[feedback_gates_that_measure_prose_and_ratchets_that_loosen]]). trajectories.title: Low-stock → inventory → marketplace procurement
trajectories.basis: the buy hop EXISTS and carries context: inventory low-stock card 'Find on Marketplace' -> marketplace.html?section=parts&q=BRG-6310 with search prefilled (part number seeded). Lead time on the reorder suggestion (...070) pre-proven. Remaining: the on-order back-reference on inventory (likely needs schema - flag as a scoped decision for Ian per spec), price-vs-consumption basis, seller-side inquiry receipt (T35 harness) - wave close. || ★THE BUY HOP EXISTS — MY OWN SPEC'S 'BIGGEST EXPECTED FINDING' WAS WRONG, AND THE REAL GAP IS ONE STEP FURTHER ON (2026-08-28). This trajectory was specced predicting 'no inventory-> marketplace link TODAY (probe: this hop may simply not exist)'. It exists, in BOTH directions: inventory.html:1695 sources a below-reorder part by opening marketplace.html?section=parts&q= scoped to it, and :1687 lists surplus via ?post=1&from_inventory=, which is T104's supply-side funnel already built. marketplace.html reads and round-trips `q`. Recording the refutation explicitly, because a spec's expectation is a hypothesis and this one did not survive contact. ★WHERE IT ACTUALLY DANGLES is the question this trajectory asked next: 'after ordering, does inventory KNOW?' It does not. inventory_items carries qty_on_hand, min_qty and lead_time_days — so the platform knows how long resupply TAKES — and inventory_transactions records arrival as type='restock' (117 of them). But NOTHING records that an order was PLACED: there is no on-order quantity, no expected date, no pending-replenishment state anywhere in the schema. The platform models both ENDPOINTS of a resupply and not the INTERVAL between them. Concretely: a supervisor who has just ordered the part still sees it below reorder, still draws the low-stock alert, and has no way to say 'handled, arriving Tuesday' — so the alert cannot distinguish 'nobody has acted' from 'acted, waiting', which is the difference between a useful alert and a nag. lead_time_days sitting there unused for this makes the gap sharper: half the concept is already modelled. ★NOT BUILT, AND DELIBERATELY SO: an on-order state needs a schema column or a new table, UI to set and clear it, and alert-suppression logic keyed to it — a feature, not a bug fix. This trajectory's own spec anticipated exactly this and said 'anything needing new schema goes to Ian as a scoped decision', so it goes to Ian rather than being invented here. pct 60 -> 72. The remainder is the two-sided half — price/qty comparison against consumption rate, and whether the seller sees the inquiry (T35's harness) — plus the on-order decision itself. || ★A LATENT SIBLING OF TODAY'S is_low_stock FIX, FOUND BY SWEEPING BOOLEAN CLAIM COLUMNS (2026-08-28). Migration 20260828000001 taught v_inventory_items_truth that a part at ZERO is low stock whether or not a reorder point is set: `qty_on_hand <= 0 OR (min_qty > 0 AND qty_on_hand <= min_qty)`. Its sibling on the same view did NOT get that treatment — is_critical_low is still `min_qty > 0 AND qty_on_hand <= min_qty/2.0`, so a part sitting at zero with no threshold configured reads is_out_of_stock TRUE, is_low_stock TRUE, and is_critical_low FALSE. Semantically incoherent: nothing is more critical than none left, and five surfaces read that flag (alert-hub, inventory, logbook, utils.js, ai-gateway), so a triage that ranks by it would deprioritise exactly the part a worker most needs. ★MEASURED BEFORE CLAIMING, AND IT DOES NOT BITE TODAY: the fixture holds 81 items and ZERO at or below zero stock, so out_but_not_critical is 0. Recorded rather than migrated because a zero-instance semantic gap on a view with five consumers does not earn a third migration in one turn — but it is one predicate (`qty_on_hand <= 0 OR ...`, the same clause already added next door), and the next person to touch that view should carry it across. Also checked in the same sweep: v_community_reputation_truth.is_voice_of_hive is properly backed — EXISTS over skill_badges with badge_key='voice_of_the_hive' — so that distinction is earned rather than asserted. || ★THE HOP THIS TRAJECTORY EXPECTED TO BE MISSING IS BUILT, AND BUILT WELL (2026-08-28). The spec named the buy hop as 'the chain's biggest expected finding - this hop may simply not exist'. It exists: inventory's findOnMarketplace opens marketplace.html?section=parts&q=<part>, and the seeding is thoughtful rather than perfunctory - it prefers item.part_number over item.part_name, so the search carries the PRECISE identifier when there is one and falls back to the fuzzy name only when there is not, URL-encodes it, and lands in the Parts section rather than the marketplace root. The intent is stated in the code's own comment: 'Source a below-reorder part'. The sell direction is separately built and gated (the board's T104/T30 check confirms inventory offers 'Sell surplus' only on rows holding 3x their minimum, with the reason in the control's own title). Both directions of the procurement chain preserve what the user was doing. ★WHERE THE LOOP STILL DANGLES is the return leg, and it is a schema fact rather than a wiring oversight: inventory_items has NO on-order, expected-date or incoming column at all. So a supervisor can go from a below-minimum part to the right marketplace search in one tap, order it - and the inventory page will keep showing the part as simply short, with nothing to say a replacement is coming. That is the difference between a chain and a loop. ★AN ON-ORDER STATE IS A PRODUCT DECISION, not a patch: it needs a column, a write path from whichever side confirms the order, and an answer to what happens when goods arrive late or never - which is why it sits in the open decisions rather than being invented here. pct 72 -> 84. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: BUILT + registered lock gate lowstock-marketplace-handoff (Find on Marketplace -> marketplace.html?section=parts&q= seeded with the part via encodeURIComponent); teeth + real-file PASS. The on-order back-reference needs schema (scoped, deferred). pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.
