trajectories.note: ★THE RIGHT-TO-ERASURE IS VOICE-ONLY, AND THE PAGE NEVER SAID WHERE TO GO (2026-08-27). Tracing what a worker can take back took FOUR corrections, and every intermediate answer would have shipped a false statement into the platform's most private surface: (1) 'there is no delete' - WRONG: voice-handler's _isErasureRequest detects "delete my voice history" / "burahin mo lahat", the agent asks for a yes because it cannot be undone, a scoped DELETE runs against that worker's rows and an audit row records it; (2) 'you can say OR TYPE it' - WRONG: the check sits in _converseInline, called only from _onStopRecording, so it is reached ONLY after a voice recording, and this page's typed box goes processTurn -> callJournalAgent -> ai-gateway without ever touching voice-handler; (3) there is no typed route anywhere - assistant.html has no erasure path and the companion panel has no text input; (4) a SINGLE note cannot be removed at all, because renderHistory offers only 'Speak again' and ai-gateway persists the row inside the same call that generates the reply. ★WHY VOICE-ONLY MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS: this page's typed fallback exists, in its own words, for 'a loud plant floor, a denied mic, or a worker who cannot speak' - precisely the people left with no way to invoke the right. ★AND THE FIX WAS ALMOST DUPLICATION: the permanence was ALREADY disclosed on the primary surface ('saved as soon as the assistant replies ... an entry cannot be edited or removed here afterwards'), and a first attempt added a SECOND copy of it inside a collapsed <details> nobody opens - a new element surfacing what already had a home. Reverted. What was genuinely missing was the other half: the copy said a note cannot be removed HERE and never said where it CAN be. One clause now completes that sentence, pointing at the documented Data Rights Request route which validate_erasure_path_intact already proves the database honours. The voice phrase is deliberately NOT advertised as the remedy, because for a worker who cannot speak it is not one. ★STILL OPEN (product decision, and small): wiring the typed path to the same check - both _isErasureRequest and _executeErasure are already exported, and _executeErasure needs only db + hive_id + worker_name, all available on this page - plus whether a per-entry delete should exist at all given the row is embedded for retrieval.

trajectories.title: Every export control produces a truthful, complete artifact
trajectories.basis: flagship audited GREEN by design: audit-log's Export CSV does a paginated FULL fetch (range-walked, never the display window), resolves the range filter the same way the screen does, falls back HONESTLY ('exports the N entries loaded' - named, never silent), and the artifact STATES ITS OWN SCOPE in embedded meta (hive, range) - the compliance-export row-cap class is extinct here. Remaining: the export-fidelity sweep across engineering-design BOM/SOW CSVs + resume + PDF exporter, psql row-count audits per artifact (wave close). (2026-08-26: one more capped export found and fixed by a different lens - logbook's TEAM branch exported the loaded window (~30) instead of the filtered whole (941). See T129.) EXPORT-FIDELITY SWEEP COMPLETED 2026-08-26 - every download path on the platform enumerated and each judged against the cap class: (1) logbook CSV - MINE branch already paged (earlier arc), TEAM branch FIXED today (was exporting ~30 of 941; now paginated with the same filters + honest shortfall toast, proven 941==941); (2) audit-log CSV - already hardened 2026-08-19 for this exact class, with the scope resolved the same way the screen resolves it; (3) resume exports (cover letter .txt, JSON Resume, .docx) - a single document per person, no cap by shape; (4) engineering-design BOM CSV + SVG diagram - written from the in-memory working set the user just generated, which IS the artifact, not a bounded DB read. So the capped-export class is closed on every path that has one. Remaining: basis/window STAMPED INSIDE the artifacts (a spreadsheet outliving its context), phone download reality, empty-set export honesty. BASIS-INSIDE-THE-ARTIFACT advanced same pass, including a claim MY OWN fix had just falsified: the logbook CSV's meta block said 'Scope: team view (current search results)' - true while that branch exported the loaded window, misleading the moment it started paging the whole filtered history. Rewritten to state what the file now contains AND the cut it was made with: 'Scope: whole team history for hive Baguio Textile Mills, filtered by from=2026-08-18 + to=2026-08-25' (verified by evaluating the export's own inputs in-page). A spreadsheet outlives the screen that made it, so it has to carry its own scope. Harness note: the download itself resisted capture (no download event, no blob interception under the probe), so the mechanics were proven by row count (941==941) and the copy at its source - stated rather than implied. Remaining: the same stamp audited on the other artifacts, phone download reality, empty-set export honesty. || THE STAMP AUDITED ON THE OTHER ARTIFACTS 2026-08-27 - every export surface on the platform, and each one already carries its scope in the form its FORMAT expects. logbook.html builds a meta block and prepends it to the CSV itself (:5985-5997): 'WorkHive logbook export', the worker, Scope - team-history-for-<hive> with the filters joined, or the literal 'no filters applied' so a reader is never left guessing - plus entry count, date range and export timestamp. resume.html's JSON export stamps through the JSON Resume spec's own meta field (cleanResume :1902: version, generator 'WorkHive Resume Builder', lastModified), which is the conformant place for it rather than a bolted-on comment. audit-log's CSV was the flagship and was already done. ★ONE ARTIFACT IS CORRECTLY UNSTAMPED: the cover-letter .txt download (resume.html :1882) is the user's own prose on its way to an employer - a scope line inside it would corrupt the document, not document it. That is a real covered-by-nature, reached by checking what the stamp would DO rather than by assuming. ★AND THE FIRST READING WAS WRONG: grepping for the CSV's 'Scope:' wording scored resume.html at zero and would have filed a missing stamp - the stamp was there in the format's own idiom. A cross-format audit has to ask what each format's provenance slot IS. Remaining: phone download reality, empty-set export honesty. || EMPTY-SET EXPORT HONESTY VERIFIED 2026-08-27. Both DATA exports refuse rather than hand over a file that could be read as loss: logbook.html :5947 and audit-log.html :839 carry the identical guard - if there are no entries, showToast('No entries to export.') and return, no file - so the two surfaces also speak with one voice. Each finishes with a receipt naming the count ('Exported N entries.'). The DEGRADED path is honest too: when the full read fails, logbook falls back to the loaded window and says so in the toast, so a shorter file never passes as a complete one. resume.html is correctly NOT guarded, and that is the interesting half: isEmptyResume() exists, but it requires work AND skills AND education AND projects AND awards AND references to all be empty, so guarding the export on it would refuse a fresh graduate with only their name and contact details a perfectly legitimate file. For a user-authored DOCUMENT, sparse is not the data-integrity ambiguity an empty CSV is. Remaining: phone download reality (needs a device-shaped run). || ★CORRECTION 2026-08-27: the audit above said 'every export surface on the platform' and that was WRONG - it grepped *.html only, so it saw three surfaces and missed the .js one. engineering-design.js carries a BOM CSV (downloadBomCsv :30994) and an SVG diagram export, and the BOM is precisely the case the stamp exists for: it writes _bomItems.filter(it => it.checked !== false) - a SUBSET - as bare header+rows with no provenance at all. A BOM with unchecked lines dropped reaches a supplier looking like the complete bill of materials, and an incomplete one was indistinguishable from a complete one on disk. A denominator that only looks at one file extension is how a surface stays unaudited while the audit reads as exhaustive. FIXED: the CSV now opens with a meta block naming the export, the project, the calculation, the export time, and - the load-bearing line - 'Items: N of M selected', with ' - unselected lines are NOT in this file' appended ONLY when N < M, so a complete export carries no false alarm. Verified by evaluating the builder on sample data (3 of 7 warns, 7 of 7 is quiet, an unnamed project falls back to '(unnamed)'); engineering-design.js parses and _calcType/_bomItems/_lastInputs are all in scope at the call site. The SVG diagram is deliberately left alone - it is a drawing, not a data slice. Remaining: phone download reality, and the PDF exporter's own row-count audit. || THE PDF/PRINT AUDIT DONE 2026-08-27, and it is a DIFFERENT AXIS from the one already locked. export-reads-its-own-set holds the ROW axis: an export must not inherit the render buffer's cap, so no row goes missing. The PDF surfaces fail differently. All three (resume.html, project-report.html, engineering-design.js) render the PDF from the DOM - html2pdf/jsPDF capture #report-panel or the print stylesheet - so the artifact is a picture of the screen, and the risk moves from the row to the CELL. FOUND: project-report.html rendered every daily-progress log through `.slice(0, 200)` with nothing appended. That page exists to be PRINTED and handed to a stakeholder, and on paper there is no hover, no expand, no scroll: a 350-character blocker arrived as a complete-looking 200-character sentence, usually cut mid-word, with no way for the reader to know anything had been removed - and Blockers is precisely the field that carries WHY a project is late. ★THE FIX IS NOT 'STOP TRUNCATING': the printed column is real and text has to fit. The cap stays; what changed is that it now SPEAKS - a conditional marker on the cell plus a one-line note under the table, appearing ONLY when the cap actually bites, so a complete report carries no false alarm. Both are print-safe (a disclosure hidden by @media print discloses nothing to the person holding the printout) and --muted #5B6878 on white paper is legible. VERIFIED LIVE on WO-2026-001: 6/6 rows render (matching the DB), zero marks and no note because no fixture value exceeds 200, while clip() on a synthetic 500-char value keeps exactly 200 and marks it and a 50-char value passes untouched; no page errors. ★TWO INSTRUMENT FAULTS CAUGHT EN ROUTE, both mine: I first probed a project in ANOTHER HIVE and read the empty section as my own regression - it was RLS refusing correctly - and then read a 7-second load as a broken page when it simply had more data than the previous one. Neither was a product defect. Gate printed-truncation-is-disclosed registered, 5/5 synthetic negatives (bare slice, unconditional helper, marker hidden in print, helper with no marker, real surface clean); one of those negatives initially replaced a string absent from the source and so tested the UNCHANGED file - a negative control that negated nothing - and was fixed to strip every marker token including the title attribute. Remaining: phone download reality (T44's installed-mode lane). || PHONE DOWNLOAD REALITY — CAPTURED 2026-08-27 at a 390 viewport, by intercepting the actual download event rather than asserting the button exists. An export control that produces nothing a worker can find is not an export, and the phone is where that fails. RESULT: the download fires, the file is named workhive-logbook-<worker>-<date>.csv - self-identifying on both axes, so it is findable in a downloads folder a week later - and the CSV OPENS WITH ITS OWN BASIS: 'Worker: ...', 'Scope: whole team history for hive Baguio Textile Mills, filtered by from=2026-08-20 + to=2026-08-27', 'Entries: 1', 'Date range: ...', 'Exported: ...'. That scope line is the property this trajectory exists for: the artifact states the FILTER that produced it, so a one-row export cannot be mistaken for the whole history - the compliance-export row-cap incident in reverse, where the file now argues its own limits. Verified end to end with no page errors. The only cosmetic note is a space in the filename ('Leandro Marquez'), which is legal everywhere the platform ships and is recorded rather than 'fixed' into a finding. Remaining: nothing owed beyond the wave-close re-earn - the row axis, the cell axis (printed truncation) and now the phone download are all measured. || ★EVERY CSV EXPORT WAS MOJIBAKING FILIPINO NAMES IN EXCEL - FIXED (2026-08-27). Neither CSV export on the platform emitted a byte-order-mark, so Excel opened them as the system codepage and an asset like 'Pena Line 2' (with the tilde n that this platform's own diacritic-folding code exists to handle) arrived mangled. On a product whose users are Filipino and whose machines and workers carry that character routinely, every exported logbook and audit trail was arriving wrong in the tool people actually open them with. ★AND audit-log LOOKED CORRECT: its blob already declared type 'text/csv;charset=utf-8'. Excel ignores the MIME charset and sniffs the bytes, so the declaration reads exactly like the fix while doing nothing - the most expensive kind of near-miss, because it stops anyone looking further. FIXED both blobs to lead with ﻿, VERIFIED AT RUNTIME by intercepting Blob construction on both pages: startsWithBOM true, type text/csv;charset=utf-8, zero page errors. ★MY OWN DETECTION LIED TWICE FIRST: a scan for 'BOM' reported logbook and engineering-design as compliant, because in THIS codebase 'BOM' means BILL OF MATERIALS ('asset-BOM prioritization', 'specify refrigerant type in the BOM') - domain vocabulary colliding with the thing I was searching for. Then searching the real character found ﻿ in logbook and ph-intelligence, which turned out to be at line 1 before <!DOCTYPE html> - the HTML FILES were saved with a BOM, nowhere near the export path. Two false greens before the true answer: no export had one. ★AND THERE WAS A THIRD CSV EXPORT, found only by auditing EVERY Blob rather than the two I had already fixed: engineering-design.js's BOM/SOW export, same missing byte-order-mark. Now fixed, so all three lead with ﻿ and declare charset=utf-8. Its runtime path needs a completed calculation to produce a blob, so it is source-verified rather than runtime-verified - the identical idiom is runtime-proven on the other two. ★THE OTHER DOWNLOADS WERE CHECKED AND CORRECTLY LEFT ALONE: resume's application/json must NOT carry a BOM (it breaks strict parsers) and the SVG export needs none. The mark belongs to the format Excel sniffs, not to every download - a sweep that added it everywhere would have broken the JSON export to fix the CSVs. ★ONE MORE SELF-INFLICTED DETAIL: my first patch wrote a LITERAL invisible U+FEFF character into the JavaScript source instead of the ﻿ escape. It works identically at runtime and is a maintenance trap - an invisible character someone will eventually delete or a tool will strip, with no visible diff. Replaced with the readable escape the other two already used. || ★LOCKED 2026-08-31: the wave-close re-earn landed and every gate this row names read PASS on a FULL board (export-reads-its-own-set,printed-truncation-is-disclosed). That was the only item its basis still owed. pct 99 -> 100.

fixes: project-report.html: daily-progress Notes and Blockers now truncate OUT LOUD - a conditional clip() marker plus a table note, both print-safe; the 200-char column cap is unchanged

trajectories.note: ★THE EXPORT FIX WAS UNGATED (2026-08-26). The team-branch export had already been corrected - it used to hand over the feed's render buffer, producing a compliance file that looked whole - but nothing stopped that returning. Gate export-reads-its-own-set asserts every exporter pages its own set with a TOTAL order and never reuses the buffer, and checks the assertion is non-vacuous against real volume (largest hive 1,700 rows vs a 30-row page). Its own first version made TWO false accusations from a fixed character window that ran past the function into a comment and the handler's announced fallback; bodies are now brace-matched. Teeth proven on buffer reuse and on a paged read missing its tiebreak. ★EMPTY-SET EXPORT HONESTY: CHECKED, AND ALREADY SATISFIED (2026-08-27) - recorded as a bounded NEGATIVE result so the item closes instead of being re-investigated. Enumerated every export surface rather than sampling one: audit-log refuses with 'No entries to export.' and logbook with the same sentence, and logbook additionally warns when a fallback would hand over a SHORTER file ('Could not read the full history, so this exports the N entries currently loaded') - which is the sharper half of the same honesty and was already there. resume's downloads are GENERATED artifacts (cover letter, PDF) rather than row-set exports, so the empty-set question does not apply to them; integrations' !rows.length guard is on the IMPORT side. Nothing to fix here. The remaining T49 items are the basis stamp on the other artifacts and phone download reality, both of which need the artifact in hand rather than a source read. ★THE BASIS STAMP ON THE OTHER ARTIFACTS - CHECKED, AND THEY ALL CARRY IT (2026-08-27). logbook's CSV writes a meta block before the rows: Scope (team vs personal, and 'filtered by X' or the explicit 'no filters applied'), Entries, Date range, Exported timestamp. audit-log's does the same and handles the partial case honestly - when the full read fails it exports what it has and SAYS so - with its reasoning written in the source: 'an auditor holding the CSV has no page around it, so completeness must be legible from the artifact rather than inferred from where it came from.' resume's JSON export deliberately carries NO stamp, and that is correct: it emits standards-conformant JSON Resume, and non-schema meta risks breaking the ATS parsers the whole format exists to satisfy. A basis stamp belongs on an artifact DERIVED over a window, not on a document that is simply itself. ★AND THE PDF KEEPS ITS PROVENANCE - VERIFIED UNDER PRINT MEDIA, AFTER I REASONED MY WAY TO THE WRONG ANSWER. project-report has no class='page', so I inferred from a truncated line that the E3 source chip fell back to document.body and was therefore killed by `body > *:not(#ar-print-wrapper) { display: none }` - which would mean the client-facing PDF dropped the one element saying where its numbers came from. Emulating print showed the opposite: the chip's host resolves to main#wh-main-content INSIDE the wrapper, and under print media it computes display:block with its text intact ('Recomputed when this report is generated · Based on your project...'). The inference was wrong because it rested on a line I had only seen truncated - the partial-read trap aimed at myself. Checking cost one probe; recording it would have cost a false finding in the register.

trajectories.title: Destructive-action sweep: proportional confirm + undo everywhere
trajectories.basis: the DENOMINATOR instrument built: tools/build_destructive_control_registry.py generates substrate/reference/destructive_control_registry.json (20 files, 52 whConfirm/whPrompt call sites with message heads + lines, atomic, --check) - the platform's own are-you-sure vocabulary as an unshrinkable roster. Kick/reject/complete confirms consequence-audited in T25/T20/T10 walks. Remaining: the proportionality + undo + receipt sweep across all 52 entries + Z3 adjacency (wave close). || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): audited all 52 registry entries for consequence-naming, and most are strong - 'Linked RCM strategies will cascade', 'They lose the verified badge until re-verified', 'kept for history', 'This cannot be undone'. ★ONE WAS NOT, AND IT WAS THE MOST EXPENSIVE: logbook's 'Remove this asset from the registry?' guarded a real asset_nodes delete while naming NO consequence. Read from pg_constraint, not guessed: that row CASCADES seven children (asset_edges, asset_embeddings, pf_intervals, rcm_fmea_modes, sensor_readings, sensor_topic_map, weibull_fits) and detaches five more (logbook, anomaly_signals, drone_inspections, pm_knowledge, child assets) - and a supervisor reaches it on an APPROVED asset, so months of reliability history could go behind a four-word question. Rewritten to name both halves, because 'what survives' is the half that decides whether someone proceeds. ★AND THE GATE THAT EXISTS FOR THIS CLASS WAS VACUOUS: cascade-confirm-parity's consequence pattern accepted `removes?`/`deletes?`, i.e. the ACTION VERB, so 'Remove this asset...' passed on the word 'Remove'. Nearly every destructive confirm is phrased that way, so it had been reporting 0 while asking nothing. Tightened to require a statement BEYOND the ask; proven by resurrection (old pattern 0, new pattern catches it) and it revealed no other site, so the close cost no backlog. Also regenerated the destructive_control_registry, whose line numbers had drifted. REMAINING: the undo/receipt half and Z3 adjacency across the 52 (wave close). || 51 OF 51 DESTRUCTIVE CONTROLS ARE CONFIRM-GATED, AND THE APPARENT SHORTFALL WAS A UNIT MISMATCH (2026-08-27). The registry - the denominator this trajectory exists to make un-shrinkable - holds 51 destructive controls across 20 files, while validate_destructive_safety reports 29 confirm-sites across 14 pages and passes. That gap reads like 22 unguarded controls until you notice the two are counting DIFFERENT THINGS: the gate counts distinct whConfirm CALL SITES, the registry counts CONTROLS, and several controls legitimately route through one shared handler. Walked every registry entry against its own handler body: 51 examined, ZERO without a whConfirm / confirm / whPrompt gate. ★WHICH IS WHY THE REGISTRY MATTERS MORE THAN THE GATE'S OWN NUMBER: a confirm-site count can look like coverage while saying nothing about how many controls exist, and a control that never entered the registry would be invisible to both. The registry is the denominator no one can silently shrink - that was this trajectory's whole design - and it now reconciles against the handlers rather than against another count. Remaining: proportionality (does each confirm NAME what dies and what survives) and the undo story for the reversible ones - both judgement passes over a set that is now provably complete rather than a sample. || ★A DESTRUCTIVE CONFIRM WAS SAYING 'OK' BECAUSE ITS LABEL OPTION WAS SILENTLY DROPPED (2026-08-27, found while measuring dialog contrast). The contrast probe rendered inventory's remove-a-part confirm and its button read 'OK'. Reading the call: whConfirm(..., { title: 'Remove part', confirmLabel: 'Remove', tone: 'danger' }) - and whConfirm reads okLabel and cancelLabel. All THREE keys were ignored, silently: passing an unsupported option throws nothing, it simply does not apply. So the author explicitly tried to name the consequence, this trajectory's whole property, and the platform quietly rendered a generic OK on a cannot-be-undone action. FIXED to okLabel:'Remove', cancelLabel:'Keep' and PROVEN side by side in one run: old options -> ['Cancel','OK'], fixed -> ['Keep','Remove']. 'Keep' is the better decline too - it names what happens if you say no, so both outcomes are stated. ★AND MY AUDIT MISSED IT: a platform-wide sweep of whConfirm option keys reported 33 okLabel / 33 cancelLabel and effectively no misuse - because the pattern excluded braces, and THIS call's message is a template literal full of ${...}. The one call that got the options wrong was the one shape my regex could not see. Remaining: proportionality wording across the other 50 registry entries, and the undo story for reversible cascades. || PROPORTIONALITY AUDITED ACROSS EVERY CONFIRM, WITH A PARSER THAT COULD ACTUALLY SEE THEM (2026-08-27). Re-ran the sweep using balanced-paren extraction instead of a brace-excluding regex - the exact flaw that had hidden inventory's broken call - and the result is trustworthy: 49 whConfirm calls platform-wide, and only TWO lack an okLabel. One is utils.js:3458, which is whConfirm's own DEFINITION (its parameters are literally `message, opts`) - a false positive. The other is design-system.html:154, 'Delete this demo row?', a component-showcase row that no user acts on, and which also passes { danger: true } - another option whConfirm does not read. So 47 of 48 real destructive confirms name their action rather than saying OK, and the one genuine production outlier was inventory's remove-a-part, fixed this pass. ★THE LESSON IS ABOUT THE PARSER, NOT THE PLATFORM: the first audit cleared the codebase and the second found the defect, using the same corpus - the difference was whether the pattern could read a call whose message is a template literal. A sweep that cannot parse the codebase's ordinary idiom does not report zero findings, it reports zero VISIBILITY, and the two look identical. Remaining: the undo story for reversible cascades. || A NEW CHECK FOR THIS REGISTRY'S SWEEP, found in T27 (2026-08-28): ★DOES THE CONFIRM'S NAMED WAY BACK EXIST UNDER THAT NAME? project-manager's completion confirm said 'Subsequent edits will need to reopen it' and the page has no Reopen control at all - the way back is Put on hold, which stays enabled on a completed project and which the sentence never mentions. The remedy was real and unfindable, which is the walkable-remedy class applied to a CONFIRM rather than a refusal. The sweep should therefore check three things per destructive control, not two: the consequence is named, the reversibility is stated, and any control the copy names ACTUALLY EXISTS with that label. The third is the one no oracle here covers today and the one a reader cannot detect - prose naming a plausible-sounding button reads as correct until someone goes looking for it. Second instance from the same walk: the branch fired by the RISKIER path (completing with open scope items) omitted the reversibility sentence that the safe branch carried, so the sweep should compare branches within one control, not just controls against each other. || ★A REFUSED DELETE ANNOUNCED SUCCESS - FOUND, FIXED, RESURRECTION-PROVEN (2026-08-28), and it is the sharpest instance this registry has. logbook's delete button called confirmDelete(), a wrapper around deleteEntry(). deleteEntry is careful: it confirms, deletes with .select('id'), and speaks honestly on BOTH failure paths - a refused write ('The delete did not go through. The entry is still there.') and an RLS-empty result ('you can only delete your own entries.'). The wrapper undid all of it. It asked THE SAME QUESTION AGAIN, then called deleteEntry, then announced 'Entry deleted. Any XP it earned was reversed.' unconditionally - so on a refusal the honest message appeared and was OVERWRITTEN a moment later by a claim that the entry was gone and its XP reversed. MEASURED against the pre-fix file with a bogus id (the RLS-empty path, no data touched): confirms=2, toasts=['Could not delete: you can only delete your own entries.', 'Entry deleted. Any XP it earned was reversed.'] - the truth first, the lie last, and the lie is what a person reads. After: confirms=1, one toast, the honest one. ★AND A THIRD DEFECT IN THE SAME CONTROL: the button ran document.getElementById('modal').classList.add('hidden') SYNCHRONOUSLY right after calling the async confirm, so the entry's modal vanished before the person had answered and CANCELLING still closed it. deleteEntry closes the modal itself, only once the delete has landed. Three defects in one destructive control, and the registry sweep should look for all three shapes: a wrapper that re-asks, a success message that does not check, and a state change that runs before the answer. || CLASS SWEPT immediately after (2026-08-28): searched every page for the same shape - an awaited call followed by a success toast ('deleted/removed/saved/updated/reversed/complete/sent/approved') with no check in between. THREE instances, all in logbook: the delete receipt inside deleteEntry (guarded - the error and empty-result checks return before it), the 'Entry updated.' receipt (guarded - a comment at the site records it was deliberately placed AFTER the 0-row guard, the same lesson learned on asset-manager: never write a receipt for an amendment the database refused), and the offline 'Edit saved offline' receipt (follows an awaited queue write). Only the confirmDelete wrapper was unguarded, and it is fixed. So the shape is common and the platform is mostly disciplined about it - which is exactly why the one exception was worth finding: it sat inside a page whose OTHER two receipts were carefully guarded, so nothing about the file looked careless. || ★THE LAST NATIVE confirm() IS GONE, AND IT WAS GUARDING THE MOST PUBLIC ACTION THE PLATFORM HAS (2026-08-28). 48 call sites already went through whConfirm; one did not, in founder-console, and it gated publishing a piece of feedback to the PUBLIC roadmap. Its REASONING was already excellent and written down - the comment names the irreversibility precisely ('once /feedback/ is indexed by Google the content can be cached even after un-publishing') and the guard is proportional, firing only on the newly-public transition while un-publishing and saving a private item pass through untouched. The message named what could leak: contact emails, worker names, internal notes. Only the MECHANISM was off-standard. ★WHY THAT MATTERED ANYWAY: a native dialog cannot be translated - the same reason dayplanner, platform-actions and resume each recorded when they migrated - and it renders as browser chrome at the exact moment somebody is about to make another person's words permanently public. Now an awaited whConfirm carrying the same content bilingually, with named buttons ('Publish publicly' / 'Cancel') rather than OK/Cancel, so the irreversible choice is the one that says what it does. saveDrawerChanges was already async, so nothing structural changed. ★VERIFIED: the page parses and boots clean, whConfirm sites 48 -> 49, and the only remaining match for a native confirm anywhere in the codebase is the comment I wrote explaining this migration. pct 96 -> 96. || ★AND THE MIGRATION I JUST MADE BROKE A DIFFERENT RULE, CAUGHT THE SAME DAY (2026-08-28). The bilingual confirm I wrote to replace the native dialog contained an EM DASH in both languages ('nothing private — contact emails, worker names, internal notes'). Arc P bans em dashes in DISPLAYED copy and holds a forward-only ratchet at 0; the gate went red naming founder-console with 2 prose instances, and they were both mine, written about an hour earlier. Replaced with colons, which carry the same 'here is the list' beat. Re-run: 0 displayed em dashes, back to baseline, page boots clean. ★THE PATTERN WORTH RECORDING: I improved one property (a translatable, consequence-naming confirm) and silently regressed another (displayed-copy typography) in the same edit, because I was thinking about dialogs rather than about the platform's copy rules. A gate board is what makes that survivable - the second rule was enforced by something that does not get tired at the end of a long session. Fifth self-inflicted regression caught by this platform's own instruments today, and the argument for every one of them. || 2026-09-01 LOCK INSTRUMENT BUILT: tools/validate_destructive_proportional_confirm.py (destructive-proportional-confirm) — wraps build_destructive_control_registry.py --check (roster current = no destructive action escapes a confirm) + HARD: no blank confirm message + forward-only floor on the roster count; REPORTS (never fails) consequence-light confirms (proportionality of prose is the hand-audit, not a lint - avoids the units_at_boundary over-reach). Self-test teeth-proven (blank/shrink redden, light counted-not-failed). REMAINING to lock: regenerate the roster post-board (build_destructive_control_registry.py - my session edits changed confirm sites, --check is STALE now; regen touches substrate so defer past board 3) + register the gate + board green. Then this row locks on its denominator + the already-done proportionality audit. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered the lock gate destructive-proportional-confirm (built earlier this session, self-test PASS + real-file PASS after regen); the destructive-confirm roster (52 controls) is current + forward-only; okLabel/cancelLabel proportionality fix. Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 96. || LOCKED 2026-09-03: post-board promote - every named gate PASS on the 2026-09-02 full board (1028 PASS run). pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Multi-hive worker switches hives mid-day
trajectories.basis: walked 390 as pabloaguilar (2 hives): a FRESH device learns both memberships (wh_hives rebuilt from server), 'Switch Hive (2)' visible on hive board, switch flips hive name AND ROLE (Lucena supervisor -> Manila worker - role re-scope correct), the next page (pm-scheduler) answers for the new hive, switch-back restores. The .maybeSingle multi-hive fix + hive-capture invariant holding. Remaining: mid-session switch injection on OPEN pages (stale-figure sweep), per-hive draft/filter scoping, chrome current-hive indicator on every page (wave close). CHROME INDICATOR SWEPT + FIXED 2026-08-26: census found 5 pages rendering hive-scoped data with NO current-hive indicator; 3 owed one and got the pm-scheduler chip pattern (dayplanner top-bar, skillmatrix header, achievements header - self-filling from wh_hive_name, live-proven all 3 render 'Baguio Textile Mills' signed-in at 390). Exclusions by design: marketplace (cross-hive surface), voice-journal (journal_private, personal). Probe lesson: the first null readings were the SIGN-IN WALL (signed-out context), not a missing element - auth state is part of the instrument. Remaining: mid-session switch injection on OPEN pages (stale-figure sweep), per-hive draft/filter scoping audit; chip is load-time - live re-scope on switch rides the injection walk. (2026-08-26: per-hive/per-user draft+filter scoping advanced from the T121 side - both are now owner-stamped, so state no longer crosses between people on one device.) || PER-HIVE DRAFT SCOPING: THE STAMP CARRIES WHO AND WHEN, BUT NOT WHERE (2026-08-27). whAutoSaveDraft stores `{ __owner: _draftOwner(), __savedAt: Date.now() }` and refuses to restore a draft belonging to somebody else (T121's shared-device fix) or to restore one silently once it is stale (T57's age stamp). Both guards are right and neither one covers THIS trajectory's axis: a multi-hive worker is the SAME OWNER in both hives, so the ownership check passes by design and a draft typed against hive A restores into the same form after a switch to hive B. The seeded data already has 2 members in more than one hive, so this is a real population, not a hypothetical. ★WHAT IT COSTS: the machine PICKER would not match after a switch, so the wrong-plant submission is not silent - but the TYPED fields are, and a symptom note describing hive A's bearing failure sitting in a hive B entry is the wrong-plant record this whole trajectory exists to prevent. Not a security hole (both hives belong to that person) but a correctness and confusion one, and precisely the T51 class. ★THE FIX IS THE PATTERN ALREADY THERE, ONE FIELD WIDER: stamp the active hive alongside the owner and refuse the restore on mismatch - the same shape as __owner, so the draft is preserved for the hive it belongs to rather than purged. SEQUENCED AFTER THE BOARD: utils.js is read by a large number of gates and editing it mid-run is exactly what voided this session's earlier board. Remaining: that hive stamp, plus the mid-session switch injection on OPEN pages (stale-figure sweep). ★AND IT IS TWO STORES, NOT ONE - FILTERS CARRY THE SAME GAP AND MAY BITE HARDER. whAutoRememberFilters has its OWN owner stamp (`{ __owner: _fOwner() }`) and its own restore guard (`if (!s || !s.__owner || s.__owner !== _fOwner()) return;`), independent of whAutoSaveDraft's _draftOwner - two separate implementations of the same T121 lesson, and neither knows about the hive. For a multi-hive worker the owner check passes in both, so filters cross the switch exactly as drafts do. ★THE FILTER CASE IS THE NASTIER SYMPTOM: a remembered filter pinned to a hive-A machine or asset, restored after switching to hive B, matches NOTHING - and the page renders an empty list, which this platform has spent a great deal of effort teaching to mean 'there is nothing here' rather than 'your filter is from another plant'. A worker would reasonably conclude the new hive has no records. That is the empty-vs-filtered confusion the E2 family exists to prevent, arriving through the back door of remembered state. So the fix is the same one field wider, applied to BOTH stamps - fix every path that remembers, not just the one I walked. Still sequenced after the board, since utils.js is read by a large number of gates. ★COMPLETENESS PASS BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING - EVERY REMEMBERED STORE ENUMERATED, AND THE FIX IS EXACTLY TWO POINTS. whRememberView is the base, so I walked all of its callers rather than fixing the two I happened to find. THREE in utils.js: whAutoRememberFilters (:2400, owner-stamped, needs the hive), whAutoSaveDraft (:2461, owner-stamped, needs the hive), and whAutoRememberTabs (:2419) which carries NO stamp at all - correctly, because it remembers only which tab is active, and the same tabs exist in every hive, so there is nothing to scope. THREE on pages: alert-hub's 'alert-filter' is a .restore() of state the helper stores (covered by the helper fix); marketplace's 'mkt-section' is again a tab selection; and marketplace-seller's 'draft_svcquote_' LOOKED like a page-local draft bypassing the owner stamp - a real leak if true - but reading it shows the call is a .clear() after a successful send, with `function () { return {}; }` as a dummy capture to satisfy the signature. The actual store is whAutoSaveDraft('svcquote_' + request_id, ...) at :1952, so a provider's typed quote goes through the shared owner-stamped path like every other draft. ★SO TWO EDITS IN utils.js COVER EVERY CONTENT-BEARING REMEMBERED STORE PLATFORM-WIDE, and the hive read is whHiveId() (:2591), the canonical accessor with the registered-alias fallback chain - not a fourth hand-rolled localStorage read. Declared but not yet applied, so this line is a plan, not a claim. || FIXED IN BOTH PLACES - AND MY FIRST 'PROOF' WAS AN ARTIFACT I HAD TO THROW OUT (2026-08-27). utils.js: added _stateHive() (reusing whHiveId(), the canonical accessor with the alias chain, returning '' rather than null so a blocked-storage save and restore compare equal) and stamped __hive into BOTH shared stores - whAutoRememberFilters and whAutoSaveDraft - with a matching guard in each restore. Legacy entries carry no __hive and are not restored, the same one-time cost the owner stamp chose. logbook.html: its draft store is PAGE-LOCAL ('wh_logbook_draft_' + WORKER_NAME, raw localStorage, never touching whAutoSaveDraft), so the shared fix could not reach it; keyed by hive AS WELL, which is better than stamp-and-refuse here - each hive keeps its OWN draft, so nothing is discarded and switching back finds the note where it was left. ★TWO MISTAKES OF MINE, BOTH CAUGHT BEFORE THEY SHIPPED AS CLAIMS. (1) My first utils.js edit put a // comment on a line that CONTINUED with live code, and the comment swallowed the rest of the statement including its closing brace - node --check caught it immediately; the repair moved the swallowed ids.forEach onto its own line and made the comment a BLOCK comment. That is the backtick-in-a-comment class exactly. (2) Worse, my live 'proof' was FALSE: I forced wh_active_hive_id to a hive the signed-in worker does not belong to (Leandro Marquez is a member of Baguio ONLY), saw the field come back empty, and read that as the guard working. It was an impossible state - the page could not resolve a foreign hive at all - and logbook's restoreDraft has NO hive check, so the draft would have restored. Verifying the MECHANISM instead of the symptom is what exposed it: the stored key is now 'wh_logbook_draft_<hiveId>_<worker>', which is the property, checked directly. ★AND MY EARLIER 'COMPLETENESS PASS' WAS INCOMPLETE FOR A NAMEABLE REASON: I enumerated callers of the shared helper and called that every store - but the gap lives precisely in the store that OPTED OUT of the helper. Enumerate the behaviour, not the abstraction's users. Remaining: the mid-session switch injection on OPEN pages (stale-figure sweep). || ★THE SWITCH IS CORRECT WHERE IT HAPPENS AND INVISIBLE EVERYWHERE ELSE - the THIRD instance of one pattern found today (2026-08-28). Switching hives updates localStorage (wh_active_hive_id, wh_hive_id, wh_hive_name) AND the in-page globals in the same breath, with a genuinely careful offline branch - when the membership check cannot reach the DB it fails OPEN and trusts the cached role 'so the worker stays in', rather than locking somebody out of their own hive because the network blinked. On the switching page, nothing is stale. ★BUT 15 FILES CACHE wh_active_hive_id AND ONLY 3 LISTEN FOR `storage` (companion-launcher, session-timeout, and nav-hub - the last of which only started listening today, for the community badge). There is no reload on switch, so a contractor with the logbook open in one tab and the hive board in another switches to hive B and the logbook keeps showing hive A's entries, silently, under a chrome that may or may not have updated. For a MULTI-HIVE worker - the entire persona of this trajectory - that is not a stale badge, it is looking at the wrong plant's data believing it is the right one. ★AND IT IS A CLASS, NOT AN INCIDENT: today produced three instances of the same shape - the community badge (T144), the hive NAME after a rename (T140), and now the ACTIVE HIVE. All three are identity written to localStorage by one tab and read at boot by others; localStorage already broadcasts every one of those writes to every other tab, and almost nothing listens. One shared listener in the chrome that every page loads would close all three at once, which is the argument for treating this as a platform fix rather than three page fixes. pct 78 -> 88. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate hive-seating-is-by-identity re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100. || REVERTED 2026-09-04: named gate FAILED on the 1034/60 board (false 100%; post_board_promote over-locked). pct -> 90.

fixes: index.html (resolveActiveHiveContext seats by auth_uid, not by display name)

trajectories.note: ★THE TENANT SEAT WAS CHOSEN BY NAME (2026-08-26). resolveActiveHiveContext() picked which hive a session lands in via .eq('worker_name', displayName) against v_worker_truth, whose worker_name IS worker_profiles.display_name - so it leaned on profiles_read_own (auth_uid = auth.uid()) to mean 'mine'. No live defect (measured: 1 visible profile row; both filters return the same 2 memberships for a real multi-hive account), but the safety was the POLICY's, not the query's, and any widening of profile reads would have seated a person in a namesake's hive. Now keyed on auth_uid, passed explicitly from both call sites, with solo mode as the answer when identity is unknown. Gate hive-seating-is-by-identity asserts the page half AND that the RLS policy is still self-scoped. Third face of the same day's defect family with T185's namesake join and T1's records-linked notice: a name is not an identity. ★THE XP LEDGER IS KEYED BY NAME, AND A NAME IS NOT A PERSON (2026-08-26) - the fourth face of the same defect family found this session. achievement_xp_log has no auth_uid and no hive_id, and its RLS reads by worker_name; worker_name is unique per HIVE, so two different people in two hives sharing a name would merge totals, compute each other's LEVELS, and be able to read each other's ledger rows (source_action, source_id) from a hive they never joined. Measured: 982 rows / 20 names / ZERO names held by two people - not happening, which is exactly why it was worth gating now: the backfill onto auth_uid is only unambiguous while that stays true. Gate xp-belongs-to-one-person fails the moment a cross-hive namesake appears and retires itself once auth_uid exists. THE FIX IS IAN'S CALL, scoped not smuggled: add auth_uid, backfill, and move the four readers (achievements x2, logbook, pm-scheduler) plus the RLS predicate onto it - a schema change to a ledger with reversal semantics.

trajectories.title: The engineer role's day (the third persona)
trajectories.basis: model truth established: 'engineer' is a NAV LENS (nav-hub roles filter), not a membership role (hive_members has worker/supervisor only). The lens is coherent: Eng.Design + Analytics + Asset Hub + Project Manager/Report + PH Intelligence = the design-and-reliability lane. First-class engineer ROLE (authz, landing emphasis) = a schema+RLS product decision FLAGGED for Ian, not built. ★BASIS CORRECTED 2026-08-27: this line used to read 'Eng.Design (engineer-only)'. It is not, and has not been since T173 tagged it ['engineer','supervisor'] with its reason in the source - 'no separate engineer auth exists (the engineer persona IS supervisors in practice, T52); a supervisor needing a calc could not find Eng. Design here'. My own record had gone stale against a later decision, which is why the lens-content question had to be re-measured rather than recalled. ★CLOSED 2026-08-27: lens-content gated (engineer-lens-covers-its-lane) and the lane walked LIVE (journey ENG1, R/J/T/X green across all four core pages). TWO PRODUCT QUESTIONS REMAIN FLAGGED FOR IAN, neither blocking: (1) a first-class engineer ROLE (authz + landing emphasis) is a schema+RLS decision, not built; (2) NEW - the Supervisor lens is a no-op, identical to All, so the chip either retires or the field tools lose their supervisor tag. pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★PREMISE CORRECTED, THEN THE REAL DEFECTS FOUND. The spec calls the engineer 'the third persona'; there is no third role (hive_members.role is CHECK-constrained to worker | supervisor), so the probes as written - 'what does an engineer SEE that others do not', 'are they denied surfaces by role' - had no subject. The trajectory's real question is whether the two ENGINEER LENSES cohere, and they did not: the hub lens and the asset-hub toggle shared a word and no state, and the toggle did not even reflect its own stored value until an asset was opened. Both fixed and gated. REMAINS: whether the nav-hub 'engineer' tool filter actually selects the right tools for that work, which is a content question about the TOOLS registry rather than a state question. ★THE OPEN CONTENT QUESTION, ANSWERED AND GATED (2026-08-27). The note above left one thing open: 'whether the nav-hub engineer tool filter actually selects the right tools - a content question about the TOOLS registry rather than a state question.' Measured: 24 tools, 13 visible in the Engineer lens, and every member of the design-and-reliability lane present. ★THE FINDING IS THE SHAPE OF THE LENS, not a missing tool: EVERY engineer-tagged tool is also supervisor-tagged, so the Engineer lens is a strict SUBSET of the supervisor lens - a FOCUS filter that removes field tools, never a distinct capability set. That is coherent with the corrected premise (a lens, not a role) and is exactly why it needs holding: a future tool tagged roles:['engineer'] alone would sit in NO role's default spine, since no engineer ROLE exists to grant it - reachable only by someone who had already switched the lens by hand, and invisible to the supervisors who ARE the engineers here. That is the retired-page class (a live control behind a door most people never open), and nothing was holding it. New gate engineer-lens-covers-its-lane asserts both halves: no engineer-only orphan, and every lane member engineer-visible. 5 selftest cases, the two RED ones being an engineer-only tool and a lane member leaving the lens. ★AND WHAT I DID NOT DO: 'Reports' is engineer-visible while the lane does not name it, and I left it. The registry records that tagging with a reason, and a validator overturning a judgement call on my preference would be bending the code to the gate. The lane is gated as a FLOOR, not a ceiling. Sibling gate engineer-lens-is-one-lens is untouched - it holds STATE coherence between the two switches; this one holds lens CONTENT, so no redundancy. REMAINS for the wave close: the engineer-lens journeys on the core pages. ★THE LANE JOURNEY IS LIVE, AND THE LENS MECHANISM WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS ASSERTED (2026-08-27). A probe first, because a journey written against guessed selectors measures its own assumptions: the hub renders its tiles EAGERLY (no FAB press needed - my first draft would have clicked a button it did not need), and the four modes give 11 / 13 / 20 / 20 tiles for engineer / field / supervisor / all. ENG1 then walks the lane signed in as the supervisor who IS the engineer here: lens declared ONCE on index, then engineering-design -> analytics -> asset-hub -> project-manager, asserting on EVERY page that the mode is still engineer, the lane tool is present and all three field-only tools are absent. R/J/T/X all green, LIVE. ★THE X ASSERTION IS THE POINT: logbook is hidden from this lens and must still open by direct URL, because a lens is not authorization - no role denies it. A display filter that quietly became a permission would be the retired-page class, a live control unreachable because a preference hid its only door. The journey restores the default mode at the end so later journeys are not walked through an engineer lens. ★A NEW FINDING, FLAGGED NOT FIXED: the Supervisor lens and the All lens render IDENTICAL tile sets - 20 each, set difference empty both ways, measured. So two of the four mode chips are indistinguishable for a supervisor: pressing Supervisor after All changes nothing, which is the click-that-changes-nothing class. The cause is taxonomy drift - every non-hidden tool is either universal or supervisor-tagged, so supervisor-narrowing is vacuous. MY VERDICT, for Ian to take or leave: either retire the Supervisor chip (All already IS it) or un-tag the field-only tools from supervisor so the chip means something. I did not pick one, because which tools are 'not a supervisor's' is a product judgement, and it cannot be gated green today in either direction - the invariant would fail on the current registry. Recorded as a measured finding, not a silent fix. ★AND ONE INSTRUMENT SELF-CATCH: the gate I wrote an hour earlier said 'every lane member is engineer-VISIBLE' while computing role TAGGING. They differ - isVisibleInMode drops every hidden:true tool from EVERY mode, and two of this lane's six are hidden Phase-B pages reached from a parent button - so the label claimed something the code never measured. Caught by reading isVisibleInMode while writing the journey, before it could go false-green; wording, docstring, board label and two new selftest cases all now say TAGGED. The oracle-does-not-match-the-claim class, in my own fresh work.

trajectories.title: Plant manager / read-mostly executive
trajectories.basis: the read-mostly lane assembled from walked surfaces: analytics (basis-rich, T22/T47 hand-check PASSED), alert-hub triage (T19), report-sender schedule path (T23), maturity-locked intel pages honest (T65/66) - a clean daily read exists with zero forced-write walls on the read path (reads are member-open; the only walls are committing actions). Fat-finger safety: all destructive verbs confirm-gated (T50 registry, 52 entries). Remaining: an exec-shaped landing emphasis question (design note) + read-mostly persona lane in journeys (wave close). || THE READ-MOSTLY LANE WALKED, AND THE MEASURABLE HALF IS CLEAN (2026-08-27). The exec question splits in two: a design call about landing emphasis (Ian's), and a checkable one that needs no decision - does a person who only READS ever get forced into a write? Walked six exec-shaped surfaces signed in (index, analytics, alert-hub, analytics-report, asset-hub, pm-scheduler) and recorded what a pure reader meets on arrival, before touching anything: ZERO blocking modals, zero body-scroll locks, zero sign-in/pick-a-hive walls, zero stolen focus (nothing autofocuses an input at a reader), zero page errors. analytics and alert-hub hand over 243 and 109 figures respectively without a single interaction. ★TWO SURFACES LOOKED THIN AND BOTH TURNED OUT HONEST when I read the actual words instead of the character count: analytics-report shows 374 chars and NO figures, which is the correct state - it says 'Click Generate Report to compile the latest analytics into a print-ready document' with the period and audience controls already on screen, so the emptiness is an instruction, not a dead end. And asset-hub was not thin at all: a slightly longer wait shows 'Asset fleet mostly healthy, a couple of things to do - 4 pending - TOTAL ASSETS 25', which is precisely the verdict-at-a-glance this persona wants; my 562-char reading had caught it mid-render, so the low count was my timing, not the page's content. A figure count is a proxy; the words are the property. Remaining: the exec landing-emphasis design note (Ian's) and the read-mostly persona lane in journeys at wave close. || THE READ-MOSTLY LANE IS NOW LOCKED, AND THE HALF THAT NEEDED NO DECISION IS THE HALF THAT GOT A GATE (2026-08-28). The walk had measured the property clean and left it as prose, which protects nothing: the exec lane has no journey of its own because every existing journey asserts an ACTION succeeds, and an action-shaped oracle cannot see this persona's defect - being stopped before reading anything. tools/prove_read_only_lane.mjs walks the six exec-shaped surfaces signed in and requires no blocking modal, no scroll lock, no sign-in/pick-a-hive wall, no focus stolen into a text input, no page error. ★THE SIXTH CLAUSE CARRIES THE GATE: the other five are ABSENCES and a BLANK PAGE satisfies every one, so an all-absence oracle would grade a dead page as a perfect reading experience. It also requires the reader got WORDS - visible text, not figures, since this trajectory's own walk twice misread a healthy surface as thin (once mid-render, once by counting figures on analytics-report, whose correct state is an instruction with none). 6/6 green at 1280; teeth 5/5, each clause injected on a real page and each checked NON-VACUOUS against a clean baseline, because a gate over already-correct behaviour has never been seen to go red. Remaining: only the exec landing-emphasis design note, which is Ian's. pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★PREMISE CORRECTED, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE FINDING. The spec assumes a read-mostly executive persona. There is no read-only access ANYWHERE: hive_members.role is CHECK-constrained to worker | supervisor, so a plant manager who only wants to LOOK must be made a supervisor - which is also the role that approves assets and parts, moderates reported posts, kicks members, and reaches every destructive control this session has been fitting confirms to. The probe 'is there anything they can DESTROY by accident' has an answer, and it is: everything a supervisor can. The confirms added under T50/T67 reduce the blast radius but do not change who holds the trigger. A worker role is not the alternative either - it is scoped for doing the work, not reading across it (no analytics-first landing, no approval visibility). ★IAN DECISION, recorded not taken: whether to add a read-only role. It is a schema change (the CHECK constraint, the RLS predicates that branch on role, and every UI that tests for 'supervisor'), so it is a real piece of work rather than a toggle - and until then, the honest statement is that WorkHive has no way to let someone watch without also letting them act.

trajectories.title: New graduate onboarding (the learning lane)
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25, worker 390, three-surface ladder walk): the grad growth ladder (quiz -> badge -> resume) EXISTS end-to-end - skillmatrix offers '5 quizzes available right now' with an Achievements link, achievements' locked badges show their HOW, and the Resume Builder's 'Auto-fill from my WorkHive data' consumes skills+badges+history - but the ladder was only discoverable TOP-DOWN from the resume; no lower rung pointed up. FIXED + VERIFIED: (1) skillmatrix now states the path under its verdict ('pass a quiz -> earn the skill badge -> it lands on your Resume automatically', linked); (2) achievements now carries the resume line ('Every badge you earn here lands on your Resume automatically - employers see certified skills, not claims'). Both proven rendering live. Remaining: a grad-facing 'start here' entry (learn-cluster <-> skillmatrix wayfinding - content decision), the learn->signup->skillmatrix continuity walk as a fresh grad account, mentorship/community entry points (wave close). || ★ONE DOOR, THEN FIFTY-TWO UNSORTED ROOMS (2026-08-28). This trajectory asks whether a fresh graduate finds a coherent 'start here'. Measured: the learn hub carries exactly one sequencing affordance - 'Start here if you are new', pointing at the overview of what the platform does and how one logbook entry makes the hive smarter. That is a real and well-written first step. ★BEYOND IT THERE IS NO PATH: 53 guides, and ZERO of them carry any difficulty or level marker - no data-level, no data-difficulty, no educationalLevel, no proficiencyLevel, nothing. No prerequisite chain, no beginner/intermediate/advanced grouping on the hub. A grad who takes the one recommended step is then facing 52 titles with no signal about which is next, which assumes knowledge they came here to acquire. The ladder this trajectory describes - lesson to exam to badge to resume - exists as MACHINERY (skillmatrix exams, achievements, the resume builder all work) but is not presented anywhere as a sequence a person can see and follow. ★THIS CONVERGES WITH T152's already-open item, reading-order guidance for the learn cluster, which is on Ian's list. Recording the measurement so that decision has a number under it: the cost of adding order is 53 guides' worth of metadata, and the cost of not adding it is that the platform's stated audience gets one step and a wall. pct 60 -> 70. || ★THE LADDER IS WIRED END TO END; IT IS JUST NEVER SHOWN AS A LADDER (2026-08-28). Measured the graduate's path rung by rung and every joint holds: 37 of the learn articles link into skillmatrix, skillmatrix links onward to resume, and resume genuinely CONSUMES what was earned - 14 references to worker skills, badges and certifications, so a badge won in the matrix actually becomes a line on the CV rather than a number in a game. That last link is the one that makes the promise real for this persona: the platform's pitch to a fresh graduate is employability, and employability means the credential leaves the platform with them. It does. ★WHAT IS MISSING IS THE PRESENTATION, not the plumbing. Nothing shows the sequence AS a progression. The only onboarding stepper on the platform (onboarding.js, hive.html) is role-specific and OPERATIONAL - signed in, joined a hive, logged an entry, uploaded a photo, completed a PM - which is the right ladder for a worker starting a job and the wrong one for a graduate building a career. A grad arriving with 'what do I do first, and where does it lead' meets 37 separate doors into skillmatrix and no map saying learn -> certify -> resume -> hired. The rungs exist; the ladder is not drawn. ★That framing matters for whoever builds it: this is not a wiring job, it is a single wayfinding surface over connections that already work - the cheapest kind of improvement to make and the easiest to mistake for a big one. pct 70 -> 82. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - the new-graduate learning lane is coherent: learn-graph (articles reachable) + skill-library-wiring (the quiz->badge->resume skillmatrix path is wired) + scroll-gate-at-open. Gates [learn-graph, skill-library-wiring, scroll-gate-at-open] registered + PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Supplier/contractor persona enters via marketplace
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, davidvelasco 390, worker-seller lane): marketplace-seller dashboard graded GOOD - tier chip (Bronze) + ID Verified up top, stats first (3 Listings / 0 Sales / 0 New Inquiries), and the credit-hold economy explained inline in plain language ('10% of its price is HELD... comes back in full if it does not sell, goes to your buyer if it does; taking a listing down releases its hold immediately') - the T34 cost-transparency bar carried to the dashboard. Nav hub shows the full worker toolset, CORRECT for david (he IS a hive worker who also sells). OPEN for the true story: the PURE seller (no hive) - needs a signup-without-hive fixture to grade nav drowning (no 'Seller' lane exists in the hub's role filters), seller-only first-run, and the notification lane (inquiries reaching a hive-less account). Remaining: pure-seller fixture walk, earnings/fee-basis section at n>0 sales (aged-seller fixture), vendor community participation scope (wave close). || THE HIVE-LESS SELLER STATE IS REACHABLE - AND MY FIRST READING SAID THE OPPOSITE, TWICE OVER (2026-08-27). Question: can an account with marketplace access and no hive exist, or does the plant model swallow the supplier persona? Probe: sign in, delete wh_active_hive_id + wh_hive_name, reload marketplace. FIRST reading said the user was bounced to index.html showing 'Free Industrial Tools for Every Filipino Worker' - the signed-OUT marketing pitch served to a signed-in person, with no explanation. Both halves of that were my instrument. (1) I captured location.pathname and DISCARDED location.search, which is exactly where the explanation lives: the platform's one bounce helper is whSignInWall(), which sends index.html?signin=1&return=marketplace.html, so I deleted the query string and then reported that no explanation was given. (2) Worse, the bounce itself was a SINGLE SAMPLE. Re-run three times with the URL captured whole: marketplace.html every time, 18 listings rendered, no wall, no redirect. The first run had raced its own teardown - I removed the identity keys mid-initialisation and read the result as product behaviour. ★SO THE FINDING INVERTS: browsing the marketplace does NOT require a hive, and the pure-seller state is reachable today. One reading is an anecdote; the defect I nearly filed was the probe. WHAT REMAINS REAL: nav-hub carries a single universal 'Marketplace' entry under Connect and no seller lane, so a supplier who never joins a plant still gets the full field-tools nav (logbook, PM scheduler, inventory) they can never use - the nav-scope question stands, unaffected by the false bounce. Remaining: the seller-lane nav scope, the pure-seller fixture walk, earnings/fee-basis at n>0 sales (aged-seller fixture), and vendor community participation. || THE SUPPLIER PERSONA IS POSSIBLE IN THE DATA AND UNPAVED IN THE PRODUCT - MEASURED ON ALL FOUR LAYERS (2026-08-27). POPULATION: 17 auth users, 15 with a hive membership, and the 2 without are both PROBE accounts left by earlier walks (wh-t175-probe@, consumer.walk@) - so there is not one genuine pure-supplier account to walk, which is itself the answer to 'what does a seller-only account see'. SCHEMA: it would allow one. marketplace_listings.hive_id is NULLABLE, marketplace_sellers.hive_id is nullable, and ZERO RLS policies on marketplace_listings reference hive_members - listing visibility is not gated on belonging to a plant at all. All 27 listings carry a hive only because every seller happens to be a hive member. NAV: measured live as a real seller (Bryan Garcia) at 390 - the hub offers 17 items, of which Logbook, Inventory, PM Scheduler, Day Planner, Shift Brain and Hive Board are plant operations a supplier can never use; Marketplace is one entry among them, and no role-filter chips rendered. ONBOARDING: signup routes everyone through hive.html to create or join a hive, so a parts supplier must attach themselves to a plant to sell to plants. ★SO THE HONEST ANSWER IS NOT 'BROKEN' OR 'FINE' BUT 'UNPAVED': the data model would hold a hive-less supplier today without a migration, and nothing in the product offers, scopes or names that path. Whether the supplier is a first-class persona or deliberately out of scope for launch is a product call - and it is worth stating rather than leaving implied, because the marketplace's supply side depends on the answer. Remaining: that scoping call, then (if in scope) the seller-lane nav and a hive-less fixture; earnings/fee-basis at n>0 sales still needs an aged-seller fixture. || ★THE SELLER'S OWN DASHBOARD WAS NOT IN THE SPINE AT ALL — AND NOT FINDABLE BY SEARCH EITHER (2026-08-28). Walking the nav as this persona: nav-hub's TOOLS registry carried 24 entries and marketplace-seller.html was NOT one of them. Not `hidden: true` — ABSENT. That distinction is what made it worse than the T173 cases: `hidden` entries are still published on window.WHNavTools and merely filtered from the grid, whereas an absent page is unknown to the registry entirely. And because search-overlay.js:327 reads that same registry (`.filter(t => !t.hidden && ...)`), the page was unreachable from the global search too — no query for 'seller', 'listings' or 'my listings' returned anything, anywhere on the platform. The ONLY route was remembering to open Marketplace and spotting a 'My Listings' pill in its header at marketplace.html:762. For the supplier persona this trajectory is about, that page IS their platform, which is precisely the 'a daily tool is not an internal page' class T173 unhid Voice Journal and Shift Brain for. FIX: registered as 'My Listings' in the Connect section, universal like Marketplace itself because anyone may sell (T104's premise), reusing the pill's own label and ic-list icon so the two affordances read as one destination. ★TWO ORDERING TRAPS, BOTH AVOIDED BY READING getCurrentTool() RATHER THAN ASSUMING: it returns the FIRST match by `path.includes(m)`, so the entry MUST precede Marketplace or 'marketplace' would claim the page first — the same rule the registry already documents for Analytics Report before Analytics. And the match term carries '.html' deliberately, because bare 'marketplace-seller' is also a substring of marketplace-seller-profile.html — the PUBLIC profile a BUYER reads, a different page with a different job — which would have been mis-claimed. Verified by simulating the resolver over all four marketplace paths: seller->My Listings, and marketplace / seller-profile / admin all still resolve to Marketplace unchanged. nav-registry (no duplicate hrefs, match[] unique) and page-roster (nav_hub 24->25) both green. ★NOTED, NOT BUILT: `match` serves double duty — path detection AND search keywords — so 'sales' and 'earnings' still find nothing, and adding them would pollute path matching. A separate `keywords` field would separate the two concerns honestly; recorded here rather than built, since it touches search-overlay too. pct 25 -> 55. STILL OPEN and the larger half of this trajectory: there is no 'seller' MODE in the vocabulary (field | supervisor | engineer), so a pure supplier still sees Logbook, Inventory, PM Scheduler and the rest of the plant they cannot use — the 'drowning in plant tools' question is surfaced and unanswered. Seller onboarding, their notification lane, and vendor community scope are un-probed. || ★AND IT WAS PROVEN LIVE, because the fix was made statically and static cannot tell you a person can get there (2026-08-28). New prover, registered: it signs in, opens the real hub, and reads the LINKS a person could click — the seller dashboard now has a visible entry labelled 'My Listings' — then drives the global search with Ctrl+K (the documented shortcut, so the probe takes the path a person takes) and confirms 'seller' reaches marketplace-seller.html and 'audit log' reaches the audit trail. All five checks green. ★TEETH: with the registry entry removed AND the `!t.hidden` search filter restored, three of the five go red — '17 links, none to marketplace-seller.html' and 'no results' twice — so the prover fails for the right reason and reports the count that explains it. Asserting reachability rather than markup matters here: a check that the registry array contains a string would re-test what the static fix already guaranteed, and would pass just as happily if the grid never rendered. || ★AND THE FULL BOARD CAUGHT WHAT THE TARGETED GATES DID NOT: registering this entry as VISIBLE broke a budget I had not thought to check. validate_home_stack_coverage caps how many primary-nav tools each role sees, and both affected roles were deliberately AT their cap - so one universal entry pushed field to 14/13 and supervisor to 21/20 simultaneously. nav-registry and page-roster both stayed green throughout, because they check different properties; only the 53-minute full board found it. A change can satisfy every gate you thought to run and still break one you did not. ★THE FIX IS `hidden: true`, AND IT IS ONLY THE RIGHT ANSWER BECAUSE OF THE OTHER CHANGE THIS SESSION MADE. `hidden` used to mean UNFINDABLE - grid AND search - which is precisely the orphaning this trajectory set out to end, and would have been a retreat. Since T78 made search index hidden entries, `hidden` now means exactly what it should: not promoted, still reachable by name. The page costs nobody a nav slot, answers to 'seller' / 'listings' / 'my listings', keeps its current-page resolution, and marketplace's own pill remains the parent deep-link the home-stack gate asks for. The two fixes only work as a pair. ★AND THE LIVE PROVER WAS CORRECTED WITH IT: it asserted the entry is VISIBLE in the grid, which after this became an assertion that the cognitive-load cap is broken. It now asserts the opposite - that the dashboard takes no primary-nav slot - plus the two search reachability checks, and its PASS line no longer claims 'the grid shows it', because it deliberately does not. || ★REACHABLE, PROVEN LIVE - BUT THE SELLER HAS NO NAVIGATION IDENTITY (2026-08-28). The reachability half is settled with a live browser walk: prove_seller_dashboard_is_reachable passes all four assertions - the hub panel opens, the seller dashboard is deliberately NOT consuming a primary-nav slot (hidden by design, protecting the home-stack budget), searching 'seller' reaches it, and searching 'audit log' reaches that hidden page too, confirming the search lane genuinely serves the hidden set rather than the dashboard being a special case. Curated out of the nav and findable by name is the right answer for a page most users never need. ★THE PERSONA GAP IS THE REAL FINDING. nav-hub's role vocabulary is field, supervisor and engineer - every single role-tagged TOOLS entry draws from those three, and NOT ONE carries a seller or vendor role. So a supplier or contractor who joins WorkHive purely to sell - this trajectory's entire persona, whose world is the marketplace plus community - is bucketed into a plant-worker lane and shown a hub full of tools they will never open: logbook, PM scheduler, asset hub, shift brain. They do not drown because the nav is broken; they drown because the nav has no concept of them. ★THAT IS A PRODUCT DECISION, not a defect to patch: adding a fourth mode changes the mode switcher for everyone and only makes sense if WorkHive intends seller-only accounts as a first-class persona rather than as plant workers who happen to sell. The cheap intermediate - defaulting a seller-only account to a marketplace-first view without minting a whole mode - is available and is what the evidence here would support. Recorded for Ian with the measurement behind it: 19 role-tagged nav entries, zero of them reachable by a seller's identity. pct 68 -> 80. pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: MEASURED: there is no seller lane. nav-hub's MODES are exactly all | field | supervisor | engineer, and Marketplace is a single entry in the Connect section marked universal - so a supplier who only ever sells parts navigates a hub built for plant maintenance, choosing between three lenses that describe work they do not do, with the one surface they came for sitting among roughly 33 tools. The probe 'does a seller-only account get a sane nav, or drown in plant tools they cannot use' has a plain answer: the latter. ★THIS COMPLETES A PATTERN ACROSS WAVE G, and the pattern is more useful than any one finding. hive_members.role is CHECK-constrained to worker | supervisor, so T52's engineer is a UI lens rather than a role, T53's read-mostly executive must be given full supervisor powers to look at anything, and T55's supplier has no representation at all. The identity model is PLANT-WORKER-SHAPED, and every marketplace or observer persona rides on top of it. That is a coherent product position, not a bug - the marketplace grew out of a maintenance tool - but it is not what the roadmap's Wave G assumed, and the three trajectories cannot be walked as written until it is settled. ★IAN DECISION, recorded not taken: whether these personas get first-class representation (a role, a nav mode) or are explicitly out of scope. Either answer makes the wave walkable; the current silence does not.

trajectories.title: Co-supervisor dynamics (two supervisors, one hive)
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25, Lucena's two real supervisors pabloaguilar+christinedizon, two contexts 1280): THE DOUBLE-APPROVE RACE PROVEN under true concurrency - a seeded pending part (wh-t56-probe-1, cleaned after), both supervisors' Approve dispatched in parallel: DB shows exactly ONE approval (approved_by Christine, one timestamp - the eq(status,'pending') optimistic lock held), the winner saw 'approved and published to hive', and the loser's honest toast 'That item was already handled by another supervisor' FIRED in practice (collected via the MutationObserver rail). DEMOTE ANSWERED: no demote UI exists (promotion only via leave-handoff) - mutual demotion is impossible on the glass. TWO GAPS FIXED + VERIFIED: (1) canKick has no !isSup, so a supervisor can remove a FELLOW SUPERVISOR - the confirm now names it ('They are a SUPERVISOR - you would take sole charge...'); (2) 'Leave Without Transferring' could orphan a hive on one passing sentence - when NO other active supervisor remains, an explicit EN/FIL confirm now names the consequence ('no one can approve submissions... cannot be fixed from inside') - proven with leandro (Baguio's sole supervisor), Go back cancels, membership intact. Both fixes read window._whMembersSnapshot (membersData was loader-local - the first cut silently read an empty fallback and only LOOKED right, caught by the verify walk). Remaining: reject-race variant, moderation-action peer visibility, attribution sweep, the concurrent same-role choreography formalized for T145 (wave close). || ★THE LAST-SUPERVISOR INVARIANT IS GUARDED - BY ORDERING, NOT BY A CONSTRAINT (2026-08-28). This trajectory asks whether one supervisor can demote the other and leave a hive unmanageable. Two findings. FIRST, THERE IS NO DEMOTE PATH AT ALL: the only client write that sets a role to 'worker' does so on JOIN, never on an existing member, so 'one demotes the other' cannot arise through the product. SECOND, THE PATH THAT COULD ACTUALLY STRAND A HIVE - a supervisor LEAVING - is guarded, and guarded in the right ORDER: btn-sup-transfer-leave promotes the chosen successor FIRST, checks that write, and only then leaves, with the invariant stated in its own comment - 'If the promotion failed, do NOT leave - a hive with no supervisor can't be managed.' It also audits the handoff BEFORE performLeave deletes the departing member's own row, since afterwards there would be nobody to attribute it to. That is the correct sequence, not an accident. ★WHAT IS MISSING IS ENFORCEMENT BENEATH IT: nothing at the DATABASE level requires a hive to keep at least one active supervisor. hive_members carries only an achievement trigger and a text-cap trigger, and hive_has_other_members answers a different question (does anyone else exist), not how many supervisors remain. So the invariant rests on one client path executing in the right order - and this platform's own doctrine says elsewhere that a client guard is spoofable and the server is the real backstop. MEASURED: it holds today, every hive has at least one active supervisor (Baguio 1 of 3 members, Manila 1 of 8, Lucena 2 of 6). Recorded rather than migrated because a CHECK or trigger enforcing 'at least one supervisor per hive' is a schema decision with real consequences at the edges - the last member leaving a hive entirely, and hive deletion - that belong to Ian. pct 60 -> 78. || ★THE HIVE CANNOT BE ORPHANED BY DEMOTION, BECAUSE DEMOTION DOES NOT EXIST (2026-08-28). This trajectory worries that one supervisor could demote the other and leave a hive with nobody able to approve or manage. There is exactly ONE role-change write in hive.html - update({ role: 'supervisor' }) - a promotion. No demote-to-worker path exists in the UI at all, so the last-supervisor invariant cannot be broken this way; combined with T191's finding that the LEAVE path explicitly checks for another active supervisor and raises a bilingual consequence-naming confirm when there is none, both routes to an orphaned hive are covered - one by a guard, one by absence. ★AND THE MID-SESSION ROLE-CHANGE HAZARD WAS ALREADY FOUND AND FIXED, which is the subtler half of this trajectory. When a role synced down to 'worker', the html.is-supervisor marker stayed true - and because that class sets #my-work-card{display:none} and hides #pm-overdue-alert and #stock-alert (correct FOR a supervisor, who has their own summary), a just-demoted worker lost their own work card and both of their alerts 'while the board otherwise looked normal'. Nothing errored; the person simply had no work and no warnings. The source records it verified live - role 'worker', marker still true, all three elements computing display:none - and the fix uses toggle() rather than remove() so promotion works too. A stale privilege MARKER is more dangerous than a stale privilege, because the page keeps rendering confidently. pct 78 -> 88. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - co-supervisor dynamics are safe: no demote-to-worker path exists (hive cannot be orphaned), removal is explained to the worker, and a kicked rejoin is legible. Gates [supervisor-hygiene, removal-tells-the-worker, kicked-rejoin-is-explained] registered + PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.
