trajectories.basis: source-verified + prior-arc receipts: self-leave EXISTS (hive menu 'Leave Hive'); the confirm states the DATA-OWNERSHIP answer in as many words ('Your past logbook entries stay in the hive's records'); supervisor-leave offers TRANSFER-then-leave (promote before delete, audited in order - RLS makes the ordering load-bearing) with a deliberate 'leave anyway' escape (the supervisor-less-hive invariant is T56's question); voluntary leaver can rejoin by code (the join RPC bans only kicked). Remaining: the two-hive-view walk (hive A's view of the departed member's records) + resume-sees-pre-leave-history probe (wave close). || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): the resume-sees-pre-leave-history probe RUN, and it found a real claim-vs-behaviour gap in the platform's headline pitch to OFW engineers. Measured AS THE WORKER under RLS in a rolled-back transaction: logbook entries 571 while active -> 0 as 'kicked' -> 0 as 'deactivated'; skill badges 12 -> 12 -> 12. So 'portable' is half true and the halves are clean - badges and certifications are held against the WORKER and travel; logbook entries are hive-scoped by logbook_read (ACTIVE membership required) and go dark the moment membership ends. The resume builder reads v_logbook_truth by worker_name, so a departed worker's portfolio loses its work history entirely. ★THE SCOPING IS CORRECT TENANCY, NOT A BUG - a plant's records are the plant's, and reading them after leaving is the cross-tenant leak gated everywhere else - so RLS was NOT touched. ★AND THE APP WAS ALREADY HONEST: hive.html's leave confirm says 'Your past logbook entries stay in the hive's records', exactly right at the moment it matters. Whether you're applying for a job in Saudi Arabia...' and a personal export available 'at any time'. Both now carry the condition (export while still a member; entries stay with the plant; badges do travel), corrected in the JSON-LD and the visible FAQ together so structured-data-parity stays green. The gamification page's badge claim was left alone because measurement says it is TRUE - checking the sibling claims before editing is what kept that one from being 'fixed' into a lie. Locked as 'portable-record'. REMAINING and genuinely Ian's: whether to BUILD real portability (a personal copy at write time, or an export prompt at leave) so the original promise could be restored - that is a product decision, not a copy fix. || THE OTHER HALF OF 'ENTRIES STAY WITH THE PLANT', MEASURED FROM THE HIVE'S SIDE (2026-08-28, from T190's walk). This trajectory corrected the marketing to say entries stay in the hive's records; the complementary fact - that they genuinely DO stay, rather than quietly disappearing when their author leaves - was never measured. It holds, and by a clean mechanism: logbook_read filters on the READER's membership only (hive_id IN ... WHERE auth_uid = auth.uid() AND status = 'active'), with no join anywhere on the AUTHOR's membership, and worker_name is a plain column on each row rather than a roster lookup. Verified in a rolled-back transaction with the role set: with Bryan Garcia removed from Baguio, a still-active member reads all 314 of his entries, still attributed to him by name - his full total, not a subset. So both halves of the corrected copy are now true AND checked: the worker cannot take the entries, and the plant does not lose them. || ★BOTH SIDES OF THE DATA-OWNERSHIP CLAIM ARE NOW MEASURED, AND THE CORRECTED COPY IS TRUE (2026-08-28). This trajectory rewrote the marketing to say entries stay in the hive's records while badges travel, and locked it behind 'portable-record' - but the claim itself had never been exercised. Two rolled-back transactions with the ROLE actually set settle it. FROM THE HIVE'S SIDE: with Bryan Garcia removed, a still-active member reads all 314 of his logbook entries, still attributed to him by name - the plant loses nothing, because logbook_read filters on the READER's membership and never joins the author's. FROM THE LEAVER'S SIDE, the half that decides whether the copy is honest: reading as Bryan himself after removal returns 0 logbook entries and 7 SKILL BADGES. It is - 7 badges survive the leave. Checking the sibling claims before editing is what kept a correct one from being 'fixed' into a lie. pct 60 -> 85. Remaining is unchanged and genuinely Ian's: whether to BUILD real portability (a personal copy at write time, or an export prompt at leave) so the original promise could be restored. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate removal-tells-the-worker re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). trajectories.note: ★THE KICKED SIDE IS HANDLED WELL AND WAS UNGATED (2026-08-27). This trajectory's sharpest probe - what the REMOVED worker sees on their next app-open - is answered: a notice naming the hive and the supervisor, stating that their personal records are still theirs, and offering a next step (join another hive or create one). trajectories.title: The account-security-conscious user
trajectories.basis: findability audit: password change exists ONLY via the recovery-link loop (forgot -> email -> PASSWORD_RECOVERY -> whPrompt with 8-char floor) + supervisor-reset for workers; there is NO in-app change-password for a signed-in user, no active-sessions view, no sign-out-everywhere, no 2FA statement. Per spec this is the SCOPED PRODUCT DECISION for Ian: an account-security surface (change password + sessions + revoke + honest 2FA absence note). Reset-loop injection tests remain (wave close). || ★THE ACCOUNT-SECURITY BASICS ARE LARGELY ABSENT, AND ONE OF THEM IS A ONE-ARGUMENT FIX (2026-08-28). Walked what a security-conscious user could actually do. THERE IS NO ACCOUNT OR SETTINGS SURFACE AT ALL - marketplace-seller-profile is a seller's public page, not account controls. Consequences, each checked rather than assumed: (1) PASSWORD CHANGE: the only updateUser({password}) on the platform sits inside index.html's RECOVERY flow, behind a reset link. So a signed-in worker who wants to change their password must SIGN OUT and email themselves a reset - the one action security advice tells people to do routinely is the one the product makes hardest. (2) SIGN-OUT-EVERYWHERE: every signOut() call on the platform - hive.html, four in index.html - is the bare form. Supabase revokes ALL sessions only with signOut({ scope: 'global' }); bare signOut() ends the local one, so a worker who loses a phone cannot sign it out, and on the SHARED plant device this platform explicitly serves (T121's persona) a previous user's session survives elsewhere. That is a one-argument change, though which calls should be global is a real decision - signing every device out on an ordinary sign-out would be its own hostility. (3) No active-session visibility, so nobody can see what to revoke. (4) No 2FA, and no statement that there isn't one - the honest-absence half this trajectory asks about is also missing. ★RECORDED, NOT BUILT: an account surface is a product decision about scope and placement, not an edit, and the scope='global' question needs Ian's call on which paths deserve it. pct 60 -> 72. || ★PASSWORD CHANGE IS BUILT AND GATED, AND ITS COPY UNDERSTANDS THIS PLATFORM'S WORKERS (2026-08-28). validate_password_change_reachable passes live: a signed-in worker finds Change Password beside Sign Out, it meets the 44px touch floor, and the prompt says what will happen. The sentence that makes it right for a plant is the second one - 'Enter the email on your account for a reset link. No email on file (most field workers)? Ask your hive supervisor to reset your password for you.' Most WorkHive accounts are username-only by design, so an email-reset flow alone would strand the majority of the workforce; naming the supervisor path turns a dead end into a procedure, and it matches the supervisor-reset-password function that actually exists. ★THE GAP IS REVOCATION, and for a plant it is the consequential one. So a supervisor saw a green healthy integration while finished jobs silently never reached SAP; the worker meanwhile got a sync badge that shows unconditionally at logbook.html:2311, before the push result exists. It reads the LIVE view definition rather than a migration, so it measures what the database actually buckets. REMAINS: a setup walkthrough that can be completed, test-connection feedback, and sync-failure surfacing (who learns, where). ★A ROLLBACK THAT ANNOUNCED SUCCESS WITHOUT CHECKING - FOUND AND FIXED (2026-08-27). Sweeping for the MIRROR of the unconfirmed-write class (a false SUCCESS is worse than a false failure: the reader stops looking) found rollbackBatch. SOLD LISTING: grant_listing_reward reads the still-HELD reservation and writes a TWO-LEGGED ledger entry - the seller debited 'funded the buyer reward', the buyer credited 'reward for buying' - then marks it released_to_buyer. So on a completed sale the seller DOES part with the 10%%; it goes to the BUYER, never to WorkHive. 'There are no fees' is therefore true of the platform and would have been a half-truth to the seller - except that the page says the rest of it, verbatim: the hold is 'returned if the listing does not sell, and GOES TO YOUR BUYER AS THEIR REWARD if it does'. That is what the what_does_it_cost oracle asks for and it is rare to find it this clean. ★TWO DETAILS THAT MAKE IT MORE THAN LUCKY: the rate is fetched from the server via svcRewardPct() and warmed before first paint, so the hold the seller SEES is the hold the database ENFORCES rather than a hardcoded 10 that could drift from the knob; and grant_listing_reward refuses to let the money evaporate when the buyer cannot be resolved - it returns the credits to the seller, with the reason written in the source ('A reward with nowhere to go must never become a silent deduction'). Gates [held-credits-are-told, credit-solvency, money-trust-confirmed] registered + PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

The first read the seller dashboard with ZERO inquiries in the fixture and could have recorded 'inquiries are not surfaced'; the second seeded one but never opened the tab it lives behind, and could have recorded 'a seeded inquiry does not appear'. It IS - the wallet reads v_service_credit_ledger_truth and renders entry lines, and the amount handling is already careful (an entry whose amount did not arrive shows a gap rather than '+PHP0', because claiming an entry moved nothing is the most misleading thing a ledger can say). But the read was `.limit(3)` while the balance above it is SUM over EVERY row via provider_credit_balance(), and the three lines carried no heading. Today the largest provider ledger is exactly 3 rows, so the cap is invisible; at four, the lines stop reconciling with the total and nothing on screen explains the gap - a seller auditing their own money looking at a silent slice. ★FIXED BY PEEKING ONE MORE THAN IS SHOWN: the read takes 4, renders 3, and the list now names itself - 'Credit activity' when that is everything, 'Latest 3 entries ... earlier entries are not shown here' when it is not. trajectories.title: Marketplace-admin moderation lane
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25, leandro=platform-admin + christine=non-admin, 1280): the lane's ARCHITECTURE verified against the substrate memory - marketplace-admin.html is deliberately KEPT as a deep-browse behind a full-screen reversible RETIRED overlay (redirect-first: Grafana volumes + Platform Actions doors), with the LIVE moderation fused into founder-console#sec-mkt-mod on the same is_marketplace_admin authority. Gate proven: the non-admin supervisor is REFUSED the underlying queue (0 approve controls, refusal text). FIXED + shipped: the overlay printed 'Grafana login: admin - password in infra/mcp/.env.mcp' to ANY signed-in visitor - a credential-location pointer in page copy (T170 screen-share class, worse because the overlay is the one part everyone CAN see); replaced with 'see the infra operator notes'. INSTRUMENT NOTE: my first read graded the under-overlay queue as 'still operating' - getClientRects sees THROUGH a covering overlay; pointer-reachability, not rects, decides what a user can operate (the page-guide-chip-covered-Save lesson's twin). Remaining: the fused founder-console moderation walk (queue triage at volume, self-deal guard UX face, dispute three-party views via T35's harness), the localhost Grafana link's non-founder audience note (wave close). || THE SELF-DEAL GUARD IS EXCELLENT AND HAS NO DOOR (2026-08-27). Read apply_dispute_adjustment's definition: four distinct refusals, each naming its cause in language a person could act on - 'Only a platform admin may adjust a disputed job' (42501); 'Unknown request'; 'Only a disputed job can be adjusted (this one is %)', which INTERPOLATES the actual status rather than leaving the admin to guess; and the self-deal check, 'You are the client on this job; another admin must adjudicate it', which is the rare refusal that names the conflict AND the remedy in one sentence. That is exactly the UX face this trajectory was looking for, and it already exists at the layer that enforces it. ★BUT NOTHING CALLS IT. A search for a real rpc('apply_dispute_adjustment') invocation across every html/js/ts finds exactly three, all inside tests/marketplace-sim-aftermath.spec.ts. The only mentions in product files are COMMENTS in marketplace-seller.html and marketplace.html describing what the function would do. So the adjudication path is written, guarded, and covered by a test - and an admin cannot reach it through the glass; a real dispute would have to be settled by someone with direct database access. The guard's careful messages are, today, addressed to a test runner. ★THIS IS THE 'BUILT BUT NEVER CALLED' CLASS ONE STEP ON: not dead code, but LIVE code with no entrance - which reads as healthy on every static check because the function exists, is referenced in prose, and passes its test. Directly relevant to T97 (dispute resolution end-to-end), whose three-party walk cannot exist until this door does. Remaining: the adjudication UI in the admin lane, then queue triage at volume and the three-party dispute views via T35's harness. ★AND THE 'NO CALLER' FINDING SURVIVES THE OBVIOUS OBJECTION, WHICH I WENT AND CHECKED (2026-08-27): marketplace-admin is RETIRED behind an overlay, its moderation having moved to platform-actions.html, so the natural rebuttal is that the caller simply lives on the new page. It does not. platform-actions documents the history precisely - an 'Open disputes' card was retired 2026-08-03 because it read marketplace_disputes, a GHOST TABLE with 0 rows and no client writer, and offered a 'Refund buyer' button for money the platform never holds - and the same comment names the real mechanism: 'Real disputes are service jobs, adjudicated through apply_dispute_adjustment.' So the platform correctly removed a fake dispute UI, wrote down what the true path is, and has still never built a door to it. That is a stronger version of the finding, not a weaker one: the gap is not an oversight nobody noticed, it is a known mechanism with a documented name and no entrance. || WALKED 1280 SIGNED IN (2026-08-28): the page is RETIRED, and the retirement is the exemplary kind. A full-screen overlay states what moved and WHERE - volumes to Grafana panels, approve / verify / resolve actions to platform-actions.html - and links BOTH destinations rather than leaving the visitor to hunt. Its source comment records the design as 'redirect-first + REVERSIBLE: the original markup is preserved below (validators that scan this file still pass). To un-retire: delete this <div id="wh-retired-overlay"> block', which is how a retirement stays cheap to undo. There is also a T69 note that a Grafana CREDENTIAL POINTER was deliberately removed from the copy because 'this overlay renders for ANY signed-in visitor to the URL, not only the founder, and a credentials location baked into page copy is a screen-share/shoulder hazard' - the right instinct, and rare. ONE OBSERVATION rather than a defect: the underlying page still RUNS - my walk read live figures from behind the overlay (4 Pending Review, 20 Published, 13 Sellers, 9 Pending Verification), so a retired surface is still issuing its queries on every visit. That follows from the preserve-the-markup choice and is the price of reversibility; worth knowing rather than worth changing. || ★THE ADMIN LANE IS GENUINELY AUDITED - and the boundary where auditing STOPS is a schema fact, not an oversight (2026-08-28). marketplace-admin DEFINES writeAuditLog(action, targetType, targetId, targetName, meta) at :454 and calls it from five action paths, and the database agrees that it works: 32 admin-scope rows (listing / KYB / voucher actions) sit in hive_audit_log today. So every moderation action on this lane leaves a traceable record with an actor - the probe this trajectory cares about most, answered with rows rather than with code-reading. ★THE CONTRAST WITH ITS SIBLING IS THE FINDING. founder-console calls writeAuditLog three times and NEVER DEFINES IT; all three calls sit behind `if (typeof writeAuditLog === 'function')`, so the guard is permanently false and the owner's own actions - minting a voucher, deciding a top-up - are silently unaudited. A guard written to be defensive became the thing that hides the absence: no error, no row, no signal. ★AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL, which is why the earlier pass documented it rather than patching it: hive_audit_log.hive_id is NOT NULL. marketplace-admin can satisfy that because everything it acts on belongs to somebody's hive - a listing has a seller, a seller has a hive. founder-console acts at PLATFORM scope, where there is no hive to name, so the table has no valid row shape for its actions and the function was never written. Defining writeAuditLog there without first deciding WHERE platform-scope actions live would just move the failure from silent-skip to a NOT NULL violation on the owner's most consequential controls. ★THE DECISION Ian owes this: a nullable hive_id with a scope discriminator, or a separate platform_audit_log. Until then the honest state is that one admin lane is audited and proven, one is not and knows it. pct 70 -> 82. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate failed-read-is-not-empty re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★A FAILED READ RENDERED AS 'NOTHING TO MODERATE' (2026-08-27). marketplace-admin's three loaders each did `catch { _x = []; toast('...check your connection...') }` and re-rendered. The toast fades; the EMPTY STATE stays - so a refused read (and on an admin surface an RLS refusal is the likeliest failure of all) ended as 'No pending listings / All listings have been reviewed'. On a moderation queue that is the single most costly false sentence the product can show: it is the one that makes someone stop looking. All three now record the failure and render 'This is not an empty queue - the list could not be read', and the messages route through whReadError so a dead session stops being reported as bad wifi. ★THE PLATFORM HAD ALREADY LEARNED THIS TWICE. marketplace.html carries the diagnosis verbatim in its own source from a deepwalk - 'the toast alone was insufficient, it fades, leaving the GRID showing the first-run CTA on a full marketplace' - and seller-profile carries 'Only a read that ANSWERED may license a conclusion about this seller'. Both were fixed; the moderation queue never was. Second fix-that-did-not-travel in one session, so it is now gated: failed-read-is-not-empty. ★THE GATE FOUND A SECOND VICTIM I HAD NOT LOOKED FOR: dayplanner's plant-PM rail returned '' on a failed read and simply VANISHED - not a false claim, an invisible one, which a worker cannot tell from a quiet day. It now says why it is empty. ★AND THE GATE WAS WRONG TWICE BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, both times too NARROW or too BROAD in vocabulary: it first flagged alert-hub's legacy JSON-parse fallback (correct code - scoped it to catches that wrap a QUERY), then failed the very page I had just fixed because marketplace-admin spells its flag as a property (_readFailed.listings) and the regex only accepted bare identifiers. An oracle's vocabulary is part of the oracle, for the sixth time today.

trajectories.title: Seller-profile as the buyer's trust page
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the full chip census done - each claim checked against its enforcing query). THE PROFILE IS IN GOOD ORDER and every trust pixel is computed from data rather than decoration: Top rated = ratingAvg >= 4.5 AND ratingCount >= 5; Quick reply = avgResponseHours < 4 AND replyCount >= 5; Tier carries its own thresholds (silver 11 sales, gold 51) and says 'set by WorkHive from completed sales, not self-assigned'; ID Verified is gated on kyb_verified; Certified routes through the central whCertBadgeEarned on ALL THREE surfaces that render it (seller profile, seller dashboard, listing sheet). ★ONE READING LOOKED LIKE THE ORIGINAL BUG AND WAS NOT: the certifications SECTION tests cert_verified on its own, which is the exact shape of the recorded incident - but the whole block sits inside `if (certSection && certs.length)`, so a non-empty list is guaranteed by construction. Read verbatim before accusing; that check would have been a false finding. Locked as 'trust-claim-backed', guarding the FIXED class: no buyer-facing surface may present a certification claim from cert_verified alone - it must call the central predicate or guard on the certifications list in the same breath. The incident it protects against is concrete: three sellers once carried a violet 'Certified' chip with certifications NULL and cert_verified_at NULL, the platform vouching to a buyer about to send money for credentials that did not exist. ★MODERATION SURFACES EXCLUDED BY NAME, not for convenience: marketplace-admin, founder-console and platform-actions are where verification is GRANTED and must see the raw flag - including the 'set but no certifications on file' state this gate keeps off a buyer's screen. Blinding the moderator to what they moderate would invert the goal. Teeth proven by reverting the profile badge to the flag alone, resurrecting the original incident's shape. REMAINING: the report-a-seller path walk (wave close). || ★THE ID-VERIFIED CHIP IS QUERY-BACKED, AND I NEARLY FILED IT AS INVERTED (2026-08-28). Walked two sellers side by side and the chip looked exactly wrong: Dennis Aquino, whose listings carry seller_verified TRUE, showed NO badge, while Pablo Aguilar, whose listings carry FALSE, showed 'ID Verified'. A trust badge on the wrong person is about the worst defect this page could have, so I read the render before writing it up: the chip is driven by _seller?.kyb_verified from marketplace_sellers, NOT by marketplace_listings.seller_verified. Checking THAT column settles it - Dennis kyb_verified f, Pablo kyb_verified t - so the chip agrees with its own source on both sellers and the claim is enforced. I had compared two similarly-named fields on two different tables and read the mismatch as a defect. ★AND THE CODE ALREADY CARRIES THE LESSON THIS TRAJECTORY EXISTS FOR, at the render site: 'a verification badge requires the thing it verifies. Central rule in utils.js so all three surfaces that render this chip cannot drift apart' - the ID-verified-chip-nothing-enforces memory, fixed centrally rather than per page. ★WORTH RECORDING AS A RISK RATHER THAN A DEFECT: seller_verified (listings) and kyb_verified (sellers) are two different booleans about the same human, one table apart, and I am not the last reader who will assume they mean the same thing. THE PARAMLESS CASE IS ALSO CLEAN: the page refuses with a remedy ('No seller specified. This page needs a seller name in the URL. Open it via marketplace.html.') and its source chip names the corpora it read. || ★AND THEN THE REAL DEFECT, ONE LAYER UNDER THE NEAR-MISS: THE ID-VERIFIED CHIP DISAGREED WITH ITSELF ACROSS FOUR SURFACES (2026-08-28). Having established the chip is query-backed on the profile, I checked who ELSE renders it, and found four sites with four different predicates - marketplace card `item.seller_verified`, marketplace detail `sp.kyb_verified || item.seller_verified`, seller profile `_seller.kyb_verified`, asset-hub mini-card `r.seller_verified`. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE on the fixture: Dennis Aquino carries kyb_verified FALSE on his seller record and seller_verified TRUE on his listings, so he read as VERIFIED on three surfaces and UNVERIFIED on his own profile page. A trust badge that contradicts itself is worse than none, because each surface looks authoritative alone. ★THE CENTRALISATION LESSON WAS ALREADY HERE AND HAD BEEN APPLIED TO THE WRONG CHIP: the comment 'a verification badge requires the thing it verifies. Central rule in utils.js so all three surfaces that render this chip cannot drift apart' sits directly above whCertBadgeEarned - it governs CERTIFIED. The ID-Verified chip standing beside it never got the treatment, and drifted. FIXED with whIdVerified() in utils.js, and the rule is the CONSERVATIVE one on purpose: identity belongs to the SELLER (marketplace_sellers.kyb_verified), not to a listing row whose seller_verified is a copy that can be stale - and reading the seller record is the direction that cannot OVER-claim, which is the failure that matters for a trust signal. No fallback to the drifted field: absent evidence is not evidence. The data was already there - v_marketplace_listings_truth exposes seller_kyb_verified - so the four card queries simply select it now. VERIFIED: the helper returns true/false correctly for a seller record, for the joined column, and crucially FALSE when only the drifted seller_verified is present; the view's column matches the DB join exactly (7 of 20 published); the profile shows the chip for Pablo (kyb true) and withholds it from Dennis (kyb false); zero page errors. ★A SYNTAX ERROR I INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT: my first edit left a stray docblock fragment outside a comment in utils.js - a file every page loads. `node --check` found it immediately. Running the parser is cheaper than discovering it on a page. pct 78 -> 90. || ★AND THE GATE'S OWN CENSUS IS WHERE THE DRIFT HID (2026-08-28). validate_trust_claim_backed carries a census listing every trust claim on this page, and one line reads 'ID Verified — gated on kyb_verified'. That was true of the PROFILE, examined alone, and stated as a platform fact - while three other surfaces granted the same badge from marketplace_listings.seller_verified. A census that examines one surface and generalises is the same too-narrow-scope failure as a gate scoped to one call site, one level up: it produced a WRITTEN RECORD saying the class was safe. The gate's assertion only ever guarded the CERTIFIED chip. Extended now to the identity chip too: a buyer-facing render may not grant the badge from the drifting per-listing copy. TEETH-PROVEN by putting `item.seller_verified` back on the marketplace card - FAIL naming marketplace.html:2183 - and green again on restore, with 8 identity-badge renders counted and 0 from the wrong column. pct 90 -> 95. Remaining: the response-time and sales-history claims still want the same treatment the identity and certification chips now have. || ★THE ROOT OF THE ID-BADGE DRIFT IS IN THE VIEW, AND IT IS LATENT RATHER THAN FIXED (2026-08-28). The client fix routed every identity badge through whIdVerified(), and trust-claim-backed now holds it there — 8 identity-badge renders, 0 reading the drifting copy. But the copy itself is still MANUFACTURED, one layer down: v_marketplace_listings_truth computes `COALESCE(ms.kyb_verified, false) OR COALESCE(ms.cert_verified, false) AS seller_verified`. That OR conflates two different verifications — an identity check (KYB) and a trade-credential check (certifications) — into one boolean whose NAME reads as identity. A seller with certifications on file and no identity check would therefore be seller_verified = true, and any surface that ever reads that column for an ID badge would vouch for an identity nobody confirmed. ★MEASURED, AND IT IS NOT MANIFESTING TODAY: the fixture holds 4 KYB-verified and 4 cert-verified sellers with ZERO divergence, so no seller currently sits in the gap. That is why this is recorded rather than migrated — the semantics are wrong but nothing renders wrongly, the badge decision no longer consults the column, and a gate fails any surface that starts consulting it again. The trigger case to watch for is the first seller granted cert_verified without kyb_verified; splitting the column (or renaming it to say what it means, e.g. seller_any_verification) is the real fix and touches every consumer of the listings view, so it goes to Ian rather than being done quietly under a badge fix. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: the fix is verified and the registered gate trust-claim-backed PASSES standalone (re-run this session). Awaiting the next full-board earn to promote to locked. pct -> 100.

fixes: utils.js whIdVerified + 4 render sites (one rule for the ID-verified chip)

trajectories.title: Status page & public trust surface
trajectories.basis: both halves true: (1) FIXED reachability-from-failure - whListError now renders 'Is it just you? Check the platform status page' under every failure state (ONE central utils.js edit -> ~20 adopter pages; status.html is static-first so the link works during the outage that broke the read); (2) PROVEN resilience - under a total rest+functions block, status.html loads and reports '0/10 probed surfaces healthy - 10 DOWN' with per-surface HTTP/latency/error. SLO targets stated (28-day window). NOTE: utils.js edit -> sw CACHE v239 at Ian's deploy + the one deferred re-earn absorbs the expiry. Remaining: incident history + whReadError connection-branch pointer (wave close). ERROR->STATUS POINTER LANDED 2026-08-26 (central): whReadError's connection fallback - the one every read-failure state ends at - now answers 'is it me or them?': '...Still failing on good internet? Open status.html - it shows if WorkHive itself is having trouble.' The pointer's honesty VERIFIED: status.html loads under total backend outage (rest+functions aborted) and reports '0/10 probed surfaces healthy - 10 DOWN'. Remaining: incident history surface. || INCIDENT HISTORY SCOPED 2026-08-27, and the obvious build is the WRONG one. status.html makes ZERO database calls by design - that is the property its own gate enforces (status-survives-the-outage FAILS the page for containing a supabase client, a getDb, or any table read), because a status page that needs the database cannot report a database outage and fails exactly when someone finally needs it. So 'add an incident list from the DB' would close this item by breaking the gate that locks this trajectory. THE DATA IS NOT THERE EITHER, checked rather than assumed: wh_health_status exists but is CURRENT-STATE shaped (surface, status, latency_ms, detail, updated_at - one row per surface, no started_at/resolved_at/severity) and holds 0 rows, with no producer writing it. An incident history rendered from that today would be a trust signal with no living producer behind it, which is the failure mode this page already refuses in its 'All systems operational' check. SO THE REMAINING ITEM IS A SCOPED BUILD WITH A FORK FOR IAN, not a slice: it needs (1) an incident MODEL with a start, an end and a severity, (2) a PRODUCER that detects and records one, and (3) a delivery shape that keeps the page database-independent - the natural candidate being a build-time static artifact shipped with the site, the way platform_health.json already is, rather than a live read. Recorded here so the next session does not reach for the DB read and quietly cost the page the one property it exists for. || INCIDENT HISTORY — CHECKED THE MACHINERY BEFORE CALLING IT SCOPED, 2026-08-27. The CURRENT status is live and unusually careful: status.html pings each edge function's /health with a bounded 8s abort and grades FOUR states whose distinctions are the honesty - ok, slow (200 but over the threshold), nohealth (the function is UP but exposes no probe, explicitly a coverage gap and NOT an outage) and down (5xx, network failure or timeout). It is also deliberately self-contained, loading no utils.js, so it keeps working during the degradation it exists to report. Nothing here is a hardcoded 'all systems operational'. ★HISTORY IS THE PART THAT DOES NOT EXIST, and I looked for a source rather than assuming: wh_health_status carries the right columns (surface, status, latency_ms, detail, updated_at) but is POINT-IN-TIME with 0 rows - updated_at, not a time series - and automation_log does hold a real dated history (201 success / 4 failed, 2026-07-20 to 2026-08-27) but is HIVE-SCOPED job runs, which is the wrong subject for a PUBLIC trust page and would leak per-hive detail if rendered there. So an incident history needs a producer that snapshots platform health over time plus a retention policy - net-new infrastructure, not a fix - and that is a scoped decision rather than a manufactured blocker, reached by checking three candidate sources and the page itself. || ★THE STATE LIST RECORDED ABOVE IS NOW STALE, AND THE CHANGE IMPROVED THIS PAGE'S HONESTY (2026-08-28, from T198's side). This basis describes 'down (5xx, network failure or timeout)'. That was accurate when written and is not any more: T198 found that lumping TIMEOUT in with outage was the page's own worst claim. Its probe budget is 8s while utils.js allows 30s for an edge cold start, so the likeliest cause of a timeout HERE is a healthy function that simply has not run recently - and this page was rendering that as DOWN in red, on the surface people check to decide whether to trust everything else. There are now FIVE states: ok, slow, nohealth, timeout, down. A timeout is amber, says 'no answer in 8s (may be cold-starting)', and leaves BOTH the healthy numerator and the DOWN count rather than being folded into either. Measured: a hung function plus a real 503 read '8/10 healthy (80%) - 2 DOWN' before and '8/9 healthy (89%) - 1 DOWN - 1 did not answer in time' after; the raw 'AbortError: signal is aborted without reason' that used to print on the card is gone too. The self-contained property this basis credits the page with is what made the fix safe to reason about - its local fetch wrapper RETHROWS the abort, so the timeout is distinguishable in the catch. Second gate on this page: status-cold-is-not-down. Unchanged: the incident-history gap remains a scoped decision needing a net-new snapshot producer plus retention, not a fix. || 2026-08-31 (default taken): incident PRODUCER built + VERIFIED - tools/derive_status_incidents.py derives incidents from platform_health.json (3 open gate incidents = the board 3 fails) + automation_log transitions (3 resolved, real start/end), writes DB-independent status_incidents.json per the approved default (no new incident table, no new producer service). Remaining to lock: status.html reads status_incidents.json (browser slice) + a gate asserting the derivation is truthful. || 2026-09-01 LOCK INSTRUMENT BUILT: tools/validate_status_incidents.py (status-incidents-derived) — 4 assertions (well-formed / open-incident<=>currently-red-gate / resolved-window-sane / fresh=regeneration), self-test teeth-proven (phantom, silent-outage, negative-window all redden). Producer (derive_status_incidents.py) done+verified. REMAINING TO LOCK: (a) wire post-board regeneration of status_incidents.json (it derives from platform_health.json which each board rewrites — so the gate is a POST-board step, NOT in-board, else it false-fails on staleness during the run); (b) status.html renders status_incidents.json; (c) register the gate to run after regeneration; (d) board confirms -> lock. pct stays 92 (instrument built, not yet board-green). || LOCKING 2026-09-01: the fix is verified and the registered gate status-survives-the-outage PASSES standalone (re-run this session). Awaiting the next full-board earn to promote to locked. || 2026-09-01: registered the second lock gate status-incidents-derived (fixed a derive bug — an unrecovered historical automation incident now closes at its last bad run, so it is not "resolved with no window"); self-test + real-file PASS. T71 now double-gated (status-survives-the-outage + status-incidents-derived). pct -> 92. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★THE STATUS PAGE IS ALREADY BUILT THE RIGHT WAY AND WAS UNGATED (2026-08-27). Both halves of this trajectory's sharpest probe hold: it is LINKED from failure states (whReadError's connection branch says 'Still failing on good internet? Open status.html'), and it SURVIVES the outage it reports - measured: zero Supabase client, zero getDb, zero table reads, so it renders with the database down. It is also not a static 'all good': it pings each edge function's public /health endpoint and renders a live card per service, ambering past the interactive SLO, with a Refresh. Nothing was broken; nothing protected it. Gate status-survives-the-outage asserts the DB-independence, the live checks, the absence of a hardcoded green, and the pointer in utils.js that sends people there at all. ★STATUS IS LINKED FROM FAILURE STATES - CORRECTED MID-CHECK (2026-08-27). Grepping the pages for href="status.html" returns ONE file (founder-console), which reads as 'the status page exists and nothing points at it' - the failures-point-nowhere gap this trajectory names. Wrong, and wrong the same way the archive check was twenty minutes earlier: the link is generated CENTRALLY. utils.js carries an actual <a href="status.html"> inside the error render at :1735 and the sentence 'Open status.html - it shows if WorkHive itself is having trouble' at :2188, with a comment noting status.html is static-first so it loads even when the DB that broke the page is down - which is precisely the property this needs. A worker who hits a connection failure is pointed somewhere true. ★SECOND NEAR-MISS OF THE SAME SHAPE IN ONE SESSION: a capability absent from every PAGE is not absent when the platform centralises it. Grep the helper layer before writing the finding. ★WHAT IS GENUINELY MISSING is the INCIDENT HISTORY: status.html is 213 lines of SLO targets and current-state language, with no list of past incidents - so it answers 'is it me or them RIGHT NOW' but not 'has this been happening'. That is the recorded remaining item and it is a build, not a bug: whether a public incident log is worth keeping (and who writes the entries) is Ian's call. ★INCIDENT HISTORY: CHARACTERISED, NOT JUST 'MISSING' (2026-08-27). I first called this Ian's call because 'who writes the entries', then checked whether it could be DERIVED instead - the same move that turned T94's wallet from a missing feature into a number already being computed. It cannot. The platform's health surfaces (v_service_slo, v_wh_traces_slo, v_cron_health, v_storage_health) are CURRENT-STATE only: v_service_slo carries a rolling window_days parameter, the others carry no time dimension at all, and nothing anywhere stores what the platform's health WAS on a past day. So an incident history is not a rendering problem hiding behind a missing view - it needs new machinery, and there are two shapes with different costs: periodic health SNAPSHOTS (derived, no authorship, but a new writer and a retention policy) or human-authored incident entries (honest and richer, but someone has to write them during an outage, which is exactly when nobody has time). trajectories.title: Achievements page beyond the ladder (T17's home)
trajectories.basis: walked 390: arrival states its bases inline ('XP this week: points earned in the last 7 days', 'max 1,200 = 12 domains x level 100'), denominators everywhere (8/12 domains active), verdict line with pace. Remaining: locked-achievement how-to-unlock coverage (only 1 'to unlock' string found at rest - check tabs), standings privacy, marketplace-tier vocabulary bridge (wave close). HOW-TO-UNLOCK FIXED 2026-08-26: expanding a no-activity domain said only 'No activity yet' - a dead end on exactly the card a worker opens to learn its HOW (regular cards never rendered def.desc; only legendaries did). The empty branch now teaches from the definition: live-proven 'No activity yet. How to earn: Manage inventory and BOM - XP lands here automatically as you do that work.' Remaining: standings privacy posture, marketplace-tier vocabulary bridge. || THE TIER-VOCABULARY BRIDGE EXISTS AND IS CORRECT - THE TWO SYSTEMS ARE ONE (2026-08-27). The open worry was that achievements and the marketplace both say bronze/silver/gold for different things, which is the one_vocabulary failure: same word, two meanings, and a worker who earns 'Gold' somewhere cannot tell which ladder moved. Read the code and the worry is unfounded in the best possible way - achievements.html reads v_service_provider_truth, the SAME view the marketplace surfaces render from, and displays that row's own tier field. There is no second tier ladder to collide with; there is one ladder shown in two places. ★AND IT IS SHOWN WITH ITS NEXT STEP, which is the property T74 and T98 both want: not a bare badge but '10 more completed jobs reach Silver' / '25 more jobs and a 4.5-star average reach Gold' / 'Top tier - you get first look at new hails', so the ladder is predictable rather than mysterious. It is also correctly scoped: a member who is not a service provider gets the section rendered as NOTHING rather than an empty or zeroed tier ('not a provider: render nothing'), so a plant worker who never sells is not shown a Bronze badge for a ladder they are not on. ★THE MEASUREMENT NEEDED CARE: a raw grep for 'tier' in achievements returns mostly CSS COMMENTS about the type scale ('joined the 18px title tier', 'the text tier exists for exactly this') - typography prose, not the domain concept, and counting those would have manufactured a vocabulary problem out of a stylesheet. Remaining: standings PRIVACY posture - there is no opt-out, hide-me or anonymise control anywhere on the page, so every hive member appears in the standings by default. Whether that should be opt-out-able is a product call (a team leaderboard is normal; being unable to leave it is a different thing), so it rides as Ian's. || ★AN XP REVERSAL RENDERED AS '+-20' ON THE REWARD SURFACE (2026-08-28). achievements.html builds every XP row through one helper, xpText, and that helper hard-codes a '+' in front of any finite number. Negative amounts are not hypothetical here - they are the reversible XP ledger this programme deliberately built, so deleting work takes its XP back. SEEN LIVE on Bryan Garcia's Wrench Chronicle card: 'Logbook entry submitted +-20', 'Logbook entry closed +-50', beside a correct 'Logbook entry closed +50'. ★AND THE SITE ALREADY CARRIED A LONG COMMENT ABOUT THIS EXACT HELPER - it was hardened against null ('+null' rendered ten times on one screen), against Number(null) coercing to 0, and it even reasons about why '+0' would be 'a lie of a different kind'. Every one of those guards is about the ABSENT case. None is about the NEGATIVE case, because when the guard was written negatives could not occur; they arrived later with the reversal ledger. That is the sibling-fix shape this codebase keeps meeting, in its subtlest form: not a fix applied to one of two call sites, but a guard that was complete on the day it was written and was never revisited when a NEW FEATURE widened its input domain. FIXED: a negative already carries its own sign, so only a gain has one added. Verified live - the three rows now read -20, -50, +50, no '+-' anywhere on the page - and across the helper's whole domain: +20 | -20 | +0 | 'XP not recorded' for null, undefined and empty, so the absent-case guards the comment describes still behave exactly as before. A reversal is the one XP event a worker most needs to read correctly. || AND THE SWEEP FOUND ITS SIBLING 140 LINES AWAY (2026-08-28). Having fixed xpText I swept every page for the shape - a hard-coded '+' in front of an interpolated value - rather than stopping at the instance. NINE hits. Seven are engineering-design overflow counts ('+3 more', '+2' beside a truncated list) where the value is positive by construction, guarded by the if (n > visible) that produces them. The eighth was the fix itself. THE NINTH IS REAL: achievements' WEEK hero renders `+${weekXP}`, and weekXP is a plain SUM of xp_earned over seven days (init :1197, reduce over the rows), so a week whose reversals outweigh its gains is genuinely negative and the headline tile would have read '+-30'. Fixed the same way, and its subtitle now explains the case rather than reading as nonsense: '-30 XP this week - more was taken back by deleted work than earned'. Verified: the live positive case is unchanged (+1780), the negative renders -30 with that sub, zero still reads +0 / 'No XP earned in the past 7 days'. ★THE SWEEP IS THE POINT - one fix would have left a headline number lying while the detail rows beneath it told the truth, which is worse than either alone. || ★EVERY ACHIEVEMENT SAYS WHAT EARNS IT, AND THE CATALOGUE IS ORGANISED BY MOTIVATION RATHER THAN BY FEATURE (2026-08-28). The probe is whether a locked achievement teaches its own HOW. Each definition carries a desc that names the activity in plain language - 'Log and close maintenance jobs', 'Complete PM tasks on time', 'Identify root causes of breakdowns', 'Write detailed entries and handovers' - so a worker reading the catalogue learns what the platform wants from them without opening anything. ★AND THE GROUPING IS DELIBERATE PSYCHOLOGY, not a feature index: every achievement is tagged to one of three pillars - competence, autonomy, relatedness - which is the self-determination triad, the standard model of intrinsic motivation. wrench_chronicle and uptime_guardian sit under competence; safety_sentinel and skill_climber under autonomy; hive_architect and voice_of_hive under relatedness. Somebody designed this to answer 'why would a worker care' rather than 'what features do we have', and that is the difference between a progression system and a list of badges named after modules. ★THE HONEST LIMIT: the descs name the ACTIVITY, not the THRESHOLD. 'Complete PM tasks on time' tells a worker what to do and not how many, so 'what do I need for my next badge' - this trajectory's plan-your-next-badge probe - is answerable only in direction, not in distance. Thresholds exist in the awarding logic; surfacing them beside the desc is what would close it. pct 78 -> 88. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - every achievement teaches its own HOW: the achievements gate + earning-moment-is-announced prove each badge names what earns it and the earning moment reaches the earner. trajectories.title: Dayplanner as a planning tool (beyond T13's read)
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the SC 2.5.7 drag question ANSWERED platform-wide). ★THE WALK'S PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO: it listed 'touch drag/reorder alternative (SC 2.5.7)' as dayplanner's remaining risk, and dayplanner has NO drag machinery at all - no draggable, no dragstart, no touchmove reorder. There was no drag to provide an alternative for. Swept every production surface instead: only THREE drag hooks exist. integrations' CSV drop zone is exemplary (role=button, tabindex=0, onclick -> file-input.click(), and visible copy reading 'Drop file here or click to browse' - drag is the shortcut, not the door), and the other two are nav-hub's and companion-launcher's FAB repositioners. ★THOSE TWO ARE ALLOWED BY A RULE RATHER THAN BY NAME, because a name-based exemption would be a licence: the gate decides on what the handler WRITES. Both assign only style.left/right/top/bottom - they move a control and confer no capability, since opening the hub is a tap and `didDrag` exists precisely so a drag does not fire it. And the need a reposition serves - a fixed control covering content - is already met for everyone structurally by the reserve and lift rules in that same file (read while fixing T184 this session). If such a handler ever starts mutating data (insert, splice, sort_order) it stops matching the position-only test and the gate speaks up - proven by a teeth test that adds a dragstart calling splice(). Locked as 'no-drag-only', guard-the-absence, with maplibre-gl.js (third-party) and survey_ufai_rubric.js (internal measurement, never shipped) excluded and stated. REMAINING: week rollover behaviour and the plan-vs-pm-scheduler duplication vocabulary (wave close). || MERGE NOTE (same day): 'no-drag-only' already existed - T117 built it - so this work MERGED into that one gate rather than adding a second. ★AND I DAMAGED THINGS GETTING THERE, which is worth the record: I wrote my version straight OVER the T117 file after reading 'updated successfully' as 'created' (the file was untracked, so git had no copy), and then removed 102 unrelated gate registrations with an over-greedy cleanup regex. The registry's duplicate-id guard caught the first; a diff against HEAD caught and exactly repaired the second (865 = 803 HEAD + 62 program gates, 0 missing, no dupes, both halves re-run green). T117's findings - session-timeout's touchstart as an activity SIGNAL, wh-persona's draggable=false, the .wh-scroll-x keyboard trap closed centrally - were recovered from its registry label and folded back in. A duplicate id is a signal to MERGE two efforts, never to register the same name twice. || NUMBER-TRUTH WALK, 390, SIGNED IN (2026-08-28) - and the page passes the check that once failed here. The PM rail reads '30 of 80 PMs': a display slice that names its whole. The code shows this is deliberate rather than lucky - the query carries count:'exact' with a comment saying WHY ('the .limit(30) below is a DISPLAY slice, and the header next to this rail states a number. Without the count it stated data.length'), and the label is conditional, falling back to a correctly pluralised 'N PM' / 'N PMs' when nothing is being truncated. That is the exact defect T22's basis records dayplanner having had - printing its 30-row slice as the count while 80 were due - now fixed AND explained at the site. The logbook rail states its source in the same breath ('2 open items from Logbook'), and every overdue PM card carries its asset, its make/model and its due date rather than a bare 'Overdue'. Zero page errors at 390. || ★THE DAY PLANNER SHOWED THE DAY OUT OF ORDER - found, fixed, proven (2026-08-28). It IS a planning tool, not a read view: six insert/update/upsert/delete paths, and the item form collects a Start Time and End Time (#m-start / #m-end, type=time). But loadSchedule ordered by .order('date').order('id') and NOTHING ELSE, so two items on the same day never sorted chronologically. Worse than creation order: schedule_items.id is a TEXT key like 'svc-<uuid>', so the tiebreaker sorts on a random string. Measured on real rows, one worker's day read 10:30 -> 09:00 -> 07:00 -> 08:00. A planner that asks when a job starts and then lists the afternoon above the morning is not showing the worker their day, and 36 same-date multi-item days exist in local data alone. ★FIX: .order('start_time', {ascending:true, nullsFirst:false}) between date and the id tiebreaker. start_time is TEXT in zero-padded HH:MM, so a lexicographic sort IS chronological - no cast needed. nullsFirst:false is the load-bearing half: 126 of 228 rows are UNTIMED, and the default nulls-first would have floated every untimed to-do above the scheduled work, making the majority case worse than the bug I was fixing. Timed work now reads in order, untimed follows. PROVEN on the same rows: 07:00 -> 08:00 -> 09:00 -> 10:30. ★AND THE DATA HAD TWO SPELLINGS OF 'NO TIME SET': 126 NULL plus 2 empty-string starts (3 empty ends). They mean the same thing to a person and sort oppositely to a database - '' precedes '07:00', so those rows would have floated to the TOP of the day while NULLs correctly fell to the end, the same untimed item landing in opposite places depending on which spelling was stored. Migration ...004 normalises '' -> NULL and adds a CHECK so the pair cannot drift again - fixing the representation rather than widening the sort to special-case it. VERIFIED THREE WAYS: teeth (an empty start_time INSERT is rejected by name), non-breakage (a NULL start_time still inserts, so the 56% untimed majority still saves), and idempotency (re-run yields UPDATE 0 / UPDATE 0 and no duplicate-constraint error). ★VALIDATED NEGATIVE: no drag/reorder machinery exists anywhere on this page - no draggable, dragstart, sortable or touchstart - so WCAG 2.5.7 (dragging movements needs a single-pointer alternative) is not violated here; there is no dragging to provide an alternative for. The only 'drop' match was backdrop-filter in CSS. Sorting by time is also what makes reorder unnecessary: the day orders itself from the times the worker already enters. ★SUPERSEDED WITHIN THE SAME TURN, and the correction matters more than the original: the CHECK described above was the WRONG SHAPE and I removed it in migration ...005. Walking T192 immediately afterwards asked what dayplanner actually SENDS, and the answer was '' - an empty <input type="time"> yields empty string at :1988 and the quick-add path coerces to '' at :2084 - so that CHECK would have REJECTED every untimed task, i.e. 126 of 228 rows, the majority case. The teeth test I ran proved the constraint bit; it never asked whether the thing it bit was a legitimate write. A guard verified only against the payload you INTENDED is half-verified. Replaced by a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger that normalises '' to NULL instead of refusing it, plus the client normalising at its single send boundary - same invariant, but an already-open page keeps saving. The ordering fix and its 07:00->10:30 proof are unaffected and stand. pct 60 -> 84. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate no-drag-only re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Shift-brain generation & regeneration (beyond T13's read)
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25, supervisor 1280, two generation runs): VERIFIED-GOOD - inputs are VISIBLE on the glass ('Based on your shift plan - Top-risk + PMs-due + carry-forward + parts, composed by shift-planner-orchestrator'), the brief is grounded with defined denominators ('9 carry-forward (open >8h)', '29 PMs due this window', '3 parts to stage'), staleness honesty present (STALE badge machinery + 'loaded from storage, not regenerated just now'), and DRAFT labeling on the action brief. PREMISE FINDING (check-the-premise): there is NO manual-edit surface on the glass (zero edit/reassign controls) - 'edit-then-regen honesty' has no UI face; regen_respects_edits exercises a DB-side path no user can take from this page, so the crew-facing manual-vs-generated marking question is moot until an edit surface exists (scoped decision). FIXED + VERIFIED: rerunPlan disabled `btn || gen` - with both buttons present the CLICKED Generate stayed live 3s into a ~90s cold-start run (double-press = two orchestrator runs, double AI spend, racing writes); now BOTH lock ('Running...') and both restore (proven: disabled at 1.5s, re-enabled after ~7.5s on a warm run). Remaining: cancel affordance for the cold-start-length run (PP2), fairness legibility (rest-day/rotation vocabulary absent from the glass), worker-side brief parity (T13 seam), the edit-surface decision (wave close). || FAIRNESS LEGIBILITY RESOLVES AS 'NOTHING TO MAKE LEGIBLE YET', AND THE PRODUCT ALREADY SAYS SO IN THE RIGHT PLACE (2026-08-27). The open item read 'rest-day/rotation vocabulary absent from the glass', which sounds like a UI gap. It is not: the platform has NO leave or rest-day MODEL at all, and tools/psql_probes/shift-brain__rest_days_respected.sql already pins that structurally - it asserts zero leave/rest_day/day_off/vacation columns across hive_members, worker_profiles, schedule_items and shift_plans, and is written to FAIL the day such a model lands so the claim gets re-examined against a schema that finally has one. Absent vocabulary is the honest rendering of an absent model. ★AND THE AI IS TOLD, WHICH IS THE PART THAT COULD EASILY HAVE BEEN MISSING: shift-planner-orchestrator's prompt states 'no headcount, no leave or rest-day calendar. So never state how many workers, technicians...' - the generator is explicitly forbidden from inventing the fairness data it does not have, which is what stops a plausible-sounding rota from being confabulated into a crew briefing. ★MY OWN GREP LIED FIRST, TWICE: searching shift-brain*/index.ts found nothing because the function is named shift-planner-orchestrator, and then a case-insensitive /rest/ reported 10 hits of which NINE were substrings inside restrict/restore/REST. One real line, found only after checking the premise and adding a word boundary - the same   lesson as this session's date-field census ('end' inside 'trend'). Remaining: the cancel affordance for the cold-start-length run (PP2) and the worker-facing manual-vs-generated marking. || WALKED 390 SIGNED IN WITH THE NEW OCCLUSION-AWARE WALKER, dropped 0 - so this is the page, not a sample of it (2026-08-28). Every figure on the crew-facing read carries its noun AND its basis: '29 preventive tasks due this window', '9 jobs still open from before this shift (open >8h)' - which defines carry-forward rather than assuming the reader knows it - and '3 parts to stage'. The zero is explained rather than left bare: 'TOP RISK THIS SHIFT · 0 · No assets above the risk threshold', which distinguishes a measured none from a missing read. The verdict ('Heavy shift: prioritize hot assets and carry-forward') reconciles with the numbers beneath it - 0 high-risk but 29 PMs and 9 carry-forward IS heavy - so the headline and the detail agree, which is the failure this session found twice elsewhere. Shift windows are labelled with their hours (06-14 Morning / 14-22 Afternoon / 22-06 Night) rather than by name alone. The action names its count ('Clear 9 carry-forward →'). Zero page errors. pct -> 70 on the READ axis; the generate/regenerate half (does an edit survive a regen, on the glass) is still the open one. || ★THE EDIT-THEN-REGEN PROBE IS MOOT: THERE IS NO EDITING SURFACE (2026-08-28). This trajectory asks whether regeneration honours a supervisor's hand-tuned changes and says on the glass which survived. shift-brain.html has ZERO editable controls - no input, no textarea, no contenteditable - so a supervisor cannot hand-tune a generated plan there at all. The regen_respects_edits recipe protects a property the UI does not currently let anyone create, and shift_plans carries generated_by but no edit-tracking column. That is the same shape as T153's calculators: the trajectory assumed a capability the product deliberately does not have, and the honest answer is to say so rather than to record a pass on an untested property. ★WHAT THE PAGE DOES DO WELL is freshness, which for a shift plan is the property that actually bites. There is NO edit. So a supervisor holding an AI-drafted failure mode that is NEARLY right must either approve it as written or delete it and re-author from scratch — and on FMEA that asymmetry has teeth, because these rows drive maintenance strategy and risk scoring. The cheap path is to approve, so an imprecise mode ('bearing wear' where the truth is outer-race spalling from misalignment) gets published because editing costs more than accepting. ★THE PATTERN ALREADY EXISTS ON THIS PLATFORM: resume's review sheet renders each extracted item as an EDITABLE input (data-review-value, resume.html:1224) — accept / amend / reject per row — which is the shape this trajectory's own spec asked for. So the gap is not that the idea is unproven here. ★WHAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A COPY IS A PROVENANCE QUESTION WITH NO OBVIOUS RIGHT ANSWER: the rows carry a fmea-source-pill, and ai-draft-shows-its-basis locks that the basis is shown. If a supervisor rewrites an AI-drafted mode, what does the pill say afterwards? Keep 'AI' and the platform overstates what the model contributed; switch to 'human' and it erases that AI seeded a safety-relevant record. Both are defensible, and AI6 makes it a truth question rather than a styling one — so the edit path is specced with its provenance semantics rather than guessed at on a surface where the record outlives the session. Remaining: that provenance decision, then the edit path; empty-history honesty; per-suggestion grounding drill. || ★THE OPEN QUESTION FOR IAN IS ANSWERED BY THE ARCHITECTURE - RETIRING THE FORK (2026-08-27). The pending question was: does the source pill still say AI after a human rewrites an AI-drafted failure mode? Measured rather than debated. THERE IS NO IN-PLACE REWRITE: the only two writes to rcm_fmea_modes are an INSERT (new mode) and an UPDATE that sets ONLY approved_by + approved_at, guarded with .is('approved_at', null) so the first approver's name cannot be overwritten - a guard whose comment records the live-proven last-write-wins bug it fixed ('writerB re-approve affected 1 row and overwrote Supervisor A'). A human therefore never edits an AI row's text; they APPROVE it, or they author a separate manual one. ★SO THE TWO FACTS NEVER COLLIDE: `source` records who DRAFTED (ai_logbook / ai_template / manual / imported, CHECK-constrained), `approved_by` + `approved_at` record who VETTED, and the row renders BOTH - the AI/manual pill and the approved/pending status side by side. The pill staying 'AI' is correct rather than stale, because it is not a claim about who endorses the mode; the approval chip is. LIVE STATE: 300 modes, 85 carrying ai_confidence, 245 approved. The table is rcm_fmea_modes and it carries source, ai_confidence, created_by, approved_by and approved_at - a fabricated name producing a false absence, the same class as this session's fabricated hive UUID. pct -> 88. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Analytics orchestrator daily brief (AMC)
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, supervisor 390, live alert-hub read): the 6am brief VERIFIED-GOOD on every core probe - freshness stamped ('stored brief, generated Aug 25, 10:00 AM' + 'Refreshing this brief with live data...' stored-then-refresh honesty), model attribution ('model amc-v1'), the approval's GATE stated in words ('Supervisor approval blocks AMC dispatch' - the fork names what the answer gates), Approve brief/Reject controls present, content GROUNDED in named assets ('Flygt NP 3171 critical PM overdue 37 days, assign tech now' + four named medium-critical PMs), and brief->action links live ('Clear 51 critical/high ->'). Remaining: the missed-cron morning (does a skipped 6am label yesterday's brief honestly - needs a cron-miss injection), approve->dispatch ripple walk, claim->data grounding drill (37d vs pm_completions truth), the scheduled-artifact freshness oracle (wave close). || THE MISSED-CRON MORNING — PROVEN LIVE 2026-08-27 by INDUCING it, not by reading the code. The fixture had today's brief present, so the honest state was unobservable; today's row was moved to a sentinel shift_date (one row, by id), the page walked, and the row restored and verified (shift_date 2026-08-27 / approved, one row for today, zero sentinel rows left). WHAT A SUPERVISOR SEES on a morning the 6am cron did not run: 'NOT GENERATED — No brief was generated for this shift. The brief is written at 6am PHT and has not run for today. The most recent one covers <date>; it is below, and it is not a substitute for today.' That is the whole property in one paragraph: it names the STATE, names the SCHEDULE so the reader knows what was supposed to happen, names the DATE of the most recent brief rather than showing it undated, and explicitly refuses to let it stand in. The mechanism behind it is a shift_date equality read (.eq for the today panel, .neq for the history), so a stale brief cannot reach the panel at all — the honesty is structural rather than a message someone remembered to write. ★AND THE PROBE'S OWN ASSERTION MIS-READ ITS RESULT: namesPriorDate came back false because the regex looked for a 2026-08-2x date while the page correctly named the sentinel it actually found. The page was right and the check was wrong — read before believing a red. Remaining: approve/reject flow scope (whose approval, what it gates). || APPROVE/REJECT SCOPE — ANSWERED 2026-08-27, and nothing needed fixing, which is recorded as a result rather than a shrug because the question was 'whose approval, and what does it gate'. WHOSE: a supervisor's, enforced in TWO places that agree - the RLS policy amc_briefings_update_supervisor allows the write only to a supervisor of that hive, and the UI shows the approve/reject controls only when HIVE_ROLE === 'supervisor' AND the brief is still pending. WHAT IT GATES: not VISIBILITY. The read policy (amc_briefings_read) filters on active hive membership and says nothing about status, so every member sees the brief whether or not it has been approved. That is a defensible design and, importantly, the glass does not hide it: the status pill carries the state, a NON-supervisor looking at a pending brief gets an explicit read-only note, and an approved brief names WHO approved it and WHEN. So approval here is an ACKNOWLEDGEMENT the crew can see, not a publication gate - and a supervisor cannot mistake the state, only possibly the consequence. ★I DID NOT MANUFACTURE A FINDING OUT OF IT: the obvious candidate was the pill printing brief.status raw, but 'pending' / 'approved' / 'expired' are ordinary English words, not the lowercase_with_underscores jargon the no-raw-enum gate exists for (re-run: 22 pages, 0 fail). Turning readable status words into a defect to have something to fix would be the opposite of the job. Whether an UNAPPROVED AI brief should be visible to the crew at all is a product question, not a bug, and it is left as one. || Remaining: nothing owed beyond the wave-close re-earn - the approve/reject scope question above IS the answer to the item this trajectory had open, and the missed-cron morning is proven live. || ★THE BRIEF'S FIRST STAT WAS MISLABELLED IN THE LAYER THAT GROUNDS THE AI (2026-08-28). Walking alert-hub I found the AMC tile carrying data-rag-label='AMC assets checked' while the tile the supervisor reads says 'High Risk' - opposite readings of the same zero: one means the brief examined nothing, the other means it found nothing wrong. THE DATA SETTLES IT rather than my reading: the value is brief.asset_count falling back to top_assets.length, and today's row carries asset_count 0, top_assets [], headline 'Routine shift: 5 PM task(s) due, no risk escalations'. So it counts ESCALATED assets and the VISIBLE label was the correct one; the rag-label was wrong. That attribute feeds the RAG grounding, so the wrong name there is how an assistant ends up telling a supervisor their morning brief checked no assets on a morning it checked them and found them fine - a metric's label is a claim, and this one is read by a machine that will repeat it. The other three tiles (PMs flagged/PMs Due, parts at risk/Parts, crew alerts/Crew) agree and were left alone. ★I DECIDED NOT TO GATE THIS, and the reason is worth keeping: I built the census first, and of 75 data-rag-label attributes only FOUR sit in a markup shape where a visible sibling label can be paired automatically - so a gate would police 5% of the population while a shared-word heuristic flags even the CORRECTED pair ('AMC high-risk assets' vs 'High Risk' share no whole token because of the hyphen). Low coverage plus a false positive on the known-good case is a bad instrument, and shipping it would have added a red that teaches people to ignore reds. ★AND I MADE THE COMMENT-INSIDE-A-TAG MISTAKE AGAIN while fixing it - the same one caught on pm-scheduler's button earlier the same day - putting an HTML comment BETWEEN two attributes, where a browser parses it as bogus attributes. Caught by reading the file back, and the live check now asserts it explicitly: bogusAttrs [] on the element, label and tile both intact, zero page errors. || AND THE MISTAKE IS NOW GATED RATHER THAN JUST NOTICED (2026-08-28). Making the same comment-inside-a-tag error twice in one session - pm-scheduler's button, then this tile while fixing its label - is a class, not two accidents, and its failure mode is silence: a browser parses the comment's words as BOGUS ATTRIBUTES, never errors, and the element quietly loses whatever attribute came after. Both instances were caught by reading the file back, which is luck dressed as discipline. New gate no-comment-inside-tag scans every served html file with a real parser walk (quote-aware, so a `<!--` inside an attribute VALUE is legal text; script and style bodies blanked but their newlines kept so line numbers stay true). 242 files, 0 offenders, so it locks a clean floor rather than ratcheting a debt - and teeth-proven by reproducing the exact mistake between these two attributes and watching it name alert-hub.html:347. The instrument that catches my own recurring error is worth more than the fix that prompted it. || AND THAT GATE NOW CHECKS ITS OWN SCANNER BEFORE IT CHECKS THE TREE (2026-08-28). no-comment-inside-tag is a HAND-ROLLED parser, and a hand-rolled parser that quietly stops matching reports a clean tree - the permanent-false-green shape this codebase keeps meeting, most recently in prove_route_numbers where an eaten   killed a branch silently. So the eight edge cases I used to validate it are now embedded and run on EVERY invocation, before any file is read: the marker is legal inside a quoted VALUE and inside a script body, a bare < or > in prose is not a tag boundary, and the mistake must be caught in all three ways it has actually been written (plain, multi-line, single-quoted attributes). PROVEN: neutering the scanner's match makes the run FAIL with 'the SCANNER is wrong, so its reading of the tree means nothing' and names the three cases that broke, instead of scanning 242 files and reporting zero. A detector that cannot find the bug it was written for is worse than no detector, and the cheapest way to keep that true is to make it prove itself every time rather than the once when it was written. || ★LOCKED 2026-08-31: the wave-close re-earn landed and every gate this row names read PASS on a FULL board (missing-brief-says-so). That was the only item its basis still owed. pct 97 -> 100. || REVERTED 2026-09-04: named gate FAILED on the 1034/60 board (false 100%; post_board_promote over-locked). pct -> 90.

trajectories.title: Semantic search across the hive's knowledge
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25): REACHABILITY MAPPED first (the trajectory's own bar): the global Cmd+K palette is EXACT-KEYWORD over four truth views (assets/jobs/parts/PMs, click jumps to source) while the semantic-search fn is consumed ONLY inside assistant.html as RAG context (JWT-forwarded tenancy, 6s ceiling, proceed-without-RAG fallback) - the capability is reachable CONVERSATIONALLY, a legitimate split, but a natural-language phrase typed into the palette dead-ended ('No matches. Try a shorter or different query.') with no pointer to the surface that answers by meaning. FIXED + VERIFIED: the palette's zero-results state now names its own scope ('matches exact words in assets, jobs, parts, and PMs') and offers the bridge ('Asking in your own words? The AI Assistant searches by meaning ->' -> assistant.html) - proven rendering on a live NL query. search-overlay.js is NOT SW-shelled (no bump). Remaining: tenant-scoping probe as-user (foreign-hive phrase must recall nothing), the write->findable embedding-lag oracle, citation provenance drill in assistant answers (T16 seam), carrying the query text into assistant.html?q= (the deep-link contract exists - a scoped enhancement) (wave close). || TENANT SCOPING OF SEMANTIC RECALL — PROVEN 2026-08-27 without spending an AI call, by testing the layer that actually enforces it. The knowledge RPCs (search_fault_knowledge, search_all_knowledge, match_procedural_memories) all take the hive as a CLIENT-SUPPLIED parameter - search_fault_knowledge(query_embedding vector, match_hive_id uuid, match_count int) with WHERE hive_id = match_hive_id - which on its own would be injectable: pass another hive's id and ask for its knowledge. ★WHAT MAKES IT SAFE IS TWO FACTS THAT HAVE TO HOLD TOGETHER, and both were checked rather than assumed. The function is SECURITY INVOKER, not DEFINER, so the caller's RLS applies; and fault_knowledge / knowledge_graph_facts have RLS ENABLED with the policy 'auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND hive_id IN (SELECT hive_id FROM hive_members WHERE auth_uid = auth.uid() AND status = active)'. So a foreign match_hive_id narrows to rows the caller cannot see anyway - they are filtered BEFORE the vector comparison, not after ranking. Had the function been DEFINER, that same parameter would be a cross-tenant read of the entire knowledge corpus. EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION in a rolled-back transaction: fault_knowledge returns 3812 rows as postgres (RLS bypassed) and 0 rows as anon (RLS applied). A foreign-hive phrase recalls nothing because the rows never reach the comparison. Remaining: the write->findable embedding-lag oracle and the citation-provenance drill (both need AI invocations, so they wait on a quota decision). || ★THE SEARCH IS REACHABLE AND TENANT-SAFE; ITS LAG IS REAL AND UNDISCLOSED (2026-08-28). Reachability, the probe this trajectory puts first, is answered: semantic-search is invoked from assistant.html - a real user surface, not a function-only capability - through fetchWithTimeout, so it is bounded like every other slow call after T146. And the tenancy is done the RIGHT way: the call forwards the USER'S SESSION JWT so the function's Pillar I check binds to the actual caller, rather than running under a service key that would see every hive and rely on a hand-written filter - the exact failure recorded in [[feedback_edge_fn_service_role_hive_id_injection]]. ★THE GAP IS LAG HONESTY. Indexing is asynchronous by design: writes land, enqueue_for_embedding puts a row in embedding_outbox (a proper retry-shaped queue - enqueued_at, attempts, next_attempt_at, claimed_at, done_at, last_error), and a drainer processes it later. So there is a real window in which an entry EXISTS but is not yet FINDABLE, and no surface says so: zero matches for indexing / not-yet-searchable / may-take-a-moment copy on assistant.html or logbook.html. A worker who logs a repair and immediately asks the assistant about it is told there is nothing - which reads as the platform having forgotten what they just typed, not as 'not indexed yet'. That is the search-lag oracle this trajectory specs: the window must be stated, or measured and stated. ★A LOCAL NUMBER I DELIBERATELY DID NOT BANK: the local outbox shows 6,944 undone of 10,390 with draining stopped on 2026-08-20 while rows kept arriving through 08-27, which looks exactly like a broken pipeline. It is not one. tools/drain_embedding_outbox.py is a MANUALLY-run local tool, so the backlog measures how long since I ran it in dev, not how the product behaves. Reporting it would have been a true reading of the wrong subject - the same trap as T158's stale public feed. pct 75 -> 84. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate search-term-survives-punctuation re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only).
