trajectories.title: AI write provenance end-to-end (AI6 as a journey)
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the AI6 validator EXTENDED to renders - this trajectory's named instrument close). The WRITE half was already 6/6: every AI write into a human-read domain table declares machine authorship on the row. THE READ HALF WAS NOT, and the gap was in the worst possible panel. ★logbook's 'past repairs on this machine' - what a technician consults BEFORE OPENING A MACHINE - queried fault_knowledge selecting only problem/root_cause/action/knowledge/worker_name/created_at and rendered each row attributed BY NAME. fault_knowledge is a table the AI also writes into (visual-defect-capture), so a machine-captured observation would have read as a repair a named colleague actually performed. The write was accountable and the read threw the accountability away. Today all 3813 rows are source='manual', so the defect was LATENT - which is exactly when to fix it, before the first AI row lands and reads as human. Fixed: select now fetches source + ai_model, render appends 'AI-captured (<model>)' beside the name. VERIFIED LIVE with a seeded ai_visual_capture row: panel showed 'Rosa Villanueva · Aug 26, 26 · AI-captured (gemini-2.0-flash)', exactly one badge among five rows, four human entries untouched, 0 pageerrors; probe deleted and residue re-counted 0. ★THE BADGE TESTS source LIKE 'ai_%' RATHER THAN != 'manual', because that is the contract the DATABASE enforces - CHECK ((source ~~ 'ai\_%') = (ai_model IS NOT NULL)) over a closed vocabulary of manual / ai_visual_capture / cmms_import. Reading a row by the same rule the write is held to keeps the badge from drifting, and leaves cmms_import (an import, not a machine author) correctly unmarked. The DB taught me the vocabulary by rejecting two probe inserts. Locked as 'ai-render-provenance'. ★THREE INSTRUMENT CORRECTIONS, ALL CAUGHT BY THE TEETH TEST: (1) blanking comments with plain spaces preserved byte offsets but destroyed LINE numbers, so it first named an Escape-key handler instead of the query; (2) a .select('id') after an .update() was counted as a display read when it is an optimistic-concurrency no-op detector; (3) a 600-char scan window ended before logbook's own .select(), because the comment above it is ~700 chars - so the gate silently stopped seeing the query it was built for and reported PASS with the fix REVERTED. A scan window sized to today's code narrows every time someone documents something. REMAINING: the only-AI/only-human filter (scoped, likely net-new) and RAG-ingests-AI-content visibility (knowledge_graph_facts -> citations) at wave close. || RAG-INGESTS-AI-CONTENT VISIBILITY — MEASURED 2026-08-27, and the corpus is currently CLEAN, which is a result worth recording precisely because it is the state a future ingest can silently end. fault_knowledge carries the provenance machinery (source, ai_model, ai_confidence) and holds 3812 rows, of which 3812 are source='manual' and ZERO have an ai_model. So no AI-authored text is feeding the retrieval corpus today, and the AI6 risk - a model citing its own earlier output back as evidence - has no material to work with. ★THE SHAPE OF THAT CLEANLINESS MATTERS: `source` is NOT NULL on any row. Every row affirmatively CLAIMS 'manual' rather than merely lacking a marker, which is the difference between provenance that is known and provenance that is absent - a null would be indistinguishable from an unmarked AI write. knowledge_graph_facts, the other ingest target, is EMPTY (0 rows) but has the fuller column set (source_type, source_ref, created_by, confidence, superseded_by, active), so the structure is right and simply unexercised. The property therefore cannot be VERIFIED end to end yet - it can only be violated once something writes AI content - so what is banked is the measurement plus the fact that the columns which would reveal it exist and are populated affirmatively. Remaining: the only-AI/only-human filter (net-new UI) and re-measuring this the moment an AI ingest path goes live. || THE PROVENANCE COLUMNS ARE IN PLACE AND CORRECTLY EMPTY (2026-08-27). Enumerated every table carrying an AI-provenance column: fault_knowledge (source, ai_confidence, ai_model - the fullest, recording WHICH MODEL wrote a row), rcm_fmea_modes and rcm_strategies (source, ai_confidence), shift_plans (generated_by), plus a dozen tables with a plain source. Measured how full they are: fault_knowledge holds 3,812 rows, ALL source='manual', with ai_model set on ZERO and ai_confidence on zero; rcm_strategies 172 rows, ai_confidence on zero. ★THAT IS THE CORRECT STATE, NOT A WRITE-ONLY COLUMN: the columns are NULL because no AI has written to these corpora yet, which is exactly what NULL should mean. The distinction matters because a column that is always empty looks identical whether the writer is missing or the CASE is - and here it is the case, confirmed by every row declaring itself manual. The schema is ready for an AI ingest path that has not run. ★AND MY QUERY LIED FIRST, IN A NEW LANGUAGE: `column_name ILIKE '%ai_%'` returned domain, detail, failure_reason - because in SQL LIKE the UNDERSCORE IS A WILDCARD, so '%ai_%' means 'ai' followed by any character and matches dom-ai-n, det-ai-l, f-ai-lure. Escaping it ('ai\_%') gave the real list. Same class as this session's missing   in regex, one syntax over. Remaining: unchanged - the only-AI/only-human filter is net-new UI, and this measurement is the baseline to re-run the day an AI ingest path goes live. || ★A FAILING GATE WHOSE PAGE WAS ALREADY CORRECT - the instrument was the defect (2026-08-28). AI6's WRITE half is green and proven: validate_ai_write_provenance reports 6/6 = 100%%, every AI write into a human-read table declaring machine authorship on the row, and ai-draft-shows-its-basis passes too (AI-drafted failure modes record the cluster they came from and show it to the engineer being asked to approve them). ★THE RENDER half was reporting FAIL - '1 read that drops machine authorship', naming logbook.html and the fault-history panel, which is the panel a worker consults before opening a machine. Reading the page rather than trusting the gate: the DISPLAY read at logbook.html:3301 already selects source and ai_model, and carries a T87/AI6 comment from 2026-08-26 explaining why. What the gate had actually flagged was the COUNT query a few lines below - .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true }) - whose entire job is to say 'showing 10 of 47'. A head query ships NO ROWS and therefore cannot drop provenance. The exemption existed but only skipped queries with NO select list at all, and a count query does carry one. ★FIXED THE GATE, NOT THE PAGE: the exemption now also skips a select whose own arguments carry head:/count:, read through a PAREN-BALANCED helper rather than a character window - because a fixed window on a page that lists rows and then counts them would read the count's options object and exempt the DISPLAY read, the exact inverse of this gate's job. ★AND IT NOW HAS TEETH, which it had none of: a --selftest with 5 cases pins the head/count exemption, a provenance-less display read being CAUGHT, a provenance-carrying read passing, a post-mutation select being exempt, and the disclose-nowhere case being caught. All 5 green, and the live run is now PASS across 3 display reads. A gate whose only witness is the live tree cannot tell 'the page is wrong' from 'I am wrong about the page' - which is how this one spent its time accusing a fix that had already shipped. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate ai-render-provenance re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

The state machine is three-valued by CHECK constraint - pending_verification / verified / rejected - with per-state evidence on the row: created_at when filed, verified_at and verified_by when resolved, so 'who decided and when' is answerable. A first grep for a rejection path in founder-console found nothing and I was one step from recording 'a bad receipt has nowhere to go'. It does: svcTopupDecide writes `verify ? 'verified' : 'rejected'` - a TERNARY, which is why a keyword search for reject-near-topup missed it - behind a confirm whose button reads 'Verify and mint' or 'Reject', with a 0-row guard ('No change saved. Are you signed in as the platform admin?') and an honest success line, 'Rejected. No credits were minted.' ★AND THE SELF-DEAL GUARD IS PROPERLY TWO-SIDED: guard_service_topup_status blocks a party from deciding their own top-up in BOTH directions - the person who says they paid, and the account the credit would land in - with its own comment explaining that verifying someone else's top-up into your own provider account is self-minting too. Intake facts are immutable by migration. That is the admin-bypass-before-the-party-check lesson applied correctly. ★THE REAL GAP IS SMALLER AND IS ABOUT THE PAYER: the rejection writes STATUS ONLY. The table has a `note` column and the rejection does not fill it, so a payer reading their own row through v_service_credit_topups_truth sees 'rejected' with no reason - and the admin confirm text says outright that they will 'need to raise it with you directly'. The refusal reaches the right person and tells them nothing actionable, which is the why_refused bar this platform meets almost everywhere else. pct 60 -> 76. || ★FIXED: A REJECTION NOW CARRIES ITS REASON. The confirm used to end 'they will need to raise it with you directly' - an honest description of a gap rather than a design, since the update wrote STATUS ONLY and the row's `note` column sat empty. Rejecting now prompts through whPrompt, mirroring hive.html's approval-queue rejection almost word for word ('Tell them why, so they can fix it or send the right reference instead of guessing', with inputLabel 'Reason (the provider sees this)'), and writes the answer to `note`, capped at 500 chars. Verify keeps its plain confirm - a mint needs no excuse - and a blank reason writes nothing, because an empty note is not a reason. ★CHECKED THE GUARD BEFORE WRITING, and it mattered: guard_service_topup_status enforces that a top-up's INTAKE FACTS are immutable, so I confirmed the frozen set is account_type / account_id / payer_auth_uid / amount / gcash_ref - `note` and `status` are not among them. Had `note` been frozen, this change would have broken rejection outright rather than improving it. Proven live: a status+note update inside a transaction returned the row with both set, rolled back, and the table is unchanged (1 pending, 2 verified, 0 notes). ★AND THE GUARD IS WORTH RECORDING FOR ITS OWN SAKE: it blocks self-minting from BOTH sides, freezes the receipt so an admin cannot rewrite account_id while verifying (a real past defect - one statement credited the admin's own provider), and refuses to walk a DECIDED top-up back to pending, which had made a refused payment mintable in two steps. pct 76 -> 84. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - the GCash money-in loop is honest: payment-rails + payment-disclosure + money-trust-confirmed prove the top-up path discloses cost and the ledger balances. trajectories.title: Credits lifecycle comprehension
trajectories.basis: the user-facing ledger EXISTS: marketplace-seller renders v_service_credit_ledger_truth (entry_type/amount/note/created_at) with the null-amount em-dash honesty ('commission +P0' class fixed); balance = SUM(ledger) via provider_credit_balance; top-ups on platform-actions. Remaining: the UNIT stated at the boundary (the units_at_boundary debt), holds-vs-spends distinction on the glass, buyer-side wallet view, hand-checkable balance math (wave close). UNIT-AT-BOUNDARY LANDED 2026-08-26: the Credit wallet card now states the rule its peso sign silently assumed - 'WorkHive Credits - 1 credit = P1, fixed - spendable in WorkHive only, not withdrawable' (the migration-declared truth: 20260803000012 forbids a rate column). The units_at_boundary debt on this surface is paid. Remaining: holds-vs-spends distinction, buyer-side wallet view, hand-checkable balance math. || HAND-CHECKABLE BALANCE MATH MEASURED 2026-08-27, and it does NOT reconcile for a person-owned provider. Summed service_credit_ledger per account against the balance functions: two accounts matched exactly (340=340, 1000=1000) and one did not - provider 393af1b7 has two entries (commission -200, adjustment +200) summing to 0.00 while provider_credit_balance() returns 500.00. THAT IS NOT A MATH BUG: the function deliberately delegates to person_credit_balance when sp.auth_uid IS NOT NULL, and its own comment gives the reason - 'a person-owned provider shows the PERSON's balance, because that is what they can actually spend'. THE FINDING IS THE PAIRING. marketplace-seller renders the wallet from TWO different accounts at once: the balance from provider_credit_balance (:2113 - the PERSON's money for this shape) and the ledger list from v_service_credit_ledger_truth filtered `.eq('account_type','provider').eq('account_id', provId)` (:2131 - the PROVIDER's rows). So a seller who adds up the lines in front of them gets 0 while the headline says 500, with nothing on screen accounting for the difference - the exact failure this trajectory's remaining item names. The code even asserts the opposite in a comment at :2134 ('the BALANCE above it is SUM(ledger) over ALL rows via provider_credit_balance()'), which is true only for a hive-owned provider. NOT FIXED UNILATERALLY: the symmetric repair is to source the ledger from whichever account the balance reports, but this is a money surface where a previous session already warned that changing WHICH ACCOUNT a card reports is 'a second money defect in place of the first' (:2121), so the account-shape decision is Ian's. Still owed after this: holds-vs-spends on the glass, buyer-side wallet view. || ★THE ACCOUNT-SHAPE DECISION IS STILL IAN'S, BUT THE LIE IS FIXABLE WITHOUT IT (2026-08-27). Re-read the wallet card end to end. TWO REFINEMENTS to the finding above. (1) The misleading CLAIM lives in a code COMMENT, not on the glass: the comment at :2190 asserts 'the balance is SUM(ledger) over EVERY entry, via provider_credit_balance()', which is false for a person-owned provider - but the visible label is the neutral 'Credit activity' / 'Latest 3 entries'. So the page does not TELL the seller the lines add up to the headline; it simply places them together and lets the adjacency imply it. That is still the defect (a balance of P500 above entries summing to P0.00, with nothing accounting for the difference) but it is a SILENCE, not a false sentence - which matters, because silence can be cured by adding a sentence rather than by changing which account the card reports. (2) ★THE PAGE ALREADY FETCHES WHAT IT NEEDS TO DETECT THE CASE: seller_credit_balance(WORKER_NAME) is called at :2132 for the reserved figure, and it is PERSON-keyed. When its total equals the provider_credit_balance headline, the delegation has happened and the two panels are describing different accounts - detectable client-side, with data already in hand, no new query. So the interim repair is DISCLOSURE: when those coincide, name what the list is (this provider account's entries) beside a balance that is the person's spendable total. That is the platform's own state-the-basis pattern, it makes the arithmetic checkable again, and it does NOT pre-empt the account-shape question - which stays Ian's, exactly as the earlier session left it. PREPARED, not applied: marketplace-seller.html is a root page and a full board is mid-run. Remaining: apply that disclosure after the board, then Ian's account-shape decision. || THE DISCLOSURE IS IN, AND TEETH-PROVEN ON THE EXACT PROVIDER THE FINDING NAMES (2026-08-27). marketplace-seller now captures the PERSON's total from seller_credit_balance (which already returns TABLE(available, reserved, total) and was already being called for the reserved figure - no new query) purely to DETECT the delegation: when it equals the provider_credit_balance headline, the two panels are describing different accounts. In that case, and only that case, the card says: 'These are this seller account's entries. The balance above is your personal spendable total, so the two will not add up.' ★VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS with real accounts, not by reading the code. FIRES for Pablo Aguilar Mechanical Works (393af1b7, the provider this finding was written about): the card now reads 'P500.00 ... Credit activity: adjustment +P200 - commission P-200' followed by the explanation, so the arithmetic that could not close is now accounted for on the glass. STAYS SILENT for Bryan Garcia Home Services, whose balance is P0.00 with nothing to reconcile - a note on every wallet would be noise, and a card people stop reading is worse than one line shorter. Zero page errors in both walks. ★AND IT DOES NOT PRE-EMPT THE OPEN DECISION: which account the wallet SHOULD report is still Ian's, exactly as the earlier session left it - changing that silently would be the second money defect in place of the first. This only stops the page from implying an identity between two figures that are not the same thing. ★REACHING IT TOOK THREE PREMISE CHECKS: the wallet renders only for a service provider (the supervisor account is not one), only inside the Services tab (clicked, not called by hand), and only for the person-owned case - each of which produced an empty reading that could have been misread as a broken render. Remaining: Ian's account-shape decision, and the buyer-side wallet view. pct -> 100.

trajectories.note: ★THE CREDIT SURFACES ARE HONEST AND WERE UNGATED (2026-08-26). This trajectory asks whether a user can see every movement of their credits with the unit stated, and the answer is yes: the seller wallet renders the balance in ₱, states the peg outright ('WorkHive Credits · 1 credit = ₱1, fixed · spendable in WorkHive only'), shows a pending top-up as what you sent and that it is waiting on a human, and - the part worth protecting - renders an ABSENT amount as a gap rather than ₱0, because a filed ₱300 top-up once appeared as ₱0.00 and a ledger line of unknown value as '+₱0'. whFmtPeso holds that centrally (absent and non-finite give a gap; a real zero still prints ₱0), and the three ad-hoc '₱' + Number(x || 0) sites are all else-branches of a typeof-whFmtPeso fallback, unreachable while utils.js loads. Gate absent-money-is-not-zero asserts the centre AND the absence of a live bypass. Its own exemption logic needed FOUR delimiters before one was correct - each wrong one either exempted a real bypass or accused a legitimate fallback, and all four are recorded in the source. ★HOLDS-VS-SPENDS CLOSED, AND NOTHING HAD TO BE INVENTED (2026-08-27). Listing HOLDS credits: guard_listing_requires_reservation writes a credit_reservations row, sweep_listing_holding_fee eats into it monthly, release_reservation_on_delist gives it back - and this very page already says 'holds P50 in credits' at listing time. Held credits are not spendable. ★THE PLATFORM WAS ALREADY COMPUTING THE ANSWER: seller_credit_balance(worker_name) returns THREE numbers - available, reserved, total - with available = ledger balance MINUS everything held. The wallet called provider_credit_balance() instead, which returns the ledger sum alone, and labelled it the balance. So a seller with live listings was shown more than they could spend, on the same page that had just told them listing would hold some of it. That is not a missing feature - it is the glass reading the WRONG ONE of three numbers that were sitting there, the built-but-never-called shape with money in it. ★AND THE HEADLINE FIGURE WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE, which is the part I nearly got wrong. provider_credit_balance carries a distinction seller_credit_balance does not: a person-owned provider shows the PERSON's balance, a hive-owned one shows the HIVE's, and its own comment records why - 'two cards for one human showing different numbers is how this defect stayed invisible on screen'. seller_credit_balance is person-keyed, so swapping the call would have silently changed WHICH ACCOUNT a hive-owned card reports: fixing one money defect by introducing another. Only `reserved` is taken, and shown beside the total. It renders only when something IS held, because a 'reserved P0' on every wallet is noise and a card people stop reading is worse than a card one line shorter. ★MEASURED, not reasoned: credit_reservations is EMPTY on this stack, so the gate creates a 50-credit hold inside a transaction and rolls it back - available=-50, reserved=50, total=0, the split exact, 0 rows surviving. The probe row has to reference a real listing because the table enforces num_nonnulls(listing_id, request_id) = 1; the schema taught me its own invariant mid-probe. Gate held-credits-are-told, teeth: a single-balance wallet RED, fetching the split without showing it still RED, fetching AND naming it green. REMAINS: buyer-side wallet view, hand-checkable balance math (wave close). ★THE BUYER-SIDE GAP IS CONFIRMED WITH EVIDENCE, AND IT IS AN ASYMMETRY (2026-08-27). The buyer DOES have a balance and it is carefully built: marketplace calls my_credit_balance, an RPC that computes the total WHERE THE ROWS ARE rather than summing a capped client read - its own comment notes the tempting .limit 'would have produced a quietly WRONG balance for exactly the users holding the most rows' - and the spend cap comes from service_request_price, 'the SAME function guard_reward_spend_cap asks, never a second derivation', with the earn figure from listing_reservation_amount(), the same function that sized the provider's hold 'so what the buyer is promised and what the provider reserved are one number by construction'. That is single-sourcing done properly. ★WHAT THE BUYER CANNOT DO IS CHECK IT. v_service_credit_ledger_truth is read by founder-console, marketplace-seller and platform-actions - the seller and admin surfaces - and by NO consumer surface, while the ledger genuinely holds consumer rows. So the seller gets a movements strip beside their balance and the buyer gets a number with no history: the same money, two roles, and only one of them can audit it. T47's bar is that a figure is verifiable when the glass alone suffices to recompute it, and for the buyer it does not. ★THE FIX IS A SURFACE, not a query - the view exists, the rows exist, and the seller-side strip (now labelled with whether it is showing everything) is the shape to copy - which is why this is recorded with its evidence rather than half-built at the tail of a session: the next pass starts from where it goes, not from whether it is missing.

trajectories.title: Listing price change on a watched item (buyer notifications)
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25, premise-first): watching IS a bookmark, not a subscription - marketplace_watchlist is written/read ONLY by marketplace.html (heart toggle, My Watchlist sheet, dead-listing cleanup); NO fn or notify lane consumes it, and no price-change/stock notification exists (the spec predicted 'watch-notify may be net-new'). The existing copy is HONEST everywhere ('Save to watchlist', 'track listings you care about' - nothing promises alerts). FIXED + VERIFIED: the watch-semantics statement added to the sheet header ('Your saved listings, synced to your account. Check back for price or stock changes - WorkHive doesn't send watchlist alerts yet.') - proven rendering with the sheet open; the comment binds it to be updated the day a notify lane ships. THE SCOPED DECISION recorded for Ian: a watch-notify lane (price/stock deltas -> the T105/T107 notification stack) - demand evidence = watchlist row counts. Remaining: price-history honesty on listings (anti fake-discount DP probe), unwatch friction check, the semantics statement joined to the claim-honesty lint (wave close). REMAINING PROBES RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-08-26: (1) fake-discount DP probe = N/A BY SHAPE, verified not assumed - marketplace_listings has ONE price column (no was-price/original_price/history table) and no strikethrough or comparison rendering exists anywhere on the page, so the dark pattern has no vector to ride; (2) unwatch friction = symmetric, one tap each way (toggleWatchlist deletes on the saved branch, scoped worker+listing); (3) the watch-semantics statement is on the glass ('WorkHive doesn't send watchlist alerts yet') with a same-change update note. Scoped-new idea recorded, not built: a price/stock-change digest on the watchlist would need a price-history table (schema decision for Ian). || PRICE-HISTORY HONESTY / ANTI FAKE-DISCOUNT — MEASURED 2026-08-27, and the dark pattern is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE here, which is a stronger answer than 'we checked and it looks fine'. The fake-discount DP needs an ANCHOR: a 'was' price to strike through so the current one reads as a saving. marketplace_listings has exactly ONE price column - `price` - and the schema contains no old_price, previous_price, compare_at_price or original_price on any table, and no price-history table at all. So there is nothing to anchor against and nothing to inflate. Confirmed on the glass too: no line-through, strikethrough, 'was', '% off' or slashed-price rendering exists in marketplace.html or marketplace-seller.html. ★THE THREE 'DISCOUNT' MATCHES ARE A REAL MECHANISM, NOT A DP, and the distinction is the point: they belong to service VOUCHERS, where the buyer pays a reduced amount and 'the provider gets the discount reimbursed as credits' - the platform funds it, so the saving is genuine money rather than a struck-through number nobody ever charged. Grepping for 'discount' and stopping at the count would have flagged an honest feature as a dark pattern. Remaining: unwatch friction and whether watching a listing PROMISES anything (the watch-semantics statement). || THE OTHER TWO AXES CLOSED 2026-08-27. WATCH SEMANTICS: the statement exists, is user-facing, and is honest in BOTH languages - 'Your saved listings, synced to your account. Check back for price or stock changes - WorkHive doesn't send watchlist alerts yet.' / 'Balikan para sa pagbabago ng presyo o stock - hindi pa nagpapadala ng watchlist alerts ang WorkHive.' It is backed by the schema: marketplace_watchlist is (id, worker_name, listing_id, created_at) with no notification machinery, so watching IS a saved list and the copy says exactly that instead of letting someone wait for a price-drop ping that will never come. Its source comment carries the maintenance rule too - 'Becomes false the day a notify lane ships - update it in the SAME change.' UNWATCH FRICTION: none, and symmetrically so - toggleWatchlist is ONE function where `isSaved` decides delete-or-add, driven by the same heart control, optimistic either way, with no confirmation on the way out. The classic dark pattern is making opt-out cost more than opt-in; here they are literally the same code path. Worth noting the anon case too: a tap before sign-in is STASHED as intent and replayed after auth, so the crossing does not silently eat the action. Remaining: nothing owed beyond the wave-close re-earn - price-anchor impossibility, watch semantics and unwatch symmetry are all measured. || ★LOCKED 2026-08-31: the wave-close re-earn landed and every gate this row names read PASS on a FULL board (watchlist-says-what-it-does). That was the only item its basis still owed. pct 92 -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★'DOES WATCHING DO ANYTHING' IS ANSWERED, AND HONESTLY (2026-08-26). It does not: no edge function or cron consumes marketplace_watchlist, so the star is a bookmark - and marketplace.html SAYS SO, in words, 'WorkHive doesn't send watchlist alerts yet.' That is the right handling of an unbuilt capability, and the risk is drift rather than a present defect, so the gate is a two-way PARITY check: the disclosure must stay while there is no sender, and must GO once one appears, because a stale disclaimer under a working feature teaches people to ignore the one place the product tells them the truth. A consumer means a function or cron, not the page reading its own list to draw stars. Teeth proven in both directions. STILL OPEN as a product question, unchanged: whether watch-notify should be built at all is Ian's call - this only guarantees the promise matches the reality.

trajectories.title: Order/inquiry lifecycle: buyer and seller converge
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, two contexts: bryan buyer 390 + davidvelasco seller 390): the INQUIRY HOP proven end-to-end - the ?listing= deep link opens the detail sheet cold, the inquiry form's guards are honest ('All fields are required.' + the anti-spoof 'Send this under your WorkHive name' identity check), the buyer gets a receipt WITH the expectation set ('Inquiry sent! Seller responds within 48 hours'), and the seller's inbox shows the same object (buyer name, 'Re: <listing>', message, volunteered contact, Send Reply / Mark Replied / Close controls) - DB row 'pending' naming both parties; probe row cleaned. The CONTACT-EXCHANGE boundary is by-design explicit (the buyer volunteers contact in a labeled field at inquiry time). INSTRUMENT NOTE: the first run under-filled the form and the honest refusal toast expired before the read - a probe must fill every required field before accusing the pipeline. Remaining: the REPLY hop back to the buyer (where does the buyer read replies?), the goods lifecycle states beyond inquiry (agreement/handover/confirm two-sided), non-response timeout honesty (wave close). THE REPLY HOP BUILT 2026-08-26 - a real SILENT-WORK defect closed: sellers answer into marketplace_inquiries.reply_text/replied_at (their console writes it; mkt_inq_read lets the BUYER read their own rows) but NO buyer surface ever read those columns - an answered inquiry looked identical to an ignored one, so the seller believed they replied while the buyer saw nothing. FIXED: marketplace now renders 'Replies to your inquiries' (truth-view read, bounded 10 newest with a total order, silence-is-golden when empty, deep link back to the listing). Live-proven as the buyer on a staged replied inquiry, probe row cleaned. Remaining: goods lifecycle states beyond inquiry (agreement/handover/confirm two-sided), non-response timeout honesty. || THE GOODS LIFECYCLE IS FULLY DEFINED IN THE SCHEMA AND HAS NEVER BEEN EXERCISED (2026-08-27). marketplace_orders carries a CHECK constraint enumerating six states - pending_payment, escrow_hold, buyer_confirmed, released, refunded, disputed - which is a genuine escrow flow with both a happy path (pay -> hold -> buyer confirms -> funds released) and its two exits (refund, dispute), and it answers T96's 'do both sides see the same states' question at the schema level: there is ONE status column, so buyer and seller cannot be looking at different vocabularies for the same order. ★BUT THERE ARE ZERO ORDERS, AND NOTHING CAN MAKE ONE: marketplace_orders appears in exactly one place in the seeder tree - reset.py's TRUNCATE list - so the fixture layer knows how to DELETE orders and has never known how to create one. The lifecycle is therefore unproven end to end: no state transition on this table has ever been walked, and 'the constraint allows it' is not 'the product does it'. This is the build-the-structure case rather than a ceiling - the move is to write the order fixture (a seeded order per state, then a two-context walk asserting buyer and seller read the same state at each step, plus the non-response timeout). SEQUENCED, NOT DEFERRED: writing rows into a table while a full board is mid-run is the data twin of mutating schema under a running gate, and this session has already voided one board that way, so the fixture lands once the board clears. Remaining: build that order fixture, then the two-sided state-agreement walk and non-response timeout honesty. || THE FIXTURE IS BUILT, WIRED AND RUN - THE GOODS LIFECYCLE IS WALKABLE FOR THE FIRST TIME (2026-08-27). Rather than write a new one-off script, extended the EXISTING test-data-seeder/seeders/marketplace.py with seed_marketplace_orders(client, log, ctx) in the same shape as its siblings, and wired it into orchestrator.py right after seed_marketplace_sellers - a seeder nothing calls would have been the same built-but-never-called trap this session found in apply_dispute_adjustment. RUN FOR REAL against the local stack: 6 rows, one per state, verified in psql - pending_payment, escrow_hold, buyer_confirmed, released, refunded, disputed, with real buyers, sellers and prices taken from seeded listings. ★THE ROWS ARE INTERNALLY CONSISTENT, WHICH IS THE PART A FIXTURE USUALLY GETS WRONG: a released order carries BOTH buyer_confirmed_at and released_at; buyer_confirmed carries only the first; pending, escrow and disputed carry neither; refunded carries a confirmation because it was confirmed before it was refunded. A fixture that contradicts its own schema teaches a walker the wrong thing about the product, and every later assertion inherits the lie. ★AND ONE PER STATE RATHER THAN A RANDOM SPREAD, deliberately: the two-sided walk needs to FIND a buyer_confirmed order to look at, not hope one was rolled. Remaining: the two-sided state-agreement walk itself (buyer and seller reading the same state at each step) and non-response timeout honesty - both now unblocked. || ★I SEEDED THE WRONG TABLE FIRST, AND FINDING OUT WHY IS THE REAL RESULT (2026-08-27). marketplace_orders looked like the goods lifecycle - a full escrow flow in a CHECK constraint - so I built its fixture. Then I checked who READS it: exactly one page, marketplace-admin, which is RETIRED behind an overlay. The live goods path is contact-only, stated plainly in the seeder's own docstring ('contact-only flow per current launch plan'): a buyer sends an INQUIRY against a listing, the seller replies, contact details are exchanged and the deal completes off platform. marketplace-seller reads v_marketplace_inquiries_truth in SIX places and never reads orders at all. So marketplace_orders is a FUTURE escrow model, not a gap - and 'the schema describes it' was never evidence that the product does it. The orders fixture is kept (the table is now walkable if that model is ever switched on, and its rows are state-consistent) but it is NOT the current flow. ★THEN BUILT THE ONE THAT MATTERS: seed_marketplace_inquiries, six rows across pending / replied / closed, wired into the orchestrator beside its sibling. Replied and closed rows carry BOTH reply_text and replied_at, since a reply with no timestamp is a state the UI cannot render honestly. ★WALKED IT LIVE as a seller and the two-sided view works: the Inquiries tab names the buyer, shows the message and the state, and the 'New Inquiries' tile reads 0 for Bryan Garcia - which is CORRECT, because his two inquiries are replied and closed, not pending. A count that could have looked like a bug is the page being precise about what 'new' means. Zero page errors. Remaining: the buyer-side view of the same thread (does the asker see the reply), and non-response timeout honesty. || ★THE BUYER CANNOT SEE THEIR OWN UNANSWERED QUESTION - PROVEN WITH TWO ACCOUNTS (2026-08-27). The buyer lane exists: marketplace.html's loadMyInquiryReplies() reads v_marketplace_inquiries_truth filtered .eq('buyer_name', WORKER_NAME) into #mk-my-replies. But it also filters .not('reply_text','is',null) - it renders ONLY inquiries a seller has already answered - and returns early when that comes back empty. MEASURED with two real signed-in buyers against the seeded threads: Romeo Beltran, whose inquiry was REPLIED, sees his thread and the counterparty; Pablo Aguilar, whose inquiry is PENDING, sees NOTHING - no message, no state, no acknowledgement that he ever asked. Same page, same code, opposite experience, decided entirely by whether the other party has gotten round to it. ★THAT IS WORSE THAN A TIMEOUT PROBLEM, which is how this trajectory's remaining item framed it. A late reply is a wait; an invisible SENT MESSAGE is indistinguishable from one that never sent - the buyer cannot tell whether to follow up, re-ask on another listing, or give up, and the platform holds the answer the whole time. It is the same shape as this session's other findings where a SILENCE does the lying: the record exists, the reader is simply not shown it. ★THE FIX IS SMALL AND THE SECTION'S NAME IS THE ONLY REAL QUESTION: dropping the reply_text filter and rendering a state ('Waiting for a reply - sent 3 days ago') would show the whole thread, but #mk-my-replies is literally 'my replies', so including unanswered asks changes what that section IS. Recorded rather than redesigned unilaterally: the evidence is unambiguous, the shape of the fix is known, and what the section should be called is Ian's call. Remaining: that decision, then the pending-state render. || FIXED AND PROVEN ON BOTH SIDES (2026-08-27). Dropped the .not('reply_text','is',null) filter so the buyer's panel carries EVERY inquiry they sent, re-ordered by created_at (the newest ask leads whether or not it has been answered - replied_at is NULL for pending and does not sort usefully), renamed the heading from 'Replies to your inquiries' to 'Your inquiries', and gave the unanswered rows their own line: 'Sent to <seller> <date> - waiting for a reply'. The date is not decoration; the buyer's actual question is HOW LONG it has been, and 'waiting' with no date is the same silence one step quieter. VERIFIED with the two accounts that produced the finding: Pablo Aguilar, who saw NOTHING before, now reads 'YOUR INQUIRIES - 1 | You asked: What's the hour meter reading... | Sent to Leandro Marquez Aug 19, 2026 - waiting for a reply'; Romeo Beltran's replied thread renders exactly as before. Zero page errors on either. ★AND THE 'NAMING DECISION' I NEARLY DEFERRED ON WAS NOT A FORK. I recorded this as needing Ian because including unanswered asks changes what the section IS - but mk-my-replies is an internal id, the only user-visible string was one heading, and 'Your inquiries' is strictly more accurate than 'Replies to your inquiries' for a panel that now shows both. A label is not a product decision when the alternative is a buyer who cannot see their own sent message. That is the manufactured-fork shape: naming something Ian's to make deferring it feel principled. trajectories.title: Seller reputation earned over N sales (longitudinal)
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25): tier MECHANICS verified at the SSOT (mig ...065 unified the two divergent definitions): tier = DISTINCT COUNTERPARTIES across sold listings (identity prefers auth uid -> normalised contact -> name, so one buyer phone written three ways counts once), thresholds are per-hive knobs (platform defaults Silver 11 / Gold 51). THE FINDING, fixed + verified: progression was ILLEGIBLE - the chip named the tier but never what advances it, so a seller could not plan toward Silver. The dashboard now reads the REAL per-hive knobs via db.rpc('service_knob') (never hardcoded - a hive can adjust its ladder) and renders 'Silver at 11 sales to distinct buyers (Silver 11 - Gold 51)' under the chip, best-effort, only when both reads land; proven live as davidvelasco (bronze). Remaining: the longitudinal N-sales walk (seeded sales fixture - per-sale reputation events visible, tier flip moment, proportionate bad-outcome effects), tier-benefit ENFORCEMENT oracle (what does Silver actually unlock - claims <-> gates), T70's trust-claim parity (wave close). || ★THE 'completed_sales' CLAIM IS ENFORCED — checked because the day's other findings came from columns whose NAME was a claim the query did not keep (2026-08-28). v_marketplace_listings_truth exposes `completed_sales`, which is not computed there at all: it is COALESCE(ms.total_sales, 0) — the seller row's column, RENAMED. A rename is exactly where a claim can outrun its data, so the maintainer was traced: recompute_seller_sales_and_tier derives it as COUNT(DISTINCT counterparty) over marketplace_listings WHERE status = 'sold'. The claim holds — a sale must be SOLD to count. Better than required, in fact: it counts distinct COUNTERPARTIES rather than rows, with an identity fallback chain (buyer auth uid, then a normalised contact, then the typed name) so one buyer written three ways is one sale, and a sold listing with no linked inquiry still counts once under its own id rather than being silently dropped. v_project_truth.approved_change_orders was checked in the same pass and filters status='approved' correctly. ★RECORDED AS A NEGATIVE ON PURPOSE: this is the same shape as the PM 'pm_completed_count' defect found today, and the same shape as the certification chip that once rendered on a flag with no certifications behind it. Two of those turned out real and these two did not; an unrecorded check is indistinguishable from one never run, and the next session should not have to re-derive that this one is clean. || ★REPUTATION IS EARNED, NOT SETTABLE - enforced in the database, not in the UI (2026-08-28). trajectories.title: Marketplace search & discovery quality
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25, worker 390, six-query gauntlet vs the seeded catalog): case-insensitivity VERIFIED ('BeArInG' = 'bearing' = 6 cards); zero-state honesty VERIFIED (names its scope 'in parts for your filter' + remedies); true-miss behavior correct ('6205' with only 6313 in stock -> honest zero). THE FINDING, fixed + verified: a one-letter typo ('berring') silently missed in-stock bearings - no fuzzy tolerance, a lost sale. FIX: a client-side did-you-mean on the zero-match verdict (edit-distance<=2 against a PERSISTENT title-word vocabulary accumulated at every non-empty load - the first cut read _listings, which holds the post-filter view and is EMPTY exactly when the suggester runs; caught live, root-caused, re-wired via window._mkTitleWords). Proven: 'berring' -> 'No exact matches... did you mean "bearing"?'. marketplace.html is SW-shelled - covered by this release's v239 bump. Remaining: alternatives on true product misses (nearby category / hail-a-service door - the X1 probe), saved-search re-run semantics (T95 seam), filter-combo usability at 390, part-number format variants ('6313-C3' vs '6313 C3') (wave close). ALTERNATIVES + A CONFLATION FIX 2026-08-26: (1) a TRUE miss now offers real next moves, CHECKED not asserted - the same query counted live in the other sections ('Nothing in parts matches "Refresher", but 1 in training does - switch section tab') and, when nothing matches anywhere, the services door ('Nobody is selling it right now - you can hail a service provider instead, or post a wanted listing'). Both live-proven through the real search box. (2) FOUND+FIXED a conflation the did-you-mean work exposed: the verdict card's first-run branch keyed on `mine === 0`, so a BUYER searching a 9-listing section was told 'No parts listings yet - be the first to post'. The GRID had learned the _filterActive discriminator in an earlier arc and the VERDICT never did - one page, one path fixed (fix-EVERY-path class). Remaining: saved-search re-run semantics, filter-combo usability at 390, part-number format variants. || ★ZERO-RESULTS HONESTY IS ALREADY RIGHT, AND THE BUG IT REPLACED WAS A GOOD ONE (2026-08-28). A filtered-zero on marketplace used to render the first-run 'be the first to sell' CTA - which told a BUYER, on a marketplace that demonstrably has listings, that it was empty and invited them to become a seller. That is the empty-versus-filtered confusion with about the worst possible outcome: the person came to source a part and left believing there was nothing to source. Fixed, with the reasoning written into the source: _listings is SERVER-filtered, so a zero with a search or category active means 'nothing matched', and _filterActive now distinguishes the two states explicitly. The distinction this trajectory cares most about is made, and made for a stated reason. ★THE REMAINING GAP IS SMALL AND NAMED: the no-match message is a sentence without an ACTION. 'No listings match those filters.' tells a buyer what happened and leaves them to work out that they should widen the search themselves - no clear-filters control, no nearby-category suggestion, no 'hail a service instead' hop. For a buyer with a part number that nobody stocks, that sentence is the last thing they read. ★NOT BUILT, and the reason is specific rather than cautious-in-general: there is no clearFilters function and no single filter-state object - the filters are chips (#filter-chips) plus a _query and a _cat variable read at load time - so a clear-filters control means reconstructing that state machine's reset path, which is real work on a page I have not read end to end. trajectories.note: ★A COMMA IN THE SEARCH BOX RETURNED HTTP 400 (2026-08-26, measured live). PostgREST splits or=(a,b) on top-level commas, so an unquoted comma inside a value rejected the whole filter - and 'Bearing, spherical roller, 22320 E1 XL C3, SKF' is simply how a part is named, the platform's own example elsewhere. Four sites escaped the LIKE wildcards % and _ and left the DELIMITERS alone: the logbook feed, the logbook EXPORT, community's feed and the global search overlay. marketplace was the exception - it strips them - which is why the same phrase worked there and nowhere else. The page renders the 400 as a failed READ, so a legitimate search looked like an outage. Fixed centrally with utils.whSafeSearchTerm (delimiters removed, wildcards escaped) at all four sites; verified end to end, the same read now returns 200 with an empty array. Gate search-term-survives-punctuation, teeth proven on both clauses. ★AND THE AI'S OWN RETRIEVAL HAD IT, SILENTLY (2026-08-26). agentic-rag-loop's logbook lane sanitised the user's natural-language QUESTION for LIKE wildcards but not for the PostgREST or() delimiters - and commas in a question are the common case, not an edge case. Worse, it read the result as `const { data: logs } = await q`, discarding the error; supabase-js RETURNS {data:null,error} instead of throwing, so the 400 never reached the catch and became an ordinary empty result. The AI simply answered with less grounding and nothing said why. visual-defect-capture passed an asset TAG into an .or() with no escaping at all. Both fixed (delimiters stripped, wildcards escaped, the error logged rather than discarded) and covered by search-term-survives-punctuation, which now also fails the `const { data } = await q` shape that makes such a failure invisible. NOTE the sanitiser's comment cited the data-engineer skill: the author followed it correctly and the SKILL was incomplete - it covered wildcards, not delimiters. NEEDS A DEPLOY (Ian's gate): both are edge functions. ★PART-NUMBER FORMAT VARIANTS, MEASURED (2026-08-27): the search is exact about spacing and punctuation, and a buyer who types the number the way it is PRINTED ON THE BOX finds nothing. Driven against the real catalogue with the same ILIKE the page uses: '6313 C3' -> 3 hits, '6313C3' -> 0, '6313-C3' -> 0; 'ACS580' -> 1, 'ACS-580' -> 0, 'acs 580' -> 0; 'GA75' -> 3, 'GA-75' -> 0. Every variant a person would plausibly type is a dead end. ★AND A ZERO-RESULT SEARCH IS THE WORST FALSE NEGATIVE A MARKETPLACE CAN PRODUCE, because it does not read as 'your spelling missed' - it reads as 'they do not have it', and the buyer leaves. The listing exists, the seller waits, and neither side ever learns why. ★THE FIX IS NOT CLIENT-SIDE, which is why this is recorded rather than shipped at the tail of a long turn: the client builds a PostgREST .or() filter, and PostgREST cannot apply an expression like regexp_replace(title,'[^a-z0-9]','') in a filter. Matching a normalised term needs DB-side support - a generated normalised column with an index (cheapest, keeps ILIKE), or a search RPC. That is a schema change with an index decision behind it, so it is Ian's call rather than a quiet addition. The measurement above is the evidence for making it: this is not a hypothetical tolerance nicety, it is eight typed strings of which five return nothing against listings that are sitting there.

trajectories.title: Listing quality & the AI assist
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, davidvelasco 390, one live assist invocation): the AI assist VERIFIED-GOOD - it names its own inputs ('drafts a category and description from your title, part number, and photo'), and from the bare title 'bearing 6205 skf new' produced a BOUNDED 173-char description with zero invented specs (no fabricated dimensions/load ratings/brands - everything derivable from the title; the T84 invention-guard bar holds on this sample), with an AI-drafted/review marker present (AI6). The composer carries the 10%-hold cost truth (T34) and a character counter (T130). THE GAP recorded: NO preview-as-buyer affordance exists on the composer (the J3 preview bar + the spec's draft-preview==published-render parity check) - a scoped enhancement. Remaining: photo-grounded assist probe (does a photo change the draft honestly), quality feedback ('what's missing for a GOOD listing'), the preview decision, photo ergonomics at 390 (T9's bar) (wave close).  || THE RECORDED GAP IS CLOSED 2026-08-26: the composer now has a PREVIEW AS BUYER control. Posting is a commitment - it spends a credit hold, it goes to moderation, and it is the first thing a stranger judges the seller by - so J3's preview-before-irreversible bar applies. The preview reads the SAME inputs the insert reads, so it cannot show a seller one thing and publish another, and it renders in the BUYER's vocabulary: a blank price reads 'Negotiable' and a filled one goes through whFmtPeso, which is how a buyer actually sees money. It says plainly that nothing has been posted, because a preview that looks like a confirmation is worse than none. ★THE FIX FAILED TWICE, SILENTLY, AND BOTH FAILURES LOADED WITH ZERO CONSOLE ERRORS. First: the handler called getElementById at script-parse time and returned early because the composer was not in the DOM yet - the button rendered perfectly and did nothing, the declared-but-never-wired class. Second: rewritten as a delegated listener, it was inserted INSIDE the submit handler's function body, so it only registered once a seller pressed Post - the one moment a preview is useless. A live CLICK found both; a source check or a page-load error check would have been green through each. That is why the gate clicks rather than greps. LOCKED BY gate listing-preview (4 behavioural assertions), resurrection RED both ways - with no control at all, and with the listener deliberately un-wired. Remaining: photo ergonomics at 390 (the T9 photo bar) and the draft-quality feedback the spec asks for. || THE INVENTION GUARD IS REAL, AND IT IS TWO DIFFERENT KINDS OF GUARD (2026-08-27). The listing assist's risk is a model that writes confident specifications a photo cannot support - '5,000 hours', 'fits Grundfos CR 95-3', 'CE certified' - which on a used-parts marketplace is not a bad sentence but a false claim a buyer may act on. TWO LAYERS, and the distinction matters. INSTRUCTIONAL for prose: the system prompt says 'NEVER invent specifications, dimensions, model compatibility, running hours, warranty, or certifications', which is the only kind of guard a free-text description can have. STRUCTURAL for enumerations: the category, urgency and mode the model returns are validated server-side AFTER the call - cats.includes(String(out.category)) ? ... : null - so an off-list value does not become a warning or a best guess, it becomes null. The model cannot widen the taxonomy no matter what it emits. ★THAT SPLIT IS THE RIGHT ARCHITECTURE rather than an inconsistency: you can whitelist an enum and you cannot whitelist a sentence, so the enum gets enforcement and the prose gets instruction plus human review before publish. Worth stating explicitly because 'the AI is guarded' otherwise reads as one uniform claim, when half of it is a promise and half of it is a mechanism. Remaining: photo ergonomics at 390 (the T9 photo bar) and the draft-quality feedback the spec asks for. || ★THE ONE GAP THIS TRAJECTORY FOUND IS CLOSED AND GATED LIVE (2026-08-28). The walk had already cleared the AI half - the listing assist names its own inputs and invented no specs from a bare title, which is the invention guard T84 asks of every AI-drafting surface. The single recorded gap was that a seller could not see their listing AS A BUYER WILL before publishing, and publishing is not a soft action here: it spends a credit hold and puts the listing in front of other plants. validate_listing_preview now passes live on six assertions - opens, showsTheDraft, blankPriceIsNegotiable, pricedViaHelper, closes, and zero page errors - with the verdict 'a seller can see the listing as a buyer will, before it becomes a commitment.' ★TWO OF THOSE ASSERTIONS ARE THE INTERESTING ONES. blankPriceIsNegotiable means a seller who leaves the price empty sees 'Negotiable' in the preview rather than ₱0 - the absent-is-not-zero discipline (T133) carried into the one screen where a wrong zero would be read by a BUYER as an offer. And pricedViaHelper means the preview renders money through whFmtPeso rather than its own formatter, so the preview cannot drift from what the marketplace will actually show. A preview that formats differently from the real thing is worse than no preview, because it is confidently wrong at the moment of commitment. pct 72 -> 90. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25, worker 390): the safety POSTURE verified honest - trust chips per seller (ID-verified, listing counts, 'new seller'), NO false protection claims anywhere, and the MK8 'Before you pay' education (RA 11967-grounded: inspect first, meet at a business address, avoid paying in full up front, 'WorkHive never holds your payment, so we cannot reverse it') sits at the INQUIRY step - exactly where the money risk lives (my first probe read the detail sheet and missed it - the education is one step deeper, correctly placed). THE GAP, fixed + verified: NO report door existed from the listing detail; a dedicated report lane needs new schema (recorded scoped decision - no report/flag table exists for listings), so the zero-schema door is wired: 'Something wrong with this listing? Report it' on every detail sheet opens the platform feedback panel with the listing title+id prefilled into the subject (proven live: panel open, subject 'Report listing: New (boxed) Pressure Transmitter... (5f07...)'). Remaining: the dedicated report lane decision (schema + moderation queue + author notice - T24's shape), fraud-signal surfacing (marketplace_fraud_signals computed but not shown at decision points), first-contact safety note timing probe (wave close). SIGNALS SURFACED + A STALE BASIS CORRECTED 2026-08-26: the remaining line claimed 'marketplace_fraud_signals computed but not shown' - VERIFIED FALSE, no such table exists on this platform (nor any fraud/*signal* relation beyond anomaly_signals for assets). The signals that DO exist are in v_marketplace_sellers_truth, and they were absent exactly where money risk lives: the safety note warned about 'a new seller' with no way to tell whether THIS one is new. FIXED: the inquiry composer now states this seller's standing, query-backed - live-proven 'This seller is new here: no completed sales yet - on WorkHive since 2026 - not ID-verified.' Payment-protection honesty was already correct (contact-only, no escrow, 'WorkHive never holds your payment'). Remaining: the dedicated report lane decision (schema + queue + author notice, T24's shape - scoped product decision). || ★THE PROTECTION STORY IS TOLD HONESTLY, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE USUAL FAILURE (2026-08-28). Most marketplaces imply a safety net they do not provide. This one states the absence in plain words, repeatedly and in its own source: 'This is a CONTACT-ONLY marketplace with no escrow, so 100%% of the money risk' sits with the parties; 'free + contact-only, so there is no checkout/payment'; 'no fees, no payments'. A buyer cannot come away believing WorkHive stands behind the transaction, because nothing says it does. ★AND THE TRUST CHIPS WERE WORDED NOT TO OVERREACH: a comment records that a label 'says where to look rather than implying a guarantee' - somebody consciously chose phrasing that points at evidence instead of promising an outcome, which is the same discipline the ID-verified chip lesson taught the hard way. ★THE BEST PART IS A DISTINCTION MOST PRODUCTS NEVER MAKE. The source says of the moment a buyer goes off-platform: 'Saying "payment is off-platform" states the fact but does not WARN.' Someone noticed that a factual sentence and a protective one are different things, at the exact step where a person is about to take a stranger's word for money, and rewrote toward the second. That is the buyer-safety bar this trajectory is asking for, met deliberately rather than by accident. A report path exists alongside it. ★NOT VERIFIED: whether computed fraud signals (marketplace_fraud_signals) are SURFACED at the decision point rather than only collected for admins - the 'show buyers what the platform already knows' half. pct 75 -> 88. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate marketplace-warns-before-payment re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★THE BUYER-SAFETY WORK IS DONE AND WAS UNGATED (2026-08-27). This trajectory's core probe - is the payment-protection story told honestly - is answered on the page: a 'Before you pay' warning at the decision point (inspect the item, meet at a business address or public place, avoid paying in full up front to a new seller) and the sentence that matters most, 'WorkHive never holds your payment, so we cannot reverse it', harvested from RA 11967's consumer-education requirement. The report door was added 2026-08-25 through the existing feedback intake, since a dedicated lane needs schema. Nothing was broken; nothing protected it. Gate marketplace-warns-before-payment asserts the warning AND the absence of any escrow / buyer-protection / money-back promise, because the opposite failure is worse than silence - a buyer who believes there is protection behaves as though a loss is recoverable. It also holds the credits-are-spend-only sentence and the trust bar's 'badge per seller' wording, both of which the page already got right for recorded reasons.

trajectories.title: Service provider availability honesty (supply side)
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, davidvelasco 390, Services tab): the availability control VERIFIED well-built - a real role='switch' with aria-checked, honest state labels ('Online: receiving jobs' / 'Offline: go Online'), svcRequireOnline guard, 0-row-update detection with an honest refusal ('Couldn't change availability - refresh and try again'), and updated_at stamped for the reconcile lag. All 7 service providers read availability='online' and NONE sits on_job - the symptom that once stranded 43% of supply is absent. ★BUT 'EVERYONE IS ONLINE' IS EXACTLY WHAT A WRITE-ONCE TOGGLE LOOKS LIKE FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION, so the number alone proves nothing: a field that never changes and a field that is correctly at rest are indistinguishable until you check what it SHOULD say. Availability is not a field somebody remembers to update - it is driven end to end: accept_service_request sets it when a job is taken, sync_provider_availability keeps it in step, guard_service_provider_writes stops a client writing it directly, and reconcile_provider_availability is the safety net that fixed the write-once stranding. ★THE RECONCILER IS CORRECT AND SAYS WHY IT EXISTS: it frees every provider sitting on_job with no request in accepted/en_route/on_site/in_progress, and its comment names the human cost rather than the mechanic - 'drift here means a provider who cannot be found and does not know why'. It returns the count freed, so the repair is observable instead of silent, and it is SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path. ★SO THE RESTING STATE IS EXPLAINED RATHER THAN LUCKY: 7 providers online, 0 on_job, 0 active requests - the reconciler would free any drift, and there is none to free. The 43%-stranded class cannot silently return, because the condition that produced it is now swept by a scheduled function whose whole job is to disbelieve the flag. Remaining: a seeded active request to walk the transition live (accept -> on_job -> settle -> online), and the area-coverage editing walk. pct -> 84. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - provider availability is function-driven (accept sets it, sync keeps it) - supply cannot silently vanish write-once; new teeth-tested gate provider-availability-driven (live PASS). pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Pricing transparency across the economy
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, commit-point read sweep): every economic commit point STATES its cost at the moment of commitment, in ONE vocabulary - listing publish ('No fees are charged on sales... Publishing holds 10% of your asking price in credits; the hold is returned if you remove the listing, and it funds your reward when it sells'), inquiries free-and-stated ('buyers contact you directly'), the service hail ('You pay the provider directly on completion... When the job settles you get 10% of it in credits back, and you can spend credits on a job OR earn them on it, never both' - deliberately the same 'credits back' wording as the parts chip, per its own comment), and the top-up surface states the unit ('1 credit = P1'). No fix needed at this bar. Remaining: the consolidated fees-summary surface decision (scoped - none exists), the fee-parity oracle (stated <-> charged, psql-checked), price-change notice policy, the standing admin-price decision (T67, Ian) (wave close). FEE-PARITY ORACLE BUILT + REGISTERED 2026-08-26 (gate fee-parity): the stated fee and the charged fee are wired INDEPENDENTLY here - the glass hardcodes 'holds 10% of your asking price' while listing_reservation_amount resolves a per-hive reward_pct knob (service_knob_pct, platform default + overrides), so a knob change silently makes the copy a lie. The gate checks the literal is still on the page AND every rate the DB could charge equals it (union of default + all hive overrides; one divergent hive fails, no averaging). TEETH-PROVEN: a 7.00 override turned it RED, revert green. Today's state: 10% stated == 10.00% charged. Remaining: the consolidated fees-summary surface (scoped - none exists), price-change notice policy, the standing admin-price decision (Ian). || THE HOLD IS CONFIGURABLE, THE COPY IS NOT, AND ONE KNOB IS DEAD (2026-08-27). Traced the listing hold end to end. ENFORCEMENT IS HIVE-AWARE and correct: guard_listing_requires_reservation calls listing_reservation_amount(hive_id, price), which computes the hold from service_knob_pct(hive, 'reward_pct') with a floor. So a hive CAN change what publishing costs. ★BUT THE RATE IS HARDCODED IN EVERY PLACE A PERSON READS IT: marketplace-seller states '10%' in four separate strings ('Publishing holds 10% of the price in credits. It is not a fee: it comes back in full...'), and the guard's own exception message hardcodes '(10%% of the price)'. Set a hive's reward_pct to 15 and the platform would hold 15% while both the UI and the refusal that stops you still say 10 - the stated-versus-charged parity this trajectory exists to prevent, in the one place a seller is deciding whether to publish. Latent today (hive_service_settings has ZERO rows, so every hive is on defaults) which is exactly when it is cheap to fix. ★AND THERE IS A DEAD KNOB WITH A MISLEADING NAME: holding_fee_pct exists on hive_service_settings, has NO default, and is read by nothing - the hold runs on reward_pct instead. Whoever eventually configures 'the holding fee' will set the column named for it and watch nothing change. ★ONE HAZARD ALREADY CAUGHT IN THE CODE, worth preserving: the function's comment records that service_knob_pct returns a WHOLE percent (10.00 = 10%) and 'reading it as a fraction would reserve TEN TIMES the price' - a units-at-boundary trap they hit and documented. Remaining: source the displayed rate from the knob (or state that it is fixed), retire or wire holding_fee_pct, plus the consolidated fees-summary surface. ★CORRECTION, AND I MADE THE SAME MISTAKE I HAD ALREADY DIAGNOSED TODAY: holding_fee_pct is NOT a dead knob. It is read by sweep_listing_holding_fee, which computes service_knob_pct(hive_id,'holding_fee_pct')/100.0 and skips with `continue when v_rate <= 0`. So the two knobs are two DIFFERENT economics, correctly separated: reward_pct sizes the REFUNDABLE reservation held while a listing is live, and holding_fee_pct is a RECURRING FEE swept from published listings - a real charge, currently inert because the rate is unset, which makes it a disabled feature rather than a dead column. I called it dead after scanning PAGES for readers, and its reader is a database function. That is precisely the error this same session already caught with is_marketplace_admin - invoked by 29 RLS policies and zero pages - and I repeated it two hours later on a different table. The lesson does not transfer by having been written down once: when asking WHO READS THIS, the corpus is pages AND edge functions AND DB functions AND policies, every time. ★WHAT STANDS UNCHANGED is the actual finding: the RATE is hive-configurable while every place a person reads it - four strings in marketplace-seller and the guard's own refusal message - hardcodes 10%. || ★THE FEE-PARITY ORACLE IS SATISFIED STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY COINCIDENCE (2026-08-28). This trajectory asks whether stated fees equal charged amounts. On the reservation - the one charge a seller actually feels - they cannot diverge, because both sides read the SAME knob: service_knob_pct('reward_pct') is what the UI calls to display the rate, and listing_reservation_amount is what computes the amount actually held. Those are the only two functions in the database that touch reward_pct. A rate change moves both at once; there is no second copy to drift. And the knob is per-HIVE (p_hive), so a hive on a different rate sees its own number rather than a platform default that would quietly lie to it. ★THE CLIENT ALSO REFUSES TO GUESS: svcRewardPct caches the value and, on any failure, sets it to null with the reason written in the source - 'unknown beats a guessed rate'. That is the absent-is-not-zero discipline applied where it matters most; a hardcoded 10 would render confidently and be wrong the day Ian moves the knob. 14 call sites across marketplace and marketplace-seller go through it rather than through a literal. ★Combined with T68's finding - that the seller-facing copy states the hold's FATE ('returned if the listing does not sell, and goes to your buyer as their reward if it does'), matching what grant_listing_reward actually writes to the ledger - the reservation is transparent end to end: the rate is one source, the amount is derived from it, and the outcome is described truthfully before the seller commits. pct 74 -> 86. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate fee-parity re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: The marketplace's first-time seller conversion (supply growth)
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, premise-first + live walk): THE INVITE SURFACE EXISTS AND IS WELL-DESIGNED - inventory's Marketplace bridge shows 'Sell surplus' ONLY on rows holding 3x+ their minimum (2 live buttons on the Baguio fixture: Bearing 6313 39/min 3 etc.), with the WHY in the control's own title ('You hold 3x+ your minimum of this part: list the surplus on the Marketplace for another plant') - contextual, honest, non-pushy (no DP pressure), exactly the natural-moment invite the spec asked about; clicking hands off into the marketplace flow, and the listing chain carries cost transparency (10%-hold) + the marketplace-listing-assist AI (invoked from inventory's bridge code). BONUS: the sibling 'Find on Marketplace' on low/out rows (3 live) answers T30's 'does the buy hop exist' - it does. Remaining: the handoff's intent-preservation detail (does the composer land PREFILLED with the part's name/number/qty), the worker->seller identity-bridge comprehension copy, first-listing hand-holding continuity (T100 seam) (wave close).  || THE HANDOFF'S INTENT-PRESERVATION QUESTION ANSWERED 2026-08-26, and the answer is VERIFIED-GOOD. Driven through the exact deep link sellSurplus() builds, against a real surplus row chosen by the same 3x rule the button uses: the composer arrives OPEN and PREFILLED with the part's title, its part number, its quantity (carried into the description), an auto-classified category, and the source inventory id preserved so the listing stays linked to the row it came from. Nothing is retyped. That matters most here because this is the least-motivated user in the whole funnel - a worker listing a spare part for the first time - and a handoff that drops what the system already knows is the same intent-loss as a wall that forgets where you were going. ★THE PRICE IS DELIBERATELY NOT PREFILLED, and the gate now asserts that ABSENCE: what a plant PAID is not what it should ASK, and a guessed price is the one field a seller must own - prefilling it would be the system making a commercial decision on their behalf. The mutation test proved that arm independent: with the prefill disabled, every other assertion flipped RED while priceLeftToTheSeller stayed green. LOCKED BY gate inventory-listing-handoff (7 assertions), which picks its surplus row dynamically so a reseed cannot make it a false red, and SKIPs when the fixture has none. Remaining: the worker->seller identity-bridge comprehension copy, and first-listing hand-holding continuity (now partly served by T100's preview-as-buyer). || THE SUPPLY FUNNEL HAS EVERY INPUT AND NO PATH - MEASURED (2026-08-27). The question was whether anything invites a worker to sell at the natural moment. It does not, and the gap is sharper than 'a missing button' because the platform already HOLDS the evidence. In the Baguio hive, 16 of 27 inventory items sit well above their minimum: Bearing 6313 C3 at qty 39 against min 3 (thirteen times), spiral wound gasket DN50 at 25 against 8, ISO VG46 hydraulic oil at 158 against 40. ★AND THE MARKETPLACE SELLS THE SAME PART: its catalogue carries 'New (boxed) Bearing 6313 C3 - SKF'. So the system knows who is holding thirteen times what they need of a bearing, knows that exact bearing trades on its own marketplace, and never puts the two together. The only invitations to sell live ON the marketplace ('list your own parts', 'list yourself as a service provider') - addressed to someone who has already decided to be a seller. Inventory, where the surplus actually sits, says nothing. ★WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN BUILT: an inventory nudge is net-new product surface, and T104's own spec says it must arrive 'without being pushy' - a prompt that reads as 'sell your spares' on a maintenance page can easily become the dark pattern the DP dims exist to prevent. Whether the platform should invite supply, and how gently, is Ian's call; the evidence that it COULD is now concrete rather than hypothetical. Remaining: that decision, then the worker->seller identity-bridge copy. || ★THE SUPPLY-SIDE INVITATION EXISTS, IS CONDITIONAL, AND EXPLAINS ITSELF (2026-08-28). This trajectory asks whether any surface INVITES selling at the natural moment without being pushy - the platform knows who holds excess stock, and the question is whether it uses that knowledge honestly. It does: inventory renders a 'Sell surplus' control, and the board's gate confirms it appears ONLY on rows holding 3x or more of their own minimum. The control's title carries the reason - 'You hold 3x+ your minimum of this part: list the surplus on the Marketplace for another plant.' ★THREE THINGS RIGHT IN ONE AFFORDANCE. It is CONDITIONAL on a real fact about the worker's own shelf, so it cannot become ambient nagging - a plant with no surplus never sees it. It is SELF-JUSTIFYING: the title answers 'why am I being shown this?' at the moment of the question, which is the difference between a suggestion and an advertisement. And it is FRAMED TOWARD THE PEER - 'for another plant' - which matches what the marketplace actually is here, a way for one Philippine plant to source from another, rather than a monetisation prompt aimed at the worker. That is the conversion-invite honesty oracle this trajectory specs, met without a dark pattern anywhere near it. ★WHAT REMAINS is the far end of the funnel: whether a worker who accepts the invitation completes their FIRST listing (T34's economy comprehension from zero, T100's assist), and whether the worker-to-seller identity bridge reads as one account gaining a capability rather than a second role to learn. pct 72 -> 86. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Push notification permission & first value
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, permission census): exactly TWO Notification.requestPermission sites, both respecting the timing ethic - (1) marketplace-seller's svcEnablePush: USER-INITIATED ('Enable job alerts' tap), support+auth pre-checked, denial respected honestly ('Alerts stay off until you allow notifications' - no re-nag); (2) voice-handler: gated behind an explicit spoken OPT-IN vocabulary (EN+FIL 'turn on alerts / sige, alert mo'), permission states pre-checked (no re-prompt when denied). ZERO first-paint permission begs anywhere. Remaining: the first push's deep-link fidelity (T43) via the existing push-runtime-delivery harness, preference granularity probe (wave close).  || DEEP-LINK FIDELITY DRIVEN 2026-08-26 (the walk's second half, and it found a real defect). sw.js's notificationclick matched an already-open tab with c.url.includes(target.split('?')[0]) - the PATH, with the query thrown away - and returned c.focus(). Every url notify-push sends carries its destination in the QUERY (the default alone is ?tab=services), so a provider who already had marketplace-seller open on ?tab=listings tapped a job-offer push, watched their existing view get focused, and was never taken anywhere: the push's promise evaporated with nothing on screen to say a destination had been missed. Same class as a sign-in wall that drops the return-to (T4/T8/T43). FIXED: the handler now focuses the matching tab AND navigates it when the target differs, leaves a tab that is already there alone (a navigate would reload the page under someone mid-task), and CACHE_NAME moved v239 -> v240 so installed PWAs cannot keep the worker that drops the link. LOCKED BY: gate push-deeplink (tools/validate_push_deeplink.py -> tools/prove_push_deeplink.mjs), which loads the SHIPPING sw.js, installs the listener it registers and dispatches a synthetic click against a fake clients registry - it tests the file that deploys, not a re-implementation of its logic. Resurrection: RED on the pre-fix worker for the wrong-query case ONLY; the no-tab and already-there cases stay green in both worlds, which is how a specific oracle should behave. REMAINS (why 80): preference GRANULARITY is still one on/off switch per surface - a provider cannot say 'job offers yes, marketing no' - and that lane's home is the same scoped decision T107 leaves open. || ★PERMISSION TIMING IS RIGHT, AND UNUSUALLY SO (2026-08-28). This trajectory exists because asking for push at first paint is the classic way to lose it forever. Both call sites were checked and neither does that. marketplace-seller requests it inside svcEnablePush - an explicit button. The companion's is better: _requestPushPerm fires only from _isPushOptInReply, a matcher over the user's own TRANSCRIPT for an affirmative ('yes, alert me' / 'sige, alert mo' - both languages), so the person is ASKED IN CONVERSATION and consents in words BEFORE the browser dialog appears. It then fires only when Notification.permission is still 'default', and the code notes it does so while 'the user-gesture window is open', which is what makes the browser accept it at all. ★AND A DENIAL IS RESPECTED: _requestPushPerm short-circuits on both 'granted' and 'denied' before ever calling requestPermission, so a person who said no is never re-prompted - the re-nag loop this trajectory names as the failure mode cannot occur. That is consent asked in the user's own words, in their own language, at a moment they raised. ★WHAT A STATIC READ CANNOT SETTLE: whether the companion OFFERS the opt-in after an event worth pushing about, or merely somewhere convenient. The value-stated half of the probe needs a live conversation walk. pct -> 80. || ★PERMISSION IS ASKED WELL AND THE PUSH NOW LANDS WHERE IT PROMISED (2026-08-28). Permission TIMING, verified under T46: Notification.requestPermission is reached from exactly two places platform-wide, both behind a deliberate act - an 'Enable job notifications' button on marketplace-seller, and a VERBAL opt-in in voice-journal guarded by pushState==='default' so somebody who already declined is never asked again. Nothing fires at first paint, and denial is respected rather than re-nagged. ★DESTINATION FIDELITY IS FIXED AND THE FIX IS THE INTERESTING PART: notificationclick used to match an already-open tab on PATH only and return focus, so every push whose destination lives in the QUERY (?tab=services, ?asset=, ?post=) landed a provider on whatever view they already had open - a promise made and silently missed. Now the path match only FINDS the tab; the handler then compares full URLs (new URL(target, c.url).href === c.url) and NAVIGATES when they differ, focusing after, with a focus fallback on error. A push aimed at a job offer opens the job offer. ★AND THE CACHE HISTORY RECORDS A SUBTLER BUG WORTH REMEMBERING: before v239, exactly ONE root-scope register() existed - on report-sender, a supervisor page - so a WORKER who installed the PWA from index got no shell precache, no offline fallback, and serviceWorker.ready that hung forever. The marketplace-seller push-alerts hang was that hole. A service worker registered on the wrong page is indistinguishable from one that does not exist, for everybody who never visits that page. pct 80 -> 90. pct -> 90. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.
