trajectories.note: ★BROWSER PERMISSION IS NOT A SUBSCRIPTION - FOUND AND FIXED (2026-08-27). Found by sweeping for WRITE-ONLY TABLES (the table-level twin of the captured-columns sweep): of 54 tables the UI writes, 2 are read by no page after resolving reads through views, and push_subscriptions is one. marketplace-seller WRITES a subscription on enable and never reads one back, and the in-context push card renders only while `Notification.permission !== 'granted'` - so the moment permission is granted the card disappears FOREVER and nothing ever confirms a subscription row exists. Those are two different facts about the world. A push subscription is lost routinely - the browser rotates the endpoint, the service worker is replaced, the upsert failed, the row was cleared - and permission stays 'granted' through every one of them. The provider is then shown NOTHING while believing the page's own promise that they will 'hear new hails with this tab closed'. A claim no query enforces, on the one capability whose whole value is working while nobody is looking. MEASURED: push_subscriptions holds 0 rows. ★FIXED with a THIRD state rather than a louder second one: not-granted asks as before; granted-but-no-row says '🔕 Job alerts are not actually on ... we have no subscription for this device' with a one-tap repair; granted-with-a-row stays silent. ★AND A FAILED READ MUST NOT ACCUSE ANYONE: the lookup returns null for UNKNOWN and only `false` triggers the warning, so a refused or errored read can never tell a correctly-subscribed provider that their alerts are off. ★THE FIX ALSO CLOSES THE WRITE-ONLY GAP that hid it - the table now has a reader, which is why the sweep found it at all.

trajectories.title: Email digest lifecycle
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, premise-first): NO unattended email digest exists - the digest CONTENT lane is scheduled-agents' failure_digest (grounded by contract: 'do NOT invent, change, or recompute any number'), saved as a report that reaches email ONLY through a supervisor's deliberate report-sender send - a conservative, honest posture (no inbox pressure to audit). Content links carry REPORT_META deep links; the stop path is T111's new footer line; empty-week suppression is N/A (no unattended sends). The auto-digest subscription (frequency control, one-click unsubscribe) is a SCOPED FUTURE decision recorded for Ian. LINK->ARRIVAL FIDELITY DRIVEN 2026-08-26, and it found a real defect. Every 'View in WorkHive' link in send-report-email's REPORT_META pointed at a BARE PAGE ROOT: a PM Overdue report - a document whose entire subject IS the overdue set - landed its reader on the unfiltered schedule, and both logbook reports landed on that page's default MINE view while the report itself is hive-wide. That is T19's two-windows-one-metric mismatch arriving by email, at whoever the supervisor forwarded it to, where there is no Retry and no context. MEASURED BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING (the premise check): ?filter=overdue is a real chip value AND genuinely filters - live readings gave ontrack 0 rows, duesoon 2, overdue 10 against 10 for bare, so the param does work rather than just highlighting a chip. (The first measurement of this used #pm-list, which does not exist, and returned 0 rows for every case - a reading that would have proved nothing had I not noticed both arms were identical.) FIXED: pm_overdue -> ?filter=overdue, failure_digest and shift_handover -> ?view=team (T19's own deep link). The other five target analytics.html and project-manager.html, which read NO query params at all per the generated param registry, so their links are already as specific as those pages allow - a page limit recorded as a page limit, not papered over. LOCKED BY gate report-link-fidelity, whose central assertion is not that links carry params but that every param they carry is one the target page ACTUALLY READS: a link decorated with ?window=7d would look more specific while delivering nothing. Resurrection BOTH ways - RED on the pre-fix bare links, RED again on a mutation adding a plausible ?window=90d analytics never reads. REMAINS (why 80): the digest-content grounding drill, and the edge fn needs a REDEPLOY for this to reach real inboxes - Ian's gate. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate report-link-fidelity re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: In-app alert center coherence (alerts vs notifications)
trajectories.basis: WALKED LIVE 2026-08-26, and the walk CORRECTED the earlier inferred basis. That basis - read off the T108 registry rather than the page - said 'there is NO designed personal-notification surface'. False: hive.html has a bell (notif-wrapper/notif-badge/notif-list) with seven producers, two of them personal (approval, approval-in). Signed in as a supervisor the tray held four entries - PM Due Soon, Assets With PM Overdue, Open work orders, Low stock - EVERY one a plant condition already painted as a tile on that same page and again in alert-hub. So the finding is not absence, it is BLENDING: one bell carrying 'work waiting on you' and 'a restatement of the board' with nothing to tell them apart. Second finding, measured in the same walk: unread existed only as background:rgba(255,255,255,0.03) - a 3% white tint on a dark surface, real in code and unfindable in use, and the sole unread signal, so a badge over ten rows could not say WHICH were new. FIXED: the tray now renders two named lanes ('Waiting on you' / 'Plant conditions', the latter saying it is also on this board and in the alert hub, with a link there), and unread carries an orange left edge + a dot + an sr-only '(unread)' - visible to sighted users AND announced to a reader. Verified live at 390: 4/4 unread marked, hub link present, 0 pageerrors. Read-state: localStorage wh_notifs_read_<hiveId> is DEVICE-local, and the walk closed that as CORRECT rather than a gap - the tray re-derives its contents from live data every load instead of holding delivered messages, so the marker means 'this device has looked', and clearing it on a phone must not hide a still-true overdue-PM summary from a PC. Recorded in state_scope_registry.json (device_level + the T107 tension closed). LOCKED BY: gate notification-taxonomy (tools/validate_notification_taxonomy.py, registered Platform) - asserts structure not wording: two lanes named, plant lane points home, unread perceivable to both audiences, every pushNotif type classified. Resurrection: RED on the pre-fix page for 3 of 4 assertions; the 4th mutation-proven by injecting a 'mention' producer (FAIL), removed (PASS). REMAINS (why this is 80, not 100): whether the personal lane deserves a home beyond the hive board - T105 push and T106 email would feed it - is a scoped product decision for Ian, and 4 of 8 T108 registry rows still read 'none' for their someone->you path. || CROSS-DEVICE READ-STATE RE-CONFIRMED FROM THE RECORD, NOT RE-LITIGATED (2026-08-27). Measured: the seen-marker is localStorage wh_notifs_read_<hiveId> (hive.html), and there are ZERO server-side read-state columns anywhere - no read_at, is_read or seen_at on any table. That looks like a cross-device gap until you read why it was closed: the tray RE-DERIVES its contents from live data on every load rather than holding delivered messages, so 'read' can only honestly mean 'this device has looked'. A server-side read-state would assert a delivery model the platform does not have. trajectories.title: Quiet hours & notification pressure (PHT reality)
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, pressure census): the notification pressure surface is MINIMAL by construction - no unattended emails (T106), push ONLY for explicitly-enabled job alerts (an opt-in work-finding channel where piercing quiet is arguably the point), and the 6am PHT AMC cron writes an IN-APP brief, not a push. Quiet hours therefore have almost nothing to govern today - an honest absence, not a gap; the posture becomes a real design question only when personal notification lanes (T107/T108) ship. PHT correctness: crons schedule in UTC with PHT-labeled intent (amc 6am PHT = 22:00 UTC; my summaries cron Mon 05:00 PHT). Remaining: shift-aware delivery + urgency tiers WHEN a personal lane ships; timezone boundary probes (T132 seam) (wave close). MEASURED 2026-08-26: there are NO quiet hours anywhere - push_subscriptions carries no window or timezone column, notify-push has no time gate, and no preference exists. Checked the other half too, which is what makes this honest rather than a gap report: NOTHING CLAIMS quiet hours - no page, no policy line, no notification copy promises a window - so the platform is silent, not lying. What DOES exist to build on: an urgency vocabulary already distinguishes 'Urgent job nearby' from 'New job nearby' at broadcast time, and shift-brain holds real shift schedules, so a night worker's 'morning' is knowable. The build would need a per-user quiet window + timezone + an urgency tier that pierces it (safety-critical always delivers, a digest never) - schema, preference UI and delivery logic together, i.e. a scoped product decision rather than a slice. Recorded with its shape so the decision is cheap to make. Remaining: the decision (Ian), then shift-aware delivery; timezone boundary probes (T132's lane, midnight flip already proven correct).  || THE ABSENCE IS NOW GUARDED, NOT JUST OBSERVED (2026-08-26). Recording 'no quiet hours exist and nothing claims them' was true but inert - it said nothing about whether the absence would STAY harmless. Measured the structural reason it is harmless: EVERY push producer on the platform is EVENT-DRIVEN. All eight (mention, reply, best answer, assignment, approval decision, report, pending submission, service completion) fire from a person acting; NOT ONE is clock-driven, and no cron enqueues a push. So a phone cannot buzz at 3am unless somebody in that hive acted at 3am, which on a round-the-clock plant is a night shift and is legitimate news. Also verified the PHT-named crons really are PHT: amc-brief-0600pht runs at 22:00 UTC = 06:00 PHT, and the 0555/0550 pair likewise - the classic 6am-UTC-means-2pm-local bug is not present. The night-hour crons that DO exist (predictive, ml-retrain, failure-signature-scan, hierarchical summaries) are compute jobs that notify nobody, which is exactly where heavy work belongs. LOCKED BY gate no-clock-driven-push, which is written to FIRE ONE DAY: when the scheduled digest T106 records as a future decision gets built, it goes red, forcing the quiet-window question to be answered BEFORE the first scheduled push reaches a phone rather than after. Mutation-proven by scheduling a 3am-PHT digest cron - caught by name - then unscheduled. REMAINS (why 70): shift-aware delivery and an urgency tier that may pierce a quiet window are only needed once a clock-driven producer exists; the per-user window + timezone build stays a scoped decision for Ian, now with a guard that will demand it at the right moment. || ★QUIET HOURS EXIST AND ARE WELL-BUILT — AND THEY MUTE THE NIGHT SHIFT DURING ITS OWN SHIFT (2026-08-28). Three of this trajectory's four questions answer YES, from the code rather than hope: voice-handler's _isQuietHours() mutes non-critical proactive companion output 22:00-06:00 PHT; the window is computed as (getUTCHours() + 8) % 24, so it is correct no matter what the DEVICE clock says (which also settles T150's skew concern for this path — a phone 30 minutes fast cannot move it); and urgency tiers are explicit in both the code comment and the injected prompt anchor: 'Critical / safety items still surface in full', quiet hours 'never block safety signals'. Alert-hub separately implements per-alert SNOOZING (snooze_until, filtered while live), so pressure is controllable at the item level too. ★THE FOURTH QUESTION — shift-aware delivery — IS THE REAL GAP, and it is now evidenced rather than hypothetical: shift_plans.shift_window carries THREE windows and the fixture holds 32 plans for 06-14, 29 for 14-22 and 13 for 22-06. The platform demonstrably plans NIGHT SHIFTS, and the quiet window is a fixed 22:00-06:00 — so a night worker's companion goes quiet for precisely the hours they are working, which is the one group for whom 'night' is the working day. ★AND THE CHEAP FIX IS WRONG, which is why this is Ian's rather than mine: shift_plans is scoped to hive_id with NO per-worker column, so the only no-schema option is 'is a night shift_plan active right now?' — and that would disable quiet hours for EVERYONE in a 24/7 hive, including the day worker who picks up their phone at midnight and should still be left alone. A correct fix needs a per-worker shift assignment, which is a schema and product decision. pct 70 -> 82. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate no-clock-driven-push re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Notification storms under real activity
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, architecture map): the push path is OUTBOX-MEDIATED - a DB fn enqueues (consumer 'notify-push', auth_uids+title+body+url) into service_outbox, drained by the 1-min cron to the notify-push fn - so the drain is the natural batching point, and volume is bounded by real broadcast traffic; but NO per-user collapse exists ('5 replies = one line' - each outbox row becomes a push). Acceptable at today's event volume (opt-in job alerts only); becomes a storm risk when personal lanes (T107/T108) ship. Remaining: the storm-injection probe (N outbox rows for one user -> pushes counted) on the EXISTING push-runtime-delivery harness (tests/), catch-up UX after a storm, badge-list cap discipline (T19's lesson) (wave close). COALESCING MEASURED + THE SAFE SLICE SHIPPED 2026-08-26. Measured first: there is NO coalescing anywhere in the lane - enqueue_user_push inserts one outbox row per event and the drain sends one push per row, so in a busy hive a worker can be pushed the same sentence several times a minute (two triggers on one PM going overdue, a supervisor's repeated save, a retrying client). Migration 20260826000001 adds the narrow, safe half: an identical push (same recipients+title+body+url) still UNSENT within a 2-minute window returns the PENDING row's id instead of enqueueing a second - callers unchanged, since the contract is still 'an id comes back'. Deliberately NOT done here: digest-style merging of DIFFERENT notifications ('3 new replies'), which is a wording+cadence design decision, and suppression of a repeat whose predecessor was already DELIVERED - that is news, not a duplicate. PROVEN in a rolled-back txn: identical -> same id (2 rows not 3), different body -> its own row. Remaining: the digest decision, storm-injection probe on the push-runtime harness, catch-up UX after a storm. (2026-08-26, T61's measurement: the enqueue layer is already O(1) rows per event - recipients travel as an array - so the dedupe window added here is the right and only place the storm can be bounded before delivery.)  || THE DEDUPE WINDOW IS NOW LOCKED (2026-08-26). It had shipped with NO gate, and the same day it became load-bearing: four new producers landed (T108's mentions/replies/best-answer plus a trigger on every pending submission), and the submission trigger depends on this window BY DESIGN - its copy names no row precisely so a bulk CMMS import of 200 assets collapses to ONE push. An unlocked storm guard underneath four new storm sources is the gap worth closing before any further producer. Gate push-dedupe-window holds FIVE assertions, and the third is what separates a correct dedupe from a mute button: a repeat whose predecessor was already DELIVERED must get its own row, because that is news, and suppressing it would silently drop real notifications. It also holds that a different body and a different RECIPIENT each get their own row - a blanket one-per-user-per-window would swallow different news and merge two people's deliveries. The whole gate runs inside a transaction that is ROLLED BACK and then verifies nothing survived, so it writes nothing it must clean up. Resurrection: with the dedupe removed (also inside a rollback - DDL is transactional, so the mutation could never escape) identical pushes returned different ids and wrote 2 rows, RED on both. REMAINS (why 80): the digest-style merge of DIFFERENT notifications ('3 new replies') is a wording+cadence design decision for Ian, and catch-up UX after a storm is unbuilt. || GATE RECORDED 2026-08-27: push-dedupe-window (registered, verified exit 0). The basis called it a gate and described its resurrection - identical pushes returning different ids and writing 2 rows with the dedupe removed - but the gates field was empty, so the registry did not know this trajectory owned an instrument. push-runtime-delivery is deliberately NOT recorded: the basis names it as the EXISTING harness in tests/ that the storm probe will run on, which is a tool this trajectory USES, not one it owns. The distinction matters because a scan that matched any registered id inside a basis proposed 61 refs across 50 trajectories, most of them page names colliding with gate ids - recording those would have put other trajectories' instruments in this one's ledger. || 2026-09-01 DESIGN FINDING: coalescing needs a CATEGORY dimension the enqueue_user_push contract lacks (payload = auth_uids/title/body/url, no type). Cleanest honest paths: (a) add p_category param (signature change, all callers default it), or (b) key coalescing on recipient-set + url-tab. Ian default (N new X on the 2-min window) DECIDES to do it; the category KEY is the impl choice - not a fragile title-parse. Build with (a) next: additive param, callers pass their existing notification type. || 2026-09-01 MIGRATION STAGED: 20260901000002_push_digest_coalescing.sql — additive p_category param (default null=old behaviour, no caller breaks); coalesces same-recipient+category pushes into honest incrementing N-new-X on the existing 2-min window; DROPs the old 4-arg sig first to avoid a PGRST203 overload. APPLY+VERIFY post-board (function replace contends). Remaining to lock: apply + a caller opts in (pass its notification category) + the T110 storm probe green + board. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate push-dedupe-window re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

THE GAP, fixed: the footer said only 'Sent via WorkHive Report Sender' - the recipient of an outward irreversible email could not tell WHICH PERSON sent it nor how to stop receiving them. The footer fix had shipped with NO gate, so a regression would have silently returned outbound mail to an unidentified sender with no stop path - and email is the one surface no UI test watches, that reaches people without accounts, and that cannot be corrected once sent. Gate outbound-email-honesty holds four properties, and the FIRST is the one that matters most for a trajectory named 'the re-engagement email that lies': exactly the known set of functions may build outbound email, which turns the census from a one-time observation into a living claim - a new marketing lane cannot appear un-audited. trajectories.title: Webhook-driven state changes reach the user (bounce example)
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, evidence assembly): the webhook->glass architecture per class - BOUNCE: resend-webhook-receiver is LIVE (fails closed pending Ian's signing secret; the unterminated-regex fix commit 46d3b12a) and the sender-side bounce surface exists in report-sender (prior arc, verified then); PAYMENT: gcash-receipt-inbound fails closed pending its secret (T93); CMMS: cmms-webhook-receiver exists for the T63 lane. Replay/idempotency: the send side is Idempotency-Key'd (hour-bucket dedup). What CANNOT be walked until the secrets land (Ian-gated): a live signed webhook -> automation_log -> user-visible state within stated lag. Remaining: the mocked-signature end-to-end per class once secrets land, admin failure-to-process visibility (T69 observability), the webhook->glass latency oracle (wave close).  || REPLAY/IDEMPOTENCY DRIVEN 2026-08-26 via the local-substitute move, and it uncovered TWO LATENT BUGS that would have fired the moment Ian set the signing secret. (1) IDEMPOTENCY: the receiver ended in a bare INSERT while Svix delivers AT LEAST ONCE and retries on any non-2xx or timeout - it READ the stable svix-id header to verify the signature and then threw it away, so a retry wrote a second bounce row, double-listing one failed send and over-reporting deliverability problems. Fixed with a partial unique expression index (mig 20260826000004) rather than a check-before-insert, because two near-simultaneous retries both pass a SELECT-then-INSERT; the receiver now writes [svix_id=...] and treats 23505 as SUCCESS so the provider stops retrying something already stored. (2) FOUND WHILE BUILDING THE PROOF, not by looking for it: automation_log's CHECK allows success|failed|skipped|warning, and the receiver wrote 'failure' while send-report-email's circuit breaker wrote 'deferred'. Both refused with 23514 - and NEITHER read the insert error, so the errors vanished and both functions reported success. The bounce lane would have answered Resend 200 'recorded' while storing nothing: a permanently empty bounce surface with every layer above it healthy. Fixed by growing the vocabulary honestly (mig 20260826000005 adds 'warning', because a delayed delivery is genuinely neither a completed failure nor a skip and forcing it into 'failed' would over-report real problems), correcting 'failure'->'failed', and mapping the breaker to 'skipped', which already means exactly 'we did not attempt this'. LOCKED BY two gates: bounce-idempotency (4 assertions incl. a real concurrency race - two writers, one row, one refusal) and automation-log-status (the CLASS gate: every status literal allowed, checked against BOTH the migration and the live constraint, plus a forward-only ratchet on unchecked inserts). Resurrection on both. REMAINS (why 70): the HTTP round trip - a real signed webhook hitting the deployed function twice - is still Ian-gated on the secret, and the edge fns need a REDEPLOY. || ★THE CLASS GATE GREW ITS MISSING HALF (2026-08-28). automation-log-status asserts every status literal is PERMITTED by its CHECK constraint. That answers 'may this value be stored' and never 'does anything downstream know what it means' - and the second question is where the real defect was hiding. cmms-push-completion wrote external_sync.sync_status='failed' as the durable marker for a completion that never reached the CMMS; the CHECK permits five values so a constraint-shaped gate passes it happily, but v_external_sync_truth buckets exactly three (is_active/is_deleted/is_error), so the marker built to make a lost completion VISIBLE landed in the one value that made it invisible to the truth view as well. New gate status-literals-are-classified asserts the other half: every status literal the code WRITES must be one the consuming view CLASSIFIES. It reads the LIVE view definition rather than a migration, so it measures what the database actually buckets. Resurrection-proven - restoring 'failed' names the orphan value and its exact line. ★AND ITS COLUMN PATTERN CARRIES A WORD BOUNDARY, which cost a wrong reading earlier the same day: without one, `sync_status` matches the tail of `last_sync_status` - a different column, on a different table, with its own vocabulary ('failed'/'success') and its own reader at integrations.html:1792. Two columns whose names overlap are not one column. || ★AND THE NEW GATE HAD THE FALSE-GREEN SHAPE ITSELF, FOUND BY REVIEWING MY OWN WORK THE SAME DAY (2026-08-28). status-literals-are-classified reads the LIVE view definition, so on a machine where the database is unreachable every pair SKIPPED, `problems` stayed 0, and the run printed PASS - a zero meaning 'I could not look' rendered identically to a zero meaning 'nothing wrong'. That is the skipped-partition-reads-as-covered shape this whole board exists to prevent, shipped inside the gate written to prevent a cousin of it. It now counts what it actually CHECKED and fails when that is zero: 'NOTHING was checked: the database was not reachable, so this run has no opinion about the code. That is not the same as finding it clean.' The convention was already here to follow - fb1_webhook_idempotency_live raises on an unreachable psql rather than shrugging. TEETH-PROVEN by pointing it at a container that does not exist: FAIL, not PASS; restored, exit 0, and the PASS line now states how many column/view pairs were examined so the reader can see the denominator rather than trust the verdict. || ★THREE WEBHOOK CLASSES, THREE DIFFERENT ANSWERS TO 'DOES IT REACH A PERSON?' (2026-08-28). The platform receives three kinds of external event and they land very differently. (1) gcash-receipt-inbound REACHES THE USER by construction: its effect is credits appearing in the payer's balance and a service_credit_ledger row, so the person who sent the money sees the outcome without anyone building a notification - the event and the visible state are the same thing. (2) cmms-webhook-receiver has the STATE to be surfaced: integration_configs carries last_sync_at, last_sync_count, last_sync_status and last_sync_error, so a failed sync is recoverable and showable on the integrations page rather than only inferable. (3) resend-webhook-receiver does NOT reach anyone: a bounce is written to automation_log - an operations table keyed by job_name - while report_contacts, the list the SENDER actually looks at, has no delivery or bounce column at all. So the supervisor whose Friday report never arrived keeps sending to the same dead address, and the one signal that exists lives where only an operator would find it. ★THE PATTERN THIS EXPOSES: an event 'handled' means three different things here - handled INTO a user-visible state (gcash), handled into a state that COULD be shown (cmms), and handled into a log (resend). Only the first is what this trajectory means by reaching the affected user, and the distinction is invisible from the receiver's own code, which returns 200 in all three cases. A webhook that answers 'recorded' while nobody will ever read the record is the shape to watch for. pct 80 -> 88. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate automation-log-status re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

trajectories.note: ★THE BOUNCE CLASS REACHES THE SENDER - TRACED END TO END (2026-08-27). T112 asks whether an external event becomes visible truth for the affected user, and for email delivery it does. The chain: Resend calls resend-webhook-receiver, which records the event into automation_log under job_name 'report_email_bounce'; report-sender READS those back (hive-scoped, last 30 days, limit 200) and maps each lowercased address to what happened, parsing bounced / marked as spam / delayed out of the detail. The reasoning is written above it and is exactly right: 'a full mailbox or a retired address is accepted with a 200, and the failure arrives later as a webhook … without reading them here the report is "sent" forever and nobody is told.' ★TWO DETAILS WORTH KEEPING because both are lessons this platform paid for elsewhere: the read is ordered by triggered_at AND id, a TOTAL order, because two bounces can share a timestamp and a non-total order paginates unstably; and a FAILED read leaves the map untouched rather than empty, so the page 'does not claim either way, rather than claiming everything is fine' - the failed-read-is-not-empty discipline applied to a surface where the empty reading would be 'every address is fine'. ★WHAT IS STILL PENDING IS IAN'S, not the code's: the Resend signing secret, without which no real event reaches the receiver. The pipe is built and honest; it is waiting to be turned on.

trajectories.title: Small phone 320: the floor viewport
trajectories.basis: the floor JOURNEY ran (not just rest-state): the full logbook wizard at 320x640 - picker, all fields, 3 steps, save - completes with NO horizontal scroll and the entry lands visibly; save button in-viewport and tappable (86x107 - wraps tall-narrow sharing its row at 320, cosmetic note). Z2 rest-state coverage pre-existing in the lens. FIXED-CHROME BUDGET AUDIT DONE 2026-08-26 and locked. The individual pieces of furniture were each reasonable and had never been measured TOGETHER, which is how a floor screen quietly loses a third of itself before one row of content is drawn. Measured across the eight pages a field phone lives in: mean 26.1% of the 320x640 viewport is persistent chrome, worst 36.6% (pm-scheduler), and on SEVEN OF EIGHT the largest single contributor is the same 64px page-guide chip - the component already on record for covering every modal's Save. Coverage is a UNION of viewport rows, never a sum, so overlapping chrome costs one band rather than inventing a number nobody experiences. VERDICT: 26% is a real cost but not a defect, so the honest outcome is a locked forward-only measurement rather than a fix hunting for a problem - chrome may shrink, never grow. ★THREE INSTRUMENT CORRECTIONS BEFORE ANY NUMBER WAS BANKED. Run 1 reported index.html at 87.5% and blamed #cursor-glow, a 440px pointer-following gradient that is pointer-events:none, z-index 0 and 5% alpha - decoration sitting BEHIND everything, costing a person nothing. Run 2 reported logbook at 50.9% and blamed a 280px div.card that turned out to be the Log a Repair FORM, sticky top-6 and 843px tall on a 640px screen: sticky cannot engage for something taller than the viewport, so it scrolls exactly like the content it is. Banking either would have sent someone deleting furniture that does not exist or a panel a worker needs. The rules that survived - chrome INTERCEPTS A THUMB or gets ANNOUNCED, and chrome PERSISTS WHILE CONTENT MOVES UNDER IT - are what the gate now encodes. MODALS AT THE FLOOR DONE 2026-08-26, and they were not clean. The dialog prover swept 390/641/1280 - the widths with banked rows - so 320 had never been measured. Made the sweep overridable (default UNCHANGED, because silently adding a fourth width would change what the registered cj_dialog_layout gate MEANS without anyone deciding to) and ran the floor: THREE real defects. (1) pm-scheduler's PM COMPLETION SHEET hung its primary action 21px past the panel - a worker on a budget Android reaching for a Save button whose right edge was off the sheet, in the core field flow. btn-primary is width:100% by design but shares a flex row with Cancel, and at 320 the content box is 278px, which cannot hold both however the remainder is divided; two attempts to make them SHARE went 21 -> 10 -> 14px, which was the measurement telling me the premise was wrong, so they stack at the floor. (2) analytics' results panel pinned three columns by inline style and pushed tiles 52px past it; auto-fit now drops to two. (3) public-feed showed a 229x12px link - and it was NOT a floor defect: it lives in whListError, so it sat in ~20 PAGES' read-failure states and was failing at 390 too, unnoticed, in the exact state a person reaches when something has already gone wrong. It was also MY OWN edit from earlier the same day (the T71 status-page pointer), written as a bare inline anchor while the correct idiom - inline-flex + min-height:44px - already existed two functions away in the same file. AFTER THE FIXES: 43 of 50 gradable dialogs pass at 320 with zero failures, and the default 390 sweep went from 1 failing to 0. LOCKED BY gate dialog-floor. The prover's own rail earned its keep: the first 320 run reported 0 of 50 graded (my override collided with a hardcoded 390 reference) and it REFUSED to call that a pass - 'zero failures over an empty denominator is not a pass' - so a probe bug cost five minutes instead of banking 'the floor is clean'. Remaining: T10/T13 journeys walked end-to-end at 320. || HANDED OVER FROM T45's N1 WALK 2026-08-27 — a real floor-viewport finding, language-independent. The '← Back to Basic Worker' link (a.btn-secondary.text-xs.py-2.px-4) extends past a 390 viewport by +45px on inventory and +35px on logbook, with its parent computing overflow:visible, so it is cut at the viewport edge rather than clipped deliberately. Verified in BOTH languages at the same offsets, so it is a layout bug and not a translation-length one. The page does not scroll horizontally, which is why it has survived: nothing about it trips a scroll-based check, but part of a tappable control sits off-screen on the floor viewport this trajectory owns. || FIXED 2026-08-27 — and the ROOT was not the element that looked wrong. The '← Back to Basic Worker' link measured +45px (inventory) / +35px (logbook) past a 390 viewport, so the obvious move was to shorten the button. I did, and it was WRONG twice over: the label span used `hidden sm:inline`, and wh-tw.css compiles NO .sm\: variants at all — so the span was hidden at EVERY width and desktop silently lost the full label — while the link, now only 101px wide, STILL sat at 438 in a 390 box. The measurement that ended it was the container's own numbers: navScrollW 438 vs navClientW 384. The row was over-full because the LEFT group ('Digital Logbook' / 'Inventory Monitor' with tracking-widest) would not shrink — a flex item defaults to min-width:auto and refuses to go below its content width, so it held the row open and pushed the button off-screen. THE FIX is min-w-0 on the left group plus truncate on the section label, letting it ellipsize instead: both pages now read the FULL button label at 390 with linkRight 364 < 390 and navScrollW == navClientW == 384. Re-swept 8 pages at 390: 7 clean, the 8th a JS-injected span carrying the document title inside an overflow:hidden parent — clipped by design, not visible overflow. mobile, link-target-existence and jargon all green over the change. ★WHY IT SURVIVED THIS LONG: the page never scrolls horizontally, so every scroll-based check reads clean while part of a tappable control sits past the edge — worth a probe of its own on the floor viewport. || GATE BUILT + REGISTERED + RESURRECTION-PROVED 2026-08-27: control-within-viewport (tools/prove_control_within_viewport.mjs). The fix alone was not the lock — the reason that overflow survived is a HOLE in what the floor-viewport checks look at, and the hole outlives the one navbar. Scroll is a SYMPTOM of overflow, not a definition: this page never scrolls horizontally, so every Z2 / WCAG 1.4.10-shaped check reads clean while a button hangs past the edge. The gate asks the question those checks cannot — at 390, does any rendered element with its own text (or any link/button) extend past the right edge without a scrolling or clipping ancestor? Fixed and absolute decoration is ignored, so it reports only what a thumb genuinely cannot reach. Walks 16 pages signed in as supervisor; currently 0 offenders. TEETH, and a real red->green rather than a synthetic one: removing min-w-0 from the flex group turns it RED (exit 1, naming a.btn-secondary at +228px AND #hive-chip-name at +5px, a second overflow the same root was hiding), restoring it turns it GREEN (exit 0) — files backed up and verified restored either side. Narrowed --page runs write their own report, so a spot-check cannot clobber the sweep. || ★THE GATE WAS GUARDING THE WRONG BOX (2026-08-27). This trajectory IS 'the floor viewport, 320', and the gate I registered for it ran at 390 and called that the floor. 390 is the common phone, not the floor; the declared floor is 320 (WCAG 1.4.10). Re-pointing it found TWO more off-screen elements the same day, both invisible at 390: (1) community's post action row - a supervisor viewing their OWN post gets FIVE icon buttons instead of four (edit, pin, public, flag, delete), and the fifth is Delete, which also carries a deliberate 22px Z3 gap so a destructive control is never adjacent to a routine one. Those 22px are exactly what pushed it 15px off-screen, so the delete control was unreachable on precisely the posts its owner is most likely to manage - and only for the author, which is why every four-button row read clean. (2) analytics' 'Stage 3' badge 10px past, because .hdr-right is deliberately flex-shrink:0 (its EN/FIL buttons owe 44px on BOTH axes) so the row had nowhere to give. ★BOTH FIXED BY WRAPPING RATHER THAN SHRINKING, which is the point: the obvious fixes - trim the Z3 gap, let the 44px buttons shrink - would each have bought viewport space by spending a different guarantee. Wrapping keeps the destructive-adjacency separation AND the touch minimums AND puts the control back on screen; rows that already fit are unchanged. Width is now a parameter defaulting to the FLOOR, a non-default width writes its own report, and 320 and 390 are both green over 16 pages. Remaining: T10/T13 journeys walked end-to-end at 320. || T10/T13 WALKED END-TO-END AT 320 + GATED 2026-08-27 (flow-fits-the-floor). ★THE REASON THIS NEEDED ITS OWN INSTRUMENT: control-within-viewport walks pages AT REST, and the controls that decide whether work gets RECORDED do not exist at rest. The PM completion sheet, the deferral control and the add-task sheet are built or revealed mid-flow, each a different layout from the page hosting it — so the resting sweep can be green over all 16 pages while the Save button of the sheet a worker must press sits off the edge. Same class this trajectory already found twice, one interaction deeper than any resting check can reach. Walks T10 (complete a PM, plus its honest alternative, recording a DEFERRAL) and T13 (the clock-in handover) at the floor; all clean, 7 controls in the sheet and 124 on the handover. ★IT ARRIVES THE WAY A WORKER DOES: alert-hub hands pm-scheduler an ?asset=, the detail opens, a REAL scope item's mark-done control is clicked. My first cut called openSheet() by hand and measured an EMPTY sheet — the same seven controls whatever the task, because markDone() is what fills in the item text, asset name, frequency badge and findings. That would have proved the sheet's chrome fits, not the sheet. ★AND THE FIRST RUN CAUGHT ITSELF: page.evaluate takes ONE argument and I passed three, so every flow errored — reported as UNREACHED rather than as three tidy clean surfaces, which is the rule this arc keeps re-learning (an empty reading is the instrument, never the property). PROACTIVE guard, so teeth are synthetic negatives, one per independent failure mode, 4/4 verified: off-screen control, absent required control, absent surface, and the real sheet clean. A width negative alone is NOT enough — at --width 200 the handover went RED while both PM sheets still passed, which is exactly why the missing-control half needs its own negative. Gate registered (973 total). Remaining: the wave-close re-earn, same as its siblings. || ROSTER WIDENED 16 -> 23 PAGES, AND THE SEVEN NEW ONES HELD A THIRD DEFECT (2026-08-27). The sweep guarded 16 pages while 22 are banked, so a third of the roster was left to be discovered by a user; project-report is walked WITH its ?project_id= because a paramless walk is a different page. FOUND on project-manager: all FOUR project cards - each a tappable control that opens its project - sat exactly 8px past the right edge at 320. ROOT: .card-grid used repeat(auto-fill, minmax(310px, 1fr)), and a bare 310px floor is a floor the CONTAINER can be narrower than. At 320 main's 18px padding leaves 284px of room, auto-fill still produced one 310px column, and 18 + 310 = 328 - the +8px the gate measured, identical on every card because it is the grid track, not the content. FIXED with minmax(min(310px, 100%), 1fr) in BOTH grid rules (the second one, under .group-content, would otherwise have kept the bug for grouped views - the same fix-every-path discipline that caught the second discipline/category refusal earlier today). Desktop verified unchanged: 1280 still lays out 3 columns at 404px across 2 rows. All 23 pages now green at 320 and at 390. || AND THE DIALOG DENOMINATOR MADE THE PLATFORM'S, NOT MINE (2026-08-27, gate dialogs-fit-the-floor). flow-fits-the-floor walks four flows I picked by hand, and a gate whose subject list I wrote can only ever find what I thought to look at. tools/dialog_targets.mjs is already the ONE source of truth for how each V2/V3 dialog opens - every entry's path read from source, with the `ref` line that establishes it - so this gate consumes it, and any dialog added there is covered for free. 42 subjects, 26 measured, ZERO unreachable controls at 320x844. ★THE SUBJECT TEST IS THE WHOLE GATE, and the first run got it wrong. The registry holds fixed overlays AND in-flow panels/tabs/lists, and bottom-checking the in-flow ones flagged SIX 'unreachable' controls - asset-hub's FMEA and Weibull panels, engineering-design's history tab, analytics' summary, alert-hub's AMC card, voice-journal's history list - every one reachable by simply SCROLLING THE PAGE. Six false findings, about to be banked against pages that are fine, and the tell was that they all sat on ordinary page sections rather than dialogs. The property is UNREACHABILITY, not off-screen-ness: the bottom axis applies only where the surface is fixed AND nothing in its ancestry scrolls, because a centred non-scrolling dialog past its fold is a button that cannot be pressed, whereas page content past the fold is what scrolling is FOR. ★AND TWELVE 'ok' ROWS HELD ZERO CONTROLS: a surface with nothing to measure proves nothing about control reachability, so it is now reported as unmeasured rather than padding the pass count - the denominator says 26 measured of 42, not 41 clean. Teeth 6/6, including the two that matter: a FIXED sheet IS bottom-checked, an IN-FLOW surface is NOT. || DIALOG COVERAGE 26 -> 33 OF 42, and the seven that were unmeasurable taught the sharpest lesson of the arc. marketplace's openSheet(name) opens BOTH `#overlay-<name>` and `#sheet-<name>`: the overlay is the BACKDROP and the SHEET carries the content. The gate was measuring the scrim, which is empty by design, and after a REAL listing click it stayed empty for ten seconds with no page errors - a reading that looked exactly like 'tapping a listing opens a blank full-screen sheet on the smallest phone', which is what I was one step from filing against a marketplace that is completely fine. Reading openSheet is what stopped it. ★THAT IS THE THIRD INSTRUMENT FAULT IN THIS ARC WEARING THE SAME COSTUME - a resting toast placeholder read as a save receipt, a closed <details> whose hidden children still report layout rects read as an overlap, and now a backdrop read as an empty dialog. Each looked like a product defect and each was the probe pointed at the wrong element, which is why this gate now refuses to grade anything it did not demonstrably reach. Getting in also took two honest corrections en route: listing cards bind by addEventListener on .listing-card[data-id] rather than an inline onclick, and openDetailSheet is closure-scoped so page.evaluate cannot call it - so the opener CLICKS the card, which is the real user action anyway. Seven commerce dialogs now measured (21, 6, 6, 5, 4, 14 controls), all fitting the floor. ★AND THE LABEL WAS A FALSE CLAIM: the report printed 'in-flow' for anything not bottom-checked, but marketplace's .sheet is position:fixed WITH overflow-y - fixed-but-scrolls-internally and in-flow are different facts, and only one means the PAGE can scroll to the control. On a gate whose entire subject is why a control is or is not reachable, mislabelling the reason is the one thing it must not do. Teeth re-run 6/6 after every change; one selftest run SKIPPED on a transient sign-in blip and was re-run rather than read as a pass. || COVERAGE 33 -> 35 OF 42: project-manager's detail-view was recorded as unreachable ('element is not visible') when it had opened perfectly. The registry's PRECONDITION for that target clicks a .pcard — which IS the opener — and the card list is then swapped out for the detail, so the prover's second click landed on a card that no longer existed. The gate now checks whether the surface is already up after the precondition and does not open it twice. That is the fourth instrument fault in this arc and the fourth to look exactly like a product defect; the pattern is always the same, a probe measuring a state it created rather than the one the user meets. || ALL FIVE GATES RE-VERIFIED GREEN 2026-08-28 on a restored stack, one at a time to avoid the contention that had made them lie: dialog-floor 43/50 graded 0 failing (its earlier RED was a dead runner, not a layout defect - the prover died on SIGN-IN FAILED after Docker Desktop stopped, and the gate had no infra health check; one is now wired), fixed-chrome-budget mean 26.1% worst 36.6%, control-within-viewport 23 pages 0 off-screen, flow-fits-the-floor 4/4 flows, dialogs-fit-the-floor PASS on every reachable dialog. pct STAYS 99: the basis still owes the wave-close re-earn, and gates green is necessary, not sufficient. || 2026-08-31 full-board: named gate NOT green (dialog-floor=FAIL) - blocks the lock; must go green before this row can reach 100. pct -> 99. || LOCKED 2026-09-04: board gate passed. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Landscape phone & tablet 768
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, 768x1024 sweep on index/analytics/alert-hub as supervisor): NO horizontal scroll, layouts coherent at the awkward middle - the breakpoint gap holds. Line-length nit shared with the 1920 sweep (104-131ch paragraphs, over the ~90ch readability bar - same elements at both widths, so a base-styling nit, not a 768 break). Remaining: landscape-phone keyboard-consumption on the write forms, wall-mounted glanceability (K-class at 768), touch-target density check (wave close).  || MEASURED 2026-08-26 with one probe answering both this and its sibling trajectory, AND IT CORRECTED A RECORDED FINDING. T115 had logged prose lines of 104-131ch at 1920 as a nit to fix. Every one of them was a SOURCE CHIP - 'Live . refreshed on load . Based on ...', 'Saved snapshot, computed 5h ago . ...' - the platform's freshness metadata, SCANNED in a glance rather than read left-to-right. Capping those at a reading measure would have WRAPPED them, turning a one-line label into three: the recorded fix would have made the page worse. With chips excluded, the longest genuine prose line across index/analytics/logbook/hive/pm-scheduler is 59-93ch - inside the comfortable 45-90ch measure, with logbook@768 marginally over at 93. NO LINE-LENGTH DEFECT EXISTS, and this is written down so a future session does not go hunting one. FILL: at 768 the pages occupy 87.5-100% of the viewport, so the awkward middle is used rather than treated as a big phone. At 1920 index, analytics and pm-scheduler run full width while hive (35%) and logbook (57%) cap their column - a legitimate readability choice, now recorded so it stays a visible decision. LOCKED BY gate width-utilisation, which ratchets longest-prose-line per page+width and deliberately does NOT gate fill, because 'uses the width' is a design judgement and a gate demanding a fill percentage would be enforcing an opinion. The ch measure comes from each block's OWN font metrics via canvas rather than being guessed from a max-width. || THE 768 CONTROL SWEEP — MEASURED 2026-08-27, clean. The awkward middle is where a layout built for a phone and a layout built for a desk meet, so it is the width most likely to leave a control half-off the edge with neither breakpoint owning the result. Ran control-within-viewport at 768 across all 23 banked pages: ZERO elements past the edge, zero controls off-screen. Also re-ran the dialog sweep at 390 (42 subjects, 35 measured, zero unreachable controls), so the three defects T113 fixed at the 320 floor — project-manager's card grid, community's delete button, analytics' badge — are confirmed fixed rather than merely moved to another width, which is the failure mode a single-width fix invites. The gate's width is a parameter, so 320 / 390 / 768 / 1920 are now all covered by ONE oracle rather than four hand-written checks. Remaining: landscape-phone keyboard behaviour on forms and wall-mounted glanceability at distance, both of which are judgements about USE rather than geometry and are deliberately not gated. || Remaining: landscape-phone keyboard behaviour and wall-mounted glanceability - judgements about USE, deliberately not gated. || THE AWKWARD MIDDLE HOLDS - MEASURED AT BOTH SIZES (2026-08-27). This platform tests two lanes, 390 and 1280, and the sizes BETWEEN them are where a layout usually tears: a tablet in portrait is too wide for the phone rules and too narrow for the desk ones. Walked 8 core pages signed in at 768x1024 (tablet portrait) and 844x390 (phone landscape), measuring the objective failure - documentElement.scrollWidth exceeding clientWidth, with the probe prepared to name the widest offending element if it found one. ZERO of 8 pages overflow at EITHER size, so nothing sticks out and no page scrolls sideways in the middle range. That is the half of this trajectory a machine can settle, and it is settled. ★WHAT REMAINS IS DELIBERATELY NOT MEASURABLE: whether a landscape phone's keyboard leaves enough of a form visible to work with, and whether a wall-mounted tablet is GLANCEABLE from across a workshop, are judgements about USE rather than properties of the DOM - a page can pass every overflow check and still be unreadable at three metres. Recording them as judgement rather than pretending a probe settles them. Remaining: those two use-judgements at wave close. || ★THE PROVER MEASURED ONE PAGE FIVE TIMES AND CALLED IT FIVE PAGES (2026-08-28). validate_width_utilisation was RED with what looked like a real regression - prose lines growing on index, analytics and pm-scheduler. Reading the raw run instead of the verdict: EVERY page reported byte-identical numbers, 99.2%% fill and 73ch 'Build a verified reputation in the' at 768, 99.7%% and 70ch 'The gap: Departments run in isolat' at 1920 - for logbook, hive, pm-scheduler alike. That prose exists ONLY in index.html. Every walk had landed on index: the prover's sign-in silently failed, every gated page bounced through whSignInWall(), and the loop measured whatever was on screen and labelled it with the page it had ASKED for. The ratchet then reported prose regressions on pages the browser never opened. ★THE BASELINE SURVIVED, which is the one piece of good design here: it is dated 2026-08-26 and contains none of index's prose, so the gate refused to ratchet a poisoned reading into the record. A failing gate that does not corrupt its own baseline is worth more than a passing one that might. ★FIX IN THE INSTRUMENT, NOT THE PAGES: the prover now compares the URL it LANDED on against the page it asked for, and ABORTS when they differ rather than attributing one page's prose to another - the same discipline prove_cold_page_teaches already applies when it refuses to measure on dirty state. Nothing about the pages was wrong; the pages were never visited. ★This is the third instrument-over-page finding of the session (with the ai-render-provenance false accusation and the cold-page abort), and they share a shape: an instrument that cannot tell 'I failed' from 'the code failed' will always report the second. || ★AFTER THE FIX, THE GATE'S REMAINING RED IS ITS OWN BASELINE (2026-08-28). With the landed-page assertion in place the prover finally measures each page's OWN prose - index 36ch ('The industrial intelligence hive f'), analytics 78ch ('Hive OEE is 87%%. Wear and contamin'), logbook 68ch and 52ch, hive 85ch - all different, where the broken run had reported one identical pair of numbers for every page. The gate still FAILS, on exactly one entry: analytics 0ch -> 78ch. ★THAT COMPARISON IS MEANINGLESS, and saying so is the finding. The stored baseline recorded 0ch for analytics, which is not a measurement of short prose - it is what this prover records when it did not actually reach the page. The baseline was captured by the SAME instrument, with the same misattribution, so the ratchet is comparing a real reading against a non-reading. 78ch is also comfortably inside the gate's own stated limit (past ~90ch the eye loses its place), so nothing about the page is wrong. ★I AM NOT RE-BASELINING IT, deliberately. Re-establishing a ratchet is exactly the move that hides a real regression ([[feedback_gates_that_measure_prose_and_ratchets_that_loosen]]), and the fact that I have a good reason this time is precisely when that discipline matters. The baseline SHOULD be re-established now that the instrument is honest - but as a deliberate, stated act by Ian, not as a side effect of my own gate fix landing red. || ★THE AWKWARD MIDDLE IS THE PART THAT WORKS - measured, once the instrument was honest (2026-08-28). 768 is the width this trajectory expected to find neglected, sitting between the phone somebody designs for and the desktop somebody designs for. It is not neglected. Every page measured fills 90%% or more of it - index 99.2%%, analytics 99.2%%, hive 99.2%%, pm-scheduler 99.2%%, logbook 90.9%% - and every prose line sits inside comfortable measure, the longest being analytics at 78ch against the ~90ch point where the eye starts losing its place. A wall-mounted tablet or a supervisor's iPad gets a coherent layout with readable text. ★THE CONTRAST WITH 1920 IS THE USEFUL PART. The same pages at the wide width split: index, analytics and pm-scheduler hold 99.7%%, logbook drops to 56.7%% (defensibly - its prose caps at 52ch, a real readability choice), and hive.html falls to 35%% while letting its prose run to 85ch. So the platform's responsive work is strongest exactly where this trajectory feared it would be weakest, and weakest at the width T115 covers. Neither reading was available before, because the prover was measuring index.html under every page's name; both are only trustworthy now because that was fixed first. pct 74 -> 84. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. || LOCKED 2026-09-04: board gate passed. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: PC 1920+: the wide-screen supervisor
trajectories.basis:

The 104-131ch line-length nit recorded for the close (identify the offending elements, cap ~90ch). Based on ...', 'Saved snapshot, computed 5h ago . ...' - the platform's freshness metadata, SCANNED in a glance rather than read left-to-right. Capping those at a reading measure would have WRAPPED them, turning a one-line label into three: the recorded fix would have made the page worse.
