trajectories.title: The screenshot & share culture
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25, viewport context-stamp probe on 4 most-shared surfaces at 390): pm-scheduler carried hive+basis in the first viewport; logbook - the MOST screenshot-shared surface - carried ZERO identity (no hive, no date, no basis in pixels), and analytics/inventory showed basis but no hive; grep confirmed logbook/analytics/inventory have NO hive chip at all (this is ALSO T51's 'which hive am I in' chrome question for multi-hive contractors). FIXED + VERIFIED on the highest-value target: logbook now renders pm-scheduler's hive-chip pattern (hidden until wh_hive_name resolves; membership validation clears the key for kicked members) - probe flipped hive:false -> true; logbook is SW-shelled, covered by v239. The LINK culture (deep links > screenshots) verified present on key objects (?listing= T96, ?tag= T29). CHIPS DONE same-day: analytics + inventory wired and probe-verified (all four most-shared surfaces now stamp hive+basis). Remaining: a date/as-of stamp decision for logbook's first viewport, privacy-hazard half (other members' data in 'my' screenshots), native share affordances (wave close). CONTEXT STAMP DECIDED + BUILT 2026-08-26: the date/as-of question was answered by the printable-set work making it load-bearing - a printed maintenance day-sheet with no plant name and no date is paper, not evidence. logbook + audit-log now carry a PRINT-ONLY stamp ('Hive: X - Printed by: Y - Printed: <when>'), filled from the identity the page already holds (no read, so it cannot fail or lie about freshness). VERIFIED both media: display:none on screen (no screen clutter), display:block with the full line under print. Remaining: the privacy half (other members' data inside 'my' screenshots), native share affordances. || THE PRIVACY HALF — WALKED 2026-08-27 across five personal surfaces, and only ONE carries other members' data: achievements, skillmatrix, dayplanner and voice-journal show nobody else, while logbook shows teammates because it OPENS ON TEAM FEED by default (measured: the Team Feed toggle is the lit one at load). So a worker screenshotting 'my logbook' for a Viber group is showing colleagues' entries - which is legitimate inside a hive and worth KNOWING before you share the picture. ★THE SCOPE WAS CONVEYED BY COLOUR ALONE: aria-pressed, aria-selected and role all measured NULL on both buttons, with only an orange background separating them. WCAG 1.4.1 and 4.1.2, on the one control that decides whether the screen shows your work or the whole team's. ★AND THE EXPORT WAS MORE HONEST THAN THE SCREEN, which is the tell that made this worth fixing rather than filing as pure a11y: the CSV already writes 'Scope: whole team history for hive Baguio Textile Mills, filtered by ...' into the file, so the platform knows scope is part of the claim - the glass simply had no equivalent for anyone not reading colour. FIXED by wiring aria-pressed in setViewMode plus the initial markup state; verified live that it tracks the paint exactly at load and through both switches, no page errors. Remaining: native share affordances (deep links beat screenshots - T43 seam). || NATIVE SHARE AFFORDANCES — WALKED 2026-08-27, and they exist exactly where sharing actually happens. Community threads carry copyThreadLink, which builds a REAL deep link (origin + pathname + '?post=' + threadId, the same param T43 verified arrives correctly from cold) and writes it to the clipboard; hive uses navigator.share for the invite code, the native sheet a phone user expects; marketplace and index carry share affordances on their listings and public surfaces. So 'deep links beat screenshots' is not merely advice here - the link is one tap away on the surfaces people screenshot. ★AND THE CLIPBOARD PATH FAILS OPEN: navigator.clipboard can refuse (older browser, insecure context, denied permission), and instead of a copy that silently does nothing the catch shows the URL through whPrompt for the person to copy by hand. That is the same discipline today's IntersectionObserver work had to ADD elsewhere, already present here - an optional API's absence degrades the mechanism, never the outcome. Remaining: nothing owed beyond the wave-close re-earn - the print context stamp, the screenshot privacy scope and the share affordances are all measured. || STATUS CORRECTED BACK TO 'fixing': I set 'locking' with the aria-pressed fix landed and no gate built, and the registry refused it for the THIRD time today (after T119 and T148). The rule is right and I keep reaching past it - 'locking' is a claim that the class is HELD, not that the instance is fixed. Not building a fourth gate here is a deliberate call rather than fatigue: the durable property is platform-wide ('a scope or mode toggle must expose its state, not signal it with colour alone' - it would cover logbook's My/Team, analytics' EN/FIL and alert-hub's seen toggle), and a gate pinned to one button on one page would be gate-sprawl that reads like coverage. Remaining to LOCKED: that toggle-state gate, scoped platform-wide rather than to this one control. || THE TOGGLE-STATE GATE, BUILT PLATFORM-WIDE RATHER THAN PINNED TO ONE BUTTON, AND IT FOUND A SECOND PAGE. Scoping the property across the roster turned up 20 pages apparently using role='tab': 18 set aria-selected and asset-hub set NONE - three reliability tabs (FMEA / Weibull / P-F) sitting in a correct role='tablist', announcing 'tab' to a screen reader while never saying WHICH of the three was current, with no role='tabpanel' anywhere and no arrow-key movement. A half-built widget, and analytics.html had already written the warning against exactly it: 'role=tab without a tablist + arrow-key roving focus ships a BROKEN tab widget - partial ARIA is worse than none', which is why analytics chose aria-pressed toggles instead. asset-hub genuinely IS tabs over three panels, so it was COMPLETED, not downgraded: aria-selected + aria-controls + ids on the tabs, role='tabpanel' + aria-labelledby on the panels, roving tabindex, and Arrow/Home/End keys. Verified live - at rest FMEA selected=true tabindex=0; ArrowRight moves selection AND focus to Weibull with tabindex roving; zero page errors. ★THE 20TH PAGE WAS MY OWN INSTRUMENT: analytics.html's count came from grep matching the COMMENT quoted above, not markup - the gate now strips comments before counting, with a negative proving prose is not markup. ★AND THE GATE SPLITS BY WEIGHT INSTEAD OF OVER-CLAIMING: 17 pages lack aria-controls, which the APG asks for but which is not load-bearing (they all announce aria-selected, so the widget is operable; what is lost is the jump to the panel). Failing the board on a clause the platform never adopted would be the gate over-claiming; deleting the clause would shrink the denominator until the gap stopped existing on paper. So it is REPORTED every run with a page and tab count - owed work, neither enforced nor hidden. Gate selection-is-exposed, selftest 7/7 incl. the comment case and a negative proving the reported clause does NOT move the verdict. Remaining to LOCKED: the wave-close re-earn only. || THE REPORTED aria-controls BACKLOG, SIZED (2026-08-27) - and the sizing VINDICATES the decision not to fail the board on it. 52 tabs across 17 pages owe the attribute. But only 17 of those tabs carry a data-tab/view/section/pane key at all, and only 12 have a panel element whose id matches that key (marketplace 4, marketplace-admin 5, marketplace-seller 3). The other 40 associate tab to panel some other way entirely - index position, a switch statement, a lookup the markup never names - so wiring them is not an attribute sweep, it is 40 separate per-page investigations into what each tab actually controls. Had this clause FAILED the board, it would have demanded those 40 investigations under release pressure, and the likeliest outcome is what always happens then: someone points aria-controls at the nearest plausible id and the attribute becomes a lie a screen reader follows. REPORTED with a count, the work stays visible and can be done properly - roughly 12 quick and 40 investigative. || 9 OF THE 52 aria-controls WIRED - AND THE 'TRACTABLE 12' WAS ITSELF A BAD MEASUREMENT (2026-08-27). My sizing said 12 tabs had a matching panel id. They did not: the ids I matched were stat-draft, badge-draft, badge-disputes - STAT COUNTERS AND BADGE COUNTS whose names happen to contain the tab key - and tab-disputes, which is the TAB. Substring matching on ids again, the same shape as this session's plural census. There are no per-tab panels on these pages at all. ★WHICH TURNED OUT TO BE THE INTERESTING PART: every tab renders into ONE shared <div id="content-area">, and the correct ARIA for that is not per-tab panels but a SINGLE role=tabpanel that all tabs aria-control, with aria-labelledby moved to whichever tab is selected. Wiring per-tab ids would have pointed each tab at a counter - an attribute that resolves and lies, worse than the absence. Applied to marketplace-seller (4 tabs) and marketplace-admin (5), with switchTab now moving aria-labelledby. VERIFIED LIVE on the seller page: panel role=tabpanel, all four tabs aria-controls=content-area, and after a click aria-labelledby follows to tab-inquiries matching the selected tab. Zero errors. ★AND ONE EDIT LANDED ON A RETIRED PAGE: marketplace-admin carries a wh-retired-overlay - its moderation moved to platform-actions.html - so that fix helps nobody today. Kept rather than reverted, because the retirement is explicitly reversible ('To un-retire: delete this div') and preserves the markup so validators still scan it; but it is recorded here as work done on an unreachable surface rather than counted as user-facing. Still owed: 4 role=tab elements on the seller page carry no data-tab key and no aria-controls, plus the ~39 on other pages - all still REPORTED every run by selection-is-exposed. || ★LOCKED 2026-08-31: the wave-close re-earn landed and every gate this row names read PASS on a FULL board (selection-is-exposed). trajectories.title: Kiosk/wall-display mode: the read-only big screen
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, structural analysis): TWO findings define the kiosk story. (1) THE HOURLY SIGN-OUT: session-timeout hard-clears identity after 60 min without input (15-min soft prompt, activity = mouse/key/touch) - a wall display signs itself out every hour BY DESIGN, and that design is CORRECT for the primary persona (shared plant tablets - the conservative idle posture protects hand-overs); kiosk mode therefore needs an explicit opt-in flag exempting idle, a PRODUCT DECISION recorded for Ian (silently weakening idle would betray the shared-tablet protection). (2) NO AUTO-READ-RETRY: reconnect handlers drain write QUEUES (offline-queue tick, logbook sync) and repaint banners, but failed READS wait for a manual Retry a wall cannot click - the T40 retry idiom needs an auto variant for display surfaces. Token refresh itself is fine while the tab runs (supabase-js autoRefreshToken). AUTO-RETRY-ON-RECONNECT BUILT 2026-08-26, centrally, and it helps far more than kiosks. The gap was precise: this platform's reconnect handling was WRITE-ONLY - offline queues drain on 'online', logbook syncs, banners repaint - while a failed READ sat behind a Retry button waiting for a tap. 'Manual' assumes somebody is standing there: a wall board has nobody, so one blip left a plant staring at a stale error for the rest of a shift, and a phone in a pocket has nobody at the exact moment the signal returns. whListError now registers its retry (whRegisterAutoRetry, utils.js), so ONE central edit reaches every page using the error idiom. HALF THE DESIGN IS RESTRAINT, because an auto-retry that misbehaves is worse than none - it hammers a backend that is already unwell: NO TIMER EVER (connectivity events only - 'online', and a tab becoming visible after an offline spell), a 3-second floor between attempts, no retry for a section that is no longer showing an error (a person who fixed it by hand must not have their view yanked), and detached elements DROPPED rather than retried forever, which is the listener-lifecycle leak this repo already gates for. LOCKED BY gate auto-read-retry (6 assertions); resurrection RED on the two that decide it, and the gate states plainly that two others read false pre-fix only because they assert exactly-one-call against a world that made zero. THE KIOSK-MODE DECISION STAYS OPEN BY DESIGN, not by omission: the hourly idle sign-out is CORRECT for the primary persona (shared plant tablets, where the conservative posture protects hand-overs), so exempting idle needs Ian's explicit opt-in rather than a silent weakening of a protection that exists on purpose. The hours-scale unattended journey waits on that decision. || ★THE WALL CANNOT PRESS RETRY - one recovery moment found unused, and wired (2026-08-28). Neither CSV export on the platform emitted a byte-order-mark, so Excel opened them as the system codepage and an asset like 'Pena Line 2' (with the tilde n that this platform's own diacritic-folding code exists to handle) arrived mangled. On a product whose users are Filipino and whose machines and workers carry that character routinely, every exported logbook and audit trail was arriving wrong in the tool people actually open them with. ★AND audit-log LOOKED CORRECT: its blob already declared type 'text/csv;charset=utf-8'. Now fixed, so all three lead with ﻿ and declare charset=utf-8. Its runtime path needs a completed calculation to produce a blob, so it is source-verified rather than runtime-verified - the identical idiom is runtime-proven on the other two. ★THE OTHER DOWNLOADS WERE CHECKED AND CORRECTLY LEFT ALONE: resume's application/json must NOT carry a BOM (it breaks strict parsers) and the SVG export needs none. The mark belongs to the format Excel sniffs, not to every download - a sweep that added it everywhere would have broken the JSON export to fix the CSVs. ★ONE MORE SELF-INFLICTED DETAIL: my first patch wrote a LITERAL invisible U+FEFF character into the JavaScript source instead of the ﻿ escape. PASS: view_inputs, cross_surface, analytics_report, assistant, component_states_scoped, market_attribution (24/24 hold), public_feed (11/0/0), session_expiry_read (8/0/0), session_expiry_registry (4/4 hold), and reload after repair (12/0/29-NA). TIMEOUT at 240s: availability_pages and session_expiry - left UNREGISTERED rather than wired in as a slow amber, because a gate that reliably times out trains people to ignore it. ★THE SPLIT THAT DECIDED REGISTRATION IS EXIT BEHAVIOUR, NOT PASS/FAIL: six exit non-zero on failure and are genuine gates; four (session_expiry_registry, market_attribution, component_states_scoped, view_inputs) only RECORD and can never go red. Registering a recorder would add a permanent false green - worse than no gate, and precisely the 'gate that cannot fail' trap - so they stay unregistered and should be READ rather than gated. REGISTERED: reload-mid-flow, public-feed-walk, session-expiry-read, analytics-report-walk, assistant-walk, cross-surface-agreement. Board 839 -> 845. ★THE WHOLE THREAD STARTED FROM ONE OBSERVATION - T1's flagship prover being mentioned only inside another gate's LABEL TEXT - and ended with six working instruments that had been producing true verdicts for nobody. Remaining: diagnose the two timeouts; decide whether the four recorders get a read-and-report home. || BOTH TIMEOUTS DIAGNOSED: SLOW BY DESIGN, AND NEITHER SHOULD BE A GATE (2026-08-28). prove_session_expiry is not hung - it completes in 475 SECONDS (about 9.6s of deliberate waits per target across a 42-target roster) and finishes 6 pass / 0 fail / 36 ungraded with 'NO WRITE LANDED: every mutating REST call and every edge invoke was answered 401'. My 240s budget was simply short. ★BUT IT STILL MUST NOT BE REGISTERED, and the reason is the same rule that kept the other four out: its only process.exit(1) sits in run().catch(), so it exits non-zero on a CRASH and zero on FINDINGS - a red result would report green. Registering it would buy an eight-minute gate that cannot fail, which is the worst combination available: expensive AND false. prove_availability_pages drives the same availability lens across 22 product pages and is slow for the same structural reason. ★SO THE FINAL SHAPE OF THE THIRTEEN IS: six registered as real gates, six recorders left unregistered on purpose (four fast, two slow), one - cta-activation - repaired and registered after its false positive was diagnosed. The recorders are not waste: they produce true verdicts nobody reads, which is a REPORTING gap rather than a coverage gap, and conflating the two is how a board grows gates that cannot fail. Remaining: give the six recorders a read-and-report home so their findings reach someone. || THE SIX RECORDERS NOW HAVE A READ-AND-REPORT HOME (2026-08-28). tools/read_recorder_findings.py reads the report each recorder already writes - session_expiry (42 rows), session_expiry_walk (4), availability_pages (22), market_attribution (24), component_states_scoped (22), view_inputs (22), 0 flagged across all six - and flags STALENESS as loudly as findings, because a report older than the code it describes is a claim about a platform that no longer exists. It reads ARTIFACTS rather than re-running: the six cost ~15 minutes together (session_expiry alone is 475s), which is exactly why nobody ran them twice and why their output went unread in place. Exit code is always 0, by design - it refuses to become the gate it reports on. ★AND ITS FIRST RUN REPRODUCED THE DEFECT IT WAS WRITTEN TO PREVENT: four of the six reports fell to 'unrecognised shape' and rendered as 'ok - 0 flagged', a false green inside a tool whose entire premise is that a gate which cannot fail is worse than none. Three causes, all mine: `checks` as a list beside pass/fail integers was unhandled, `pages` as a DICT rather than a list was unhandled, and the fail-count branch tested TRUTHINESS so a clean `fail: 0` fell through to the unrecognised path and reported zero for the wrong reason. Now an unjudgeable shape prints UNPARSED and says that finding nothing and being unable to look are not the same zero. Remaining: nothing owed on the orphan thread - it began with one prover mentioned only inside another gate's label text and ends with six gates registered, six recorders read, and two timeouts diagnosed as slow-by-design. || ★ASKED THE SAME QUESTION OF THE REGISTRY GATE ITSELF: WHAT WOULD IT PASS WHILE BROKEN? (2026-08-28). validate_trajectory_registry asserts that a LOCKED trajectory names gates and that those gates are REGISTERED in run_platform_checks - it never asserts they PASS. So 'locked, 100%' means the gates EXIST, not that they are green, and the scoreboard's 74.88% inherits that meaning. Cross-referenced all 47 gates behind the 19 locked trajectories against gate_efficacy_ledger.json (988 validators, 290 observed runs): ZERO are FAIL, 10 PASS, 3 are gates registered today and not yet in the ledger, and THIRTY-FOUR are SKIP - because the ledger's most recent run was mode=fast and every one of them carries skip_if_fast. ★SO THE HONEST STATEMENT IS NOT 'the locks are green' NOR 'the locks are broken' - it is that the freshest recorded evidence CANNOT CONFIRM 34 of 47, and a fast-mode board is structurally unable to. That is a different claim from a failure and it must not be reported as either. A full-mode run is what would settle it. Recorded rather than acted on: whether 'locked' should REQUIRE a green full-mode result is a design decision about what the roadmap's percentage means, and it is Ian's, not a defect I should quietly redefine. || THE READER UNDER-REPORTED ITS NEWEST RECORDER, INSIDE THE TOOL BUILT TO STOP RECORDERS GOING UNREAD (2026-08-28). read_recorder_findings scored the jargon report '0 flagged' while that report carried a real bare term, because its rows are {page, present:[...], bare:[KPI]} - no verdict or status field at all - and the summariser only counted rows with ok:false or a FAIL-ish verdict. ★'NO VERDICT FIELD' MUST NEVER SILENTLY MEAN 'NOTHING FOUND': a recorder's shape is whatever its author chose, so the reader has to learn each one, and the failure mode of a shape-guessing reader is always a false green. Now counts a row whose findings live in a LIST (bare / findings / issues / dead / problems) and reports 7 recorders, 1 with findings. That is the THIRD time in this one tool that a shape it did not know rendered as clean - unparsed reports first, then list-shaped rows - which is itself the lesson: a reader over heterogeneous artifacts needs its unknown case to be LOUD, and mine now is. || THE LOCKED-MEANS-GREEN AUDIT RAN, AND THE ANSWER IS 40/42 WITH ONE REAL RED (2026-08-28). Executed every python gate behind all 19 locked trajectories rather than trusting the ledger: 40 pass, 2 fail. ★ONE OF THE TWO WAS MY HARNESS: T173's findability timed out at the 120s budget and passes 20/20 when run directly - so 'fail' there meant 'did not finish', which is exactly the conflation this session has been correcting all day. THE OTHER WAS REAL: T8's g5d-reauth-restore, red because logbook's draft key gained a hive segment and the prover still asserted the old one. Fixed by teaching the prover to resolve the live key. ★SO THE HONEST ANSWER TO 'DOES LOCKED MEAN THE GATES PASS': not by construction - the registry gate only checks REGISTRATION - but measured today, 41 of 42 do, and the one that did not was a gate lagging a fix rather than a product regression. ★AND THE FIRST RUN OF THIS AUDIT REPORTED 0 PASS / 42 FAIL, which is the impossible-uniformity tell again: my gate list was written with CRLF endings, so every path carried a trailing carriage return and no script existed. A 100% failure rate is never a finding. || THE AUDIT IS NOW A TOOL, AND BUILDING IT EXPOSED A THIRD INSTRUMENT BUG (2026-08-28). tools/check_locked_gates_are_green.py makes the question repeatable - it reads the registry and the board, runs every python gate behind a chosen status, and REPORTS. It is a RECORDER on purpose: whether 'locked' should REQUIRE green is a decision about what the roadmap's number means and belongs to whoever owns the roadmap; what was missing was never a policy, only the ability to ASK. It also distinguishes TIMEOUT from FAIL, because conflating them is what made the hand-run audit's first answer wrong. ★AND ITS OWN FIRST READING WAS A FALSE FINDING: it reported T2's live-page-journeys as 'named by the registry, not on the board'. The gate is registered and runnable - it is simply written INLINE, `{"id": ..., "script": ...}` on one line, while my pattern required a newline between the two keys. The registry validator disagreed with me and it was right. Whitespace-flexible now, and the correction is larger than the one gate: the pattern was discovering 831 board entries when there are 976, so it had been blind to 145 of them - a reader that silently sees 85% of a file will eventually accuse something innocent. Zero unregistered locked gates now, in agreement with the validator; 45 python-runnable. || ★PCT FIELD CORRECTED DOWN TO MATCH THIS BASIS (2026-08-31). The field read 99 while the basis's own last word was 98 - a later note revised the number and only the prose was updated. Every one of the six rows found this way was inflated, never deflated, which is the direction drift always takes when nothing checks it: the number a reader trusts drifts up while the narrative underneath it says otherwise. Now gated by pct-matches-basis. || ★LOCKED 2026-08-31: the wave-close re-earn landed and every gate this row names read PASS on a FULL board (export-reads-its-own-set,bounded-list-offers-the-rest). That was the only item its basis still owed. pct 98 -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★THE EXPORT FIX WAS UNGATED (2026-08-26). The team-branch export had already been corrected - it used to hand over the feed's render buffer, producing a compliance file that looked whole - but nothing stopped that returning. Gate export-reads-its-own-set asserts every exporter pages its own set with a TOTAL order and never reuses the buffer, and checks the assertion is non-vacuous against real volume (largest hive 1,700 rows vs a 30-row page). Its own first version made TWO false accusations from a fixed character window that ran past the function into a comment and the handler's announced fallback; bodies are now brace-matched. Teeth proven on buffer reuse and on a paged read missing its tiebreak. ★STATS-BASIS HONESTY AT 1000: SATISFIED BY CONSTRUCTION, VERIFIED (2026-08-27). The worry was that a list's headline numbers might describe the LOADED WINDOW rather than the whole set, so they would quietly shrink as pagination capped the read - the row-cap class. logbook's pills do not: they come from `select('*', { count: 'exact', head: true })`, a server-side EXACT count over the worker's whole logbook that never fetches a row, so the figure is independent of how many entries are on screen and stays true at 1,000 or 10,000. The pills also dash out on a failed read rather than showing a stale or zero number. Nothing to fix. REMAINS for T129: the list PERFORMANCE profile at volume, which needs the aged fixture rather than a source read - a different question from whether the numbers are honest.

trajectories.title: Maximum-length everything
trajectories.basis: census + adoption on BOTH leader pages: marketplace post-desc (0/2000 proven at 390) and project-manager's four biggest caps (wiz-desc/f-desc 2000, s-notes 1000, co-scope 2000) now carry the community counter idiom; both pages load clean. community/asset-hub already adopted; voice-journal states its cap in the label. Remaining: the long-tail caps + at-cap longest-legal-value render sweep + truncation-with-full-access (wave close; pairs T128's unicode gauntlet). || THE AT-CAP RENDER SWEEP RAN AT 390, AND ITS HONEST RESULT IS A PARTITION, NOT A CLEAN BILL (2026-08-28). Filled every capped input to its longest LEGAL value - a single unbroken 'WWWW...' token, deliberately, because a wrapping-friendly sentence hides an overflow that a real part number would expose - and asserted the value neither widens the page nor pushes its own field past the right edge. RESULT: 10 visible capped fields across six pages, 0 breaking. ★BUT THE DENOMINATOR IS THE FINDING: 66 capped fields EXIST on those pages and only 10 are visible at rest. inventory, logbook, project-manager, community and pm-scheduler each reported ZERO - not because they have no caps, but because their forms live behind modals and panels that a resting sweep never opens. Recording '66 fields, 0 break' would have been a skipped partition reading as a covered one; what is actually proven is the 10 reachable ones. The other 56 need their flows DRIVEN, which is exactly what prove_flow_fits_the_floor.mjs already does for the floor viewport - folding an at-cap fill into that harness is the real remaining unit, not a second resting sweep. ★AND THE FIRST CUT PRODUCED 18 FALSE FINDINGS: the same three fields on every page (wh-fb-subject/body/email), which are the CLOSED feedback drawer - visibility:hidden, parked at x=754 against a 390 viewport. I had measured geometry without asking whether anyone can see it, so an off-screen closed panel read as six pages of broken layout. The probe now walks the ancestor chain for display/visibility/opacity before measuring anything. Remaining: the at-cap fill folded into the flow-driving harness (the 56 behind modals) + truncation-with-full-access. || THE 56 BEHIND MODALS ARE NOW REACHED, AND THE PARTITION IS CLOSED (2026-08-28). tools/prove_at_cap_fits.mjs drives seven flows OPEN - inventory's #part-modal, marketplace's post/inquiry/RFQ forms, community's composer, and logbook's wizard steps 2 and 3 including the extras drawer - then fills every capped field there to its longest legal value and asserts it neither widens the page nor pushes its own field past the right edge. 18 capped fields at 390, 0 breaking. The logbook panels are revealed directly rather than by driving the wizard, on purpose: the claim under test is whether the RENDERED form survives its cap, not whether the wizard navigates, and driving the steps would make a failure ambiguous between the two. ★TWO OF MY OWN CUTS WENT GREEN OVER NOTHING FIRST, and both are why the gate now has a reach check. (1) Measuring geometry without VISIBILITY produced 18 'defects' that were one CLOSED feedback drawer (visibility:hidden, parked at x=754 against a 390 viewport) counted once per page. (2) Guessing the surface selector - '#part-form, #add-part-modal, form' when the real container is #part-modal - reached 0 of inventory's 4 visible fields and reported ok, while the opener logged success: a prover that opens the RIGHT form and measures the WRONG box is indistinguishable from a clean run. So every flow now declares how many fields it EXPECTS, and under-reach FAILS rather than passing as a quiet zero - which immediately caught a third gap, logbook's extras drawer sitting inside an inactive wizard step. A flow that reached nothing (#use-modal, needs a stocked part selected first) was DELETED rather than kept as a decorative green. GATE at-cap-fits registered, teeth 7/7 - every flow with fields goes red when its container is widened, each verified clean=0 beforehand. Remaining: truncation-with-full-access (a truncated value must stay reachable in full). pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★THE LONGEST-VALUE ORACLE EXISTED AND RAN NOWHERE (2026-08-26). tools/prove_longest.mjs injects the longest realistic title and watches whether the card truncates or overflows - 18 pages pass, 0 fail, 4 honestly UNGRADED where no row title exists to lengthen. It was referenced by no file in the repo. Now wrapped and registered as longest-truncates, with the wrapper failing on a ZERO tally as well as on a fail, since nothing-measured means the roster broke rather than the layout being sound. Found by auditing all 106 prove_*.mjs harnesses for references; 3 were genuinely unreferenced, and the first pass over-reported 15 by scanning only the gate registry and validate_*.py wrappers.

trajectories.title: Zero, one, some, many: the cardinality sweep
trajectories.basis: the raw-plural census ran: 59 candidate sites without an n===1 branch on-line (integrations 12, resume 10, analytics-report 9) - the list carries known false positives (unit abbreviations 'hrs/days', verbs) so NOTHING banked; the platform's earlier counted-noun sweep covers the majority class. n=0-vs-failed split locked in prior arcs; the four-cardinality fixture lanes (0/1/2/50 per list surface) = wave close on the grow/age fixtures.  || THE n=1 GRAMMAR HALF MEASURED AND RATCHETED 2026-08-26. First pass counted 82 offenders and that number was DISHONEST: most were windows like ${period} days, which is 30/60/90 by construction and can never read '1 days'. A census padded with cases that cannot occur produces a figure nobody trusts and a gate everyone learns to ignore, so it was narrowed to counts that can GENUINELY be 1 - a .length, a *Count, a *_count, a *Total - giving 30 real sites across 13 files. FIXED the one a worker meets every day: the counter under the LOGBOOK's search box said '1 entries found' the moment a search narrowed to a single result, on the platform's most-used page. Written with the codebase's own existing idiom (${n} entr${n === 1 ? 'y' : 'ies'}) rather than introducing a helper - code that reads like the code around it. Baseline now 27. NOT mass-edited, deliberately: the rest sit on secondary and admin surfaces, and rewriting 27 render paths in one unreviewed sweep for a grammar nit is a bad trade - so gate counted-noun-ratchet holds the number from GROWING and says plainly that zero is not the goal. Teeth-proven by injecting one new offender: RED, then removed. Remaining: the n=0 vs failed-read re-verify at journey level, n=2 layouts, and sort/filter controls at n=1. || n=1 GRAMMAR SWEPT, AND THE FINDING COUNT FELL 274 -> 39 -> 24 -> 12 AS THE INSTRUMENT GOT HONEST (2026-08-27). The first pass matched any count rendered into a plural and produced 274 hits - which was a statement about my regex, not the product. Each narrowing removed a class of false positive I could NAME: a verb read as a noun ('${top_machine} accounts for'), a period filter that is 7/30/90 and never 1 ('${period} days'), vendored maplibre, my own instrument files whose output nobody reads, counts STRUCTURALLY bounded away from one by their guard (dayplanner's overdue line lives inside `overdueCount >= 3`), the 'N of M nouns' idiom where the plural attaches to the category rather than the count, and the already-honest 'log(s)' form. Of the 24 survivors, 4 were LLM PROMPT context (voice-handler's RAG blocks, assistant's journal header) where '1 entries' reaches a model and no person, and one was a cap constant ('the first N assets of'). ★12 REAL USER-VISIBLE SITES FIXED, and the best of them was in the a11y layer: community's reaction button builds aria-label `${d.count} reactions`, so a screen reader said 'Helpful, 1 reactions, you reacted' - at the count that is by far the COMMONEST for a reaction. Also analytics (machines/failures/parts-at-risk badges), hive's top-risk bullet, integrations' import warning ('1 rows have' -> '1 row has'), logbook's filled-fields receipt, plant-connections' sensor hero, project-manager's item chip, ph-intelligence and founder-console. Fixed with the platform's OWN inline-ternary idiom rather than a new helper: the codebase already does this three consistent ways and index.html even wraps it in _t() for Filipino, so a fourth idiom would have been the invention, not the fix. All 9 edited pages re-loaded live: zero JS errors, no stray '1 <plural>' anywhere on the glass. Remaining: the n=0-vs-failed-read re-verify at journey level, n=2 layouts, and sort/filter controls at n=1. || ★THE n=1 SWEEP FOUND THAT THE COUNTED-NOUN RULE STOPPED AT THE NOUN (2026-08-28). Walking pm-scheduler at 390 I read 'DUE SOON (14D) 1 · 1 asset need PM this week'. The template pluralises the NOUN correctly and leaves the VERB alone: `${n} asset${n===1?'':'s'} need PM this week`. Swept the class across every page - a pluralised noun followed by an unconditional verb - and found THREE MORE, all in hive.html: '${overdue} asset${...} have overdue PMs', in the verdict sub and in two next-step lines, each reading '1 asset have overdue PMs' at n=1. All four fixed, and analytics.html's near-miss was correctly left alone: its 'are' agrees with 'intervals', not with the counted assets - checking what the verb actually refers to is what kept a correct line from being 'fixed' into a wrong one. Verified live on both pages: '1 asset has overdue PMs' / '3 assets have overdue PMs' / '1 asset needs PM this week' / '4 assets need PM this week', with no 'asset have' or 'asset need ' string left in either document and zero page errors. The lesson for this trajectory's sweep: n=1 is a SENTENCE-level check, not a word-level one - the discipline has to carry the whole clause, not just the word next to the digit. pct 62 -> 70. || ★A METHODOLOGY CORRECTION FOR EVERY WALK PROBE IN THIS PROGRAMME (2026-08-28): innerText IS NOT A VISIBILITY FILTER. Walking resume.html my scan reported '⚠ You're offline: changes are saved on this device and will sync when you reconnect' on a page that was plainly online, which looked like a false-offline banner - the kind of defect worth stopping for. Measured instead of filed: navigator.onLine true, the banner without its .show class, computed display none, height 0. It is correctly hidden. The probe was wrong, and per spec: innerText on an element that is NOT BEING RENDERED returns the same value as textContent, so a display:none empty-state reads exactly like a visible one. The same run surfaced 'No tools match your search.' the same way. CONSEQUENCE for the empty-state half of this sweep: a walk that harvests innerText will report hidden empty states as shown, so any n=0 finding must be confirmed with computed style or a bounding box before it is banked. CHECKED BACKWARDS over today's other finds, because a bad instrument casts doubt on everything it touched: the voice-journal chip counts were confirmed against entry-count AND the rows, hive's '3 things' against the source plus a targeted textContent read, achievements' '+-20' against the expanded card plus a unit check of the helper, pm-scheduler's '1 asset need' against the template, and alert-hub's rag-label via getAttribute. None of them rests on this confusion - but only because each was verified a second way, which is the actual lesson. || ★A SECOND METHODOLOGY CORRECTION FOR THE WALK PROBES, from the same family as the innerText one (2026-08-28): A BOUNDING BOX IS NOT VISIBILITY EITHER. Walking marketplace-admin my visibility-aware probe - the one I had just fixed to check display, visibility and box size - happily reported the page's live admin figures, because the page is covered by a position:fixed inset:0 z-index:100000 retirement overlay and everything BEHIND it still has a non-zero box and display:block. Occlusion is invisible to every property I was checking. For any walk that must distinguish what a person can SEE, the test is document.elementFromPoint at the element's centre (or Playwright's own visibility + an overlay check), not the element's own style. Neither of today's banked findings rests on this - both were confirmed against source or DB - but the probe would have reported a retired page as a live one. || ★THE THREE PROBE FAILURES BECAME ONE TOOL (2026-08-28). Three false alarms in a single session, each caught only because the finding was verified a second way, were all the same mistake wearing different clothes: asking the DOM a question that SOUNDS like 'is this visible' and is not. innerText falls back to textContent on non-rendered elements (a display:none banner read as 'You're offline' on an online page); a bounding box says nothing about OCCLUSION (marketplace-admin's live figures read straight through a position:fixed inset:0 z-index:100000 retirement overlay); and a top-N sample is not a page (project-report's 'No project specified' and 'not found' refusals sat below the cut, and I nearly filed a defect against a page that had already solved it). tools/walk_page.mjs replaces the ad-hoc scripts with the one check that answers all three: for each candidate, is document.elementFromPoint at its own centre itself or a descendant? That single question accounts for display, visibility, zero boxes, off-screen position AND occlusion. It also returns `dropped` alongside the lines, because a caller who cannot see that a result was truncated cannot tell a page from a sample. VALIDATED against both pages that fooled the old method: resume now returns its real controls with no phantom offline banner (dropped 29, disclosed), and marketplace-admin returns ONLY the retirement overlay with dropped 0 - the occluded admin figures correctly absent. Every remaining walk in this programme should use it. || ★THE n=1 GRAMMAR PROBE COMES BACK ALMOST CLEAN, AND THE ONE EXCEPTION IS FIXED (2026-08-28). Swept every page for the naive shape - a count concatenated straight onto a plural noun - and the platform is in good order: alert-hub branches on n===1 seven times, analytics and analytics-report six each, ai-quality twice, achievements once. Somebody has cared about this consistently. Exactly ONE site had not: audit-log's filter summary built 'N of M entries' unconditionally, so a log holding a single entry read '1 of 1 entries'. ★A DETAIL WORTH GETTING RIGHT RATHER THAN JUST PLURALISING: the noun belongs to the TOTAL, not the filtered count, so the branch is on _entries.length - '1 of 1 entry' is correct while '1 of 3 entry' would not be. A careless fix here would have pluralised on items.length and produced a new wrong sentence in a different place. Re-swept after: zero naive concatenations remain in any user-facing string. ★SCOPE, STATED: this sweep catches `count + ' noun'`. A plural built inside a template literal would not match, so 'clean' here means clean of THIS shape rather than of every possible one - the n=1 rendering of list cards, empty-vs-one layouts and sort controls at a single row are the rest of this trajectory's cardinality question and are not claimed. pct 70 -> 82. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate counted-noun-ratchet re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Dates, times & the PHT lens
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, Playwright clock.install + fastForward on logbook): temporal REFRESH machinery exists and fires - under a controlled +2h fast-forward, a timer-driven repaint ran and painted TODAY date-group headers that were not in the pre-forward read (something in the page re-derives temporal groupings as time passes rather than freezing the load-time rendering). The canonical whFmtDate + the two-clocks lesson stand as prior receipts. Remaining: the midnight-PHT boundary flip probe (23:58 -> 00:02 'today/yesterday' regroup), relative-time STALENESS assertions per surface ('5m ago' after an hour open), viewer-TZ policy statement, week-start (Monday PH) checks, date-input locale probes (wave close). TWO TEMPORAL PROBES RUN 2026-08-26 with Playwright clock control. (1) MIDNIGHT BOUNDARY: CORRECT - an entry stamped 23:50 reads 'Today' at 23:58 and 'Yesterday' at 00:02; the dayLabel toDateString comparison regroups exactly at the local day flip, no off-by-one. (2) RELATIVE-TIME STALENESS on a page held open: labels are computed AT RENDER, and a grep across every page finds NO timer that re-renders them - the periodic timers that exist are data refreshes (alert-hub 60s loadAll, analytics status bar, marketplace service tracking) which incidentally repaint their own labels. So a surface that neither polls nor receives a realtime event shows a frozen 'x ago' until something else re-renders it. Severity is honest: the platform's visible labels are mostly DAY-granularity ('49d ago'), where an hour of drift is invisible; the exposure is minute-granularity labels on a long-open board. Probe lessons: my first staleness probe matched SCRIPT and JSON-LD text (childElementCount===0 does not mean visible), and the second compared a pre-render empty read against a post-render one - render timing masquerading as refresh. Remaining: a minute-granularity staleness case on a seeded fresh entry, viewer-TZ policy statement, week-start checks, date-input locale probes. || WEEK-START AND DATE-INPUT LOCALE: BOTH CLEAN, AND THE SECOND ANSWER ONLY BECAME TRUE AFTER I FIXED MY OWN REGEX (2026-08-27). WEEK START - the Philippine norm is Monday, and dayplanner carries the ISO idiom explicitly: `const dow = today.getDay() || 7; // Sun=7 instead of 0`, which maps Monday=1..Sunday=7 rather than JS's Sunday=0. The only other getDay() uses are days[d.getDay()] label lookups, which carry no week-start assumption at all. DATE INPUTS - every real date field uses a native <input type="date">, so the rendered format is the browser's locale job and the value is always ISO yyyy-mm-dd on the wire; there is no hand-rolled text date field to disagree with a Filipino user's dd/mm reading. ★THE FIRST PASS SAID OTHERWISE AND WAS WRONG BY SUBSTRING: matching (date|day|when|due|start|end) anywhere in the tag reported THREE type=text date fields in asset-hub - and all three were prose. 'ask-input' matched the word 'When' in a free-text question ('When did this asset last fail? Why?'), and BOTH rcm fields matched 'end' inside 'trend' ('Vibration trend at bearing housing'). Re-run with word boundaries and restricted to id/name/aria-label rather than placeholder prose: 4 date fields, all native, zero non-native. A pattern without   does not search for a word, it searches for letters - the same class as this session's plural census and the role=tab comment match. Remaining: the minute-granularity staleness case on a seeded fresh entry, and the viewer-TZ policy statement. || ★THE DEVICE'S CLOCK REACHES PERSISTED BUSINESS TIMESTAMPS - and the platform already knows the cure, it just applied it unevenly (2026-08-28). Hunted the dangerous half of the temporal lens: not how times are RENDERED, but which ones are WRITTEN from the client. Found client-computed new Date().toISOString() flowing into DB writes across marketplace.html, marketplace-seller.html, marketplace-admin.html, logbook.html, inventory.html and project-manager.html - and crucially not only into updated_at housekeeping but into MEANINGFUL business columns: settled_at and cancelled_at on service_requests. ★WHY IT BITES: service_requests carries SIXTEEN triggers - settlement commission, cashback minting, payment guards, push fanout - and NOT ONE of them is a touch trigger, so a client-supplied timestamp is stored exactly as sent. Compare projects, which HAS trg_projects_updated_at and therefore overrides whatever the browser claims. The platform already knows this pattern and simply did not apply it to the marketplace tables (marketplace_orders, marketplace_listings, service_providers are likewise untouched). service_requests even has 2 columns defaulting to now(), so server-authoritative time is the established convention on that very table - just not for these columns. ★IMPACT IS REAL, NOT THEORETICAL: sweep_service_completions reads settled_at/cancelled_at, so a phone whose clock is wrong - common, and the premise of this trajectory's sibling T150 - can shift when a request is swept, on the same table whose objection and settlement windows the marketplace's fairness rests on. ★NOT FIXED IN THIS PASS, deliberately and with the reason stated: the fix is a touch trigger (or a DEFAULT now() plus dropping the column from the client payload) on the MOST guard-dense table in the schema, where a new trigger's firing order against sixteen existing ones - settlement, reservation release, availability sync, push fanout - decides whether it helps or breaks writes that already work. That is precisely the class recorded in [[feedback_a_new_guard_breaks_the_triggers_that_already_write]], and it deserves its own careful slice with a per-trigger interaction walk rather than being appended to a turn that already landed one migration. The evidence above is what that slice starts from. ★SCOPE CORRECTION applied while measuring: community.html:2290's created_at: new Date() is an OPTIMISTIC local row unshifted into the rendered list, not a DB write, and was excluded - a grep for this pattern catches UI objects and persistence with equal enthusiasm. pct 68 -> 80. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - dates/times honor the PHT lens: temporal-answer-names-its-window + temporal-orchestrator prove a temporal answer decomposes its window correctly, not off a raw client clock. Gates [temporal-answer-names-its-window, temporal-orchestrator] registered + PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Numbers, units & rounding truth
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, one-datum three-way parity, worker 390): the hive's open-jobs count read from v_logbook_truth (9) EQUALS index's ops-home tile ('9 OPEN JOBS') - live rendered==DB parity on the headline datum (my logbook stat-pill read missed only because I guessed the wrong element id - instrument, not page). The units machinery stands (units_visible x3 gates, counted-noun discipline, whFmtPeso). Remaining: the cross-surface numeric-parity MATRIX (same datum, every rendering - index/logbook/analytics/asset-hub), rounding-consistency sweep (sum-of-rounded vs rounded-sum), currency formatting census, precision-to-domain review (0.1h vs 6min) (wave close).  || CURRENCY-FORMATTING CENSUS DONE 2026-08-26 and it found REAL money defects on three surfaces. whFmtPeso exists for one recorded reason: Number(null) is 0 and finite, so a null amount renders as a confident PHP0.00 - a filed top-up of PHP300 once did exactly that. THE FINDINGS: (1) FOUNDER-CONSOLE, the owner's own cockpit, had ZERO adoption and a formatter that was literally Number(n || 0) - the bug itself - while the same file already carried a note saying a money number frozen at zero 'does not read as by design, it reads as a feed that died'; its GCash top-up row used Number(r.amount) with no null guard, so an absent amount printed NaN on the screen where money enters the business. (2) MARKETPLACE-SELLER's earnings formatter used Number(n), printing NaN on the dashboard of the person being PAID. (3) MARKETPLACE's service picker guarded `<= 0`, which catches null (Number(null) is 0) but NOT undefined - NaN <= 0 is FALSE - so an absent rate reached a buyer as NaN. All routed through the helper; five money pages verified live with 0 pageerrors. ★THE GATE'S OWN FIRST RUN PRODUCED FOUR FALSE POSITIVES AND I DID NOT ACT ON THEM: a ternary spans lines, so the GUARDED FALLBACK half of `whFmtPeso(n) : '<peso>' + Number(n||0)` looked hand-rolled because the helper sat on the line above. 'Fixing' those would have damaged correct code whose fallback exists precisely so a page still renders when utils.js has not loaded - verify the instrument before the page. LOCKED BY gate money-formatting, scoped to money surfaces with the one deliberate local formatter allowlisted by name and reason (platform-actions' measured 'Negotiable (listed at PHP0)' branch). Remaining: the cross-surface numeric-parity MATRIX, rounding consistency (sum-of-rounded vs rounded-sum), and precision-to-domain review. || ROUNDING CONSISTENCY PROBED STATICALLY, PLUS THE FORMATTER-ADOPTION CENSUS (2026-08-27). Checked first for the sharpest version of the defect - the SAME metric rendered at different precision on different pages, which makes two surfaces appear to disagree about one number. Across mtbf/mttr/oee/compliance/availability/downtime/spi/cpi, only MTBF is formatted through an explicit .toFixed and it is precision 1 at both sites: no inconsistency found by that probe. ★BUT THE PROBE COVERS ONE IDIOM, so 'no finding' is not 'no defect'. The census: toFixed( 694 uses across 25 pages, Math.round( 336 across 42, toLocaleString 123 across 14, against whFmtPeso 49 across 12 and whFmtNum 30 across 7 - the platform HAS a formatter family in utils.js (whFmtNum/Peso/Date/Duration/Ago) and roughly 6% of numeric rendering goes through it. That is not automatically a defect: a one-off toFixed on a locally computed value is fine, and T133's property is that ONE DATUM reads the same everywhere, not that every call site uses the helper. ★WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY THE IDIOM COUNT CANNOT SETTLE IT - the parity question is about a VALUE traced across surfaces (the same MTBF on index, analytics and asset-hub), and no amount of counting format calls answers it. Remaining: the cross-surface numeric-parity MATRIX as a LIVE trace (same datum, every rendering, compared), which is deferred past the running board rather than run against a shared local stack a gate is querying; plus sum-of-rounded vs rounded-sum and the precision-to-domain review. || THE CROSS-SURFACE MATRIX RAN, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IT FOUND IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN ARITHMETIC (2026-08-27). Traced four data against DB truth across index, asset-hub, inventory and hive. Inventory (27) and open logbook entries (9) agree exactly. ASSETS DO NOT: index shows 'PM OVERDUE (29 OF 30 ASSETS)' while asset-hub shows 'TOTAL ASSETS 25'. ★NEITHER PAGE IS INTERNALLY WRONG - THEY COUNT DIFFERENT REGISTRIES. pm_assets holds 30 rows; asset_nodes holds 30 rows of which 25 are approved (the rest pending or rejected), and asset-hub counts only approved. So the word 'assets' means PM-schedule rows on one page and approved asset nodes on the other, and a supervisor comparing the two sees their plant contain 30 machines or 25 depending which page they are on, with nothing on either explaining the difference. ★AND THE TWO REGISTRIES ARE NOT LINKED: pm_assets has NO foreign key to asset_nodes - it carries its own asset_name, tag_id, location, category - yet they describe the SAME machines: 21 distinct names on each side, all 21 present in both, zero exclusive to pm_assets. Two tables, one plant, joined only by a string. That is the name-is-not-an-identity shape at the schema level, and it is why the counts can drift apart silently: nothing structurally forces them to agree, so a rename or a rejected asset moves one number and not the other. ★MY PROBE ALSO NEARLY FILED THE WRONG BUG: the regex matched '30 ASSETS' out of a PM-overdue sentence and compared it to the approved-asset count, which is comparing two different things and calling it a defect. Reading the actual line is what turned a false arithmetic claim into a true structural one. Remaining: the naming/denominator decision (do these two counts need one vocabulary, or one registry), plus sum-of-rounded vs rounded-sum and the precision-to-domain review. || ★ROUNDING-CONSISTENCY SWEEP: A CLEAN NEGATIVE, RECORDED AS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN SILENCE (2026-08-28). This trajectory's sharpest probe is 'the same value rounded differently on two surfaces = apparent disagreement'. Swept every .toFixed() call across all root pages plus utils.js and voice-handler.js, resolving each to the EXPRESSION being rounded and grouping by domain metric (mtbf, mttr, oee, availability, compliance, risk_score, uptime, performance, quality, confidence). Two candidates surfaced and BOTH survive inspection as deliberate, not drifted: (1) analytics-report renders MTBF at 0dp on line 1228 and 1dp on lines 1563/1692/1695/1805 — but 1228 is `mtbfDays`, the FLEET AGGREGATE headline, while the others are `p.mtbf_days` / `r.mtbf_days`, PER-ASSET detail. Different variables, different scopes; a coarse headline over fine detail is an editorial choice, and no single value is shown twice at two precisions. (2) risk_score is 2dp in voice-handler's AI grounding and 0dp in the report — grounding wants precision for a model, a report wants readability for a person, and again it is not one value rendered two ways. `compliance` is consistent at 0dp throughout. ★RECORDED BECAUSE A NEGATIVE THAT WENT UNRECORDED IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A PROBE NEVER RUN — the sweep happened, the method is repeatable, and the answer is that this class is currently clean. My first pass at this DID produce false hits ('class', 'const', 'null') by capturing whatever token preceded .toFixed rather than the rounded expression; those were discarded as instrument noise, not filed. The un-swept remainder of this trajectory is sum-of-rounded vs rounded-sum and currency formatting, which this scan does not reach. || ★I BROKE THIS TRAJECTORY'S OWN RULE AND ITS GATE CAUGHT ME (2026-08-28). Earlier in this same session I added a mint-voucher confirm to founder-console - a good change, naming the consequence before a live discount code exists - and built its terms string by hand: kind === 'percent' ? value + '%% off' : '₱' + value + ' off'. The money-formatting gate went RED on it within the hour, on the exact ground this trajectory was written to defend: an absent value renders as '₱ off' or '₱undefined off' instead of a gap, and whFmtPeso exists precisely so that absent and zero stop looking alike. The same file already used the helper six times; I reached for string concatenation anyway. ★FIXED and re-verified PASS ('5 money surfaces render amounts through the helper that tells absent from zero'). ★THE PART WORTH KEEPING: this is what a gate is FOR, and it is a stronger endorsement of the rule than any of my earlier reasoning about it. The confirm I wrote is the last thing an owner reads before minting a code that costs real money on every redemption - the single worst place on the platform for a number that renders confidently and wrongly - and I still had to be caught by the machine rather than by care. A rule that only holds while its author is paying attention is not a rule; the gate is what makes it one. pct 70 -> 84. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate money-formatting re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Media truth: photos at scale and in trouble
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, live gauntlet on logbook's photo capture, worker 390): OVERSIZE (21MB fixture) -> humane refusal WITH the limit stated ('Photo too large (max 20 MB).') and the input CLEARED for retry; WRONG FORMAT (a PDF wearing image bytes) -> the pipeline attempts compression then announces honestly ('Could not read the photo: Image decode failed'), no preview, no crash, zero pageerrors. The 5MB tier guard exists on the entry-photo path (logbook:3637) and the compression-fallback refusal at 5051. NIT: 'Image decode failed' is slightly technical (names the truth, could name the remedy). Remaining: mid-upload interruption (T122 choreography), photo-in-offline-queue (T14 seam), storage-full injection, deletion-deletes-storage verification (T164 seam), thumbnail strategy under throttle (wave close). DELETION-DELETES-STORAGE PROBED + FIXED 2026-08-26: platform-wide there was NO storage delete ANYWHERE (only two upload sites, both marketplace), and the marketplace-listings bucket is PUBLIC - so deleting a listing left its photo permanently reachable by URL while the confirm said 'This cannot be undone', true of the row and quietly false of the image. FIXED: handleDelete now derives the object key from the public URL minted at upload (bucket/<uuid>.jpg) and removes it AFTER the row delete, best-effort so a storage hiccup can never block the delete the person asked for. PROVEN live end-to-end: probe object uploaded, the SAME key-derivation returned the exact key, remove() succeeded, storage.objects back to 0 probe rows. Remaining: mid-upload interruption (T122 choreography), photo-in-offline-queue (T14 seam), storage-full injection, thumbnail strategy under throttle. FIX-EVERY-PATH pass same day: the orphan had a SECOND, more frequent source - REPLACING a listing image on edit left the old object in the public bucket, and edits run far more often than deletes. Now cleaned on the edit path too, guarded so it only removes when the URL actually changed AND the old object is ours (a seller may paste an external URL), best-effort after the row update so cleanup can never cost the seller their edit. Coverage CHECKED not assumed: marketplace.html's two delete sites are saved-searches and watchlist rows - neither deletes a listing - so the seller page owns both image lifecycles. || LOCKED 2026-08-28. Both image lifecycles were fixed and left ungated - and this is the class where an ungated fix is most likely to half-rot, because the two blocks are NEAR-IDENTICAL and sit far apart in one file: an edit to one reads as complete. Gate a-removed-image-actually-leaves requires TWO remove() sites, the edit path's changed-and-ours guards, and TWO best-effort catch blocks so cleanup can never throw into the write. Selftest 5/5. ★AND ITS OWNERSHIP NEGATIVE WAS VACUOUS ON THE FIRST CUT for the same reason the code was fragile: a whole-file search for indexOf(_marker) is satisfied by the DELETE path's own copy, so deleting the EDIT path's guard left the file matching and the test passed while detecting nothing. Scoped to the edit block. Remaining: storage-full injection, thumbnail strategy under throttle (T37's lane). pct -> 82. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Legacy import: the Excel plant onboards
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, premise resolved POSITIVE): the CSV import EXISTS on integrations.html - PapaParse (CSV) + SheetJS (xlsx) lazy-loaded after file pick (A4 CWV discipline), the cmms_import_v1 capture contract governs the payload, and the copy matches the learn cluster's migration promise ('Export a CSV and upload it here. One upload brings your whole history into WorkHive') plus the post-import Live Sync story - the cmms-vs-excel content's claim has a real implementation behind it (claim-honesty resolves clean). Remaining: the MESSY-CSV walk (naming chaos fixture through the import - preview/consent per T92's bars, duplicate-name handling T127, encoding survival T128), field-mapping ergonomics, a failed-row report probe (wave close).  || WALKED LIVE 2026-08-26, AND THE TRAJECTORY'S PREMISE IS REFUTED. The spec expected the import path to be ABSENT and this trajectory to end as a scoped product decision with the learn articles' claims trued down. The opposite is true: integrations.html ships a working CSV/Excel importer, and the learn-page claims about it are ACCURATE. Driven as an operator, not by poking internals: pick a source system (sap_pm / maximo / generic / auto) -> pick an entity (work_order / asset / pm_schedule / inventory) -> upload -> Step 3 field mapping. A generic asset export (asset_id, name, type, location, manufacturer) came back with 5 OF 5 COLUMNS AUTO-MAPPED CORRECTLY (external_id<-asset_id, name<-name, type<-type, location<-location, manufacturer<-manufacturer), 0 pageerrors. The specific marketing claim - 'The CSV importer includes a visual column-mapping step' - is TRUE: buildMappingTable() renders a map-table with a per-field select, a confidence cell and a preview table, plus an Auto-suggest button backed by per-system dictionaries (SAP's EQNR/EQKTX, Maximo's ASSETNUM, and a generic set). ★FOUR INSTRUMENT ERRORS ON THE WAY, NONE BANKED, and they are the reusable lesson for this page: (1) I counted '.map-table select' when the matcher keys on [data-field]; (2) I jumped straight to goStep(3), leaving _entityType at its work_order default while feeding ASSET headers, which correctly matched almost nothing; (3) I set window._entityType and read window._headers when the real state lives in CLOSURE variables inside the page's IIFE - unreachable from outside; (4) I tried to click the entity cards before choosing a SOURCE, and #entity-section is display:none until then. Every apparent failure was mine; the product was correct each time. Remaining: the post-import verification walk (do the rows land as approved/pending assets, and is the T92 consent/preview bar met), and the SAP/Maximo dictionary accuracy against a real export. (Recorded as WALKED/25 rather than a higher pct: the registry's own gate refused 'walked' with pct 40, and it was right to - the pct is a status marker, not a quality score, and no product fix was needed because nothing was broken. The depth of the walk belongs in this basis, not in a number that would imply fixes that do not exist.) || THE POST-IMPORT VERIFICATION WALK IS DONE, AND IT FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN THE CONSENT SURFACE (2026-08-28). Drove the whole five-step wizard live as the supervisor with a 4-column Maximo asset export. WHERE THE ROWS LAND, answering this trajectory's own question: as status 'approved', NOT pending - submitted_by and approved_by both the importer, approved_at set, so a bulk import bypasses the review queue by design. Provenance IS kept (external_ids {source_external_id}, plus an external_sync row per asset and one cmms_audit_log entry), which is what makes the auto-approval defensible rather than silent; whether an import SHOULD bypass review is a product decision, not a defect, and it is recorded here rather than changed. ★THE DEFECT IS WHAT THE PREVIEW DOES NOT SAY. Step 4 warned when a WORKHIVE FIELD had no source column and NEVER when a SOURCE COLUMN had no WorkHive field - the first protects the schema, the second protects the user's data, and carrying data across is the whole point of a legacy import. MEASURED: my export's EQTYPE header is in neither dictionary, so all three assets landed iso_class 'General' with the equipment type simply gone, under a preview reading '3 rows - 3 ready to import - all valid' and an EMPTY warnings box. Someone bringing five years of plant history across has no other moment to notice a column did not make the trip. FIXED: the preview now names every unmapped source column and points at Step 3 - live 'i 1 column in your file is not mapped and will not be imported: EQTYPE.' Deliberately INFO, not a warning, because an unmapped column is often intentional; it must be said, not made alarming. ★AND THE DICTIONARY IS VINDICATED, which I nearly recorded the other way: rerunning with Maximo's REAL header ASSETTYPE mapped all four columns and raised NO notice, so the dictionary knows the true column and my synthetic EQTYPE was the non-standard one - the product declined to guess, correctly. That clean-file control is now half the gate, because a notice that fires on every import is furniture nobody reads. ★A FIFTH INSTRUMENT ERROR for this page's list: my first Import click used a has-text selector that never reached startImport(), so the walk reported 'results not shown' with the DB untouched - I checked the baseline before believing it had failed. Locked as gate import-names-dropped-columns (6 assertions, teeth-proven: disabling the notice fails exactly the three that assert it), and READ-ONLY by construction - it stops at the preview, verified leaving the DB at its 96/16/14 baseline. STATUS locking/80: the walk and the consent fix are done and gated; the SAP dictionary still wants a real export to check against, which needs a file I do not have. || ★THE UNDO DID THE REVERSE OF ITS JOB - THE SESSION'S WORST DEFECT, FOUND BY PULLING ON THE CONFIRM COPY (2026-08-28). Sweeping confirms for 'names a control that does not exist' I read rollbackBatch's text: it promises to remove 'the corresponding rows created in that batch'. Its query matched target rows by worker_name + created_at BETWEEN the audit row's timestamp and +5min, and BOTH HALVES FAIL, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. The audit row is written AFTER the data rows - measured 51.3ms for asset_nodes and 88ms for external_sync - so every row the import created sits just BEFORE the window and .gte() excludes it; meanwhile anything the same person creates in the following five minutes is INSIDE it. MEASURED END TO END: imported 2 assets, hand-made 1 unrelated asset 10s later, pressed undo - the two IMPORTED assets SURVIVED, the unrelated one was DESTROYED, and the toast said 'Import rolled back successfully.' The control a person reaches for in a panic deleted the wrong data and reported success. Work orders were worse: logbook rows carry the SOURCE system's created_at (often years old) and logbook has NO external-id column, so an import-time window can never match them - that path was a guaranteed no-op. ★FIXED by matching BATCH MEMBERSHIP instead of time: external_sync is now READ before it is deleted (hence the order read -> targets -> sync -> audit), each entity's key recomputed exactly as the import wrote it (asset->tag, inventory->part_number, pm_schedule->tag_id from the stored payload), and the read is bounded by the batch's own recorded rows_written - the last N sync rows at-or-before the audit stamp ARE that batch, and the limit stops it reaching into an earlier one. Work-order rollbacks now SAY they cannot remove logbook entries automatically rather than silently no-op'ing, and the toast reports the count actually removed instead of a flat success. MEASURED AFTER: 'Import rolled back - 2 imported rows removed', with the bystander the only survivor. ★A NEARBY DESIGN GAP RECORDED, NOT FIXED: external_sync carries a workhive_id column meant for exactly this linkage and the importer never populates it; filling it at import time would make the rollback exact rather than merely bounded, but it changes the write path for all four entity types and this fix was already load-bearing. Locked as gate import-undo-removes-the-import (7 assertions, keeps a BYSTANDER row present throughout because 'the import was removed' and 'nothing else was' are two different claims; resurrection-proven - restoring the inverted window reddens exactly the imported-rows-gone and row-count assertions; writes and cleans up after itself, asserting no WH-PROBE-UNDOGATE row survives). pct 80 -> 92. || CLASS SWEPT, not just the instance (2026-08-28): the danger was never 'a time window' - most of the ~25 .gte('created_at') uses on the platform are relative DISPLAY windows ('last 7 days', 'today') where a row falling outside simply is not shown and nothing is lost. What made the rollback different is that it was a DESTRUCTIVE operation bounded by a window anchored on a record written AFTER its own subjects. Swept for that exact shape - a .delete() paired with any time bound - across every html/js file: ZERO remain. The rollback was the only one, so the class is extinct rather than the single case being patched. pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★PREMISE REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, and worth recording as such rather than inventing a gap. The spec expected the answer to be 'no import path exists, so true up the learn articles' claims and spec one for Ian'. It exists and it WORKS. Driven live: integrations.html step 2 accepts a CSV through #file-input (PapaParse + SheetJS, lazy-loaded only after a file is chosen), and a 2-row/4-column CMMS export was read back as 'csv 2 rows - 4 columns - detected as GENERIC' with a Map Fields step offered next. 0 page errors. The first probe reported nothing because it set the file input while the wizard was still on step 1 - the wizard was right and the probe was wrong, which is the usual direction. AND THE CLAIMS ARE TRUE: connecting-workhive-to-sap-maximo-cmms promises 'batch CSV export and import for plants without API access', which is exactly what ships; cmms-vs-excel is cautionary ('do not attempt a full-plant migration'), not overselling. Nothing to true up here - the claim-honesty defect on this subject was on integrations.html's SYNC CADENCE and is fixed under T63. REMAINS: the mapping and commit steps (3-5), which write data and need probe hygiene; duplicate/merge consent on import (the T92 seam); and what an import does to a hive that already has assets.

trajectories.title: Seed/demo data honesty
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, 8-table probe-marker sweep on the local DB): ONE leaked probe row found and removed - a pm_completion from 2026-08-19 ('probe: checked, within tolerance', a prior session's residue; compliance recomputes on next read) - all other tables CLEAN (logbook/inventory/community/project_items/fmea/inquiries/schedule_items = 0), confirming this session's per-walk cleanup discipline held. Example-labeling: the Weibull worked-example pattern (Example... prefixed, baseline-exempt) verified in T26's walk; empty-state illustrations render as sentences, not fake rows. Remaining: the PROD sweep (Ian-gated - the prod smoke hive is his to delete), the sweep formalized as a scheduled gate (probe_marker_sweep in the Platform group), example-labeling coverage across the other worked-example surfaces (wave close).  || THE SWEEP WIDENED 2026-08-26 AND FOUND 245 SURVIVING MARKER ROWS. The earlier pass checked 8 tables and called them clean; a sweep across EVERY text column of the user-facing tables found: 3 rows in VOICE_JOURNAL_ENTRIES - probe transcripts AND the AI's replies to them, sitting in the platform's most private surface, inside a worker's own journal; 1 in LOGBOOK.knowledge ('probe: checked, within tolerance') - and note T136's earlier pass found and removed the pm_completion TWIN of that exact probe and missed the logbook copy, so one probe had two homes; and 241 in HIVE_AUDIT_LOG. ★THE AUDIT ROWS WERE MINE, FROM THE SAME DAY, and they are the lesson: my pending-submission prover created probe assets and deleted them, and the audit trigger honestly recorded every deletion. Those rows are TRUE - they describe things that really happened - but they describe objects that were never real, in a compliance-class table that the retention gate I built hours earlier correctly forbids any scheduled job from purging. A PROBE THAT TOUCHES AN AUDITED TABLE LEAVES RESIDUE ITS OWN CLEANUP CANNOT REACH, because the residue lands in a DIFFERENT table than the one it wrote to. Removing it required a deliberate, scoped, one-time delete - never a cron. AND THE GATE EARNED ITS KEEP ON ITS FIRST RUN: after my targeted WH-T108B cleanup it still found 34 rows under a marker I had not thought of (WH-EFFECT-PROBE, dating to 2026-08-18), proving the point that per-walk memory is not a mechanism. All 245 now removed and re-counted to zero; hive_audit_log holds 8,840 genuine rows. LOCKED BY gate no-probe-residue, scoped to user-facing tables and deliberately NOT the seeder's fixtures, since demo DATA is legitimate and a gate that could not tell seeded plant data from probe residue would fire forever. Remaining: the PROD marker sweep (Ian-gated) and the example-labeling check. || ★TWO GATES WERE FAILING ON DIRTY STATE, AND CLEARING THEM CHANGED A VERDICT (2026-08-28). This trajectory's own gate, no-probe-residue, was RED on one row: a hive_audit_log entry 'create_inventory_item / WH-EFFECT-PROBE-72872' from 2026-08-26, left behind when a scoped cleanup removed the inventory item but not the audit trail of its creation (0 live items carry the marker now, so the row was genuinely orphaned). One row is not much until you consider where it sits: a supervisor reading their plant's audit log saw a part creation that never happened. Removed; the gate is PASS. ★AND THE SECOND ONE MATTERED MORE. validate_cold_page_teaches was also RED, but not because a page failed - it REFUSED TO MEASURE, aborting because a probe account (wh-t175-probe@auth.workhiveph.com, 2026-08-27) was still standing. That is the right behaviour for a prover and it had a cost nobody had paid: with the gate silent, I had spent this same session concluding from ABSENCE that per-page first-run orientation was not a platform pattern. Removing the account (2 analytics_events rows, no hive membership) and re-running produced the real reading - 19 pages walked cold, 0 near-empty, 0 throwing - which REFUTES what I had written and corrected T175 from 72 to 88. ★THE POINT FOR THIS TRAJECTORY: probe residue is not only a cosmetic pollution of user-facing data. A leftover probe object also DISABLES the instrument that would have told the truth, and a disabled instrument is quietly replaced by somebody's inference. Cleanup discipline protects the measurements as much as the data. pct 70 -> 92. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: cleaned the WH-EFFECT-PROBE residue this gate flagged [1 voice_journal_entries AI-reply plus 2 hive_audit_log create_inventory_item rows in the Baguio hive] via a verified DELETE; no-probe-residue now PASSES. trajectories.title: Archive & retention: where old data goes
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25, policy<->behavior parity walk): retention IS stated on the glass (privacy policy: account purge within 30 days, compliance records 10/15 years; the Data retention section exists) and EIGHT retention crons actually run (gateway-audit, agent-memory, route-calls, xp-log purge, soft-expired hard-delete, embedding-cache, amc/parts-recs expiry). THE PARITY DEFECT, fixed: the policy claimed 'voice recordings are retained for 90 days... then automatically deleted' while the PRODUCT stores no audio at all (voice-journal's own code-verified disclosure: 'your voice recording is not kept' - no storage.upload anywhere, no audio column, the transcribe fn writes no bucket) - an aspirational claim telling users their voice is KEPT when it is discarded immediately; corrected to the truth ('transcribed and immediately discarded; only the text transcript is saved'). Remaining: the per-class retention statement audit (does each cron's window match a stated policy line), archive reachability (cold-archive-query, T91 seam), deletion-vs-archive vocabulary sweep (wave close).  || PER-CLASS RETENTION AUDIT DONE 2026-08-26 and the policy MATCHES the system. Five retention crons exist; every one purges a TECHNICAL or DERIVED table (achievement_xp_log 90d, agent_memory 90d, embedding_cache 45d, gateway_audit_log 365d, hive_route_calls 48h). NOT ONE touches a compliance-class record - zero crons delete from logbook, pm_completions or hive_audit_log, and hive_audit_log holds 9,019 rows with nothing scheduled to remove them - so the policy's 10-year/15-year compliance promise is currently kept. LOCKED, because that agreement is an ACCIDENT of nobody having written the cron: purging old logbook rows to save space is exactly what gets added on a slow afternoon, and the moment it lands a legal document about DOLE OSHS and ISO compliance becomes false with no user-visible symptom - the records that would prove a plant's maintenance history in a regulatory dispute being precisely the ones nobody notices missing until they are needed. Gate retention-matches-policy fails on any scheduled delete from a compliance-class table, SKIPS rather than passes if the policy sentence disappears (so it cannot go quietly vacuous), and deliberately does NOT assert record ages, since nothing is 10 years old yet and that check would pass forever while measuring nothing. Teeth-proven by scheduling a 2-year logbook purge: RED, then unscheduled and verified gone. ★BOTH REMAINING ITEMS CLOSED 2026-08-27: archive reachability ANSWERED (reachable through the assistant's cold_archive route, 18-month boundary, wired in agentic-rag-loop - not a UI control, which is a product question rather than a defect), and the deletion-vs-archive vocabulary sweep DONE (soft-delete jargon reworded on 3 surfaces + 2 in index, and the jargon gate taught a dev_compound rule so the term cannot return).
