trajectories.note: ★'SOFT-DELETE' WAS DEVELOPER JARGON WEARING AN ENGLISH FACE (2026-08-27). The deletion-vs-archive vocabulary sweep found the platform says 'delete' 22 times to 'archive' 3, and only two tables actually soft-delete (community_posts.deleted_at, projects.deleted_at) - so the words are broadly honest. What was NOT honest was the term itself: five user-facing strings said 'soft-delete', including the project DELETE CONFIRM ('Soft-delete project PRJ-1? It will be hidden from views'), a retention explainer, a table row label, and twice in index's feature copy. ★THE COPY WAS ALREADY TRUTHFUL, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A WORDING FIX AND NOT A TRUST FIX - the confirm does say 'hidden from views'. The defect is that a supervisor deciding whether to press the button had to know what a developer means by 'soft', and the meaning most people would guess ('less permanent') is right by accident rather than by being told. Now: 'Hide project X? It disappears from every view, and its record is kept so it can be brought back.' - the behaviour, not the technique. ★AND THE JARGON GATE COULD NOT SEE IT, which is the transferable part: every one of its rules catches an IDENTIFIER - snake_case, camelCase, fn(), *.md, v_*_truth, named edge functions - so a phrase built from ordinary words and a hyphen walks straight past a gate whose entire job is keeping developer language off the glass, on pages it already covered. Added a dev_compound rule (soft/hard-delete, upsert, backfill, idempotent), and it immediately caught two MORE instances in index.html that I had not found by grepping - the gate finding what the author missed, one minute after being taught. ★ARCHIVE REACHABILITY: REACHABLE, AND I NEARLY FILED THE OPPOSITE (2026-08-27). Grepping the PAGES for cold-archive-query returns ZERO callers, which reads exactly like the built-but-never-called class - a capability the platform paid for that nobody can open. Widening the grep past *.html to *.ts changed the answer: supabase/functions/agentic-rag-loop/index.ts routes to it deliberately, with 'cold_archive' in its route enum, the instruction 'question is about events older than 18 months', and a defensive 18-month boundary check for when the router gets it wrong. So the archive IS reachable - through the ASSISTANT, which is the T91 temporal-RAG path and an intended design rather than an accident. ★THE NEAR-MISS IS THE LESSON: a capability absent from every page is not an absent capability, and 'grep for it before recording it as missing' is the rule that saved a fabricated finding here. Two greps apart. ★WHAT IS GENUINELY OPEN is narrower and is a product question, not a defect: there is no DIRECT control - no 'show me January 2025' browse affordance - so a person who wants old data has to know to ask the assistant for it. Whether the assistant should be the only door to 18-month-old records is Ian's call; the door exists and works. ★LOCKED (2026-08-27): THE DONE-DEFINITION IS 'DATA LIFECYCLES STATED AND TRUE', AND BOTH HALVES HOLD. Gate retention-matches-policy runs green - the stated retention matches the behaviour, which is the whole bar - and user-facing-jargon green alongside it. The note already classifies what is left in its own words: 'WHAT IS GENUINELY OPEN is narrower and is a product question, not a defect' - there is no DIRECT archive-browse control, no 'show me January' affordance. trajectories.title: Concurrent edits on the SAME record
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, OC-guard census): concurrency protection exists on TWO edit surfaces - inventory's part edit via the CENTRAL ocUpdate helper (utils.js; conflict -> reload-and-merge message) and project-manager's scope-item edit via a HAND-ROLLED updated_at eq guard + 0-row detection ('Scope item was modified by someone else, reload to see the latest') - note the hand-rolled one should migrate to ocUpdate per the install-the-guard lesson. The OTHER mutable-record edits (logbook entry amend, dayplanner items, community post edit, PM scope edits) are presumed LAST-WRITE-WINS - the enumeration + per-type concurrent-edit injection is the remaining instrument work. The APPROVAL race class is separately PROVEN (T56's true-concurrency walk: optimistic lock held, honest loser toast). Remaining: the mutable-type census completed + injections per type, stale-form detection UX where guards exist, the silent-overwrite acceptability decision per type (wave close).  || THE ENUMERATION DONE 2026-08-26, AND IT CORRECTED THIS ENTRY'S OWN CLAIM. The line above says logbook amend, dayplanner items, community post edit and PM scope edits are 'presumed LAST-WRITE-WINS'. Measured: they are not. TEN hand-rolled OC guards exist across EIGHT pages - asset-hub:3037, community:2179, founder-console:3053, integrations:1743, logbook:4417, platform-actions:1228, pm-scheduler:2216 and project-manager at 1971/2463/3208 - plus inventory through the central ocUpdate. Eleven protected edit surfaces, not two. 'Presumed' was the word doing the damage: the presumption was never checked, and it was wrong. AND THE PROPERTY THAT MATTERS HOLDS EVERYWHERE: all ten detect the ZERO-ROW case and TELL the person. That is the half that decides whether a guard helps at all - filtering on updated_at is easy, but if nothing notices the update changed nothing, the write vanishes, the form closes, and the person walks away believing they saved work that no longer exists. A guard that returns without speaking is WORSE than no guard, because it turns a visible conflict into an invisible loss. LOCKED BY gate oc-guard-speaks, which deliberately does NOT demand migration to ocUpdate - ten rewrites of live edit paths for a refactor is a bad trade, and what protects a person is that the guard SPEAKS, not that it is shared. The install-the-guard lesson still governs anything NEW. The gate would rather MISS than LIE (a 40-line window, so distant reporting reads as a miss) because its other failure mode is a false accusation about working code. Teeth-proven with an injected silent guard. Remaining: the concurrent-edit INJECTION per mutable record type - proving the guards fire under a real race, as T145 did for approvals. || THE INJECTION RAN AND FOUND A GUARD THAT COULD NEVER FIRE (2026-08-28). The census had established the CLIENT half - ten hand-rolled guards across eight pages, every one detecting the zero-row case and telling the person - and this trajectory's remainder was to prove they fire under a real race. They mostly do. ★inventory_items DID NOT: no trigger touched updated_at, and the column's DEFAULT now() applies on INSERT only, because a default is not a rule about UPDATE. So the stamp never moved, every stale stamp kept matching, and the guard passed everyone. Measured on a disposable probe row: writer A wrote, stamp did NOT move, writer B holding A's PRE-EDIT stamp still matched and overwrote A (qty 6 -> 99). Two supervisors editing one part meant the second one's number won and the first one's edit vanished with no error - and the refusal the page promises, 'Another worker just edited this part', could never render. ★THE SOURCE ASSERTED THE OPPOSITE: the comment above the call read 'inventory_items already auto-touches updated_at on every UPDATE so this works without a trigger change'. An assumption wearing the clothes of a check, and the reason the new gate asks the DATABASE rather than the page - a page cannot be wrong about its own filter, only about the world. FIXED by migration 20260828000000 (tg_inventory_items_touch_updated, additive + re-runnable, reusing the touch_updated_at() the other eight already use); comment corrected in place rather than deleted, so the false premise is recorded. ★TWO OF MY OWN HARNESS ERRORS CALLED THE FIX BROKEN FIRST: (1) both writers inside ONE DO block, where now() is the TRANSACTION clock and therefore constant, so the stamp cannot move no matter what the trigger does; (2) 'INSERT 0 1' captured along with the returned id, leaving the stamp empty and every comparison garbage. Re-raced across SEPARATE transactions, the way two clients actually behave: A rows=1 stamp MOVED, B rows=0, final qty=6 - the guard fires, A survives, B is told. The original defect stands on pg_trigger evidence, not on those runs. SCOPE, since scope is part of the claim: 9 guarded tables, 8 already correct - ONE broken surface, not a broken pattern. GATE the-concurrency-guard-can-fire registered, 9/9 green, fails CLOSED when the DB is unreachable, teeth 2/2 by dropping the trigger inside a rolled-back transaction. Remaining: the per-record-type UI conflict copy sweep at wave close. || ★★THE FINDING ABOVE IS RETRACTED - THE GUARD WAS NEVER BROKEN, AND THE DEFECT WAS MY PROBE (corrected 2026-08-28, same day). inventory.html's payload carries `updated_at: now` (inventory.html:1510), so the UPDATE it sends moves the stamp itself; the trigger was never load-bearing. My probe issued `UPDATE ... SET qty_on_hand = ...` - a statement this page never sends - and the frozen stamp I measured was an artifact of that statement, not a property of the table. Re-raced with two PRODUCT-SHAPED writers and the trigger DROPPED: A rows=1, B rows=0, final qty=6. The conflict fires on the payload alone, so 'two supervisors and the second one silently wins' never happened to anyone. RIGHT READING, WRONG SUBJECT - and the tell I walked past was that eight sibling tables had triggers while this one had shipped for months with a comment explicitly saying it did not need one; a lone survivor of a pattern usually knows something the pattern does not. WHAT SURVIVES THE RETRACTION: (1) the migration stays, reframed as HARDENING on its own merits - it makes updated_at server-authoritative instead of trusting new Date() on a client whose clock may be skewed, and it removes the guard's dependence on every future caller remembering the field, whose omission would fail SILENTLY; (2) the gate stays, reframed as a hardening RATCHET whose red means 'this table relies on caller discipline', never 'this guard is broken'; (3) the page comment is corrected to name the real mechanism, since the original's imprecision ('inventory_items already auto-touches updated_at') is what sent me hunting - it named the wrong mechanism for a TRUE conclusion. The original T138 remainder - proving the guards fire under a real race - is met: they do, on all nine. pct -> 90. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Cascade comprehension: deleting things with children
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25, confirm census + live verify): the cascade-comprehension bar was ALREADY met with class-naming on asset-hub (FMEA delete: 'Linked RCM strategies will cascade'; RCM delete: 'Linked PM scope item will remain in PM Scheduler (unlink only)' - exemplary), and the zero-row-delete honesty guard exists (PM12). THE GAP, fixed + verified: pm-scheduler's asset delete - the highest-blast-radius delete - said 'and all its PM data' (the class, not the counts); it now ENUMERATES best-effort ('Delete "Siemens Simotics SD 200L"? This removes 5 PM tasks and 16 completion records.') via head-count reads, falling back to the class wording if a count read fails; proven live and cancelled. Remaining: the FK-graph <-> confirm-text parity oracle (confirm claims audited against ON DELETE reality), logbook/project deletes' enumeration pass, orphan-verification probes per parent class (wave close). THE ORACLE BUILT + A LOADED TRAP REMOVED 2026-08-26 (gate cascade-confirm-parity): reads the LIVE FK cascade graph (27 parent tables) and audits every client delete site against the confirm guarding it. First run flagged 6; FIVE were my own instrument (the capture regex broke on backtick-template confirms containing double quotes - six correctly-worded confirms read as 'no confirm found'), and the SIXTH was real: logbook's saveAssets() - dead code, zero callers static or dynamic - carried an UNCONFIRMED delete on asset_nodes, which cascades SEVEN children (sensor_readings, weibull_fits, rcm_fmea_modes, pf_intervals, asset_embeddings, asset_edges, sensor_topic_map). Wired up later by someone reading it as the local save path it would have destroyed an asset's entire reliability history behind no confirm at all - a dead cascading delete is a loaded trap that passes review because 'it already exists'. Removed; logbook re-proven live (picker intact, 0 pageerrors). Baseline now 0, forward-only. Remaining: orphan-verification probes per parent class, the logbook/project enumeration pass. RESURRECTION PROVEN 2026-08-26 - the lock spoke's real bar, not a promise: the deleted saveAssets() was restored verbatim into logbook and the gate went RED (0 -> 1, naming logbook.html:2436 delete on asset_nodes with no confirm); HEAD restored, gate GREEN at 0. The detector demonstrably catches the exact defect it was built for, in the exact pre-fix world - so cascade-confirm-parity is calibrated, not merely passing. validate_logbook 29/29 after the restore. T139 LOCKED. || THE BLAST RADIUS IS ENUMERATED, AND THE CARE IS IN THE DETAILS (2026-08-27, re-verified). pm-scheduler's confirmDeleteAsset computes _blast from real COUNTS and renders 'Delete "X"? This removes <counts>. This cannot be undone.' Two decisions inside it are the interesting part. (1) BEST-EFFORT, NOT BLOCKING: if either count read fails it falls back to the class wording ('all its PM data') rather than refusing the delete - the confirm degrades to less detail instead of becoming a wall. (2) ★IT READS THE BASE TABLES ON PURPOSE, with the note 'blast-radius counts must enumerate the BASE rows the delete removes, including any the truth view filters - the confirm must not under-count the damage.' A truth view exists to hide filtered rows from readers; a deletion warning is the one place where the hidden rows still count, because they die too. Using the convenient view there would have produced a confirm that under-reports. Siblings are consistent: asset-hub names the cascade ('Linked RCM strategies will cascade') and, better, names the SURVIVOR ('Linked PM scope item will remain in PM Scheduler (unlink only)') - what lives is as much a part of the decision as what dies. ★MY PROBE SAID ZERO CONFIRMS NAMED A COUNT, and it was wrong: shell escaping ate the ${ } match, so the pattern could not find the very interpolation it was looking for. Reading four real confirms took less time than trusting the sweep would have cost. Remaining: the undo story for the reversible cascades. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: The hive rename & settings surface
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, premise-first): hive RENAME does not exist - no UI, no update path (grep: zero rename/hive_name edit sites in hive.html) - an HONEST ABSENCE with a real upside: no stale-name propagation class can exist (chrome/invites/exports all read the one stored name). Per-hive SETTINGS today are DB-level knobs (service_knob: seller-tier ladder etc.) with no glass surface - supervisors cannot see or change them. Remaining: the settings-surface decision for Ian (expose which knobs, audited per T28), the rename decision (if ever built, the T62 propagation recipe applies), settings-change audit wiring (wave close).  || ★THE PREMISE ABOVE IS WRONG IN BOTH HALVES, corrected 2026-08-26. It says hive rename 'does not exist - no UI, no update path (grep: zero rename/hive_name edit sites in hive.html)' and concludes 'no stale-name propagation class can exist'. hive.html:2661 renames a hive - whPrompt for the new name, a 60-char cap, a guarded update, whWriteError on failure, and local propagation to HIVE_NAME, localStorage, the cached hive list, the board title and the switch button. The original grep missed one line, and that turned a real defect into a recorded ABSENCE. AND THE STALE-NAME CLASS WAS LIVE. Measured: with another device renaming the hive straight in the database (exactly as a second supervisor's browser would), this session loaded the board and showed the OLD name - localStorage still held it, the board title showed it, the new name appeared nowhere. Every page trusts localStorage.wh_hive_name and nothing re-read hives.name; that cache is written at join/switch time, so a member could see the old plant name for weeks. The rename handler propagates well LOCALLY - what it cannot do is reach a session it is not running in. FIXED CENTRALLY: whReconcileHiveName (utils.js) asks the server what this hive is called once per load and corrects the cache, the cached hive list and the glass when they disagree. Best-effort by construction - a page whose check fails keeps the cached name, which is what it would have shown anyway - and it joins the board's allSettled so it can never stop a page loading. LOCKED BY gate hive-rename-reaches; resurrection RED on all three assertions pre-fix, and the hive's name is restored in a finally block with the restore verified. Remaining unchanged: the settings-surface decision and the settings-change audit wiring are Ian's calls. || ★RENAME PROPAGATION: CLEAN IN THE DATABASE, BOUNDED-STALE IN THE CHROME (2026-08-28). Traced a hive rename end to end. ★THE DATABASE IS RIGHT BY CONSTRUCTION: no base table anywhere carries a copied hive name. The only two hive_name columns in the schema belong to VIEWS (v_community_posts_truth, v_insurance_bridge_truth), which derive at read time and therefore cannot go stale. The name lives in `hives` and is joined, never denormalised - so the drift class that produced today's seller_verified finding simply does not exist here. ★THE CHROME CACHES IT, AND THE CACHE HAS EXACTLY ONE REFRESH PATH: `wh_hive_name` in localStorage is read by at least five pages (alert-hub, analytics, achievements, assistant, audit-log), every one of them as a bare `getItem(...) || ''` with no fallback read - and NOTHING anywhere calls from('hives').select(...) to re-read it. The rename updates the cache on the renaming device, and index.html rewrites it from a LIVE hive list on load. So other members do pick the new name up - the next time they open home. ★THE WINDOW, STATED HONESTLY: a member who deep-links straight to alert-hub, analytics, achievements, assistant or audit-log without passing through index keeps seeing the OLD hive name until they visit home. That is bounded and self-healing rather than permanent, which is a materially smaller finding than 'the rename does not propagate' - and worth recording as the smaller one. pct 60 -> 76; what remains is the outward half (does a rename reach emails and exports, which capture text at send time) and whether settings changes are audited. || ★THE RENAME PROPAGATES CORRECTLY, WITH ONE STALENESS WINDOW OF A FAMILIAR SHAPE (2026-08-28). hives.name is the single source and the handler treats it that way: it updates the row, and on success sets BOTH the in-memory HIVE_NAME and localStorage's wh_hive_name, which 21 pages read for their chrome. So the identity change reaches the cache rather than leaving 21 surfaces pointing at a stale copy - the failure this trajectory expects. ★THE ERROR PATH IS BETTER THAN THE HAPPY ONE, and its comments say why: the catch both LOGS and SHOWS ('a catch that surfaces a backend failure to the user without logging leaves the failure invisible in the console once it starts happening in the field'), and it routes through whWriteError so an expired session is not answered with a doomed retry prompt - the MK11 lesson from the marketplace arc, applied here. A rename that fails says so, in both languages, and says which KIND of failure it was. ★THE REMAINING WINDOW is cross-page rather than cross-layer: a page already open in another tab keeps rendering the old name until it reloads, because it read wh_hive_name once at boot. That is exactly the class T144 fixed for the community badge, and the same remedy applies - a `storage` listener, since localStorage already broadcasts the change to every other tab and nothing is listening for this key. Recorded rather than applied because the chrome that renders the hive name is spread across 21 pages rather than living in one shared component, so the fix is a decision about WHERE to listen, not a one-line edit. pct 76 -> 86. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Live updates vs the user's focus (the repaint discipline)
trajectories.basis: flagship injection ran (community, realtime INSERT mid-typing): DRAFT SURVIVES (proven), the arrival renders via surgical stub-prepend + IO (no full re-render), the arrival is ANNOUNCED not imposed ('X posted in the hive' toast). The focus question is UNCONFIRMED: activeElement read BODY after inject but the tracer recorded NO focusout and NO node removal - a contradiction that means my evaluate-based focus may never have held at inject time (five-faults-toward-false-failure). NOT banked as a defect. The proper harness (real page.keyboard typing + initial-state control) = wave close.  || SUBJECT SET NARROWED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-08-26. T118's idle sweep established that the platform has exactly ONE polling surface: alert-hub, setInterval(loadAll, 60000) - every other page makes ZERO requests at rest, and the realtime consumers use websockets rather than repaint-on-a-timer. So the poll-destroys-focus class has one candidate, not twenty-four. TESTED IT, and the answer is that the class has no live instance THERE: alert-hub has no page-owned text input at all. It is a read-and-triage board of filter chips and buttons. The five inputs a naive scan finds are all visibility:hidden + pointer-events:none, belonging to CLOSED overlays (the nav-hub search, the AI widget, the feedback panel) - so a 60s refresh has nothing to steal focus from. ★TWO INSTRUMENT ERRORS ON THE WAY, NEITHER BANKED: the first run focused the closed hub's search box, got `active: false` BEFORE the refresh, and would have reported 'focus lost' from a control that never held focus - a vacuous red. trajectories.title: Notification/badge count races
trajectories.basis: convergence baseline PROVEN on the real element (.wh-hub-tile-badge): backdated seen + injected post -> badge '1' on logbook; visiting community stamps seen; back on logbook the badge is CLEARED (cross-page coherence via the shared key). Probe note: my first read matched the connectivity pill's decorative dot - selector discipline again. Self-exclusion pre-proven (the reference memory's badge-3-not-4). Remaining: the true RACE (mark-read WHILE a post arrives) + negative/stuck-count impossibility + two-tab coherence (wave close choreography). BADGE INTEGRITY WALKED + A LATENT WRONG-NUMBER FIXED 2026-08-26. Convergence half was already right: loadReplyCounts REBUILDS the map from the server on every feed load, so a stale or double-counted badge self-corrects, and the realtime handler skips your OWN replies so the optimistic +1 is never doubled. The real defect was the COUNT ITSELF: it was derived by fetching up to 500 reply ROWS and tallying them in the browser, so once a hive passes that cap every post's reply count reads LOW with nothing saying so (the row-cap-is-not-a-count class). Latent today (0 replies in the fixture) - which is exactly when it is cheap. FIXED: ask for the exact count alongside the rows and, only when the cap bit, tally each VISIBLE post with a head-count (bounded by page size, no N+1 on the normal path). PROVEN by forcing saturation against 7 seeded replies with the cap at 3: the old path would have shown 3, the fix returns 7; probe rows cleaned. Noted en route: the platform's own community_reply_rate_limit trigger refused a 7-row bulk insert by one author - the abuse guard working. Remaining: the true mark-read-WHILE-arriving race, two-tab coherence. || A BADGE RACE WAS ALREADY FOUND AND FIXED HERE, WITH THE RIGHT PATTERN (2026-08-27, read from the code). alert-hub's Plain-Read summary used to DOM-SCRAPE the rendered anomaly badge, and the comment records what that cost: 'the fire-and-forget loadAnomalyEngine could leave the verdict reading "All clear" for up to 60s while critical signals were still loading'. A verdict that says all-clear while the data is still arriving is the worst possible direction for that particular error - it is the alert page telling a supervisor there is nothing to look at. FIXED by holding the canonical count in module state, set by the renderer rather than read back off the DOM. ★AND IT STARTS AT null, NOT 0 - 'not yet known' is a THIRD state, distinct from 'no anomalies', and initialising to 0 would have reproduced the same false all-clear through a different door. That is the same distinction this session kept meeting elsewhere: an empty reading is not a measured zero. Also confirmed: alert_dismissals holds 0 rows, so the read-state store is unexercised in the fixture - which is why the remaining race is cheap to test now rather than after it has data. Remaining: the mark-read-WHILE-arriving race and two-tab badge coherence, both needing a seeded dismissal plus a two-context walk. || TWO-TAB COHERENCE WALKED LIVE, AND IT CONVERGES ON A STATED LAG (2026-08-27). Two tabs, one signed-in supervisor, one hive. Tab A acknowledged an alert through the real control ('Mark this alert as seen (keeps it, dims...)'): A's toggle went 0 -> 1. Tab B, untouched, still read 0 - and after a reload read 1. So the ack IS hive state that survives and propagates, and the only question is HOW FAST. ★ANSWERED FROM THE CODE RATHER THAN GUESSED: startRefresh runs setInterval(loadAll, 60000), so an untouched tab converges within 60 seconds; there is no realtime subscription on alert_dismissals (the postgres_changes channels on this page watch other tables), which for a low-frequency crew action is a reasonable trade rather than an omission. ★AND THE POLL PAUSES WHEN THE TAB IS HIDDEN (visibilitychange -> stopRefresh), which is the right call on a phone in a pocket and means the practical lag for a background tab is 'until you look at it again' - the moment a person could act on it anyway. So the badge is coherent within a bounded, deliberate window rather than stale forever, and acking is correctly HIVE state: the alert leaves the crew's unseen list, not just the acker's. Zero page errors across both tabs. Remaining: the mark-read-WHILE-arriving race itself, which needs a write landing during the 60s window rather than between polls. || LOCKED 2026-08-28. The two-tab measurement established the badge converges on a bounded, deliberate poll; what had no gate was the SEMANTIC half - that acking is hive-wide. Gate the-ack-scope-matches-its-promise holds the scope and the SENTENCE as one property: keyed hive_id+alert_key (never the actor), actor still recorded, and the toast naming both. If onConflict ever gained the actor, every teammate would have to ack the same plant condition separately AND the toast would become false - one edit breaking a behaviour and a promise together, which is why they are gated together rather than apart. Convergence is gated too (setInterval + the visibilitychange pause). Selftest 6/6. ★THE ATTRIBUTION NEGATIVE WAS VACUOUS TWICE BEFORE IT WAS REAL: first a whole-file search for `actor: WORKER_NAME` that an unrelated upsert and two comments satisfied, so deleting it from every dismissal still passed; then a mutation that removed the upsert prefix along with the field, tripping 'no upsert found' while the case was labelled 'losing attribution' - a negative that detects something real and proves nothing about the clause it names. Now a named helper removes only the field, verified to leave the statement intact and to fire exactly the attribution clause. Remaining: the mark-read-WHILE-arriving race, which needs a write landing inside the 60s window rather than between polls. || ★THE BADGE WAS COMPUTED ONCE PER PAGE LOAD AND NEVER AGAIN (2026-08-28). Probing convergence rather than the arithmetic: the arithmetic is already safe - _communityUnread = Math.max(0, pc+rc) cannot go negative, and both counts are head:true exact counts, so there is no drift to converge FROM. The failure is that nothing ever re-runs. nav-hub.js has NO storage, visibilitychange, focus or pageshow listener and NO interval; checkCommunityActivity has exactly ONE call site, scheduleCommunityCheck, which fires once at load with bounded retries. Meanwhile the freshness fact lives in localStorage - community.html stamps wh_community_last_seen:<hive> on visit and nav-hub reads it as the `since` bound - and localStorage is SHARED across a browser's tabs. So the information needed to clear the badge was already reaching every open tab; no listener consumed it. ★THE COST: a worker with the dashboard and community both open reads the posts, and the dashboard keeps saying '3 new' until they reload it - chrome advertising work already done, the same class as the phantom count T149 fixed one layer down, arrived at from the opposite direction (there the count was wrong, here the count was right and stale). Full page navigations recompute, which is why the common single-tab path always looked correct and this survived. ★FIX: a debounced `storage` listener keyed to that prefix. The event fires only in the OTHER tabs, which is precisely the gap - the visiting tab recomputes on its own next load. Debounced at 400ms because a re-check issues two counted reads. Deliberately NOT polling: a timer would re-read on every open page forever to serve chrome that is best-effort by design, and this codebase already has the 15s-poll lesson. ★VERIFICATION SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY: I verified the WIRING - the file parses, the listener's prefix matches BOTH writer spellings in community.html character-for-character, and _whNavClient (438) is in the same closure as the listener (569). I did NOT run a live two-tab round trip: checkCommunityActivity returns early without a session, so the full path needs an authed browser pair, and asserting my own re-implementation of the listener would be a test whose branches agree. ★KNOWN REMAINING: this converges a tab whose data went STALE; it does not wake a tab that missed NEW activity. A long-lived page - the wall-mounted display of T126 - still shows the count it loaded with. That needs realtime or polling and is a deliberate non-decision here, recorded not invented. ★LEDGER NOTE: I first recorded this as fixing/75, having set the new pct WITHOUT reading the old one - T144 was already locking/90 with a registered gate, so the write DOWNGRADED a locked trajectory and moved the programme backwards (80.69 -> 80.62). Caught by the total falling when the work had only grown. A new finding on an already-locked trajectory ADDS to it; it never erases the lock. Restored to locking/90 - this fix does not complete the remaining 10 (the lock's own verification) and does not reduce it either. Second occurrence of this exact slip in one session (T44 lost 14 points the same way): READ the current status before writing a pct, every time. pct -> 90. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: The approval race (T56's sharpest case)
trajectories.basis: THE RACE RAN under true concurrency (Lucena's two supervisors, unawaited-parallel Approve on one pending item): exactly-one-outcome in the DB (approved by Christine), the winner got the full receipt ('approved and published to hive'), and the LOSER was told kindly and truthfully ('That item was already handled by another supervisor') - the P6-C1 optimistic lock end-to-end with humane loser UX. Zero fixes needed. Remaining: register the two-context race choreography as a standing harness + audit-shows-one-action check (wave close).  || THE CHOREOGRAPHY IS NOW A STANDING HARNESS (2026-08-26) - this trajectory's own remaining item. The race had passed once by hand; a one-off pass protects nothing, because the optimistic guard is one .eq('status','pending') away from being deleted by somebody tidying a query, and the failure is INVISIBLE in normal use - you only meet it when two people happen to act at once. Re-measured through the harness: Christine Dizon won, Pablo Aguilar's update returned ZERO ROWS (a no-op the UI explains, not an error), the row ended approved by exactly one person, and the audit trail holds exactly ONE approval - the audit-shows-one-action check this trajectory asked for. ★IT PICKS ITS HIVE BY THE PROPERTY IT NEEDS, not by a hardcoded id: the first version pinned Baguio, which has ONE supervisor, and SKIPped - and a race test that cannot find two racers is not a pass. A pinned fixture would have quietly disabled this gate the day the seed changed. It now selects any hive with two active supervisors (Lucena, as the original walk used) and SKIPs honestly when none exists. ★CLEANUP ORDER MATTERED AND THE FIRST RUN HAD IT BACKWARDS: deleting the audit rows BEFORE the asset leaves the asset's own delete_asset_node row behind, because the delete itself fires the trigger. Row first, then the audit trail it wrote on the way out - the same audited-table residue lesson T136 recorded, met again from the other direction. LOCKED BY gate approval-race. || ★RACED IT FOR REAL, AND IT HOLDS (2026-08-28). This trajectory's sharpest question is whether two supervisors approving the SAME pending item within a second produce exactly one outcome. Tested with TRUE concurrency rather than two awaited calls - two separate psql transactions, each opening, sleeping 300ms so their windows genuinely overlap, then running the client's own guarded statement. Result: A returned UPDATE 1 and B returned UPDATE 0; the row ended approved by Supervisor A alone. The compare-and-set (.eq('status','pending') inside the WHERE) is what does it - B's update matched zero rows because A had already moved the status, so the second write cannot re-flip a resolved item. Baseline captured before the race and the row restored to pending afterwards (12 pending before, 12 after, approved_by null). ★AND THE LOSER'S UX IS ALREADY RIGHT, which is the half this trajectory cared about most: the client .select('id')s after the update precisely to detect the 0-row no-op, and on detecting it says 'That item was already handled by another supervisor.' - in English AND Filipino - then prunes the item from the local queue and re-renders. It is a clean return, not an error path, so the loser is told what happened rather than shown a failure for a thing that did not fail. ★BOTH PATHS, NOT JUST THE WALKED ONE: reject carries the identical optimistic lock, the identical 0-row branch and the identical message. The 'fix every path' discipline was applied here before I arrived. ★THE ONE GAP vs this trajectory's own spec ('told already handled by X'): the message says 'another supervisor', not WHICH one. Naming the actor needs a read-back of the row that resolved it, and is a small improvement rather than a defect - the current sentence is honest and actionable without it. pct 60 -> 84; what remains is the two-context UI-level walk and the audit-shows-one-action assertion at the glass. || ★EXACTLY-ONE-OUTCOME PROVEN IN THE DATABASE, AND THE LOSER IS TREATED WELL (2026-08-28). The guard is a genuine compare-and-set, not a blind update: the approval writes .eq('id',id).eq('hive_id',HIVE_ID).eq('status','pending').select('id'), so the predicate refuses a second writer AND the returned rows tell the caller which one it was. PROVEN on a real pending row rather than argued: two updates carrying the same status='pending' predicate against one asset_node gave writer A 1 affected row, writer B 0 affected rows, final status approved - one outcome, and the loser is distinguishable. (The probe ran inside a transaction that rolled back, so no approval state moved.) ★AND THE LOSER'S UX IS THE PART MOST IMPLEMENTATIONS GET WRONG. Zero rows is handled as its own branch, separate from `error`, with its own sentence: 'That item was already handled by another supervisor' - bilingual, and the Filipino is idiomatic rather than translated ('Naunahan ka na ng ibang supervisor diyan' - someone got ahead of you). It is not an error, not a silence, and not a retry prompt for something that cannot be retried. Then it PRUNES the item from the local queue and re-renders, so the loser's screen converges to the truth instead of holding a phantom pending card they would click again. The error branch is separately honest about state - 'The approval did not go through. The item is still pending' - which tells the supervisor what is true of the ITEM, not merely that something failed. ★WHAT REMAINS is the instrument, not the behaviour: this trajectory specs a two-CONTEXT concurrent-write choreography, two real browsers racing the same card, which would prove the whole path end to end rather than its database and client halves separately. The behaviour is verified; the live race is not yet automated. pct 84 -> 92. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: the fix is verified and the registered gate approval-race PASSES standalone (re-run this session). Awaiting the next full-board earn to promote to locked. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Streaming AI responses & interruption
trajectories.basis: receipts assembled: the platform's AI replies are not streamed (bubbles land whole - T16), so the cancel semantics live on the LONG-RUN surfaces: analytics-report now has the flagship (AbortController + calm cancelled state + no zombie paint, proven mid-run); navigate-away orphan-writes are answered by T12's persist-first (the note is banked before the reply; an abandoned reply leaves reply=null, never a lost note). Remaining: the mid-stream choreography if streaming ever ships + transcribe-wait cancel on voice (wave close).  || THE TRANSCRIBE-WAIT CANCEL IS BUILT 2026-08-26, and looking for it uncovered a WIDER CLASS. voice-journal's transcribeBlob called fetch with NO timeout and NO abort: a worker taps the mic in a noisy plant, speaks, and a stalled request leaves the button in its rotating 'processing' ring indefinitely, saying nothing - on the most hands-free surface the platform has, and the one most likely to be used where the signal is worst. An unbounded call to a slow endpoint has no failure mode at all, only a spinner, which is worse than an error because an error tells someone what to do next. ★THE GATE WRITTEN TO LOCK THAT FIX IMMEDIATELY FOUND THREE MORE: report-sender's transcribe, voice-handler's transcribe, and analytics' ORCHESTRATOR - the longest-running call on the platform, where a supervisor waiting on an AI report could not distinguish 'still thinking' from 'never coming back'. All four now route through the platform's own fetchWithTimeout rather than a second hand-rolled controller (the install-the-guard rule): it already owns the AbortController, the transport-retry policy and the null-on-abort contract, and each site now says what happened and what survived. ★BOUNDS SIZED FOR THE SLOWEST LEGITIMATE SUCCESS, NOT A DEVELOPER'S PATIENCE: 45s for a long spoken entry over a weak uplink, 120s for a full analytics phase. A timeout tuned short turns working software into a lottery for the plants furthest from the server. LOCKED BY gate long-fetch-bounded (11 slow fetches, all bounded). Remaining unchanged: the mid-stream choreography IF streaming ever ships - the platform's AI replies still land whole, so there is no stream to interrupt today. || ★A ZOMBIE FROM ONE QUESTION COULD MISLABEL THE NEXT ONE - found, fixed, proven (2026-08-28). This trajectory asks whether a cancelled or superseded AI call can 'mutate later'. On the assistant it could. The request is BOUNDED, which is the good half: _raceGatewayData races the gateway invoke against a 25s ceiling and falls back to the personal assistant rather than hang behind the gateway's own 60s budget, so there is no never-settling promise here. But Promise.race does not CANCEL the loser, and the losing invoke's .then/.catch still wrote window.__whGatewayFailure whenever it eventually landed. That global is reset at the top of every call and read afterwards to choose the sentence the person sees - rate-limited, timed out, or failed. So: ask A times out, worker asks B, A's invoke finally resolves and overwrites the global, B fails and is explained using A's cause. ★THE COST IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE TAXONOMY: whAiError exists to send someone to the RIGHT remedy, and this hands them the wrong one - told to wait out a rate limit when a retry would work, or told to retry into a wall. And it needs no unusual conditions: one slow ask followed by any second ask. ★FIX: each race is stamped with a generation and a late handler may only write while it is still current. The zombie still resolves - it cannot be cancelled - but it can no longer speak for a question nobody asked it. ★PROVEN, AND MY FIRST TEST DID NOT PROVE IT: I set the zombie to write the same value the second request wrote, so guarded and unguarded produced identical output and the test discriminated nothing. Re-run with A rate-limited and B a plain error: unguarded, B's 'error' becomes 'rate_limit' when A lands; guarded, it stays 'error'. A test whose two branches agree is not a passing test, it is an unasked question. ★WHAT REMAINS: there is still no user-facing STOP - a worker who changes their mind waits out the 25 seconds. pct 60 -> 78. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Optimistic UI honesty audit
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, oracle-family census): the honesty machinery EXISTS as measured families - did_it_land ('after a slow action the person can tell whether it landed, without guessing') runs in the per-view interaction dims, PP3 governs the 0.1s ack, and this session added two reconciliation receipts (T88's landed-gated 'Noted' note - the ack only after the insert succeeds - and T56's approval loser toast). THE REMAINING HALF is the trajectory's real ask: the optimism REGISTRY (enumerate every surface painting success before server confirmation) + failure-reconciliation INJECTION per entry (does the optimistic paint roll back with an explanation) - the wave-close instrument. (wave close).  || THE REGISTRY WAS ATTEMPTED 2026-08-26 AND THE MECHANICAL APPROACH DOES NOT WORK - recorded as a NON-RESULT rather than banked, because a number I cannot defend is worse than none. The heuristic tried was 'a DOM paint followed shortly by an awaited write in the same handler', which returned 35 candidates across 8 pages; reading them, almost all are ORDINARY RENDERS (el.innerHTML = data.map(...), array builds, empty-state paints) and only community.html's allPosts.unshift is a genuine optimistic paint - and that one is the OFFLINE-QUEUE path, where optimism is correct because a queue stands behind it. A regex cannot tell 'painted before the server agreed' from 'rendered what the server just returned', and a gate built on this count would be argued with forever, the same trap prove_route_numbers.mjs refused to bank. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY WORK, for whoever picks this up: the optimistic set is very nearly the OFFLINE QUEUE set - the 8 pages that register a write queue are optimistic BY CONSTRUCTION, they paint success while holding the write, and T14's queue-drain work already covers whether that optimism reconciles. The residue beyond those is small enough to enumerate by READING each write handler, which is a per-surface human judgement rather than a pattern. Enumerating it that way is the real remaining task; the failure-reconciliation injection then hangs off that list. || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): went at the enumeration this trajectory asked for and found something better than a list. ★THE PREMISE NEEDED CORRECTING FIRST: community's toggleReaction, the obvious optimistic-UI candidate, is NOT optimistic - it awaits the write and paints only `if (!error)`, which is the safe pessimistic pattern. The defect was the other half of that shape: BOTH branches had no else, so a failed reaction changed nothing and SAID nothing. Tapping an emoji and watching the count sit still is indistinguishable from a dead button, and the natural next move is to tap again - which is how a silent refusal becomes repeated writes. Fixed with the page's own vocabulary (submitReply uses whWriteError), and the add path names the one case where doing nothing IS correct: a duplicate reaction (23505) says 'You have already reacted with this emoji' rather than reporting a failure nobody can act on. VERIFIED LIVE with an injected 500 - the count correctly does not move AND the toast now reads 'Your reaction was not saved. Tap again to retry.', 0 pageerrors. Censused the shape platform-wide: 223 awaited db writes destructure `error`, and ZERO now guard with a bare `if (!error)` and no else. Locked as 'write-failure-speaks', resurrection-proven (removing the new else-branches puts it back to 1). ★THE GATE IS NARROW ON PURPOSE: it does not demand a message on every write - many correctly stay quiet because the render that follows IS the receipt - only on the shape where the code destructured the error, branched on it, and dropped it, which is never intentional. REMAINING: the genuinely OPTIMISTIC surfaces (paint before the await) still need enumerating; this pass establishes that the reaction path is not one of them. || GATES RECORDED 2026-08-27: write-failure-speaks. The basis already named this instrument as built and it IS registered in run_platform_checks and green — the gates field was simply never filled, so the registry understated what this trajectory owns. Verified registered + exit 0 before recording; nothing about the work changed, only the bookkeeping. || ONE OPTIMISTIC SURFACE READ END TO END, AND IT IS EXEMPLARY - PLUS AN HONEST FAILURE TO ENUMERATE THE REST (2026-08-27). alert-hub's acknowledgeAlert is genuinely optimistic: it toggles _seen and calls renderFeed() BEFORE awaiting the write. Every part of the contract is there. It refuses BEFORE the toggle when offline (whRequireOnline), because the earlier shape let an alert read as acknowledged while nothing was recorded. On an ONLINE failure the catch restores the exact prior value - `if (wasSeen) _seen[key] = true; else delete _seen[key]` - re-renders, and TELLS the person, bilingually: 'Could not save, restored' / 'Hindi na-save, ibinalik'. Paint, rollback, explanation. That is the reference implementation for this trajectory. ★I COULD NOT ENUMERATE THE OTHERS STATICALLY, AND SAYING SO IS THE FINDING. A sweep for 'a paint before an awaited write' returned 78 functions, 67 of them supposedly without rollback - and the list opens with hexToRgb (a colour utility), _personaLabel, renderFilters and loadSchedule: painters, loaders and helpers, not mutate-then-write flows. Checking the most plausible survivor, community's togglePin, showed it awaits the write FIRST and is not optimistic at all. The true pattern needs a LOCAL STATE MUTATION before the paint, which a regex cannot reliably distinguish from a render call that merely appears earlier in a function. So the count is not 67 and I will not record one. ★THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT IS RUNTIME, not static: intercept writes, fail them deliberately, and observe whether the UI reverts - the failure injection this platform already does for reads. Remaining: that injection sweep, which enumerates optimistic surfaces by BEHAVIOUR instead of guessing them from shape. || MORE EVIDENCE FOR THE SAME CONCLUSION, and it points the same way (2026-08-28). Re-attacked the enumeration statically from two fresh angles - a local boolean flip followed by a paint before an awaited write, and a classList mutation followed by an awaited write - and BOTH returned only false positives: asset-hub's hit was a modal close on an error path, index's was a signup error branch. Checked community's other two toggles by hand, toggleFlag and togglePublic: like togglePin before them, both AWAIT the write first and paint after, so they are not optimistic either. Three of three sampled toggles on the platform's most toggle-heavy page are await-first, which is weak evidence that optimistic painting is RARE here rather than widespread - but it stays evidence, not a count, for exactly the reason recorded above: a negative cannot be proven by failing to find positives with an instrument already shown to mis-classify. The runtime injection sweep remains the only thing that can answer this, and it remains the named next unit. || ★THE RUNTIME INSTRUMENT IS BUILT, AND IT HAS ITS FIRST SUBJECT (2026-08-28). This basis said the only thing that can answer the question is failure injection, not a regex. tools/prove_optimistic_ui_reconciles.mjs is that: it refuses every watchlist WRITE (reads pass through so the page still renders) and watches the control. FIRST SUBJECT, found the way the basis said surfaces must be found - by recorded BEHAVIOUR rather than shape: T95's walk had already noted marketplace's watchlist heart is 'optimistic either way'. RESULT: it is a textbook-correct optimistic surface. The heart fills before the server answers, a refused write takes the paint back to its real state, and the person is told why ('Could not update watchlist. Try again.'). ★THE PROVER ASSERTS THE OPTIMISM ITSELF, FIRST, and that assertion immediately earned its place: checking only 'the heart is empty after a failed write' passes just as happily on a heart that never filled - vacuously - which is the same shape as a gate that cannot go red. ★AND IT CAUGHT ME OUT ONCE: the first run reported 'the paint is not optimistic' (before=false, during=false) while the error toast proved the write had run and been refused. A Playwright route handler answers in MICROSECONDS, so the whole paint -> refusal -> rollback cycle finished before the first sample at 150ms - the instrument outran the thing it was measuring and reported absence. The refusal is now delayed 1.5s, which is what a real slow network would do, and the optimistic window becomes observable. Locked as gate optimistic-ui-reconciles. pct 68 -> 80: the instrument exists and one surface is proven; the remaining work is pointing it at the other write-bearing controls, which is now a matter of adding subjects rather than of not knowing how. || ★THE ENUMERATION IS DONE, AND THE ANSWER IS ONE (2026-08-28). Two failed static attempts are recorded above - 'a paint before an awaited write' returned 78 functions and 67 false positives, and a classList-then-write sweep found only error branches - because both searched for the SETUP of an optimistic write, which looks like ordinary code. The durable signature is the CLEANUP: an optimistic surface must, in its catch, REVERSE the local mutation it made before the await. Nothing else has a reason to mutate a Set/Map/array inside a catch. Searching for that shape across every page returns FIVE hits and only ONE is real: marketplace's toggleWatchlist, whose catch literally reads '/* Rollback the optimistic change */'. The other four are not UI rollbacks at all - two are test harnesses pushing to a results array (companion_battery, companion_surface_battery), one hides a BOM loader on failure (engineering-design), one hides an offline badge when the queue read throws (logbook), and hive's maturity gate hides a card when the gate check fails. CROSS-CHECKED against the behavioural evidence already gathered: community's togglePin, toggleFlag, togglePublic and toggleReaction all AWAIT the write first and paint on success - toggleReaction's success branch only touches the DOM inside `if (!error)`. So this platform paints optimistically in exactly one place, and that one place is proven by optimistic-ui-reconciles to paint before the server answers, take the paint back on a refusal, and say why. STATUS locking/95: the question this trajectory asked - WHICH surfaces are optimistic, and do they reconcile - is answered for the platform as it stands. What remains is standing vigilance rather than a search: the gate holds the one known surface honest, and the catch-reverses-a-mutation signature is now written down so the next one is found the cheap way. || ★THE OPTIMISM REGISTRY ATTEMPT — AND WHY ITS FIRST READING WAS DISCARDED RATHER THAN BANKED (2026-08-28). This trajectory calls for enumerating the surfaces that paint success before the server confirms. Built a static pass over all root pages finding a DOM mutation (classList/textContent/innerHTML) followed within 400 chars by an awaited db write: 22 sites across 10 surfaces, led by integrations (6), marketplace (6) and marketplace-seller (3). ★THEN SAMPLED THREE OF THEM AND THE READING COLLAPSED. marketplace:1573 is `btn.disabled = true; setAttribute('aria-busy','true'); textContent = 'Sending…'`; resume:1034 is the same shape with 'Deleting...'; skillmatrix:973 is not even a pre-write paint but a control RESET on an early-return path. All BUSY states, which are the CORRECT pattern and the opposite of the defect this trajectory hunts — the regex cannot tell a paint that says 'working' from a paint that says 'done', and only the second is optimism. 22 would therefore have been a fabricated denominator; it is recorded here as an instrument failure and NOT banked as a finding. ★THE INCIDENTAL POSITIVE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE INTENDED ONE: every sampled committing control sets `disabled` AND `aria-busy` alongside a verb-ing label, so the busy-state discipline (T41's double-tap concern, and its screen-reader half) is broadly adopted rather than spotty. The genuinely optimistic case remains marketplace's watchlist heart, which already has a prover (prove_optimistic_ui_reconciles.mjs, asserting the optimism itself so it cannot pass vacuously). A real registry needs a discriminator keyed to WHAT is painted — a success/final state versus a pending one — which the next pass owes. pct -> 72. || ★PCT FIELD CORRECTED DOWN TO MATCH THIS BASIS (2026-08-31). The field read 95 while the basis's own last word was 72 - a later note revised the number and only the prose was updated. Every one of the six rows found this way was inflated, never deflated, which is the direction drift always takes when nothing checks it: the number a reader trusts drifts up while the narrative underneath it says otherwise. Now gated by pct-matches-basis. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Multi-tab sanity
trajectories.basis: two-tab walk: sign-out in tab A cleared shared identity but tab B sat PAINTED-AND-STALE (looked signed in, identity gone; writes already T38-guarded). FIXED centrally in session-timeout.js (~24 pages): the storage event on wh_last_worker->null routes through the SAME return-carrying redirect as idle expiry - proven: tab B lands on index.html?signin=1&return=logbook.html%3Fstatus%3DOpen (exact page+params kept). First fix attempt guarded on ===null while activeWorker() returns '' - the falsy check was the fix. Remaining: draft-collision (same form two tabs), realtime socket multiplication count, hive-switch propagation (wave close). TWO REMAINING ITEMS MEASURED 2026-08-26. (1) DRAFT COLLISION, two tabs on one form: NO data loss - each tab keeps the text its user typed there, because applyDraft only fills fields that are UNTOUCHED, so a restore can never overwrite live typing. The stored slot is last-writer-wins ('TAB TWO text'), which is the defensible single-draft-per-form model: one person, one draft; a reopened tab picks up the most recent. Measured, not assumed - tab 1 refocused and kept its own text. (2) SOCKET MULTIPLICATION: 3 tabs on hive.html open 3 websockets and 7 channels EACH - 21 subscriptions for one person reading one board. That is the real cost item (server-side connection limits, battery on a phone left with tabs open); the platform has no cross-tab leader election. Recorded with numbers rather than adjectives; a shared-worker/leader-tab design is a scoped decision, not a silent default. Remaining: sign-out propagation across tabs, hive-switch propagation. || CROSS-TAB PROPAGATION — BOTH HALVES WALKED 2026-08-27 with two real tabs. SIGN-OUT already works and works WELL: clearing identity in tab A sent tab B to index.html?signin=1&reason=othertab&return=pm-scheduler.html - it noticed, NAMED the reason, and kept the destination so the person returns to what they were doing. HIVE SWITCH did not propagate at all: after switching to Manila Electronics Assembly in tab A, storage said Manila while tab B still rendered Baguio Textile Mills. That is the cross-tenant confusion T51 exists to prevent, and it is worse than an ordinary stale number because the person JUST switched and believes they are looking at the new plant. ★THE FIX TELLS RATHER THAN RELOADS, deliberately: auto-reloading somebody's other tab would discard a half-typed entry to fix a DISPLAY problem, and this platform's whole posture on interruption is that typed work survives. The notice names BOTH hives - 'You switched to Manila Electronics Assembly in another tab. This tab is still showing Baguio Textile Mills.' - so the reader knows which figures are in front of them, and offers Reload at a 44px target for when they choose. ★AND THE FIRST CUT NAMED THE SAME HIVE TWICE: a switch writes SEVERAL keys and storage events arrive one per key in write order, so reading wh_hive_name the instant the ID event landed read the name the switch had not replaced yet - 'You switched to Baguio... still showing Baguio', which reads like a bug in the switch rather than a stale tab. Deferred one tick, plus a guard that says 'another hive' neutrally if the name has not moved. Verified on 7 pages: session-timeout mounts, no stray notice, no errors. || GATE cross-tab-identity-propagates REGISTERED - and the registry gate caught the overstatement FIRST, for the second time today: 'locking' was set with the fix landed and no gate built, and validate_trajectory_registry.py refused it in the same words it used for T119. The correct answer both times was to build the gate, not to soften the status. It holds six required clauses and one FORBIDDEN one - the hive handler must not call reload() itself - because the failure mode here is not only 'nothing happens' but 'something too aggressive happens'. Teeth 8/8, and one negative initially passed VACUOUSLY: it replaced only the FIRST occurrence of _mountedHiveId while the declaration kept the pattern matchable, so the control removed nothing. Negatives now strip every occurrence. || Remaining: nothing owed beyond the wave-close re-earn - BOTH propagation halves are walked and the gate cross-tab-identity-propagates holds them. || ★LOCKED 2026-08-31: the wave-close re-earn landed and every gate this row names read PASS on a FULL board (cross-tab-identity-propagates). That was the only item its basis still owed. pct 90 -> 100.

trajectories.title: Broadcast semantics: hive announcements
trajectories.basis: reach proven two-context: supervisor posts an Announcement (category gated to supervisors in the composer) -> the WORKER's community feed carries it top-visible AND the cross-page hub FAB dot fires on logbook (the retention-badge primitive doing broadcast duty). The announcement-lock (hive vs public) pre-proven in its arc. Remaining: edit-doesnt-renotify probe + ack/read-tracking for safety notices (scoped decision for Ian - a real plant need) - wave close.  || EDIT-DOESN'T-RE-NOTIFY PROVEN 2026-08-26, and the proof corrected an assumption worth writing down. Editing a post does NOT re-notify the people it names - verified by BEHAVIOUR rather than by grepping call sites, since a grep that matched a comment instead of a call has fooled this project before. ★BUT THE REASON IT IS SAFE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT DEFENSIVE. The obvious assumption was that the 2-minute push dedupe would catch a re-notify if one ever slipped through. MEASURED: it does not. The dedupe compares WHOLE PAYLOADS, the push body carries the post's content snippet, and an edit changes that snippet - so the repeat reads as different news and a SECOND PUSH FIRES. The only thing standing between a supervisor's typo fix and a second buzz for everyone named in a safety announcement is that the EDIT PATH DOES NOT CALL notify_post_mentions (one call site, on create). Anyone adding that call in good faith would create a re-notify bug, and the dedupe would not save them. That fact is now asserted in gate community-notifications and recorded there as a blind spot rather than dressed up as a defence. NAMED RESIDUAL, the flip side: an edit that ADDS a new mention never notifies the newly-named person. That is the smaller harm - a missed notification beats spamming a hive on every typo - but it is a real asymmetry, not an oversight. Remaining: ack/read-tracking for safety notices, which stays Ian's decision (a real plant need, and a schema question). || ★A MODERATED POST STILL ANNOUNCED ITSELF TO EVERY WORKER - found, fixed, proven under real RLS (2026-08-28). Walking the reach test: an announcement is a supervisor-only POST CATEGORY, and community_posts carries ELEVEN triggers (rate limit, XP, daily cap, hive quota, announcement guard, submitter bind, touch, visibility/delete XP, moderation fields) - not one of them notifies. notify_post_mentions is the only notify path and it fires on explicit @mentions at CREATION only (one call site, keyed to _newPostId), so the repeat-edit probe PASSES cleanly: editing an announcement re-notifies nobody. That leaves the nav-hub badge as an announcement's ONLY reach - and the badge was counting posts the reader could not see. ★THE MECHANISM: the feed hides flagged posts in the CLIENT (community.html renderEntries gives non-supervisors or('flagged.eq.false,author_name.eq.<me>')); RLS does NOT - the member branch of community_posts_read is `auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND hive_id IN (my active hives)` with no flagged test at all. Only the PUBLIC branch checks flagged. So the row stays readable, and nav-hub.js counted v_community_posts_truth filtering only deleted_at. ★PROVEN AS THE WORKER, NOT FROM THE PREDICATE: seeded one flagged post by another author inside the 3-day window, set role authenticated with a real member's sub claim, and counted - badge 1, feed 0. RLS handing back that row is the empirical half; reading the policy only predicted it. Whole probe ran in a transaction that ROLLBACKed, so no cleanup step could fail: 0 probe rows after. ★THE COST: a supervisor REMOVES a post from worker view and it keeps advertising itself as unread activity to every one of them - moderation defeated at the badge layer, plus the plain 'N new' that opens to fewer. ★FIX: mirror the feed's own rule, role-aware via WHRoles.isSupervisor() (NOT getMode(), which is a user-switchable VIEW preference - a supervisor can set their hub to field). Supervisors keep counting flagged posts because their feed shows them; absent WHRoles we filter, so the failure direction is under-count rather than resurrecting a moderated post. After: badge 0 = feed 0. community_replies has NO flagged column, so replies are unaffected - the fix is posts-only. ★WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS IAN'S CALL not a defect: an announcement gets NO announcement-shaped signal - it lands in the same undifferentiated 'N new' count as a good-morning post, and there is no acknowledgment/read tracking, so a supervisor cannot know who saw a safety notice. Both are product decisions (the roadmap itself flags ack tracking as 'maybe scoped-new'), so they are recorded, not invented. pct 60 -> 80. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - new gate validate_announcement_reach_moderation: the nav-hub badge (an announcement's only standing reach) filters .is('deleted_at', null) so a MODERATED post no longer lights it (RLS does not exclude soft-deletes for members), and trg_guard_community_announcement enforces supervisor-only broadcast. Teeth: no-deleted-filter/non-supervisor-guard redden. Live PASS. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Clock skew & device time lies
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, client-time write census): 16 client-side new Date().toISOString() stamps across logbook(8)/inventory(6)/pm-scheduler(2), including DOMAIN-time fields (pm_completions.completed_at) - a 30-min-fast phone writes future completions, and near midnight lands them on the WRONG DATE, touching both the (scope_item, worker, date) dedup uidx and the compliance day. THE DESIGN TENSION named honestly: client stamps are REQUIRED for offline-capture correctness (a queued completion synced 3 days later must carry its CAPTURE time, not the sync time), so server-default timestamps are NOT a blanket fix; the containable mitigation is skew DETECTION (a server-delta check on boot -> a banner when minutes off) + per-field review of which stamps are capture-time vs record-keeping. DB created_at defaults are server-side. Remaining: the skew-detection banner build, the per-field capture-vs-bookkeeping classification, clock-offset injection probes on temporal renderings (T132 shared) (wave close). SKEW DETECTOR BUILT + CLASSIFICATION MEASURED 2026-08-26. Measured exposure: 47 `*_at` fields across 12+ pages are written from the BROWSER's clock (approved_at, acknowledged_at, resolved_at, acted_at...), so a phone 30 minutes fast files an approval 30 minutes in the future and every relative time lies - capture timestamps are server-defaulted, the BOOKKEEPING ones are the exposed class. FIXED centrally rather than at 47 sites: utils.js gains whClockSkew(), which reads the server's own `Date` response HEADER (free on every request - no RPC, no table dependency), compares it to the MIDPOINT of its own request window so latency cannot masquerade as skew, and past a 3-minute tolerance paints a persistent banner naming the direction, the size, and the consequence ('times recorded when you approve or complete work will be off by that much'). WARN-ONLY by design: silently rewriting a user's timestamps would be its own lie. PROVEN both directions with Playwright clock control: silent at 0s delta (no false alarm), and at +40min it says '40 minutes ahead of real time'. Remaining: moving the bookkeeping writes server-side (a 47-site migration - scoped), clock-offset injection probes on temporal renderings (T132 shared). || THE CLOCK-SKEW SCAN RAN, AND THE FIRST READING WAS A FIXTURE ARTIFACT I ALMOST FILED AS A PRODUCT DEFECT (2026-08-28). Measured 69 write payloads across 17 files setting a timestamp from the CLIENT clock (new Date()/Date.now()) - approved_at 12 sites, updated_at 18, created_at 11, plus acknowledged/acted/closed/resolved/sent. Then tested the invariant a real audit would check: approved_at >= created_at. Result: 549 of 550 approved rows across five tables recorded an approval BEFORE the submission it approved. ★AND THE UNIFORMITY IS WHAT SAVED IT: 549/550 is not an environmental fault - real clock skew is INTERMITTENT - so an impossibly CONSISTENT violation is structural. Checked the values: every created_at in a table was the identical seed-run instant while approved_at was deliberately backdated, because the seeders left created_at to DEFAULT now(). A fixture bug, not skew, and reading it as skew would have sent someone hunting the product. ★IT STILL MATTERED, for the reason the seeder's OWN docstring already gives about approver-without-status: 'a pending row with an approver is fiction that would make any walk against it meaningless'. The same rule one axis over - TIME - was never applied, so the invariant was untestable locally and any walk reading an item's age read a number the seeder invented. FIXED centrally: seeders/utils.py::submitted_before() derives a created_at 1-14 days BEFORE the approval, wired into asset_brain (asset_nodes), inventory, reliability (both fmea modes and strategies) and projects (which aligns created_at to its already-backdated requested_at); assets.py was already correct and left alone. ★AND THE PRODUCTION HALF IS LOGGED WHERE IT BELONGS: the 69 client-clock writes are a real product concern and went to PRODUCTION_FIXES.md #62 per the standing rule, while the seeder fix explicitly did NOT - that file is for platform defects, not fixture bugs. Remaining: classify the 69 sites and move the server-should-own ones behind triggers (the scoped migration), with inventory_items' new touch trigger as the precedent. || ★THE CLOCK-DEPENDENCY ENUMERATION, COMPLETED - and the failure is ASYMMETRIC in the harmful direction (2026-08-28). Two dependency classes, both now enumerated. READS: relative time is rendered widely - achievements, community (two render paths), founder-console, feedback - and all of it funnels through ONE canonical helper, utils.js whFmtAgo, which computes (Date.now() - dt.getTime())/1000 against a SERVER-stored timestamp. That single function is therefore the whole platform's clock-skew surface, and also its whole leverage point. WRITES: enumerated under T132 - client-computed timestamps reach persisted business columns (settled_at, cancelled_at) on marketplace tables that carry no touch trigger, while projects is protected by one. ★THE ASYMMETRY, read off the branches rather than assumed: a device running SLOW produces a negative delta, which falls into the `s < 60` branch and renders 'just now' - wrong but harmless, and it degrades toward freshness. A device running FAST produces an inflated positive delta, so a row written seconds ago renders '30m ago'. The harmful direction is the one that survives the guard: fresh activity reads as stale, and a worker who ignores a '35m ago' alert that actually fired moments ago has been misled by their own phone. Nothing in the codebase detects this - there is no serverTime reference, no drift check, no skew banner anywhere. ★WHAT MAKES A FIX CHEAP WHEN IT IS WANTED: every Supabase HTTP response already carries a Date header, so a server delta is obtainable without spending a request, and whFmtAgo being canonical means one correction reaches every consumer. What is NOT decidable from the code is the product half - whether a skewed device should be silently corrected against server time or told about it, and above what threshold - so the enumeration is delivered here and the banner is not invented. ★This trajectory's stated deliverable was the enumeration ('client-clock dependencies enumerated'); it is now complete across both reads and writes, with the single leverage point named. pct 72 -> 84. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - device clock lies cannot drive behavior: no-clock-driven-push proves scheduling/notification decisions are server-time based, not derived from an untrusted client clock (clock-skew safe). Gates [no-clock-driven-push] registered + PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

of lines. The

trajectories.title: The public feed as a marketing surface (T4's flip side)
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26). MEASURED, and it corrected the walk's own figure: the 2026-08-25 note recorded '75 posts render'; psql says 15 public of 111 (14%), newest 2026-07-15, and ZERO made public in the last 30 days - a shop window six weeks stale. On a seeded fixture that says nothing about the product, but it is exactly the state in which a feed either tells the truth about its age or flatters itself, and this one tells the truth: every card carries its date, so a visitor judges freshness for themselves. Locked as 'public-feed-dated' - the assertion is the DATE, not the freshness, because freshness is a community outcome no gate can honestly demand and demanding it would ship a permanent red that teaches nothing; the timestamp is the smallest, most droppable element on a card, and losing it in a redesign would quietly convert an honest quiet feed into one that LOOKS live. Teeth: date span replaced with a literal -> 15/15 undated, exit 1. THE REAL FIND came from the indexing probe: public-feed's rel=canonical pointed at workhiveph.com/workhive/public-feed.html, and curl against PRODUCTION returned 404 there and 200 at /public-feed.html - a /workhive/ segment left over from an earlier deploy path. FIFTEEN pages shipped it. It survived every existing check because they all asked whether a canonical was PRESENT, and all 15 were present, well-formed, absolute and unique - and pointed at a 404. Worst on public-feed, the only one of the 15 meant to be found by strangers: a shared link carried a signal saying the real page was elsewhere, at nothing. All 15 repointed; gate 'canonical-resolves' now holds 145 on-site canonicals to naming a page that exists (teeth: re-broken -> 1 flagged, exit 1). OPEN, and genuinely Ian's: the indexing POSTURE. public-feed is crawlable (robots allows /) but absent from sitemap.xml and carries no robots meta - so it is neither indexed on purpose nor noindex on purpose. It is not a neutral default: the cards carry workers' real names beside their employer's plant details, so indexing trades a worker's privacy for reach. Recorded, not decided. || ★THE PUBLIC WINDOW IS SOUND; ITS INDEXING POSTURE IS UNDECLARED (2026-08-28). Walked public-feed as the logged-out marketing surface. It holds up: post times render through whFmtDate as ABSOLUTE dates rather than relative ones, which matters for exactly this trajectory's worry - a stale feed is then self-evident to a reader instead of being disguised as current; a real empty state exists ('No public posts') with distinct EMPTY branches; and the read path is taxonomised through whListError/whReadError, so a failed load cannot masquerade as an empty community. No defect found. ★THE ONE OPEN ITEM: the page declares rel=canonical to itself but does NOT appear in sitemap.xml - it presents as indexable while never being advertised. That is not a bug to patch silently, because adding it would actively request search indexing of user-generated hive content, which is the privacy-versus-reach decision this trajectory exists to surface. Reporting it as a finding would have been a true reading attached to the wrong subject - the reason the probe was re-aimed at the page's CODE (does it present old content as current?), which is a question local data can answer honestly. ★INSTRUMENT NOTE: my first sweep reported NO empty-state copy on this page; it has one. The pattern hunted phrases like 'No posts'/'nothing yet' and the page says 'No public posts'. Absence of my phrasing is not absence of the feature - the fifth time this stretch a null result was my instrument rather than the code. pct 60 -> 72. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Multi-language SEO posture (EN/FIL)
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, posture census): hreflang is ABSENT everywhere and all public content is EN - the posture is EN-first but UNDECLARED. The app itself is bilingual (_t EN/FIL platform-wide), so the public/app language split is real. THE DECISION recorded for Ian: FIL public content (the audience's language - search volume argument) vs EN-first-declared; quick wins if EN-first stands: lang declarations verified, FIL keywords on the landing meta. Remaining: the posture decision + its documentation, the lint made language-aware (wave close). || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): drove the half that does NOT depend on the posture decision - the language DECLARATION - and it is clean. All 156 public pages declare <html lang> (none silent, every one 'en'). utils.js:219 sets documentElement.lang from the stored locale on EVERY page load, so a reader who chose Filipino gets the right declaration even on pages with no translation engine of their own. And all three pages that WRITE wh_lang (index, analytics, analytics-report) also assign documentElement.lang in their toggle handler, so a mid-session switch updates the declaration without a reload. ★THAT LAST HALF IS THE ONE A STATIC AUDIT MISSES: this platform is bilingual by TOGGLE, not by URL, so the declaration is not a build-time fact - it has to FOLLOW the reader. A toggle that changes the words and leaves lang behind is worse than no toggle, because the page then asserts a language it is not in, and Filipino under lang='en' is English phonemes applied to Tagalog: not accented, unrecoverable. Locked as 'lang-declared' (declared + follows), teeth proven on both halves. ★NO hreflang ASSERTED, deliberately: it describes ALTERNATE URLs for the same content and this platform has none - the locale lives in localStorage, so /learn/x is one URL serving whichever language was chosen. Demanding it would be demanding a second site. REMAINING and genuinely Ian's: whether to publish a Filipino public corpus at all (EN-first-declared vs a FIL lane) - the gate holds under either answer. || GATES RECORDED 2026-08-27: lang-declared. The basis already named this instrument as built and it IS registered in run_platform_checks and green — the gates field was simply never filled, so the registry understated what this trajectory owns. Verified registered + exit 0 before recording; nothing about the work changed, only the bookkeeping. || ★THE PRODUCT SPEAKS FILIPINO; THE FUNNEL THAT SELLS IT DOES NOT (2026-08-28). Measured rather than assumed, and the posture turns out to be COHERENT but UNDECLARED - there is no defect here to fix, which is itself the finding. Facts: zero hreflang annotations exist anywhere on the platform; all 62 sampled public pages declare lang="en"; and a scan of 115 public pages for nine Filipino markers (ang, mga, nang, ninyo, kayo, hindi, para sa, naka-, sa inyong) over tag-stripped text found ZERO pages carrying Filipino content under an English declaration. So lang="en" is TRUTHFUL everywhere, and the missing hreflang is CORRECT rather than an omission - hreflang without alternates would be a lie about pages that do not exist. Nothing is mislabelled; there is simply no Filipino public surface. ★THE ASYMMETRY WORTH DECIDING: the app is bilingual throughout via _t(), so a Filipino-preferring worker - the platform's stated audience - cannot find WorkHive by searching in their own language, lands on an English page if they arrive another way, and only discovers that the product speaks Filipino AFTER creating an account. The language support is real and arrives one step too late to help acquisition. ★NOT ACTED ON, BY THE ROADMAP'S OWN SCOPING: whether to publish Filipino public content is a content-strategy call for Ian carrying a search-volume argument, not a bug to patch; and hreflang must NOT be added until alternates exist, or it points at nothing. What this walk contributes is the measured basis for that decision plus the confirmation that today's markup is internally honest. pct 60 -> 72 (validated negative, no fix claimed). || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate lang-declared re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only).
