trajectories.title: Performance as SEO: the public pages' CWV
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, lab CWV at 390 on the funnel pair): LANDING CLEAN - LCP 960ms (loopback lab) on the RIGHT element (the value-prop paragraph, not chrome), CLS 0.000; the learn article's LCP element is the 'Short answer' div itself at 448ms (the ANSWER is the LCP - the AEO ideal). THE FINDING: the learn template shifts 0.17-0.38 CLS at 390 (over the 0.1 bar) - a small ~0.03 settle at ~950ms (article/nav, font-swap shaped) plus a BIG ~0.15 shift at ~1s whose sources report as anonymous/removed nodes (an INJECTED element - the template's late JS is the suspect; the shifts-sources-are-its-victims lesson applies to reading the attribution). Remaining: identify the ~1s injector (outerHTML capture), reserve its space in the template, re-measure; then the throttled-profile lane + image-weight/font strategy audit on the funnel set (wave close).  || ★HARNESS UNLOCK 2026-08-26, found while probing share cards and worth more than the thing that found it: THE LOCAL SEEDER COULD NOT SERVE THE 60-PAGE CALCULATOR CLUSTER AT ALL. /learn/, /about/, /privacy-policy/ and /terms-of-service/ each had an explicit Flask alias; /tools/ did not, and the catch-all route matches only a SINGLE path segment, so every /tools/<slug>/ request 404'd. Nothing ever complained, because no probe could reach the pages to notice. The consequence was structural: every live instrument in this program - journeys, contrast, viewport, CWV, the UFAI battery - was unable to reach the entire top of the funnel, and a cluster the harness cannot serve is a cluster no live gate can ever grade. Fixed with one route (tools_alias, mirroring learn_alias); the seeder's reloader is deliberately disabled, so it was restarted per its own documented workflow and re-verified: /learn/, /tools/oee-calculator/, /tools/bolt-torque-calculator/, index and logbook all 200, sign-in intact, and a calculator page renders live with 0 pageerrors for the first time.  || THE ~1s INJECTOR WAS IDENTIFIED 2026-08-26 - AND IT IS NOT AN INJECTOR. The recorded suspicion was 'the template's late JS'. A MutationObserver armed ALONGSIDE the shift observer recorded NO insertion of any size at all; what the timeline showed was a 0.182 shift at 903ms and document.fonts.ready at 907ms. Isolated by blocking each candidate: fonts blocked -> CLS 0.000, Tailwind CDN blocked -> CLS 0.156. THE FONT SWAP WAS THE WHOLE CAUSE - five Poppins weights loaded with display=swap, reflowing every line of text once they arrive. (The shift's reported sources were ARTICLE, NAV and anonymous text nodes: the victims, exactly as the recorded lesson warns.) FIXED with one parameter across 113 public pages: display=swap -> display=optional. optional gives the font ~100ms and then NEVER swaps, so the page cannot jump - and measured on a real load it still renders Poppins, so the brand is intact. The only reader who now sees the fallback is on a genuinely slow first load, which is precisely the reader who previously got a 0.384 jump instead. VERIFIED 0.000 CLS on learn articles, tools calculators and the landing page, with the correct font and zero pageerrors. LOCKED BY gate funnel-cls, which asserts the PARAMETER rather than a CLS number, because a lab reading on loopback is optimistic and noisy and a gate that fails intermittently gets ignored. Remaining: LCP/INP under a real mobile throttle (the loopback lab flatters both), and image weights on the landing hero. || ★THE FUNNEL'S IMAGE WEIGHT WAS ONE FILE, AND IT WAS 229 KB (2026-08-28). Censused every local image the public funnel references and there is exactly ONE: brand_assets/workhive-logo-transparent.png, 1024x1024, 229 KB - carried by 193 HTML files, which is the landing page, every learn guide and every app page. A quarter of a megabyte of logo on the first paint of the conversion funnel. ★I NEARLY SHIPPED IT TOO SMALL, and checking is what stopped me: the obvious display sizes are 36px (nav) and 80px (hero), which argued for a ~240px asset at 19.9 KB. Scanning all 242 html files for every sized render of that logo found a 260px instance on index.html - so a 240px asset would have been UNDER its largest display and soft there, blurry on any retina screen. Measure the largest use before choosing the size. SHIPPED 640x640 (2.5x the true 260px maximum, sharp on 2x displays): 229 KB -> 81 KB, 64% smaller, 148 KB saved on every page load across 193 pages. The 1024px master is preserved beside it as workhive-logo-transparent-1024.png, so the full-resolution source survives without reaching for git, and no HTML changed - optimising in place means all 193 references benefit with zero edits and zero chance of a missed one. VERIFIED LIVE on the landing page: naturalWidth 640, rendering at 80px and 40px, none broken, 81 KB actually over the wire, RGBA alpha intact, zero page errors. pct 65 -> 78. Remaining: LCP/INP under a real mobile throttle, which the loopback lab still flatters. || ★★THE PWA SHELL WAS PRECACHING 4.2 MB OF IMAGES TO DRAW A 56px AVATAR (2026-08-28) - the largest single performance defect this programme has found. Chasing the funnel's image weight I checked what ELSE sits in sw.js SHELL_FILES and found brand_assets/hezekiah.png and zaniah.png: 1254x1254 masters at 2016 KB and 1997 KB, BOTH precached, so every installed PWA downloaded ~3.9 MB of portrait before it could work offline - on a platform built for Philippine plant workers on phones, whose own T37 arc is about Slow-3G. ★THE INTENT WAS ALWAYS RIGHT AND THE FILES WERE NEVER BUILT: wh-persona.js carries a comment reading 'PWA-conscious: 256x256 progressive JPEGs (12KB each) generated from the 2.2MB source PNGs'. Those derivatives never existed - a 2026-07-03 fix for the resulting 404 repointed at the MASTERS, which stopped the broken image and shipped 4 MB instead, leaving a comment that still promised 12 KB. They exist now: 9.6 KB and 9.8 KB, progressive JPEG, and the source carries no alpha (mode=RGB), so JPEG was the correct format all along. The masters stay in brand_assets for print and for explainer_studio; they are simply no longer shipped to every device. ALSO: the logo went 1024px/229 KB -> 640px/81 KB, sized from the LARGEST real render (260px on index, found by scanning every sized instance - the obvious 36px and 80px would have produced a 240px asset that was soft on the hero). NET: shell brand assets 4,242 KB -> 100 KB, about 4.14 MB off every PWA install. VERIFIED LIVE with service workers ENABLED: cache workhive-shell-v242, all 31 files precached, worker active, the page fetching zaniah-256.jpg at 9.8 KB, zero page errors - and every SHELL_FILES entry confirmed present on disk first, because a precached missing file fails the whole install. CACHE_NAME bumped v241 -> v242; without it an installed device keeps precaching the masters and never sees the derivatives. || AND THE REST OF THE ASSET WEIGHT IS NOT ON ANYONE'S CRITICAL PATH, which is worth stating so it is not mistaken for outstanding work (2026-08-28). A repo-wide sweep first showed 426 MB of media and looked alarming; the two biggest directories - remotion_scenes/out (rendered video, 26 MB a file) and 'temporary screenshots' (12 MB PNGs) - are GITIGNORED, so they are local build artifacts that never reach the deploy. Measuring only what git tracks gives the honest figure: 227 media files, 78.9 MB, of which the heaviest are a 3.4 MB landing-page screenshot committed at the repo root, five ~2.5 MB promo posters, a 4.4 MB demo video and the portrait masters. NONE of them is fetched by a page - they are deploy weight, not load weight, and no visitor pays for them. THE DISTINCTION IS THE POINT: the only images on a user's critical path were the shell precache (fixed above, 4.04 MB off every install) and the funnel logo (fixed, 148 KB a page). Filing the other 79 MB as a performance defect would have been counting bytes nobody downloads. The stray root screenshot is untidy rather than harmful and is left for a deliberate tidy-up rather than smuggled into a performance arc. || ★THE LOOPBACK LAB MISLEADS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and I nearly banked the second one (2026-08-28). T160's basis already records that the lab FLATTERS timing (no latency). It also PENALISES bytes, and that half was not written down: the local seeder serves UNCOMPRESSED while Netlify serves brotli. Measuring a page load over loopback gave 'index.html 2,366 KB, logbook.html 3,577 KB' - numbers that read like an emergency. Compressing the same files gives the shipped reality: utils.js 312K raw -> 107K gzip -> 88K brotli; index.html 328K -> 92K -> 71K; logbook.html 387K -> 110K -> 87K; nav-hub 96K -> 23K brotli; companion-launcher 94K -> 26K. The five together are ~295 KB brotli against 1,217 KB raw - a FOUR-FOLD difference between what the lab shows and what a visitor pays. Filing the loopback figure would have manufactured a crisis out of the instrument. ★AND IT SHARPENS THE utils.js QUESTION rather than answering it: at 88 KB brotli it is still the largest single script on the critical path, but the 'half of it is comment prose' observation buys less than it sounds - prose is exactly what compresses best, so stripping it saves a fraction of the raw 50%, not half the transfer. Any decision about splitting utils.js should be argued in BROTLI bytes, which is the only number a phone on 3G actually experiences. || ★AND MY OWN FIX EXPOSED A CACHE-POLICY GAP THAT PRE-DATED IT (2026-08-28). _headers grants a year of immutable caching to /*.png, /*.svg, /*.webp and /*.woff2 — and had no rule for /*.jpg. Moving the companion portraits from 2 MB PNGs to 9.6 KB progressive JPEGs therefore quietly cost them a year of caching: A FORMAT SWAP INHERITS THE CACHE POLICY OF ITS NEW EXTENSION, NOT THE OLD ONE, and nothing would have reported it. ★THE GAP WAS WIDER THAN THE TWO FILES THAT REVEALED IT, which is why I enumerated from `git ls-files` instead of from the extensions I happened to be thinking about: 51 tracked .jpeg assets had never been covered either, nor .ico — the favicon, fetched on EVERY page load — nor the 7 .mp4s. Coverage went from 168 of 227 shipped media files to 227 of 227. ★AND ONE ABSENCE IS CORRECT AND STAYS: there is no immutable rule for /*.js, and there must not be, because these scripts are not content-hashed — immutable caching would make a deploy unpickupable. Checking WHY a rule is missing before adding it is the difference between completing a policy and breaking one. cache-invalidation, csp-ratchet and precache-coverage all still pass. pct 88 -> 92. || FONTS WALK CLEAN, WITH ONE MISMATCH WORTH A DESIGN DECISION (2026-08-28). The loading strategy is already the good one: preconnect to BOTH fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com (the second with crossorigin, which is the half people forget), and display=optional — the strongest anti-CLS setting there is, stronger than swap, because an uncached face is simply not used rather than swapped in under the reader. Five weights are requested (400;500;600;700;800) and all five are genuinely used: 600 appears 110 times, 700 150, 800 68 across the sampled files, so nothing is being downloaded for nothing. ★THE MISMATCH RUNS THE OTHER WAY: font-weight 900 and Tailwind's .font-black are used 45 times combined, and 900 is NOT among the requested weights (nor is the one use of 300). Those elements fall back to the nearest loaded face (800) or a synthesised bold — with display=optional there is no shift and no blocking, so the cost is fidelity, not performance: text designed as black renders as extrabold. Two honest fixes and both are Ian's call, not mine: request 900 as well (one more face, ~15-20 KB) or change those 45 usages to font-extrabold so the markup asks for what is actually loaded. Recorded rather than chosen — it is a visual-weight decision, and either way the page is not currently broken. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: the fix is verified and the registered gate funnel-cls PASSES standalone (re-run this session). Awaiting the next full-board earn to promote to locked. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Content freshness governance (the 92-page lesson)
trajectories.basis:
FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the dated-claim INVENTORY built and the staleness lint landed). Scanned 115 public pages for years sitting near a statistic. THE INVENTORY CORRECTED ITS OWN PREMISE, which is the finding: a first pass reported 33 'claims 3+ years old' and nearly every one was a CITATION or a STANDARD EDITION - ISO 14224 (2016), CIBSE Guide D:2015, IEC 62305:2010, DENR DAO 2016-08, Nakajima 1988 for the origin of OEE. Those years are part of the source's IDENTITY, and gating them would have demanded the pages stop citing their standards precisely - the opposite of the goal, with 33 false findings on the way. The shapes that actually rot are narrower and both measured ZERO: a present-tense claim pinned to a past year ('as of 2024, the average plant...'), true when written and quietly false later because nobody re-reads a shipped sentence; and a statistic dated in a year that has not happened, always a typo or template copy that reads as authoritative until checked. Locked as 'dated-claim-freshness' - a guard-the-absence gate in the no-clock-driven-push family, since a property that holds by CARE rather than structure lapses in silence. Its as-of window SLIDES with the clock (current year + two), so it keeps supervising without anyone re-tuning it. Teeth proven on both shapes at once (injected 'as of 2021' + '2029 survey' -> 2 flagged, exit 1). With the count-claim class already clean from the 2026-08-25 walk, both halves of this trajectory's drift concern are now measured and gated. REMAINING: the per-page last-reviewed visibility decision (wave close). || THE DRIFTING-COUNT CLASS CAUGHT ONE, VIA T151's CENSUS (2026-08-28): engineering-design.html's meta and assistant.html's AI grounding both claimed '46 calculation types' against a real 55, and both named Structural (plus Vertical Transportation in the assistant's) as disciplines that do not exist in CALC_TYPES_UI. Fixed and locked by the-calc-count-is-true, which COUNTS THE REGISTRY instead of comparing two hand-maintained strings - the freshness discipline this trajectory exists for, applied to the one claim class that drifts silently because the number was correct when it was typed. || THE DATED-STATS FRESHNESS AUDIT RAN AND FOUND NOTHING STALE - RECORDED AS A MEASURED NEGATIVE, NOT AN ASSUMPTION (2026-08-28). Scanned all learn + tools pages (comments, script and style stripped) for statistics ANCHORED to a year - the 'in 2022', 'as of 2021', 'according to 2019' shape that ages silently while the prose around it still reads fine. Six references to 2023-or-earlier, and every one is a narrative EXAMPLE rather than a statistic: 'the asset was decommissioned in 2022', 'a spreadsheet written by someone who left in 2021', 'a Cabuyao plant solved it in 2023', 'we panic-bought during a supplier crisis in 2022'. Those are illustrations of a scenario and do not decay - an example set in 2022 is still a valid example. NO year-anchored STATISTIC exists on the public pages to go stale, so the class this trajectory worried about is absent rather than unhandled. ★WORTH RECORDING PRECISELY BECAUSE A COUNT ALONE WOULD HAVE READ AS SIX DEFECTS: the difference between a statistic and an anecdote is not visible to the regex that finds both, and filing those six would have sent someone editing correct, deliberately-dated storytelling. The real drifting-count defect this session was in META, not body prose, and it is fixed and gated (the-calc-count-is-true). || APPLIED THE SAME QUESTION TO validate_audience_block AND THE ANSWER WAS CLEAN (2026-08-28). After L4 exposed what validate_tool_aligned_cta would still pass while broken, I asked the sibling content validator the same thing: it reads SOURCE, so it would pass an audience block that exists in markup and never renders - the exact blind spot that produced 18 false a11y findings earlier today. Walked five articles live at 390: every one renders its .audience-block visibly with the 'Who this is for' label and SEVEN roles, none pushed past the right edge. The blind spot is real and the property holds anyway, so nothing is owed. ★AND MY PROBE WAS WRONG TWICE BEFORE IT SAID SO: it searched h1-h4 for the heading and reported heading:false on all five, because the label is a

, not a heading tag. A gate reporting PASS while my probe reported a total absence is a disagreement where the instrument is the likelier suspect, and it was - the third time this session that checking the probe before the product saved a false finding. || ★THE COUNT-CLAIM INVENTORY, RUN (2026-08-28). The roadmap named '53 guides vs 49/55 reality' as this trajectory's specimen drift. RESOLVED and now accurate: learn/index.html says '53 guides' and there are exactly 53 learn//index.html articles. The only other N-guides hit is the local test-data-seeder template, not production. ★THE LIVE ONE: 'WorkHive has 28 connected tools' appears FIVE times on the platform guide - the meta description, the JSON-LD description, the JSON-LD FAQ answer, and the two visible FAQ copies - and the page NEVER ENUMERATES THEM. There is no list of 28 anywhere on it; the 'four stages (Capture/Plan/Analyze/Act and Prove)' it is grouped under is a marketing taxonomy with no headings in the document, not the nav's 6 sections. The nearest enumerable SSOT is nav-hub.js's TOOLS registry: 25 entries (17 visible, 8 hidden) across 6 sections. Root app pages are 42. Nothing on the platform produces 28. ★THIS IS THE DEFECT SHAPE T161 EXISTS FOR: a count with no living producer, replicated into STRUCTURED DATA where answer engines will quote it (the T154 seam), drifting silently because nothing recomputes it. ★I DID NOT CHANGE IT TO 25, deliberately. One trajectory earlier (T162) I was one edit from 'correcting' a true '8 disciplines' to 6 because two valid denominators shared a noun; the discipline that saved it was reading what each number COUNTS before editing. Here I cannot recover what 28 counted, and guessing would replace an unverifiable number with a confidently wrong one. Ian's intent decides whether 'connected tools' means the 25 nav entries or a curated product list - and until then the honest state is recorded, not overwritten. The durable fix is the count-claim staleness lint this trajectory already specs (claims must name a producer), which belongs at the LOCK step, not as a mid-roadmap ceremony. || 2026-08-31 full-board: named gate NOT green (md-twins-current=FAIL) - blocks the lock; must go green before this row can reach 100. || 2026-08-31 FIX LANDED: index.html markdown twin had drifted; regenerated via build_md_twins.py - md-twins-current GREEN standalone (119/119 current). trajectories.title: The competitor-comparison honesty (CMMS-vs-Excel etc.)
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26). Read the three comparison surfaces as a skeptical evaluator (workhive-vs-maintainx, workhive-vs-upkeep, best-free-cmms-software-philippines) plus a superlative sweep of all 115 public pages. THE COMPARISONS ARE HONEST AND NEEDED NO FIX: every competitor price is DATED ('published entry pricing, August 2026'), SOURCED ('vendor published pricing and feature pages, accessed August 2026'), CAVEATED ('SaaS pricing moves, confirm current terms with the vendor before deciding') and generous to the competition ('MaintainX is the strongest mobile-first product in the category'). ★THE SUPERLATIVE SWEEP CORRECTED ITSELF: 72 raw hits, and all but two were ordinary English - 'the first 90 days', 'the best answer', 'the first step'. A gate on that pattern would have been 70 false findings, so none was built. ★THE REAL FINDING WAS HIDDEN INSIDE THE QUALITY: all three pages print 'Pricing verified against vendor and directory listings on 5 August 2026' and 'This comparison is reviewed quarterly'. Those are COMMITMENTS with a clock, not descriptions - and unattended they decay into the worst kind of claim: a confident printed promise of currency beside prices nobody re-checked in a year. A reader trusts the page MORE for that sentence, which is what makes it expensive when it goes false. Locked as 'review-cadence-kept' (verified date must stay inside the promised cadence; quarterly = 92d; no grace, since the page names its own bar; passing output counts down the days). Currently 21 days old and clean - and BUILT TO GO RED around 5 Nov 2026 unless someone re-verifies, which is the point: it turns a marketing sentence into a maintained obligation. Teeth: date aged to 5 Jan -> 233d against a 92d promise, exit 1. RECORDED FOR IAN, not decided - two unverifiable market-position absolutes: index.html 'WorkHive is the first hive designed to close all of them' and ph-industrial-benchmarks-intelligence 'the only Philippine-specific industrial benchmark dataset that exists'. Both are claims about the MARKET that neither I nor a gate can check, and softening positioning copy is a founder's call. || ★TWO TRUE NUMBERS THAT MADE EACH OTHER LOOK LIKE LIES - and I nearly 'fixed' the correct one (2026-08-28). Audited the 4 comparison guides. Competitor honesty came back GOOD and is recorded so nobody re-walks it: no unqualified self-superlatives (the two 'best free CMMS in 2026?' hits are a question in a heading and its JSON-LD twin), and every competitor pricing claim is dated AND caveated - 'verified against vendor and directory listings on 5 August 2026; SaaS pricing changes', 'as of August 2026', dateModified 2026-08-24. That is the responsible shape for content asserting facts about another company. ★THE SELF-CLAIM axis was where the rot was. Content says '60 calculators across 8 disciplines'; index.html and the platform guide say '6 disciplines'; the registry gate (validate_engdesign_registry.py, CALC_TYPES_UI as sole SSOT) says 55 calcs across 6. It read as the platform contradicting itself, and one sentence looked SELF-refuting: '60 calculators across 8 disciplines (HVAC and cooling, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, machine design)' - eight claimed, six named. I was one edit from changing 8 to 6. ★READING THE SECTION SAVED IT: the table above that line lists eight disciplines WITH counts - Electrical & Power 15, Plumbing & Pumps 14, HVAC 10, Mechanical 10, Fire Protection 5, Reliability 2, Vertical Transport 2, Boiler 2 - summing to exactly 60, matching the 60 /tools/ directories. So 60-across-8 describes the PUBLIC tool pages and 55-across-6 describes the IN-APP suite: two different decompositions of the same coverage, both true, neither drifted. The 'contradiction' was an artifact of two subjects sharing one noun. ★WHAT WAS ACTUALLY FALSE, and fixed: (1) that parenthetical had been filled in from the APP's six groupings under the PUBLIC set's count of eight - names now match the table it sits under; (2) the platform guide claimed 'All 60 engineering calculators now exist twice: inside the hive, and as 60 standalone pages', asserting 60 IN THE APP where the gate reports 55 - now states 55-across-6 in the hive and 60 standalone, both figures derived rather than asserted. ★REVIEWED AND DELIBERATELY LEFT: FAQ/JSON-LD lines offering 'the 60 engineering calculators' free - the 60 public pages ARE free and usable by anyone, so that is true of the total offering; only 'inside the hive' was the false framing. ★THE LESSON: my two earlier probes this trajectory BOTH failed as instruments before finding anything (an array regex against an object literal; a slug diff whose sets use different granularities and returned 0 overlap). A cross-file number mismatch is not evidence of drift until you have read what each number COUNTS - and here the platform was right and my inference was wrong. pct 60 -> 80. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate review-cadence-kept re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: "What do you know about me?" (data transparency)
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25): the transparency substrate is the privacy policy's data-class sections (what is collected, who sees it, AI scoping, the TWO parity defects found-and-fixed this session - voice-retention overclaim T137, GA4 stale denial T165's earlier fix) + the T7 join notice ('your records are now visible to your team'). NO in-app my-data view exists (scoped decision). Remaining: the policy<->RLS behavior parity probes (stated visibility == enforced visibility, sampled per class), the audience-vocabulary sweep (T166), the my-data surface decision (wave close). POLICY<->RLS PARITY BUILT + PROVEN 2026-08-26 (gate policy-rls-parity): the privacy policy's cross-hive promise is now tested against the enforcement, per named class, by impersonating a real member (authenticated role + JWT claims) and asking for another hive's rows. Measured: logbook 1700 other-hive rows -> 0 visible (own 941 -> 941), PM completions 486 -> 0 (own 538), asset records 30 -> 0, voice journal 63 -> 0 (own 151 -> 14, correctly stricter: journal_private), community posts 42 un-consented -> 0. Skill matrix reported NOT PROVEN rather than passed (the other hive holds 0 rows - the empty-set trap named, not hidden). INSTRUMENT LESSON: the first run called 8 cross-hive posts a LEAK; they were exactly the public=true rows the AUTHOR published, which is the policy's own consent clause and the reason public-feed exists - right reading, wrong subject. The gate is now consent-aware and teeth-proven (removing the consent predicate makes it see the 8 again). Remaining: the audience-vocabulary sweep (T166), the my-data surface decision. || ★THE POLICY UNDERSTATES THE PROTECTION - the rare direction, and it costs the worker something real (2026-08-28). Read privacy-policy/index.html against the actual RLS. The policy DOES enumerate the data classes (logbook entries, PM completions, asset records, skill matrix, voice journal), which is more than most manage. But measured across the whole document: ZERO visibility statements - no 'who can see', no 'visible', no 'shared with', not even the words 'private' or 'confidential' - and exactly ONE who-sees sentence, a generic 'members of your hive, per the role-based access controls you and your supervisor set up'. ★READ PLAINLY, THAT SENTENCE IS WORSE THAN THE TRUTH. The actual predicates: voice_journal_entries is `auth.uid() = auth_uid` - the AUTHOR ONLY, not the hive, not the supervisor, genuinely private. logbook is hive-scoped to active members. community is opt-in public. So the most personal thing the platform holds is the most protected, and the policy tells a worker the opposite - that what they record is shared with their hive. A person deciding whether to dictate a candid note about a bad shift reads that sentence and does not dictate it. The chilling effect is caused by the DOCUMENT, not the system. ★AND IT IS ONLY REACHABLE FROM THE LANDING PAGE: no in-app surface links it, so the worker most likely to wonder - one who has just used the voice journal - has no route to the answer, right or wrong. ★THE PLATFORM CAN CLEARLY DO THIS WELL: T164's deactivation confirm names anonymized vs revoked vs retained in three clauses. The same treatment applied per data class is the fix, and it is CONTENT, so it goes to Ian - with the evidence now precise enough to write from. pct 60 -> 74. || ★AND THIS IS THE UNFINISHED HALF OF A FIX SOMEONE ALREADY STARTED, which makes it far more credible than a fresh accusation. voice-journal.html now tells the worker plainly - 'Your spoken entries are saved privately under your account' - and its source comment shows the same reasoning I reached independently: 'private surface - voice_journal_entries carries auth.uid() = auth_uid on read, update and delete, so nobody else in the hive can reach a single row - and the page never said so.' Whoever wrote that ALSO noticed the contradiction, and their comment ends on the exact sentence: 'the ONLY private surface and the policies said otherwise.' So the PAGE was corrected and the POLICY was left saying the opposite. The worker who opens the voice journal is now told the truth; the one who goes looking for the policy - the more careful person, the one who checks before trusting - is still told their entries go to the hive. The remedy is one paragraph in a document that already lists the classes, and half the work of noticing it was done before I got here. pct 74 -> 78. || ★THE POLICY UNDERSELLS A REAL PRIVACY PROTECTION - the rare direction, and it costs the product something (2026-08-28). The privacy policy is genuinely good: updated 25 Aug 2026, it enumerates the data classes by name (profile, logbook entries, PM completions, asset records, skill matrix, voice journal recordings, fault notes, plus technical metadata including IP for security audit) and it names the actual architecture in its sharing section rather than hiding behind 'third parties' - Supabase for the database, AI providers for the assistant, email delivery providers. That is more candour than most policies manage. ★BUT IT DOES NOT DISTINGUISH THE PRIVATE CLASS FROM THE HIVE-VISIBLE ONE. 'Voice journal recordings' sits in the same sentence as 'logbook entries' under 'Operational data you enter in your hive', and the sharing clause says hive members see data 'per the role-based access controls you and your supervisor set up'. Measured against RLS, that is wrong in the worker's FAVOUR: voice_journal_entries' SELECT policy is (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND auth.uid() = auth_uid) - the author alone, not hive-scoped, not supervisor-visible. The journal is strictly private and the policy does not say so. ★WHY THE UNDERSELL MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A HARMLESS ERROR: the voice journal's whole value is a worker speaking candidly about a machine, a mistake, or a near-miss. A plant worker who reads that their recordings are 'data you enter in your hive', shared with members per controls their SUPERVISOR sets up, will reasonably conclude the supervisor can listen - and will speak accordingly, or not at all. The platform built the protection and then failed to promise it. ★NOT EDITED BY ME: a privacy policy is a legal document and its wording is Ian's, not something to rewrite from a measurement. What is delivered here is the exact mismatch and the RLS predicate that proves it, so the correction can be made confidently: per-CLASS visibility, with the journal named as private to its author. pct 78 -> 88. || LEAK FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-31, from the CD-invariant psql conversion pass rather than a walk: an ANONYMOUS visitor could read the author's internal auth_uid off every public post. public-feed.html fetches five named columns and was innocent throughout; anon held a TABLE-WIDE SELECT grant on community_posts, and PostgREST executes as the anon role, so anyone with the publishable key could request the column the page declines to show. Measured before the fix: readable on 15 of 15 public posts, exposing 7 distinct authors across 2 hives - auth_uid is stable, so this was a correlation key, not one id. Fixed by migration 20260831000001_anon_cannot_read_post_author_uid (revoke the table grant, re-grant an explicit column allowlist, and drop auth_uid from v_community_posts_truth - a column-level revoke alone is a no-op under a table-wide grant, and the revoke alone then took the whole feed down because the security_invoker view names the column itself). Verified: feed 15 rows for anon, auth_uid refused 42501 on the table and 42703 on the view, community.html's two column lists unaffected. Locked by tools/psql_probes/public-feed__public_identity_only.sql, which asserts the fix AND that the feed still works, and is now EXECUTED by the new psql-probe-suite gate - the recipes were never re-run before, so the lock would have been write-only. PCT HELD AT 88: this closes an exposure, it does not build the in-app 'what do you know about me' surface that is this trajectory's actual remaining gap. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate policy-rls-parity re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100. || REVERTED 2026-09-04: named gate FAILED on the 1034/60 board (false 100%; post_board_promote over-locked). pct -> 90.

trajectories.title: Deletion rights: forget me
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the deletion-SCOPE verification built). Read the live FK graph rather than trusting the policy's prose, and the two AGREE - which is the result, and it is not the one a 'no in-app delete button' walk would predict. 30 FKs reference auth.users from public: CASCADE on 10 carries PERSONAL data away with the account (worker_profiles, voice_journal_entries, resume_documents/versions, worker_achievements, push_subscriptions, mfa_enrollments, service_requests/credit_topups/voucher_redemptions), SET NULL on 20 lets OPERATIONAL records survive with the identity detached (logbook, pm_completions, asset_nodes, inventory_transactions, community_posts, hive_members, skill_badges...). That is exactly the operational-vs-personal tension the policy NAMES: the plant keeps its maintenance history, the person stops being in it. Nothing RESTRICTs or NO-ACTIONs, so no erasure request can be blocked at the database. ★AND THE SUBTLE CHECK PASSED TOO: zero SET NULL FKs point at a NOT NULL column - the shape that inspects clean in the graph and then RAISES at DELETE time, breaking the 30-day promise with no prior symptom. Locked as 'erasure-path-intact' with three assertions (blocked / throws / drifts) and a pinned baseline, because drift in EITHER direction is a failure: CASCADE->SET NULL leaves personal data behind after a purge that reported success, SET NULL->CASCADE destroys history the policy promised to retain. New tables are admitted with their action reported so the gate never stalls schema work. Teeth proven on all three - a throwaway RESTRICT table and a NOT-NULL SET NULL table (both flagged, then dropped, residue re-counted 0) plus a flipped baseline entry. REMAINING: the self-serve deletion door is still a real build (auth + cascade + media) and stays Ian's scope call; media deletion from storage is not covered by the FK graph and needs its own probe (T134 seam). || ★FORGET-ME EXISTS, IS REACHABLE, AND STATES ITS SCOPE - THE DIALOG WAS THE PROBLEM (2026-08-28). deactivate_my_account() is a SECURITY DEFINER self-scoped RPC, reachable from the user menu on both the desktop and mobile layouts, and the confirm already answered the hardest question this trajectory asks - the SCOPE - naming all three categories explicitly: anonymized (name and email, permanently), revoked (access to all hives), and RETAINED WITH ITS REASON (past maintenance records stay with the team, anonymized), plus 'This cannot be undone.' That is the personal-data-versus-operational-records tension named on the glass rather than buried in a policy, which is exactly what was asked for. ★WHAT WAS WRONG: it used NATIVE window.confirm while every other destructive action on the platform goes through whConfirm - and a native dialog cannot be translated. So the most consequential and least reversible decision a person can make here was the one screen a Filipino-speaking worker could read only in English, in a file that already ships _t() copy on 44 other strings. Now bilingual through whConfirm, with bilingual buttons, and the closing confirmation translated too - it is the last sentence the platform ever says to that person and the only one telling them it worked. ★AND THE FAILURE PATH STOPPED PASTING PostgREST at someone who has just tried to erase themselves: it routes through whWriteError with the fallback 'Your account was NOT deactivated. Nothing was changed.' alert() is deliberately KEPT rather than swapped for a toast - it blocks, and a failure on this action must not be missed in a fade. pct 60 -> 80. || ★AND THE CLASS IS CLOSED, NOT JUST THE INSTANCE. Swept every root page plus utils and nav-hub for native browser dialogs: THREE remain platform-wide, all window.alert, all inside this same deactivation flow, and all three are the blocking messages I deliberately kept and translated. Zero native window.confirm and zero window.prompt anywhere - the one I replaced was the last native CONFIRM on the platform, which is a better outcome than the fix I set out to make. Worth recording because it means no other destructive path is quietly untranslatable, and nobody needs to re-run this sweep to find out. || ★THE MECHANISM IS RIGHT; THE POLICY AND THE CONTROL DESCRIBE IT IN INCOMPATIBLE WORDS (2026-08-28). Forget-me EXISTS and is well built: deactivateAccount calls a real RPC, deactivate_my_account, and the confirm states exactly what will happen, bilingually - 'Your name and email will be permanently anonymized and you will lose access to all hives. Your past maintenance records stay with the team (anonymized).' That is ANONYMISATION, not erasure, and for an industrial platform it is the correct design: a machine's maintenance and failure history cannot be deleted because a technician left, or the asset's safety record dies with the employment. Under PDPA, anonymised records stop being personal data, so this satisfies the right while keeping the plant's record intact. The control tells the truth. ★THE POLICY TELLS A DIFFERENT STORY IN DIFFERENT VOCABULARY. It promises 'Delete your account and ALL ASSOCIATED PERSONAL DATA' and 'After account deletion, personal data is purged within 30 days'. A worker reading that goes looking for DELETE and finds DEACTIVATE; nothing connects the two words, and nothing tells them their logbook entries survive under an anonymised name. The two documents are reconcilable - anonymisation is HOW the personal data is purged - but nobody has written the sentence that reconciles them. ★AND ONE PROMISE HAS NO IMPLEMENTATION AT ALL: the same rights list offers 'Export your data in a portable format', which is the PDPA access right. Per T188, export_hive_data is granted only to postgres and service_role - no authenticated user can call it, and the safe caller-scoped replacement has not been built. That gap runs the harmful direction: the policy promises a right the product cannot currently deliver. ★Both are Ian's to close, and the wording is his - a privacy policy is not something to rewrite from a measurement. What is delivered is the exact pair of mismatches and the mechanism each rests on. pct 80 -> 90. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate erasure-path-intact re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

fixes: voice-journal.html (erasure route added to the existing permanence disclosure)

trajectories.note: ★THE RIGHT-TO-ERASURE IS VOICE-ONLY, AND THE PAGE NEVER SAID WHERE TO GO (2026-08-27). Tracing what a worker can take back took FOUR corrections, and every intermediate answer would have shipped a false statement into the platform's most private surface: (1) 'there is no delete' - WRONG: voice-handler's _isErasureRequest detects "delete my voice history" / "burahin mo lahat", the agent asks for a yes because it cannot be undone, a scoped DELETE runs against that worker's rows and an audit row records it; (2) 'you can say OR TYPE it' - WRONG: the check sits in _converseInline, called only from _onStopRecording, so it is reached ONLY after a voice recording, and this page's typed box goes processTurn -> callJournalAgent -> ai-gateway without ever touching voice-handler; (3) there is no typed route anywhere - assistant.html has no erasure path and the companion panel has no text input; (4) a SINGLE note cannot be removed at all, because renderHistory offers only 'Speak again' and ai-gateway persists the row inside the same call that generates the reply. ★WHY VOICE-ONLY MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS: this page's typed fallback exists, in its own words, for 'a loud plant floor, a denied mic, or a worker who cannot speak' - precisely the people left with no way to invoke the right. ★AND THE FIX WAS ALMOST DUPLICATION: the permanence was ALREADY disclosed on the primary surface ('saved as soon as the assistant replies ... an entry cannot be edited or removed here afterwards'), and a first attempt added a SECOND copy of it inside a collapsed <details> nobody opens - a new element surfacing what already had a home. Reverted. What was genuinely missing was the other half: the copy said a note cannot be removed HERE and never said where it CAN be. One clause now completes that sentence, pointing at the documented Data Rights Request route which validate_erasure_path_intact already proves the database honours. The voice phrase is deliberately NOT advertised as the remedy, because for a worker who cannot speak it is not one. ★STILL OPEN (product decision, and small): wiring the typed path to the same check - both _isErasureRequest and _executeErasure are already exported, and _executeErasure needs only db + hive_id + worker_name, all available on this page - plus whether a per-entry delete should exist at all given the row is embedded for retrieval.

Corrected to describe reality (GA4 on public pages, anonymize_ip, no-PII event params, engagement/conversion events, no ad cookies; in-app events stay first-party) and moved all three date stamps together (dateModified + visible times). Gate the-policy-matches-what-ships holds PARITY in both directions: GA4 shipping obliges the policy to name it, state its anonymization, and carry no future-tense denial; GA4 being removed would oblige the reverse, since a policy still describing it over-claims what is collected. trajectories.title: Role-based visibility comprehension (who sees this?)
trajectories.basis: composer-audience census: community's composer says the audience IN THE VERB ('Post to Hive') + supervisor public-toggle rides the announcement-lock confirm; voice-journal states privacy in its disclosure ('private spoken log', audio discarded); public-feed IS the public surface. THE GAP: the logbook composer states no audience (hive-visible implied, never said - the T7 join toast is the only place 'visible to your team' appears). One vocabulary (private/team/public) + the logbook line = wave close. AUDIENCE SWEEP + A SELF-CAUGHT ERROR 2026-08-26. Read the ACTUAL policies rather than assuming: skill_profiles, skill_badges and skill_exam_attempts are all `auth_uid = auth.uid()` - a worker's skills, badges and exam attempts are PRIVATE, invisible even to their supervisor - while skill_knowledge is hive-scoped. Two fixes: (1) skillmatrix had NO visibility statement at all and now says 'Private to you: your skills, badges and exam attempts are visible only to you, not to your supervisor or teammates' - the opposite of what a worker would assume on a team platform, which is exactly why it must be stated; (2) the join-flow welcome card written EARLIER THE SAME DAY claimed 'Only your Voice Journal stays private to you' - measurably wrong, and now corrected to name the Skill Matrix too. A visibility promise has to be read off the RLS policies, not from memory - my own copy was the counter-example. Remaining: composer-level audience labels on the remaining write surfaces, one-vocabulary check for private/team/public wording.  || THE SHARPEST COMPOSER GAP FOUND AND CLOSED 2026-08-26: voice-journal.html had ZERO audience statements while being the platform's MOST private surface. Verified against the policies rather than assumed - voice_journal_entries carries auth.uid() = auth_uid on READ, UPDATE and DELETE, so no teammate and no supervisor can reach a single row. The page never said so. The only place a worker was ever told lived on hive.html's join-flow welcome card: seen once, on a different page, at a moment they were not writing anything personal - and a privacy guarantee a person cannot see is one they cannot rely on, on the one surface where being candid is the point. It now says so directly above the box, in wording read off the RLS. AUDIENCE-COVERAGE CENSUS across the write surfaces: community, logbook and hive state their audience; voice-journal did not (now does); dayplanner, marketplace and project-manager carry no audience phrase and are the remaining candidates - lower stakes, since none of them is a place a worker writes something personal. LOCKED BY gate composer-audience, which checks BOTH ENDS - the claim on the page AND the policies enforcing it - because a promise the database does not keep is worse than no promise. It is a short NAMED list by design: a gate demanding an audience label on every input would fire on search boxes and be switched off within a week. Resurrection RED on the pre-fix page. Remaining: the one-vocabulary decision between 'your hive' and 'your team' (both in use today), and audience labels on the three lower-stakes composers. pct -> 100.

fixes: voice-journal.html: privacy stated at the composer, wording read off the RLS
dayplanner.html / inventory.html / pm-scheduler.html: each composer states its audience
tools/validate_composer_audience.py: 6 surfaces; owner-scope accepts both operand orders

trajectories.note: ★T166 CLOSED ON BOTH ITEMS (2026-08-27), and the first one dissolved under measurement. ★THE 'ONE-VOCABULARY DECISION between your hive and your team' WAS A FALSE PREMISE. Measured across every page: 585 'hive' against 123 'team' - but the split is not drift, it is a DISTINCTION the platform keeps correctly. 'Team' names the PEOPLE ('invite your team', 'your team logs', 'your team works in Filipino'); 'hive' names the WORKSPACE. One sentence uses both exactly right: 'Hive created. Invite your team.' And the drift case does not exist - searching for team-as-workspace ('switch team', 'join team', 'leave team', 'create team') returns ONE hit, which is that same correct sentence. One-vocabulary means one concept, one name; it does not mean banning a word that names a different concept. No decision was needed and none is owed to Ian - the answer was in the corpus. ★THE SECOND ITEM WAS REAL: none of the five candidate lower-stakes composers said who reads what is written. Three now do, and the answers genuinely DIFFER, which is exactly why each has to say it instead of letting people generalise from the page they were last on: dayplanner's notes are PRIVATE (schedule_items read = auth_uid = auth.uid()), while inventory's part notes and pm-scheduler's findings are HIVE-VISIBLE - and findings in particular are the maintenance RECORD a supervisor reads to learn what was actually done, which someone who thinks they are writing to themselves writes differently. Gate composer-audience widened 3 -> 6 surfaces, with dayplanner's privacy claim CHECKED against the policy rather than trusted. ★AND THE GATE WAS WRONG FIRST, in the way this file keeps being wrong: its owner-scope test matched only `auth.uid() = auth_uid` and schedule_items stores the same predicate as `auth_uid = auth.uid()`. An equality has no canonical direction, so a genuinely private table read as NOT owner-scoped and a TRUE privacy claim was reported as a promise the database does not keep. The checker was reading its own habit rather than the policy. Both orders now accepted. ★LOCKED (2026-08-27): the done-definition is 'no one publishes by surprise', and the gate measures exactly that - composer-audience passes with SIX write surfaces stating who can see what is written, AND each privacy claim checked against the policy that enforces it rather than taken at its word. dayplanner's line is the shape to keep: 'private to you; nobody else in your hive can read your planner notes', with schedule_items confirmed owner-scoped (auth_uid = auth.uid()). A claim about who can see something is worth nothing unless the database agrees, and here it was made to.

trajectories.title: The security-headers & client hardening pass (user-visible edges)
trajectories.basis: the posture census found TWO prod-only defects in _headers (which the local stack never serves - no walk could see them): (1) Permissions-Policy camera=()/microphone=() SITE-WIDE killed the voice journal's mic + logbook photo/QR in production -> fixed to (self); (2) the CSP predated GA4 (no googletagmanager/analytics endpoints) so the shipped funnel analytics were silently DEAD in prod -> allowed. Baseline posture otherwise solid: XFO DENY, nosniff, referrer-policy, frame-ancestors none, backup-page + artifact noindex, immutable-media caching, sw no-store. Remaining: HSTS decision + security.txt + the curl-based deployed-origin headers gate (prod smoke family) - wave close. Memory saved: feedback_headers_file_is_prod_only_behavior. || AN UNAUDITED PRIVILEGE SURFACE: 8 SECURITY DEFINER RPCs THAT NOTHING CALLS AND ANYONE CAN (2026-08-27). Asked which client-callable RPCs have no caller, and narrowed it honestly: 285 grantable routines -> 103 that are OURS (excluding pgvector's array_to_halfvec/binary_quantize and trigger-returning functions, which are called BY triggers) -> 76 with no DB-side caller (asking pg_proc.prosrc and pg_policies rather than grepping files, because is_marketplace_admin is invoked by 29 RLS POLICIES and no page) -> 18 with no caller anywhere: not a page, not an edge function, not another function, not a policy. ★8 OF THE 10 THAT NOTHING AT ALL CALLS ARE SECURITY DEFINER - acknowledge_alert, suppress_alert, toggle_feedback_upvote, publish_service_showcase, fetch_session_memory, rerank_kb_chunks, ai_cache_bump, ai_cache_sweep_expired - so they run with the definer's rights, bypassing RLS, and every one is granted to authenticated. A function nobody uses is a function nobody reviews, which makes it the most comfortable place for a privilege bug to sit. ai_cache_bump and ai_cache_sweep_expired are plainly internal cache maintenance that no end user should be able to invoke at all - this is the recorded definer-cron-helper-is-user-callable-by-default class, recurring. MITIGATION ALREADY PRESENT: all 8 pin a search_path (2 the stronger 'pg_catalog, public'), so the classic search-path hijack is closed; the exposure is the GRANT, not the definition. ★AND THE FEATURES THEY LOOK LIKE ARE NOT BROKEN: alert-hub's acknowledgeAlert writes alert_dismissals DIRECTLY (delete/upsert under RLS) rather than calling acknowledge_alert, so acking works and the RPC is an unused parallel implementation - redundancy, not absence, which is why nothing looks wrong from the glass. Remaining: decide per function whether to REVOKE the grant (internal helpers) or adopt the RPC and retire the direct write (feature paths) - either resolves the drift, and leaving two implementations is what lets them diverge. ★CORRECTION TO THE ABOVE, MADE BY READING ALL FOUR RATHER THAN GENERALISING FROM THE CATEGORY: there is NO cross-tenant exposure among them. The worry was an IDOR - DEFINER functions that take a caller-supplied ID bypass RLS, so they must do the scoping themselves. Each of the four that takes an id DOES: fetch_session_memory filters `am.worker_id = auth.uid()`, so a guessed session id returns nothing that is not yours; suppress_alert requires an active hive_members row matching auth.uid() for that alert's hive; publish_service_showcase refuses unless client_auth_uid = auth.uid(). These are correctly-written DEFINER functions - they carry the check that RLS would otherwise have carried. ★AND THE FOURTH IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF PROBLEM: rerank_kb_chunks reads NO table at all. It is a placeholder that echoes the ids you passed with a hardcoded 0.95 score ('actual reranking via LLM happens in edge function'), so there is nothing to leak - but if anything ever adopts it, every chunk comes back with the same fabricated confidence and the caller believes reranking happened. That is the proxy-oracle class: a function that reports success while the payoff is missing. Inert today because nothing calls it; a landmine the moment something does. ★SO THE FINDING IS SMALLER AND MORE PRECISE THAN THE CATEGORY SUGGESTED: not a privilege hole, but (a) unnecessary GRANTs on internal helpers - ai_cache_bump and ai_cache_sweep_expired are cache maintenance with no business being user-callable - and (b) a placeholder that will lie confidently if adopted. Remaining: revoke the internal-helper grants, and either implement rerank_kb_chunks or drop it so it cannot be adopted by mistake. || ★FOUR SHIPPED FEATURES WERE DEAD IN PRODUCTION, BLOCKED BY OUR OWN CSP — found by sweeping the class instead of patching the instance (2026-08-28). T169's Turnstile finding was the THIRD prod-only failure recorded in `_headers`, so rather than fix it and move on, every external host referenced by shipped code was enumerated and checked against the policy. Four more were blocked, every one a live feature on a live page: analytics.html loads Plotly from cdn.plot.ly via <script src> (charts never render); engineering-design.html loads html2pdf from cdnjs (PDF export dead); engineering-design.js calls engineering-calc-api.onrender.com for /pdf and /diagram (both dead on connect-src); and marketplace.html's map is dead TWICE OVER — tiles.openfreemap.org missing from connect-src, and MapLibre builds its renderer in a Worker from a blob: URL while `worker-src` appeared ZERO times in the file, so it inherited default-src 'self' and blocked the worker outright. None of this fails locally: `_headers` is served only by Netlify, and the sole symptom is a console message in someone else's browser. ★THE MAP IS THE CASE WORTH REMEMBERING, because nobody was ignorant: wh-map.js states the requirement in its OWN header — 'Prod CSP needs connect-src https://tiles.openfreemap.org + worker-src blob:'. It was written down, correctly, by the person who knew it, in the file that needed it, and never reached the file that ENFORCES it. A note in the consumer is not a change in the policy. That is the identical shape as the Turnstile switch, one abstraction layer over. FIX: script-src gains cdn.plot.ly + cdnjs.cloudflare.com, connect-src gains tiles.openfreemap.org + engineering-calc-api.onrender.com, and worker-src 'self' blob: is declared — granting exactly what ships, nothing wider. ★LOCKED BY A NEW GATE, csp-covers-what-ships, registered in Platform. It runs TWO independent checks because the failures arrive two ways: MECHANICAL (every external <script src> and stylesheet <link> host must be permitted) and DOCUMENTARY (any 'CSP needs <directive> <value>' written in a source comment must be honored) — the second is precisely what the map incident asked for. Teeth-proven by reverting all four grants and watching it name all four, including that an absent worker-src is a DENIAL rather than a neutral omission. Self-test: 7 cases. ★TWO INSTRUMENT FLAWS FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE THE GATE WAS TRUSTED, both by sampling its own output: (1) it read 90 characters past an href looking for rel=stylesheet, reached into the NEXT <link> on the following line, and reported 8 pages as loading a remote stylesheet from supabase.co when all 8 were rel='preconnect' — eight fabricated defects, avoided by matching the whole tag; (2) its requirement parser ended a sentence at the first '.', which lands inside a hostname, so wh-map.js's requirement was read as 'connect-src https://tiles' and the '+ worker-src blob:' half was never parsed — the gate was silently checking one of the two things it existed to check. ★HONEST SCOPE: connect-src is NOT checked against every https:// literal in the source. Those are dominated by things CSP does not govern (anchor hrefs, JSON-LD @context, canonical URLs, placeholder examples), and a check that noisy gets muted — which is worse than no check. So the onrender.com API constant is fixed but not gated; the documentary half covers that class where it matters, since whoever adds a remote API is exactly the person who writes the requirement down. pct -> 88. || ★THE PUBLISH-ROOT EXPOSURE: the missing piece was never the fix, it was the EVIDENCE that a targeted fix is safe (2026-08-28). netlify.toml sets publish = '.', so every gate baseline, audit report and platform-check log in the repo root is fetchable at the live domain — by the file's own count ~276 files, several over 70KB, whose text narrates internal architecture, table names and security findings. `_headers` marks them noindex and says plainly that 'the real fix is excluding them from the publish step', and the reason that was never done is recorded right there: design-system.html legitimately reads *_baseline.json, so a blanket block breaks a live page. ★MEASURED WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEEDED, which nobody had: exactly EIGHT root data files are fetched by shipped code — api_adoption_baseline.json, api_component_registry.json, component_adoption_baseline.json and design_component_registry.json (design-system.html), field_impact_preview.json (impact-preview.js), learn_links.json (learn-link.js), and VALIDATOR_REGISTRY.json + platform_health.json (validator-catalog.html). None is a .log, a .jsonl, a *-output.txt or a *_report.json — so those four families can be force-404'd with zero effect on any page, following the precedent already in netlify.toml, where /_fixtures/* is blocked exactly that way. Only the *_baseline.json family genuinely must stay reachable, and only two of its members. ★NOT SHIPPED, DELIBERATELY: netlify.toml is itself PROD-ONLY — nothing local serves it — so a redirect I cannot execute here is a change whose first real run is on Ian's site, and a pattern that over-matches would 404 a working dashboard rather than fail loudly. That is a deploy decision on his gate, not a default for me to pick while he is away. The evidence is what was missing, and it is now recorded: the block is safe for four families, unsafe for the fifth, and the exact eight exceptions are enumerated. || ★A SIXTH INSTANCE, IN THE OTHER HEADER — AND IT WAS LEFT BEHIND BY THE FIX FOR THE FIRST TWO (2026-08-28). The Permissions-Policy incident this file already documents fixed camera and microphone and left `geolocation=()` untouched, because nobody asked whether anything used it. Something does: marketplace-seller.html publishes a service provider's LIVE LOCATION to their client during an active job — watchPosition, one write per 15s for battery, a visible '📍 Sharing your live location with this job's client' indicator, stopping when the job set empties, with the column readable only through v_service_job_tracking. An EMPTY allowlist denies every origin INCLUDING self, so in production that feature never started. ★AND IT FAILED INVISIBLY IN THE CRUELEST WAY: its own error callback calls _svcGeoIndicator(false), so a blocked permission hides the very indicator that would have shown something was wrong — the provider sees exactly what 'no active job' looks like, and the client waiting to see them move sees nothing, with no error anywhere. Fixed to geolocation=(self), matching what camera and microphone already had. ★THE GATE NOW COVERS BOTH HEADERS, because they are one class: csp-covers-what-ships maps the browser APIs the code actually calls (geolocation / camera / microphone) to the policy features that gate them, treats `feature=()` as the denial it is, and correctly ignores an UNDECLARED feature (which defaults to allowing self) and vendored bundles like maplibre-gl that reference APIs we may never invoke. Teeth-proven by reverting to geolocation=() and watching it name the file and the reason; self-test now 10 cases. Fixing two features in a header without auditing the third is how a policy repeats itself — five weeks apart, same header, same shape. pct 88 -> 92. || ★BOARD CLOSE-OUT: 4 of the 5 full-board FAILs resolved, and the 5th is flagged as possibly the instrument (2026-08-28). The 53-minute board finished 609 PASS / 5 FAIL. Substrate freshness was my own editing wave (rebuilt, green). Home-stack coverage was MY regression, caught only by the full board (fixed). The two AI validators both carried a stale hardcoded calc count (both now DERIVE it; both green). ★THE FIFTH, CLONE DEBT, IS LEFT RED ON PURPOSE AND WITH A CAVEAT: it reports a 534-line CSS clone between ai-quality.html and plant-connections.html, but those files carry only ~105 and ~100 lines inside <style> blocks respectively, and both already share tokens.css. A 534-line CSS duplication cannot fit in ~100 lines of CSS, so the figure is measuring something other than what its label says - a denominator worth checking BEFORE anyone extracts 534 lines that may not exist. The debt is also cumulative and pre-existing (both files carry uncommitted changes dated 2026-08-26, before this session), so it is not mine to bend a baseline for. Left red as an honest signal rather than silenced, with the discrepancy recorded so the next pass starts by auditing the metric rather than the pages. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Abuse resistance as UX: rate limits meet real users
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the at-the-cap journey driven live). Drove the community composers at their real DB caps (community_posts 2000, community_replies 1000, report details 500 - all CHECK constraints, verified in pg_constraint). THE COOLDOWN REFUSALS ALREADY MEET THE BAR: 'Slow down, wait Ns before posting again' names both the limit and its reset, which is exactly what rate_limit_legible asks for. ★THE DEFECT WAS THE SILENT HALF OF THE SAME PAGE: community.html had built the right pattern and applied it unevenly - the post composer (2000) and report box (500) each carried a live 'n / max' counter, the reply box (1000) carried none. A maxlength with no counter is a SILENT WALL: the textarea stops accepting keystrokes and the person reads that as a broken keyboard, not a rule, losing the thought they were part-way through. Added the counter in the page's own idiom, wired its input listener, and reset it at BOTH clear sites (thread open + after a reply posts) because a counter holding the last message's length is a stale reading, worse than none. Live-verified all three: '37 / cap' while typing, '0 / cap' when cleared, 0 pageerrors. ★AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG TWICE BEFORE THE FINDING SURVIVED: a static scan inferring the counter id from the field id ('<id>-char-count') reported #post-content as uncounted - its counter is #post-char-count, so the convention is not a convention. It also listed 42 'uncounted' fields platform-wide, most of them 200-char part-number boxes that need no counter. Neither was banked. The prover is therefore LIVE and types into each field, because a counter is whatever visible element MOVES WHEN YOU TYPE. Locked as 'composer-caps-visible' (teeth: counter id disabled -> 'reply-content: no counter', exit 1). REMAINING: burst-sizing review for bulk-approving supervisors, and the appeal/raise path statement (wave close). The AI-quota classes ride with T39. || ★THE RESET-TIME CAPABILITY EXISTS IN ONE DOMAIN AND IS ABSENT IN THE ONE WORKERS ACTUALLY HIT (2026-08-28). This trajectory asks whether each quota's refusal names the limit AND when it clears. Split answer. THE MARKETPLACE SIDE DOES IT: marketplace.html carries _retryAfterSeconds(err), which reads err.retryAfter / err.retry_after and even digs a digit out of err.hint, with a comment noting 'most gateways answer a rate limit with Retry-After, in seconds or as an HTTP date' - and marketplace-seller and marketplace-seller-profile use the same helper. So a rate-limited buyer or seller can be told how long. ★THE AI SIDE CANNOT, AND THE REASON IS UPSTREAM OF THE COPY: ai-gateway never emits Retry-After at all - zero references in the function - so there is nothing for the client to surface, and whAiError's 429 branch accordingly says only 'You have hit the AI rate limit. Wait a moment and try again.' (bilingual, and honest as far as it goes). That is the quota a worker meets most often, because the AI budget is shared across the whole platform and drains on a busy Friday. 'Wait a moment' is exactly the sentence that makes someone retry immediately and hit it again. ★SO THE FIX IS NOT COPY: the gateway has to emit the window it already knows about, and only then does the taxonomy have something true to say. An edge-function change, and one that depends on whether the upstream provider hands back a retry window at all - which is why it is recorded rather than guessed at. The rest of the taxonomy is strong: the 401 branch names the cause AND the state of the user's work ('your typed work is still on this page'), which is the bar the 429 branch has not got the data to meet. pct 60 -> 74. || ★BUILT THE CAPABILITY THAT WAS MISSING, because the window was computable all along (2026-08-28). _shared/rate-limit.ts now carries retry_after_seconds on the BASE RateLimitResult - the base, because all six limiters share that shape and any of them can be the one that denies, notably the per-user limiter a worker meets first at 25/hour. Two helpers compute it honestly: secondsToNextHour() for the route limiter, whose counter is bucketed to the hour so the reset is EXACT; and secondsToWindowEnd(start, span) for the rolling windows, which falls back to the FULL span when a start is unreadable - over-stating the wait rather than under-stating it, since an under-stated wait sends someone straight back into the wall. Both deny paths in checkAIRateLimit populate it, day and hour, using the window starts already in hand. rateLimitedResponse now emits it three ways: a real sentence ('Try again in about 4 minutes' rather than 'in an hour'), BOTH body spellings retryAfter and retry_after (because the existing client helper _retryAfterSeconds looks for both), and an actual Retry-After header. When no window is known it keeps the old wording rather than inventing a duration - a wrong 'try again in 2 minutes' is worse than a vague hour. ★VERIFIED NUMERICALLY, since no deno is available here: both helpers were run against hour boundaries (00:00 -> 3600, 59:59 -> 1) and window ages (10 min in -> 3000, 59 min in -> 60, stale -> 1, null and garbage -> full span). All correct. ★AND A SECOND FINDING FELL OUT OF IT: rateLimitedResponse takes a `scope` parameter and NOT ONE of its ten callers passes it. So a DAILY limit hit has always reported 'Try again in an hour' - wrong by up to a day, in the direction that makes someone retry uselessly. ★WHAT IS OWED: the callers must pass rl.scope and rl.retry_after_seconds, and the gateway's composite result needs to carry them out of checkClassedRateLimit. That is plumbing across 10+ edge functions I cannot deploy or live-test from here, so it is left named rather than half-done. The hard part - knowing WHEN the window reopens - is built and proven. pct 74 -> 82. || ★AND THE WIRING IS DONE FOR THE PATH THAT MATTERS, after finding the ROOT of why nobody ever passed it. ai-gateway annotated its rate-limit result with an INLINE STRUCTURAL TYPE - { allowed, remaining, hive_remaining?, user_cap? } - narrower than what the limiters actually return.
