trajectories.title: The Turnstile & bot-defense experience
trajectories.basis: posture read: su-turnstile div ships INERT (no sitekey configured) = bot defense is OFF in prod today; the wiring is one dashboard sitekey away (GoTrue captcha + the client's conditional mount both exist). Whether to ARM it is Ian's posture decision (signup friction vs bot pressure - the prod smoke signed up unchallenged). Remaining: the defense-active prod-smoke check once armed + challenge a11y (wave close). || THE BOT-DEFENSE POSTURE READ IN FULL: DELIBERATE, FAIL-SAFE, AND CURRENTLY UNARMED (2026-08-27). Turnstile is wired configure-to-enable: mountTurnstile() returns immediately unless window.WH_TURNSTILE_SITEKEY is set, and WH_TURNSTILE_SITEKEY is set NOWHERE in the codebase - it appears only in the read itself and in two comments describing the arming procedure. So bot defense is OFF today, by choice rather than by oversight, and the choice is documented at the call site. ★THE WIRING IS CORRECTLY COUPLED, WHICH IS THE PART THAT COULD HAVE BEEN SUBTLY WRONG: a captchaToken is sent ONLY when a widget actually exists, because GoTrue REJECTS a token when captcha is disabled in the project - so a half-armed state (client sending tokens, server not expecting them) would break signup completely for everyone. The inert path therefore runs signUp() exactly as before, no token attached. Arming is genuinely two-sided and external: a Cloudflare sitekey AND the Supabase Auth > Bot Protection toggle, both Ian's to set. Remaining: unchanged - the defense-active prod-smoke check once armed, and challenge a11y (T48 seam) at wave close. || ★THE SWITCH COULD NOT BE THROWN — A LATENT FRONT-DOOR OUTAGE, ARMED AND WAITING FOR THE CONFIG CHANGE THAT WOULD FIRE IT (2026-08-28). First, the posture question this trajectory asks is answered and the answer is deliberate: bot defense is OFF. window.WH_TURNSTILE_SITEKEY is set NOWHERE in shipped code — only in tests/auth-identity-arc-i.spec.ts, using Cloudflare's always-passes test key — and the Arc I integration is a genuine configure-to-enable design (inert loader, no captchaToken sent when unconfigured), which is the right shape for a feature waiting on a provider. ★BUT THE SWITCH WAS DOCUMENTED AS TWO STEPS AND HAD A SILENT THIRD, in `_headers` — a tracked local file nobody flipping that switch would think to open. CSP script-src did not permit challenges.cloudflare.com, and NO frame-src was declared at all, so it inherited default-src 'self' and would have blocked Turnstile's challenge iframe. The consequence is not a degraded widget, it is SIGNUP DYING PLATFORM-WIDE: script blocked => window.turnstile never defined => mountTurnstile()'s render() returns early => _turnstileToken() returns null => signUp() sends no captchaToken — while step two of the very same switch tells Supabase Auth to reject exactly that. The feature meant to protect the front door would have closed it, the only evidence a console CSP violation, and `_headers` is PROD-ONLY so nothing local reproduces it. This is the third instance of that class in this file ([[feedback_headers_file_is_prod_only_behavior]]: Permissions-Policy killed mic+camera, CSP kept GA4 dead) and the first LATENT one. FIX: script-src gains https://challenges.cloudflare.com and frame-src is declared for it — Cloudflare's documented requirement — granted now, while the feature is off, so the switch is TRUE when someone finally throws it. ★AND THE GATE'S OWN SCOPE CLAIM WAS WRONG: validate_signup_bot_protection's docstring called the remainder 'the PROVIDER half = attributed, out of local scope', when one of those steps was entirely local — a ceiling written into a tool's docstring ([[feedback_a_ceiling_written_into_a_tools_docstring]]). The gate now audits the edge half too, with an ABSENT frame-src treated as a FAILURE rather than a neutral omission, because CSP's fallback makes the omission and the denial the same header to a browser. Teeth-proven on the real file (pre-fix policy => 2 FAILs naming both halves, green after) and in a self-test carrying the exact shipped policy plus a frame-ancestors decoy, since frame-ancestors answers the opposite question from frame-src and must not be mistaken for it. pct 25 -> 80; the remainder is challenge accessibility and the errored-challenge retry path, both un-probed while the widget cannot render. || ★MY OWN FIX WAS ONE KEYSTROKE FROM SHIPPING THE SAME BUG IT REPAIRED — caught by auditing my change instead of assuming it was purely additive. Declaring frame-src REPLACES the default-src fallback rather than adding to it, so introducing the directive `frame-src https://challenges.cloudflare.com` silently REVOKED same-origin framing. assistant.html lazily embeds voice-journal.html for its Journal tab (:498, frame.src = 'voice-journal.html?embedded=1'), so the Turnstile fix would have broken the assistant in production — invisible exactly the way the original defect was, since _headers has no local equivalent and a blocked frame throws nothing the page can observe. Corrected to `frame-src 'self' https://challenges.cloudflare.com`, and the gate now asserts it: a declared frame-src missing 'self' FAILS by name, with the near-miss policy added to the self-test (7 cases, all passing). The lesson generalises past this directive — a CSP directive that inherits by absence becomes exclusive the moment it is written, so ADDING one is never purely additive. (The two phrases above were eaten once already: written through a shell that evaluated their backticks as command substitution, leaving 'introducing  silently REVOKED' and 'Corrected to ,' in the record. Repaired via a quoted heredoc — the same trap, and the same fix, as the earlier regex-escape incident this session. A record that loses the exact string it is about is worse than no record, because it still reads as complete.) || ★PCT FIELD CORRECTED DOWN TO MATCH THIS BASIS (2026-08-31). The field read 86 while the basis's own last word was 80 - a later note revised the number and only the prose was updated. Every one of the six rows found this way was inflated, never deflated, which is the direction drift always takes when nothing checks it: the number a reader trusts drifts up while the narrative underneath it says otherwise. Now gated by pct-matches-basis. pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: MEASURED, so the decision can be made on facts rather than a guess. Bot defense is OFF on BOTH halves and deliberately so: window.WH_TURNSTILE_SITEKEY is assigned NOWHERE in the codebase (so mountTurnstile() is a no-op and the #su-turnstile div stays empty), and GoTrue's GOTRUE_SECURITY_CAPTCHA_ENABLED is empty. The code is correct as written - it is inert-by-default behind a documented TWO-condition arm (a sitekey AND Supabase Auth > Bot Protection), and signUp() sends no captchaToken while disabled, which matters because GoTrue REJECTS a captchaToken when captcha is off. So arming one half alone would break signup; both must move together. WHAT PROTECTS SIGNUP TODAY: GoTrue rate limits are live - verify 30/hr and anonymous 30/hr - so the door is throttled even unguarded, and there is no abuse signal to act on (0 signups in the last day on this fixture). ★NOT ARMED BY ME, AND NOT A CEILING I AM HIDING BEHIND: the provider half needs a Cloudflare sitekey and a dashboard toggle, both outside this repo, and turning it on changes who can sign up - Ian's call, made cheaper by the numbers above. Left at walked rather than advanced, because the trajectory's own done-definition is 'posture chosen, wired, humane' and only the measurement is mine to finish. REMAINS once armed: challenge accessibility (the T48 seam) and the failure path when the challenge itself errors.

trajectories.title: Sensitive-data display hygiene
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25): the class receipts - the B5 no-raw-internals dim + this session's T69 fix (a credentials-location pointer removed from a page ANY signed-in user could open - the exact screen-share hazard) + password show-toggles with aria-pressed exist on the auth modal. Remaining: the sensitive-render sweep formalized (patterns: keys, tokens, full contact chains on roster views), partial-masking decisions for emails/phones, admin-page screen-share audit (wave close). SENSITIVE-RENDER SWEEP MEASURED + ONE REAL FIX 2026-08-26. Secrets are already covered by three registered gates (hardcoded-secrets, prod-path-leak, env-secret-coverage), so the unique half is CONTACT CHAINS on the glass. Swept every render site: the founder console's 13-digit GCash reference and the seller's buyer contacts are legitimate AT THE POINT OF USE (the founder must check that reference in the GCash app; the seller must dial that number) and RLS scopes both to the party who needs them - masking them permanently would break the job. The REAL exposure was volume: the seller inbox rendered EVERY buyer's phone/email at once, so one screenshot (this platform's own share culture, T125) hands over the contact details of everyone who ever asked. FIXED with reveal-on-demand: a 'Show contact' control per inquiry that replaces itself with the copyable value on tap - zero cost when calling one buyer, no leak when not. LIVE-PROVEN as the seller on a staged inquiry: hidden before the tap, visible after, probe cleaned. Remaining: partial-masking decisions for roster emails/phones, admin-page screen-share audit. || ★A NEW PASSWORD WAS BEING TYPED IN THE CLEAR, BECAUSE AN OPTION WAS SILENTLY DROPPED (2026-08-27). index.html:2953 asks for a new password through whPrompt with { inputLabel: 'New password', inputType: 'password', okLabel: 'Update password' }. Measured live: the rendered field was type="text" with no autocomplete - the password visible on screen as it was typed, on a platform whose station tablet is shared by a whole crew and whose own T121 work exists because people look over each other's shoulders. The author asked for masking; nothing masked, and nothing said so. An unsupported option that throws no error is the worst failure mode available: the caller believes the request took effect and the evidence is invisible until somebody renders it. ★IT TOOK TWO FIXES, AND THE FIRST ONE LOOKED LIKE A FAILURE: _mount did not READ inputType (added, allow-listed to text/password/email/number/tel/url so a caller cannot inject an arbitrary type), and after that change the field STILL rendered text - because whPrompt builds an explicit object for _mount and never FORWARDED the option. Two boundaries had to agree before masking could work and only one did, so fixing the visible half changed nothing and read exactly like a fix that had not worked. Verified live: type="password", autocomplete="new-password" (correct for a NEW password rather than a remembered one). Blast radius checked across 10 pages that load utils.js - whConfirm and whPrompt present everywhere, all painted, zero page errors. Remaining: the masked-field show-toggle, and the roster email/phone masking sweep. || GENERALISED THE CLASS ACROSS EVERY SHARED HELPER, AND IT IS REAL EXACTLY ONCE (2026-08-27). Having found one silently-dropped option, the obvious question is how many more there are: 19 wh* helpers take an options object, so I compared what each READS against what callers PASS. First pass reported four - whAutoSaveDraft/auto, whModalA11y/onClose, whConfirm/danger, whGcashPasteWire/receipt - and THREE were my instrument. (1) whModalA11y DOES read onClose: it calls opts.onClose() on Escape, with a fallback that clicks the modal's own close control if none is given. My scan read only the first 2600 chars of each function and onKey sits deeper, so a fixed window turned a correct helper into a defect. (2) whAutoSaveDraft reads auto for the same reason. (3) whGcashPasteWire never receives 'receipt' at all - my key-matching regex found 'receipt:' INSIDE the string 'Read your receipt: ' in an onFill toast. ★WHAT SURVIVES: whConfirm ignores 'danger', passed only by design-system.html, a component showcase no user acts on. So the password inputType was the ONE production instance of this class, and it is fixed. ★THE AUDIT WAS STILL WORTH RUNNING - a class that costs a plaintext password once is worth checking twenty helpers for - but the honest result is that the platform's helper contracts are otherwise kept. Both correction mechanisms were the same discipline: read the WHOLE function, and do not let a pattern match inside a string. || THE CONTACT-EXPOSURE SWEEP, INCLUDING AN ANON WRITE TEST THAT LOOKED ALARMING AND IS NOT (2026-08-27). Eight tables hold contact data. THE ROSTER IS CLEAN: hive.html contains exactly one mention of 'email' and it is a COMMENT about password recovery - member emails are never rendered to the crew. Inquiry contacts are scoped to the two parties by the reads themselves (.eq('seller_name'...) / .eq('buyer_name'...)), so a contact reaches only the person transacting. ★THE ALARMING PART, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: anon holds INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and SELECT GRANTS on the base marketplace_listings table, and its write policies are roles={public}, which includes anon. That reads like an open door. It is not: every write policy predicates on seller_name IN (SELECT auth_worker_names()), which for an unauthenticated caller is an empty set. PROVEN as the anon role rather than argued - INSERT raised 'new row violates row-level security policy'; UPDATE of another seller's listing reported UPDATE 0; zero probe rows remained. Grants are broad and RLS is the gate, which is this platform's stated posture and it holds. ★AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT PROVED NOTHING: my test row priced at PHP1 was refused by guard_listing_meets_minimum, a BUSINESS rule, before RLS was ever consulted - a refusal is not evidence of the refusal you are testing, so the price had to be made valid before the security question could be asked at all. ★ONE THING WORTH STATING RATHER THAN FIXING: v_marketplace_listings_truth exposes seller_contact and anon may SELECT it - which is the contact-only marketplace working as designed (the flow IS contacting the seller), and also means a scraper can harvest every seller's number. That is a product posture, not a bug, and it deserves to be a stated choice. Remaining: the masked-field show-toggle. || THE SHOW-TOGGLE EXISTS AND IS BUILT CORRECTLY - LAST ITEM CLOSED (2026-08-27). All four password fields on the platform are type=password (index's sign-in, sign-up and repeat, plus integrations' CMMS token with autocomplete=off, which is right for a pasted API secret). All three on index carry a reveal control: onclick="togglePwd('si-password', this)" with a 44px square tap target for a gloved hand. ★AND togglePwd UPDATES THE STATE THAT MATTERS, not just the pixels: it flips input.type, recolours the button, and sets BOTH aria-label ('Show password' <-> 'Hide password') and aria-pressed. So a screen-reader user learns the control's current state AND what pressing it will do next - the same property this session's selection-is-exposed gate enforces for tab sets, applied correctly here without a gate telling it to. ★MY SEARCH MISSED IT TWICE: a scan for controls flipping an input type found ZERO, because the pattern wanted a quoted literal and this assigns a TERNARY; only the three aria-labels saying 'Show password' proved the toggles existed and forced a second look. The labels were the evidence my code-shape pattern could not see. So T170's exposure surface is measured end to end: roster clean, inquiry contacts party-scoped, anon writes RLS-denied (proven as the anon role), the prompt now masks, and reveal is a real, accessible affordance. Remaining: nothing owed beyond the wave-close re-earn; the public seller_contact stays a stated product posture rather than a defect. || LOCKED 2026-08-28. Gate a-secret-stays-masked holds both halves: every password field ships type=password and whPrompt FORWARDS inputType (the measured gap - _mount honoured it while whPrompt built its own options object and dropped it, so a caller asking for a masked prompt got a plain text box and a secret was typed in the clear, with nothing looking wrong to anyone), and the reveal toggle flips BOTH aria-label and aria-pressed, so the person who cannot check by looking is told what the control does AND whether their password is on screen right now. ★THE GATE ANCHORS ON THE ACCESSIBLE NAME, NOT THE CODE SHAPE, for the reason this trajectory already recorded: a search for controls flipping an input type found ZERO twice, because it expected a quoted literal and togglePwd assigns a ternary - the three aria-labels were the only evidence the toggles existed. Selftest 8/8. Remaining: the wave-close re-earn; the public seller_contact stays a stated product posture. || ★LOCKED 2026-08-31: the wave-close re-earn landed and every gate this row names read PASS on a FULL board (a-secret-stays-masked). That was the only item its basis still owed. pct 97 -> 100.

trajectories.title: Compliance evidence on demand (the ISO-minded client)
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the sales-claim alignment sweep run and locked). Swept all 117 public pages for certification and compliance language. THE POSTURE IS HONEST AND NOW MEASURED rather than asserted: no WorkHive self-certification exists anywhere - no SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR-compliant, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, bank-grade or military-grade. All 30 raw hits were a standard the CUSTOMER is audited against (ISO 9001/14001/45001, DOLE OSHS), a PERSON's credential (TESDA NC II/III, CMRP, PSME/IIEE), or the skill matrix's own 'certified level' vocabulary. ★ONE REAL OVERCLAIM, AND IT WAS A CATEGORY ERROR RATHER THAN A BOAST: dole-iso-audit-trail-from-logbook claimed logbook entries 'satisfy Clause 10.2', the PM dashboard 'satisfies Clause 7.1.5', safety observations 'satisfy Clause 9.1.1'. A clause is satisfied by an ORGANISATION's management system, evidenced by records - software holds the evidence, it cannot confer conformity. It reads as reassurance, so a plant could enter a surveillance audit believing a feature had covered them. Rewritten to 'gives you the records Clause 10.2 asks you to retain' / 'evidences Clause 9.1.1' plus a callout stating the distinction outright; live-verified styled and visible, 0 pageerrors, and the false wording is gone from the rendered page. Locked as 'compliance-claim-honesty' with two assertions and a deliberate NON-catch: 'the digital record satisfies three properties' and 'export patterns that satisfy auditors' both survive on that same page, because a record CAN satisfy a property and an export CAN satisfy a sampling need - only a NUMBERED clause as the object is the error. The self-certification half is guard-the-absence at zero, since that is the most tempting sentence to add to a sales page and the most expensive to be wrong about. Teeth proven on both halves. REMAINING: the evidence STORY as an assembled artifact (a compliance page or PDF) is scoped content and stays Ian's call; compliance-relevant export verification rides with T49. || ★THE ENTERPRISE CLAIM IS REAL; ITS REFUSAL WAS THE ROUGH PART - found, fixed (2026-08-28). The probe asks whether the sales-facing enterprise claims are true, with the SSO button named as the specimen. VERDICT: it is genuinely WIRED, not decoration - signInWithSSO prompts for a company domain via whPrompt, calls db.auth.signInWithSSO({domain}), disables the button with a 'Redirecting to your identity provider' state, and follows data.url. So 'Enterprise SSO (Okta / Azure AD)' is backed by real code and is not a declared-but-never-wired claim. ★THE DEFECT WAS IN THE PATH AN EVALUATOR ACTUALLY HITS. The function had two failure branches of very different quality: the catch branch already said, bilingually via _t(), 'SSO not available for this domain. Contact your IT administrator.' - while the `error` branch three lines above toasted 'SSO error: ' + error.message, EN-only, with the provider's raw string pasted in front of the guidance. That asymmetry is the whole finding, because Supabase RETURNS an error object for a domain with no registered IdP rather than THROWING - so the rougher message was the common one, and the polished one was the rare one. An IT admin evaluating the platform, typing their domain before their team has registered anything, is exactly the person who got the raw internals. ★FIX: the error branch now carries the same bilingual sentence and a more actionable one ('Ask your IT team to register WorkHive as an SSO application in your identity provider'), with the raw error routed to console.error where it helps whoever is debugging. Verified: function brace-balanced, both branches use _t(), no error.message reaches a user, raw error reaches the console. This closes one T45 FIL-parity instance and one B5 no-raw-internals instance in the same edit. ★HONEST LIMIT: whether SSO SUCCEEDS in production depends on SAML being enabled on the Supabase project and an IdP registered - prod configuration I cannot read locally. What is verified here is that the control is real and that its refusal is now humane in both languages, not that any customer's login completes. ★CHECKER NOTE: my own verification first reported 'raw error.message still shown' and 'console.error missing' - both false. The first matched the word inside the COMMENT I had just written explaining the old behaviour; the second searched a substring missing a colon. A checker that reads comments as code, or matches an inexact literal, fails in both directions. pct 60 -> 78. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate compliance-claim-honesty re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: The child/underage & terms-eligibility posture
trajectories.basis: audit ran, two findings: (1) the terms contain NO age/eligibility clause at all - the posture is UNDEFINED, not merely unstated at signup (the spec's 'posture deliberate' ask -> Ian decision); (2) HEAVIER: terms :185 PROMISES 'You may export your data at any time and delete your account' while T77/T164 established neither export-my-data nor account-deletion exists - the terms are a claim surface making promises the product does not keep (claim-honesty at legal weight; PDPA-relevant). Feeds T163/T164.  || FINDING (2) FIXED 2026-08-26, and it was the heavier one: the terms promised, in TWO places, a self-serve export and account deletion that do not exist. A marketing page overclaiming is bad; a TERMS page overclaiming is a promise at legal weight, made to a PH user exercising a PDPA right, and it is the document they would point to. THE FIX DID NOT DELETE THE RIGHT - the right is real, and the privacy policy already documents how it is honoured (email admin@workhiveph.com, subject 'Data Rights Request'). The terms now say exactly that and state plainly that it is handled by hand rather than through a button: same right, true sentence, no weaker. LOCKED BY gate legal-claim-honesty, whose design point is that each banned phrasing is PAIRED WITH THE CONTROL that would make it true: the day somebody ships account deletion, the claim becomes allowed by the same gate that forbids it today. It is deliberately NOT a prose lint - a gate that graded legal writing would produce false reds forever and teach everyone to ignore it. Resurrection RED on all three pre-fix claims. FINDING (1), the absent age/eligibility clause, remains an Ian decision - an undefined posture is a choice to make, not a bug to fix. || ★YOU COULD AGREE TO TERMS THE FORM NEVER SHOWED YOU - found, fixed (2026-08-28). So the posture is ABSENT, not INCONSISTENT: there is no terms<->signup mismatch to fix, and the eligibility decision (a PH industrial B2B platform where contracts with minors are voidable and DOLE restricts under-18 industrial work) is Ian's to make, not mine to legislate into a legal document. This is T172's own specced fix target ('the terms-consistency line at signup') and it also closes a T165 consent-moment gap. ★FIX: an agreement line inside the <form> itself, verified to sit between id="panel-signup" and </form> rather than merely somewhere on the page. Both targets resolve as directories; both links carry rel=noopener noreferrer for the project's gate; both open in a NEW TAB deliberately -- the form holds a typed password and display name, and navigating in-place to read what you are agreeing to would discard all of it. ★DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: no 'I am 18' checkbox. Signup must not assert a rule the terms do not make; adding one would manufacture the very inconsistency this trajectory checks for. ★INSTRUMENT NOTE: my first eligibility grep matched 'age' inside 'page', 'image' and 'language' and returned pure noise; the clean result came only after word-boundary patterns over tag-stripped text. A search for a short word needs boundaries before its silence means anything. pct 60 -> 82. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate legal-claim-honesty re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). trajectories.title: First-time-on-each-page: the 24-page onboarding sweep
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the remaining 19-page cold sweep DONE). Walked 19 pages with a genuinely cold account - created via signUp, identity seeded the way signup seeds it, NO hive - then deleted, with residue re-counted at 0 across auth.users, worker_profiles, voice_journal_entries and hive_members (the CASCADE proven in T164's erasure-path-intact doing exactly what it promises). RESULT: every page speaks to a first-time reader. Two bounce, and they bounce to hive.html - the right destination for someone with no hive, not a dead end. The best cold states are the SHORTEST: hive.html 'Join or create a team... Create a Hive | Join with Code' (134 chars), asset-hub 'Asset Hub needs a hive... Go to Hive', shift-brain likewise, integrations 'Supervisor access only... ask your hive supervisor'. ONE REAL GAP, FOUND AND FIXED: analytics-report offered a fully-armed generator - period chips, audience toggle, 'Generate Report' - to a reader with no hive and therefore no data, stating no precondition. It now carries its siblings' gate in their words ('Reports need a hive... Go to Hive'), hiding BOTH <main> and #ar-print-wrapper - the latter a deliberate sibling of <main> for the print rule, whose hint otherwise told a hive-less reader to 'Click Generate Report' directly beneath a gate saying Go to Hive. Both states verified live: cold shows only the gate; signed-in with a hive is unchanged (gate hidden, generator present, 0 pageerrors). ★THREE INSTRUMENT ERRORS ON THE WAY, NONE BANKED - the through-line of this trajectory. (1) The probe cleared wh_last_worker along with the hive, and 14 of 19 pages bounced to the MARKETING page - a dramatic finding that was pure artifact: signup sets that key (index.html:3196), :3650 re-seeds it from worker_profiles.display_name, and the shared guard (utils.js:3546) redirects on a missing WORKER NAME, not a missing hive. COLD means no hive, not no identity. (2) The pass threshold 'chars < 200' flagged four of the BEST cold states on the platform - they are short BECAUSE they are focused; brevity is not emptiness. (3) It read querySelector('main'), and innerText on a display:none element still returns raw text, so on the very page it had just gated it captured the HIDDEN generator and missed the VISIBLE gate sitting outside <main>; it now reads body innerText, which respects visibility. Locked as 'cold-page-teaches', asserting only the objective (something rendered, nothing threw, the account cleaned) and PRINTING each page's cold text, because an oracle that grades prose is an oracle that will be wrong about prose. This joins the 2026-08-25 pass's 5 pages: 24 of 24 walked cold. REMAINING: the celebrate-first-action probes (wave close, T182 seam). || ★ONE EXCELLENT ONBOARDING PATH, ON ONE PAGE - the 24-page premise is simply not the design (2026-08-28). There IS a real onboarding system and it is better than most: onboarding.js runs two ROLE-SPECIFIC paths - 5 steps for a worker (signed in, joined a hive, logged a first entry, uploaded a photo, completed a PM) and 7 for a supervisor (adding approve a member, register an asset, set a PM template, review the audit log, approve a daily brief) - and every step's completion is detected by a DB QUERY rather than a self-report checkbox, so progress reflects the moment the worker actually does the thing. A stepper that cannot lie about what you have done is the right build, and it is worth recording as a positive rather than only hunting gaps. ★BUT IT IS SCOPED TO hive.html, by its own header: the paths are what a worker and supervisor 'see on hive.html the first time they land'. There is no platform pattern of a page introducing ITSELF on first visit. The only page-level first-run markers anywhere are audit-log's wh_onb_audit_visited - which is not a page intro at all but step 6 of the SUPERVISOR path, the same system reaching outward - and integrations' dismissible guide. So this trajectory's framing (24 pages, 24 self-introductions) describes something the platform never attempted; what exists is one platform-level journey plus the page-guide chips T174 measures. ★THE HONEST GAP: a worker landing on analytics or shift-brain for the first time meets a working page with no orientation, and the hive.html stepper - which is about the PLATFORM journey, not this screen - cannot help them there. Whether to build per-page first-run introductions is a product investment with a real cost (24 surfaces to write and maintain), not a defect to patch, and the cheaper move already exists in the guide chips. Recorded so the decision is made on what is actually there. ★No canonical empty-state helper exists to measure adoption against - I looked for one first, because measuring by hunting phrasings is how this session's public-feed check wrongly reported a missing empty state that said 'No public posts'. pct 60 -> 72. || ★CORRECTION, SAME DAY, AND THE MEASUREMENT REFUTES WHAT I WROTE ABOVE (2026-08-28). I recorded that per-page first-run introduction 'is NOT a platform pattern' and that a worker landing cold on analytics or shift-brain 'meets a working page with no orientation'. That was reasoning from absence - I found one stepper on hive.html, found no OTHER first-run machinery, and concluded none existed. There is a GATE for exactly this claim, validate_cold_page_teaches, and it was not reporting because it REFUSED to measure: a probe account from a previous session (wh-t175-probe@auth.workhiveph.com, created 2026-08-27) was still present and the prover aborts on dirty state rather than produce a reading it cannot trust. I removed the account - it held nothing but 2 analytics_events rows and no hive membership, consistent with a cold-account probe - and re-ran it. RESULT: pages walked cold 19, near-empty regions 0, pages throwing 0, probe account removed true. PASS: 'every page walked with a hive-less account says what it is for, nothing threw'. Nineteen pages DO introduce themselves; I simply could not see the mechanism by grepping for the vocabulary I expected. ★THE LESSON IS THE ONE THIS SESSION KEPT RE-LEARNING FROM THE OTHER SIDE: a silent instrument is not a negative finding. Seven times today a suspicious ZERO turned out to be my measurement rather than the code; here a gate that could have answered me was sitting one cleanup away, and I wrote a conclusion instead of unblocking it. Before concluding a capability is ABSENT, check whether an instrument for it exists and why it is quiet. ★WHAT STANDS from the original entry: onboarding.js IS hive-scoped and IS operational rather than career-shaped, and the graduate ladder observation in T54 is unaffected. What does not stand is the claim that cold pages teach nothing. pct 72 -> 88. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Error-message comprehension census
trajectories.basis: census (164 error literals / 206 taxonomy calls / 32 pages) + THE RAW-APPEND CLASS EXTINGUISHED on all three leader pages this session: integrations 0->9 taxonomy calls, asset-hub 5->23 (21 sites: read/write/AI matched per call class), logbook +8 (search/delete/save/update/AI-fill) on top of T38's session-aware insert refusal - every converted fallback names the action + work state + next step; all three pages load clean. Remaining: the long-tail pages + the lint holding NEW strings to the bar (wave close). THE LINT BUILT + REGISTERED 2026-08-26 (gate error-taxonomy-ratchet): counts user-facing failure strings sunk into showToast/setStatus/textContent/innerHTML from a catch or error branch with NO taxonomy helper on the line - the RAW-APPEND class - forward-only from a measured 78, auto-lowering as the long tail converts. It deliberately does not grade prose: a lint that guesses at sentences produces false reds, while a count of raw appends is objective and is exactly the regression signal. TEETH-PROVEN: a planted showToast('Something went wrong...') in a catch turned it RED; removing it returned green. Remaining: converting the long-tail pages (the ratchet now makes each conversion permanent). LONG TAIL STARTED same pass, ratchet 78 -> 65: inventory's 6 and pm-scheduler's 7 raw strings converted to whWriteError, each naming what happened to the WORK rather than echoing a driver message - 'The stock was NOT deducted. Nothing changed', 'The asset saved but its PM TASKS did not, so it has an empty schedule', 'Nothing was deleted - it is all still here'. Both pages re-proven live (rendered, 0 pageerrors). The ratchet auto-lowered twice, so these 13 can never silently regress. Tail continued: report-sender (4) + shift-brain (3) converted, ratchet 65 -> 59; both pages re-proven live. Notable conversions name the OUTWARD consequence, which is what these surfaces owe: 'The report was NOT re-sent. Nothing went out', 'The plan was NOT published, so the crew still cannot see it', 'The contact was NOT removed - it is still saved and will still receive reports.' Tail continued 2026-08-26: project-manager (10) + logbook (5) converted, ratchet 78 -> 45 overall. The project surfaces now name the state of the WORK rather than echoing a driver string - 'The project was created but its SCOPE ITEMS were not, so it starts empty', 'Stock was NOT deducted for <part>. The shelf count is unchanged - deduct it in Inventory', 'Its PM tasks did NOT record, so those PMs still count as due'. whWriteError(null, fallback) verified safe in-page before relying on it. Both pages re-proven live, validate_logbook 29/29. Community's 8 converted too - ratchet 78 -> 37, under half the census this session. Community's set is the clearest example of the bar: every refusal now says what did NOT happen ('The post was NOT deleted - it is still in the feed', 'Your reply was NOT posted. It is still in the box'), which is the fact a person needs before deciding whether to retry. Page re-proven live. Remaining tail: voice-journal 4, integrations 3, founder-console 2, index 2, platform-actions 2 and a long thin tail - each conversion now permanent under the ratchet. AUDIT OF THE REMAINDER 2026-08-26 - and a deliberate STOP on the count: reading the last 37 one by one showed many are already GOOD sentences that simply do not route through a helper ('Wrong username or password.', 'A logbook entry can only be corrected by its author', 'Someone else changed this feedback. Your note was not saved'). Rewriting those to lower the number would make copy worse to move a metric, so only the two founder-console strings that ECHOED A DRIVER MESSAGE were converted (37 -> 35), and the gate's own docstring now states 'ZERO IS NOT THE GOAL' with the rule: convert what echoes a driver or says nothing; leave sentences that already do the job. Also checked and CLEARED a suspected defect: index's 'Sign-in failed. Check your connection' is only the generic catch - wrong password (401) and rate-limit (423) have their own honest branches above it. || ★THE CENSUS THIS TRAJECTORY ASKS FOR, MEASURED (2026-08-28). Parsed every showToast(..., 'error') call across the root pages and split it into top-level arguments: 63 route their message through a taxonomy helper (whReadError / whWriteError / whAiError / whListError / whAuthRequiredToast), 132 are hand-rolled — 32.3% adoption, and a real baseline where the trajectory previously had none. The debt is CONCENTRATED, not spread: project-manager (37), marketplace-seller (29), marketplace (29) and community (21) hold 116 of the 132, so four pages are most of the work. ★THE FIRST MEASUREMENT SAID 0.0% AND WAS DISCARDED AS IMPOSSIBLE. The regex captured the message argument as [^,]{1,160}, which cannot match a helper CALL — whReadError(e, 'Could not load.') contains a comma, so every correct usage was invisible and every hand-rolled one matched. A tool that reports 0% adoption of a helper known to be adopted on 14 pages is reporting on itself; re-measured with paren-depth argument splitting. ★AND THE NUMBER IS NOT A DEFECT COUNT: a hand-rolled message can be perfectly good copy. What the helpers buy is the TAXONOMY — a 401 saying the session expired rather than blaming the connection, a 429 saying when it clears — so the 132 are candidates for review, not 132 bugs. Grading them against the cause/state-of-work/next-step bar is the next slice, and it now has a denominator. || ★TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE CENSUS ABOVE, AND THE SIGNAL IT WAS ACTUALLY POINTING AT. First, the 32.3% understates adoption: whFnError is a taxonomy helper too and was missing from the pattern, so some of the 132 'hand-rolled' were routed all along. Second, and more useful — sampling project-manager showed that most of its 37 pass a VARIABLE (`m`) composed elsewhere, or are plain guidance like 'Open a project first.', which owes the taxonomy nothing. A raw count of hand-rolled calls was the wrong instrument; it measured a coding idiom rather than a reader's experience. ★THE GRADEABLE CLASS UNDERNEATH IT: 33 toasts surface a RAW error.message to a user — project-manager 13, marketplace 11, founder-console 3, marketplace-seller 2, and one each on asset-hub, community, index and pm-scheduler. A Postgres or JS error string shown to a maintenance worker is both unreadable and a quiet leak of table and constraint names (the B5 no-raw-internals bar). ★AND THEY ARE NOT 33 EQUAL DEFECTS, which is why this is recorded graded rather than filed as a number: founder-console:2164 INSPECTS the message (/duplicate|unique/i.test(...)) and maps it to friendly copy, which is exactly right; index.html's SSO toast appends real guidance about what IT must configure; asset-hub:1670 and community:2537 put the raw string FIRST with a friendly fallback second, so the human copy shows only when the error is empty — backwards, and the honest fix is whWriteError(e, '<friendly>'), which maps error CLASSES rather than pasting strings; and founder-console is Ian's own cockpit, where the raw text is arguably what the owner wants. The next slice is the raw-first pair, then the bare ones on buyer- and worker-facing pages, leaving the owner console and the two that genuinely add guidance alone. || ★FIRST SLICE TAKEN: the two raw-FIRST sites are converted. community.html's best-answer failure and asset-hub's QR-tag failure both read `error.message || '<friendly>'`, so the human sentence appeared only when the error was EMPTY — which is to say almost never, and the reader got Postgres text instead of being told what happened to their action. Both now call whWriteError(err, '<friendly>'), which maps the error CLASS (session expired / offline / refused) rather than pasting a string. The asset-hub one carried a second defect the census did not look for: it passed no type at all, so a FAILURE rendered as a neutral toast; it is now 'error'. Both pages verified to load utils.js before the call, since a helper that is not there throws inside the very catch meant to report the problem. || ★MARKETPLACE'S SIX: the file had ALREADY SOLVED THIS AND STOPPED HALFWAY. marketplace.html defines _svcErrorText(error, sent) — a local taxonomy telling a dead session from a rate limit from a lost connection, with a `sent` flag so a READ path does not claim 'nothing was sent' — and a _svcWriteError alias. Its own comment states the diagnosis outright: 'A dead session must not be reported to a person as "JWT expired". showToast(error.message) passed PostgREST's wording straight through, so the one failure a person can actually act on arrived in the vocabulary of the token layer.' That helper was applied to TWO write paths and the file kept passing raw messages everywhere else — the lesson written in a file's own comments not reaching the rest of that same file. Five sites converted: the quote-list READ (sent=false), select_quote, the settle update, redeem_service_voucher, and the client cancel; plus the receipt-OCR toast, which showed err.message first and now shows 'Could not read that receipt. Type the details instead.' — the console.error beside it is where the endpoint's real wording belongs. ★THREE LEFT DELIBERATELY RAW, because their comments make the case and it is a good one: the agreed/variance guard, the duplicate-payment check, and the credit cap, whose server message NAMES THE REAL FIGURES ('Credits may cover at most 10% of a purchase (₱2,500 here)') and is better than any generic sentence would be. A fourth pattern-MATCHES the message into friendly copy, which is the correct use of a raw string. ★AND ONE SCAN HIT WAS MY OWN INSTRUMENT: it flagged showToast(error.message) inside a /* */ COMMENT — the very comment diagnosing the bug — because the scanner blanked HTML comments but not JS ones. || ★PROJECT-MANAGER'S THIRTEEN, AND THE PLATFORM COUNT: 33 -> 11. This page was already the taxonomy's biggest adopter (whWriteError 14x, whReadError 6x, whFnError 2x) and still had 13 raw surfacings — adoption arriving one call site at a time rather than one CLASS at a time. All thirteen are now converted, each with copy naming the action rather than a generic sentence: the task status, the link, the acknowledgement, the role (save and remove), the three change-order verdicts (approved / rejected / cancelled), the project status, the report send, and the two AI catches through whAiError. ★ONE CHECK SAVED ME FROM A WORSE BUG THAN THE ONE I WAS FIXING: my grep for `^function whAiError` found nothing, and I nearly shipped calls to a function I had not confirmed exists. It does — as `window.whAiError = function (err, fallback)` inside an IIFE, which a function-declaration pattern cannot see — and utils.js:70 documents this exact usage: "page's AI catch calls showToast(whAiError(err, 'AI failed'))". A helper that does not resolve throws inside the very catch meant to report the failure, turning a bad message into a dead handler. ★WHAT REMAINS IS 11, AND THEY ARE MOSTLY RIGHT: marketplace's three documented pass-throughs where the server's message names real figures, two that pattern-MATCH the message into friendly copy, and founder-console's three — Ian's own cockpit, where the raw text is plausibly what the owner wants. The class went from 33 undifferentiated surfacings to 11 understood ones. || ★CLASS CLOSED AT 33 -> 9, AND THE LAST TWO WERE A CLONE AND A WRITE PATH. marketplace-seller carried the SAME receipt-OCR toast as marketplace.html, raw-first, in a duplicated function (svcReadTopupReceipt / svcReadPayReceipt) - so fixing one of a pair was half a fix, and both are now done. pm-scheduler's auto_hail update reported PostgREST verbatim and now names the action ('The recurring-contract setting was not saved.'). ★THE NINE THAT REMAIN ARE UNDERSTOOD, NOT UNTOUCHED: marketplace's three documented pass-throughs whose server text names real figures; two that pattern-MATCH the message into friendly copy, which is the correct use of a raw string; index's SSO toast, which appends real guidance about what IT must configure; marketplace-seller's push-subscribe failure, which has a friendly prefix, a safe fallback and a comment explaining the surface-and-log intent; and founder-console's two bare ones, on Ian's own cockpit where the raw text is plausibly what the owner wants. A count that went from 33 undifferentiated to 9 deliberate is the actual deliverable here - the number matters less than each remaining one having a reason. || ★2026-08-31 DEMOTED from locked/100: the first FULL board tripped error-taxonomy-ratchet (raw failure strings 19->20, forward-only) - a new un-routed failure string was added after this row was locked (voice-journal/platform-actions/marketplace/report-sender candidates). Deterministic, not a flake. FIX QUEUED: route the new raw string through whReadError/whWriteError/whAiError to return the count to <=19, then re-lock. || 2026-08-31 FIX LANDED: routed voice-journal onSendTyped else-branch (a genuine note-not-saved write failure) from raw "Something went wrong..." through whWriteError - error-taxonomy-ratchet 20->19 GREEN standalone; improves the copy (names cause+work-state+next-step). Re-lock to 100 when the next FULL board confirms the gate green. || ★LOCKED 2026-08-31 (post_board_close): every named gate read PASS on the fresh FULL board 2026-08-31T16:45. pct 90 -> 100.

trajectories.note: ★'TRY AGAIN' FOR SOMETHING THAT CAN NEVER SUCCEED (2026-08-26). Generalised from T185's namesake defect by censusing every unique constraint on a user-write table (5: hive_members, hives.invite_code, worker_profiles auth_uid + username, asset_nodes tag). whWriteError passes DELIBERATE refusals through in their own words - the source even explains why, citing a seller who would 'retry forever' - but 23505 was not on that list, so a taken name/tag/username fell to the caller's 'Nothing changed; try again.' Measured by calling the real function, not by reading it. Fixed centrally: the sentence now says the value is already used and to change it, stays generic so no constraint name reaches a reader, and leaves deliberate refusals and unrelated errors untouched. Gate collision-is-not-try-again EXERCISES whWriteError; teeth proven twice, after the first attempt produced a FALSE red (Node 24's getter-only `navigator` broke the shim). ★THE RAW-ECHO CLASS IS EXTINCT, 34 -> 21 (2026-08-27). The long tail was not one job but two, and only one of them was mechanical. THE MECHANICAL HALF - a driver's own sentence pasted into a toast - is now gone from every page: project-manager's four ('Code gen failed: ', 'Create failed: ', 'Save failed: ' twice) and logbook's AI-analyze and two voice handlers. Each replacement names what happened to the WORK, which the echo never did: the change-order one says nothing was SUBMITTED (a CO is an approval request, so 'saved' was the wrong word), and the scope-item one says the entries are still in the form, because that modal stays open. ★THE SHARPEST FIND WAS NOT A TOAST: project-manager rendered `<option>Error: ${e(error.message)}</option>` into the link picker, so a failed read became a SELECTABLE CHOICE - a person could highlight 'Error: new row violates row-level security policy' as if it were a record to link. Now a disabled, non-selectable option carrying whReadError. ★AND THE STOCK ONE MATTERS MOST: logbook's inventory_deduct failure echoed the RPC while the ENTRY had already landed - the shelf and the system now disagree and only a person can reconcile them. It says that, in the same 'Entry saved. ...did NOT...' shape the PM-mirror line four lines above already used. ★NEW CENTRAL HELPER whVoiceError (utils.js), because the Web Speech API reports bare codes and three sites pasted them straight through ('Voice error: network', 'Mic error: aborted'). Closed specified vocabulary, mapped once: permission, no-microphone, network, language, aborted, plus a fallback - and every branch says the thing none of the three sites said, that dictation failing never discards what is already typed. Runtime-verified across all six codes plus an event object; the ratchet was taught it with the same admission test the other helpers passed. ★A PREMISE CHECK THAT PREVENTED A WRONG FIX: index.html:3228 says 'Sign-in failed. Check your connection' and I was about to call it the misattribution class - until reading ten lines up showed wrong credentials are answered ABOVE it at !_resp.ok ('Wrong username or password'), so that catch really does only fire on a transport throw. Left alone. The same check went the other way on logbook's three equipment reads, where 'Check your connection' WAS the only remedy offered for a read that also fails on an expired session or an RLS refusal - those now route through whReadError, so a dead session stops sending people to look at their wifi. ★WHAT 'DONE' MEANS HERE, AND WHY IT IS NOT ZERO: the 21 that remain are hand-written sentences that already name cause, work state and next step, and several are deliberately BETTER than any generic helper output - voice-journal's 'Your note IS saved - it is in the list below', marketplace-seller's 'unknown rather than zero', platform-actions' someone-else-changed-this. Driving a forward-only counter to 0 would eventually pressure someone into replacing those with 'Save failed. Try again.', which is the gate destroying the thing it exists to protect. The target was the RAW-ECHO class, and that is met; what remains is a per-string quality READ, not a mechanical conversion. ★A DIAGNOSIS WRITTEN AND THE STRING LEFT ALONE (2026-08-27). Sweeping for WRITE paths that blame the connection found three on dayplanner - and all three already routed through whWriteError, so the sweep nearly passed them. The defect was in the FALLBACK text, and the comment three lines above it had already diagnosed the problem in its own words: 'The network branch above already claimed anything connection-shaped, so "check your connection" was actively misleading here: what reaches this line is a REFUSAL.' The analysis was correct, was committed, and the string was never changed. ★A refusal answered with 'check your connection' sends someone to their wifi for a problem their wifi cannot fix. The fallbacks now state the outcome instead: 'Could not save that change. Nothing on your schedule changed.' and, for delete, the one certain consequence - 'It is still on your schedule.' ★THE TRANSFERABLE PART: a comment that names a defect is not a fix, and it reads like one to every later grep. Search for the STRING, not for whether a helper is present - all three sites looked compliant from the helper's point of view. ★THE 'SEARCH FOR THE STRING' LESSON APPLIED TO ITSELF, AND IT FOUND ITS OWN MISS (2026-08-27). T176's own transferable rule - search for the STRING, not for whether a helper is present - was run platform-wide, and the first thing it caught was T176's own incomplete fix: dayplanner's save has TWO failure paths and only the `error` branch was changed. The CATCH at :820 still said 'Save failed: check your connection' while both delete paths and the save's error branch had been fixed. ★AND THE BLAME THERE IS DOUBLY WRONG: that line is reached only AFTER the offline queue has already tried and failed to absorb the write, so if the problem really were the network the queue would have taken it. Now states the outcome, matching its sibling three lines above. ★THEN THE SWEEP FOUND A DIFFERENT AND WORSE CLASS. whReadError(err, what) does not PRINT `what`, it SPLICES it: 'Your session expired, so ' + thing + ' could not be loaded.' Four callsites passed a whole SENTENCE, so what shipped was 'Your session expired, so Could not load your equipment list. Check your connection. could not be loaded. Sign in again to see it.' MEASURED in the browser rather than reasoned. Every site had been CONVERTED to the taxonomy - the right move - with the old sentence forwarded into the slot; logbook even carries a comment above it explaining that the upstream sentence belongs in console.error and never in the notice. The author had the principle and still handed the helper a sentence. ★INVISIBLE TO EVERY OTHER CHECK: the helper is present so adoption sweeps pass it, no raw error text so the raw-echo ratchet passes it, nothing throws - and the garbled sentence only appears when a session dies mid-read, which is exactly when nobody is watching. Gate noun-slot-takes-a-noun locks it (52 callsites, 0 offenders), scoped to whReadError because whWriteError and whAiError take a fallback MESSAGE by design. ★FOUR FALSE LEADS DISCARDED ALONG THE WAY: four other connection-blaming strings sit in the `typeof whReadError === 'function' ? ... : '...'` ELSE branch, which fires only when utils.js did not load - where blaming the connection is exactly right, and 'fixing' them would have made them worse. ★A WRITE THAT CAME BACK EMPTY IS UNCONFIRMED, NOT FAILED - 4 SITES FIXED (2026-08-27). The error-string CENSUS T176 asked for was finally built (79 page-authored strings across 17 pages; what existed before was tools/error_taxonomy_baseline.json holding {"count": 20}, the forward-only counter T176's own note warns is the wrong instrument). Grading them surfaced a class nobody had named: 18 sites do `.insert(...).select(...)` and then branch on `if (!data || !data.length)` - and 8 told the user the write FAILED. It did not necessarily fail. supabase-js resolves with { data: [], error: null } when the INSERT SUCCEEDED and the RETURNING read was refused, because RLS gates SELECT separately from INSERT. ★THE ADVICE WAS THE DANGEROUS HALF: 'Request didn't save - please try again' on a service hail re-broadcasts a SECOND job to every nearby provider for work the client wants done once, and the registration equivalent creates a second provider profile. Both messages now say what is actually known ('may have been sent - we could not confirm it') and point at the LIST rather than the button. ★AND EACH ONE WAS TWO SITES, NOT ONE: the hail has a catalog path and a custom-scope path, registration has a hive path and a freelancer path, and my sweep's dedup-by-message had hidden the twins - the Edit tool refusing an ambiguous match is what revealed them. 4 fixed. ★THE PLATFORM ALREADY KNEW THE RIGHT SHAPE in four other places ('Couldn't update - the job may have moved on', 'No change saved: that top-up was already decided'), which is what makes the 8 a drift rather than a gap. ★NOT GATED YET, DELIBERATELY: 6 remain and they are the idempotent actions (availability, cancel, alert subscription, rating) where retrying costs nothing, so each needs its own verdict. A ratchet whose baseline holds untriaged entries launders unknowns as accepted - the lesson na-premise-holds was built on. They are the next slice. ★AND THEN THE TRIAGE WAS DONE, SO IT IS GATED AFTER ALL (2026-08-27, same session - correcting the line above that said 'not gated yet'). Each of the 6 survivors was checked against the SCHEMA rather than by eye: founder-console's voucher INSERT is protected by service_vouchers_code_key UNIQUE(code); the rating INSERT by marketplace_reviews_one_per_request_direction UNIQUE(request_id, direction); availability, cancel and the marketplace update are idempotent UPDATEs; the push subscription is an UPSERT with onConflict:endpoint. In every one a retry is either refused by the database or writes the same row, so 'try again' is honest advice even though 'didn't save' is imprecise - a wording item, not a hazard. THAT is what makes a baseline legitimate: 6 entries each carrying the constraint or the idempotency that justifies it. Gate unconfirmed-write-is-not-a-failure now runs over 170 write sites with 0 new offenders. ★AND THE GATE'S OWN FIXED WINDOW HID A FIFTH SITE (2026-08-27). The first version anchored FORWARD from each write with a 900-character horizon, and marketplace-seller's top-up has a seven-line comment between its .insert() and the branch - so the branch fell outside the window and 'Couldn't file the top-up. Try again.' went unreported on a MONEY action. It was found by READING the census rather than by the gate, which is the tell. Re-anchored to start at the BRANCH and look back for the write it belongs to, which has no horizon; the widened gate immediately flagged the site it had missed. That is the fixed-char-window class turning up inside the very instrument built to catch a different one - the third time today a window produced a false reading, and the first time it produced a false SILENCE, which is worse because nothing announces it. ★THE FIFTH FIX: re-filing a top-up is not destructive (service_credit_topups_ref_unique is UNIQUE on gcash_ref, so the same reference is refused), but the reader deserves to know the filing may have landed rather than be told their money went nowhere - which is exactly what the comment three lines above already argued about the sibling error branch. ★LOCKED (2026-08-27). T176's done-definition was 'the census green; new errors born compliant', and both halves now hold. THE CENSUS EXISTS: 79 strings the pages themselves author, across 17 pages, extracted and READ - not counted. What stood in for it was tools/error_taxonomy_baseline.json holding {"count": 20}, the forward-only counter this trajectory's own note warned was the wrong instrument, because driving a count to zero eventually pressures someone into replacing a precise refusal with 'Save failed. Try again.' ★EVERY FLAGGED STRING CARRIES A VERDICT rather than a fix-or-ignore: the six unconfirmed-write survivors are baselined against the SCHEMA (a unique index or an idempotent update makes the retry free); 'Cannot collect a rejection reason right now' names what cannot happen and gives the one safe action; and several my classifier flagged are simply good - 'Couldn't send the quote - the request may have closed', 'Nothing was saved, so reload and try again', 'You are offline and this report could not be saved. Keep this window open until you reconnect.' ★THE READ ALSO SHOWED WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, which a defect list never does: this platform routinely tells a reader the STATE OF THEIR WORK ('nothing was sent', 'this action was not recorded', 'Your note was not saved') and refuses to let a failed read read as a zero - 'Your levels are unknown right now, not zero', 'Overdue and blocked work is unknown right now', 'This is a connection problem, not an empty day'. ★NEW ERRORS ARE BORN COMPLIANT via 4 gates: error-taxonomy-ratchet (raw echo), collision-is-not-try-again, noun-slot-takes-a-noun (a sentence spliced into a noun slot), unconfirmed-write-is-not-a-failure (an empty RETURNING claimed as a failure). All four registered and green; 10 strings fixed across 6 pages.

trajectories.title: Jargon & vocabulary census (the user-facing dictionary)
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the glossary REGISTRY built - this trajectory's named DELTA). Censused the domain vocabulary the product puts on the glass and asked, per term, whether the platform explains it anywhere a reader can reach: expanded in place on a page, or taught in the learn cluster. Both count. THE HABIT IS SOUND: 11 of 13 terms were already handled - MTBF, MTTR, OEE, RCM, FMEA, RPN, CPM, LOTO, SOP and P-F each have a learn guide that spells them out. ★THE ONE THAT WAS NOT: project-manager showed supervisors 'EVM: SPI 0.87, CPI 1.02, status ... (BAC ₱..., EV ₱...)' - SIX acronyms in one line - and nothing anywhere on the platform explained a single one. Earned value was the only vocabulary the product used without teaching, so 'SPI 0.87' was a number a supervisor could neither act on nor argue with. Expanded at FIRST USE in that line ('Earned value (EVM): schedule performance SPI ..., cost performance CPI ..., ... (budget at completion ₱..., earned value ₱...)') rather than by adding a glossary page, because a glossary a reader has to go and find is a glossary they do not read. Live-verified, 0 pageerrors. Locked as 'glossary-registry'. ★ONE EXCLUSION, STATED NOT SILENT: assistant.html carries a capability CATALOG describing every other page to the model ('...daily progress, EV/SPI/CPI, and sign-off') - model-facing text, not UI, which double-counts vocabulary belonging to the pages it names, and those pages are scanned on their own. Flagging it would demand a glossary inside a system prompt. Teeth proven by reverting the fix, reproducing the exact pre-fix finding. REMAINING: the standing enum-leak and one-vocabulary gates already cover raw-value leakage and term-splitting; first-use definition for NON-acronym jargon (reservation, staging, hive) is a wave-close judgement pass. || THE NON-ACRONYM PASS ATTEMPTED, AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS NOT GOOD ENOUGH TO CONVICT OR ACQUIT (2026-08-27). Ran a source census over reservation / staging / escrow / tier / hail / credits, asking whether each is explained near its FIRST use. It reported alarming numbers - 'hail' 14 occurrences across 6 pages with ZERO explained, 'credits' 13 across 5 with zero, 'staging' 7 bare in asset-hub. Spot-checking the three strongest signals dismantled all three: marketplace's only user-visible 'hail' is self-explaining IN THE SENTENCE ('Nobody is selling it right now - you can hail a service provider instead, or post a wanted listing') and its other hit is a CODE COMMENT about pm_scope_item_id; asset-hub's seven 'staging' hits do not survive a word-boundary grep of visible text at all, so they came from script or attribute content my strip did not actually remove; and marketplace's 'credits' first use IS the definition ('Publishing holds 10% of your asking price in credits; the hold is returned if you remove the listing'). ★SO THE CENSUS MEASURED SOURCE TEXT AND CALLED IT GLASS. A term's first-use context is a property of the RENDERED page - what a reader meets, in order - and a regex over HTML source cannot see that: it counts comments, dead branches, attribute values and script strings as if a person read them. This is the same shape as this session's 274-finding plural census and the role=tab count that matched a comment. Recording NO verdict either way: the evidence so far leans toward these terms being explained where they are actually visible, but three spot-checks are not a census. Remaining: run this over rendered innerText per page (the live-text instrument), not source - deferred past the board run so a browser probe cannot add load to gates that flake under it. || LIVE JARGON CENSUS ATTEMPTED, NOTHING BANKED - THE INSTRUMENT'S ESCAPING IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY (2026-08-28). Walked seven pages signed in and tested 18 domain acronyms against rendered innerText, asking whether each is glossed somewhere on the page it appears. It reported six pages clean and analytics.html carrying a bare 'PM' and 'ISO'. ★I DID NOT RECORD THAT AS A FINDING, because the follow-up that should have printed the surrounding sentences returned EMPTY for both terms - and a term cannot be simultaneously present enough to flag and absent enough to have no context. The cause is word-boundary escaping surviving three layers (bash heredoc -> file -> JS string -> RegExp), the same corruption class that has already bitten this codebase where a heredoc turned a \b into a literal backspace. When the detector and its own follow-up disagree about whether a string exists, neither reading is evidence. WHAT THE ATTEMPT DID ESTABLISH: the live-text approach is right - source-based jargon scanning cannot see what a person actually reads - and the census must be built with the regexes constructed IN the page (string literals in an .mjs file, never assembled through a shell heredoc) before any result from it is banked. Remaining: rebuild the census as a standalone .mjs with no shell-quoting layer, then run it. || REBUILT AS A STANDALONE PROVER, AND IT CORRECTS ITS OWN PREDECESSOR (2026-08-28). tools/prove_jargon_is_glossed.mjs builds every pattern as a literal INSIDE the .mjs - no shell heredoc, no re-escaping - and walks 8 pages signed in, asking of each rendered acronym whether the page also carries its expansion (in the visible flow, an <abbr>, a title, or an aria-label). ★IT REFUSES TO REPORT A BARE TERM IT CANNOT QUOTE: every finding carries the surrounding sentence, and a term the detector flags but cannot locate prints 'NO CONTEXT FOUND - detector disagrees with itself' rather than a clean count. That is precisely the failure the shell-assembled version hid. RESULT: 4 acronym appearances across 8 pages; analytics.html renders THREE and glosses all three - so the earlier 'bare PM and ISO on analytics' was the corrupted instrument, now retracted by a working one. ONE real hit: asset-hub renders KPI unglossed - '6 critical assets: these drive every reliability KPI'. Small, and arguably common business vocabulary, but this platform's stated audience includes new graduates and non-technicians, so it is recorded rather than dismissed. Registered as a RECORDER, not a gate (a term being bare is an audience judgement; gating it would invite deleting the word rather than explaining it) and wired into tools/read_recorder_findings.py so its output reaches someone. Remaining: the wider non-acronym vocabulary (hive, reservation, staging, deferred) and first-use definitions. || THE OVERLOADED-WORD HALF IS BUILT, AND ITS FIRST RUN IS VOID BECAUSE I MEASURED UNDER LOAD (2026-08-28). Extended the prover past acronyms to the harder class: ordinary words the platform redefines - 'reservation' sounds like a booking and means a credit HOLD, 'staging' sounds like a phase and means parts pre-picked, 'deferred' sounds like cancelled while the task is still due and still overdue. An acronym at least ANNOUNCES that it is jargon; these do the opposite, so a reader glides past with the wrong meaning and never knows to ask. Scoped deliberately - 'hive' is excluded as the platform's core noun, introduced at onboarding, where demanding a gloss everywhere would be noise that gets the check switched off. ★THE RUN REPORTED 0 BARE ON ALL 8 PAGES AND THAT IS NOT EVIDENCE: pm-scheduler rendered 872 visible characters where an earlier walk this same session measured 2,561, and asset-hub 956 against 3,132. A heavy locked-gate audit was running concurrently and saturating the local stack, so a 9s settle caught partial renders and the census read an under-loaded page as a clean one. The asset-hub KPI hit found minutes earlier also vanished, which is the tell. MEASURING WHILE A BOARD RUNS PRODUCES FALSE CLEANS - the same class as a voided board, one direction over: there the edits corrupt the run, here the run corrupts the measurement. Nothing banked from it. Remaining: re-run the census on a quiet stack, and give the prover a settle-floor that REFUSES to grade a page rendering far below its known character count rather than reporting it clean. || THE SETTLE FLOOR IS IN AND THE FINDING REPRODUCES ON A QUIET STACK (2026-08-28). Each page now carries a floor at roughly 40% of its measured healthy character count, and rendering below it is reported UNGRADED rather than clean - because a term cannot be found bare in text that never arrived. ★THE FIX IS PROVEN BY THE VERY DATA THAT MOTIVATED IT: during the saturated run pm-scheduler rendered 872 characters against its floor of 1,000, so that run would now be UNGRADED instead of reporting a clean sweep. Re-run once the stack eased: all 8 pages cleared their floors, 0 ungraded, and asset-hub's KPI hit came back with the same quotable context ('6 critical assets: these drive every reliability KPI') - so the finding is REPRODUCIBLE and the earlier disappearance was load, exactly as diagnosed. STANDING RESULT: 4 acronym appearances across 8 pages, one bare (asset-hub / KPI), zero overloaded terms reachable at rest - the overloaded half needs the flows OPENED (pm-scheduler renders 'Deferred' in its completion history, not at rest), which is the same at-rest ceiling prove_at_cap_fits had to drive past. Remaining: drive the overloaded terms behind their flows; decide whether asset-hub's KPI is worth glossing (a judgement about audience, hence a recorder and not a gate). || FLOW-OPENING WIRED, AND ITS HONEST ANSWER IS 'THE FLOW DID NOT OPEN' (2026-08-28). The overloaded words live where the work happens, not on a landing state, so the census now runs an `open` step before reading. pm-scheduler's completion sheet is the one that would expose 'Deferred', and the prover reports [no mark-done control] - the resting page has no such control (it needs the ?asset= arrival prove_flow_fits_the_floor already documents). ★THAT IS THE POINT OF WIRING IT: before, a term unreachable behind a flow reported as ABSENT, which on a census reads identically to 'present and explained'. Now a flow that fails to open SAYS SO and the term stays unmeasured rather than silently clean - the difference between 'no findings' and 'I could not look', which this session has had to correct in three separate instruments. STANDING: 4 acronym appearances, 1 bare (asset-hub / KPI, reproducible with quotable context), overloaded terms UNREACHED with the reason recorded. Remaining: give pm-scheduler's flow its ?asset= arrival so the completion sheet opens, then the overloaded half finally has a denominator. || ★THE OVERLOADED HALF HAS ITS FIRST REAL FINDING, AND IT PAIRS WITH T10 (2026-08-28). With the ?asset= arrival wired, pm-scheduler's completion sheet opens and 'deferred' is reachable. Rendered text: 'Couldn't do this task today? Record it as deferred (needs a reason)'. That explains HOW to defer and never what deferring MEANS - and the meaning is the whole point: T10 established, and now gates, that a deferral does NOT credit completion, so the task stays due and keeps counting as overdue. The word 'deferred' reads as 'cancelled, handled, off my list' to anyone who has not been told otherwise, and the one moment a worker needs that correction is the moment they are choosing it. ★THIS IS THE EXACT SHAPE THE OVERLOADED LIST WAS BUILT FOR: an acronym announces that it is jargon, so a reader knows to ask; an ordinary word quietly redefined does the opposite, and the reader walks away confidently wrong. The DB is correct, the gate holds it, and the person is not told - correct behaviour that fails to explain itself. Recorded rather than fixed in this pass because a board run is live and pm-scheduler is one of the pages its gates read; the fix is one sentence in the deferral copy ('it stays due and still counts as overdue'), and it belongs in the same edit wave as any other pm-scheduler change. || FIXED AND VERIFIED, AND THE ORACLE HAD TO LEARN THE FIX'S WORDS (2026-08-28). pm-scheduler's deferral control now reads 'Couldn't do this task today? Record it as deferred (needs a reason - the task stays due)', so the glass finally says what the database has always done. ★AND THE CENSUS WENT ON REPORTING IT BARE AFTER THE FIX LANDED: my oracle accepted exactly one gloss, 'still due', and the copy says 'stays due'. An oracle's VOCABULARY is part of the oracle - a detector that only accepts the phrasing its author imagined will convict the next good fix, and whoever wrote that fix reasonably concludes the check is broken and stops reading it. Every overloaded term now carries SEVERAL acceptable glosses. The result is non-vacuous: pm-scheduler still reports the term PRESENT (1) and now GLOSSED (0 bare), so the check is live rather than switched off. STANDING: 8 pages, 4 acronym appearances, ONE bare term left - asset-hub's KPI - and every overloaded term either absent or explained. ★AND I BROKE THE MARKUP ON THE WAY: the explanatory comment first landed INSIDE the <button> opening tag, between its class and its type attributes. Caught by reading the file back rather than by trusting the edit. || THE LAST BARE TERM IS GONE: THE CENSUSED SURFACE IS AT ZERO (2026-08-28). asset-hub's tile read 'these drive every reliability KPI' - the one unglossed acronym the live census found on any page. ★FIXED BY REMOVING THE ACRONYM, NOT BY GLOSSING IT: 'KPI (key performance indicator)' would have made a short tile clumsier for no gain, while 'these drive every reliability metric' simply reads better and needs no explanation. The gloss test is a proxy for the real property - can a person READ this - and the plain word satisfies the property directly rather than satisfying the detector. This platform's stated audience includes new graduates and non-technicians who should not need the abbreviation to read a tile. VERIFIED LIVE: asset-hub renders 3,137 characters (healthy, matching its 3,132 baseline), 'reliability metric' present, 'KPI' absent, no page errors. STANDING RESULT for the whole census: 8 pages, 3 acronym appearances all glossed, the one overloaded term reachable ('deferred' on pm-scheduler) now explained, ZERO bare terms. Remaining: widen the page roster and the term list - eight pages and fifteen terms is a real denominator but not the whole platform, and a zero over a narrow scope is a smaller claim than it looks. || WIDENED TO THE FULL 32-PAGE CHROME ROSTER, AND THE SCOPING MATTERED MORE THAN THE COUNT (2026-08-28). First widened run: 11 pages with a bare term. ★FOUR OF THOSE WERE PEOPLE'S OWN WORDS, not platform copy - community and public-feed flagged MTBF and CMMS inside worker POSTS ('what's your MTBF target on critical pumps?', 'Excel? CMMS? Anything better?'), voice-journal flagged OEE inside a worker's own note that literally ASKS 'What is OEE?', and shift-brain flagged LOTO inside seeded job data (BF-002 · LOTO · PTW-2026-3875). A check that demands the product gloss its USERS is the same category error as counting a vendored library's code as your own defect, and reporting 11 would have sent someone editing worker content. User-written regions are now subtracted before the read and restored after, per page, from the REAL markup (#history-list, #risk-list/#pms-list/#carry-list/#parts-list) after my first guessed selectors missed two of the four. ★AND THE DISCRIMINATION IS PRECISE, NOT BLUNT: shift-brain's seeded LOTO is excluded while its 'deferred' REMAINS flagged, because that one is platform copy explaining the plan. HONEST STANDING RESULT: 32 pages, 13 acronym appearances, 8 pages with a bare term - alert-hub (Staging), assistant (MTBF), hive (LOTO, CMMS), integrations (CMMS), ph-intelligence (MTBF, MTTR, OEE), plant-connections (CMMS), report-sender (OEE), shift-brain (MTBF, deferred). Left as a RECORDER finding rather than eight unilateral copy rewrites: several are supervisor-facing surfaces where the acronym may be the right register, and which of the 13 deserve glossing is an audience judgement that belongs to Ian. ★THE SETTLE FLOOR ALSO EARNED ITS KEEP IN NORMAL USE: marketplace-seller-profile rendered 250 characters against its 300 floor and came back UNGRADED rather than clean - the first time the mechanism fired on a real run rather than a contrived one. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate glossary-registry re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Number literacy: every figure self-explains (CM as a sweep)
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, machinery census - verified): the per-PAGE number-literacy families run standing (what_is_this_number, units_visible x3, counted-noun discipline; reward_explained x4), and this session added route-level receipts (the AMC brief's defined denominators, the tier note's explicit thresholds, P-F's basis pill). THE DELTA: the JOURNEY-path number audit (numbers in the order a worker actually meets them along T9->T50 routes) - the families measure page-rest, not routes. Remaining: the route-audit instrument (wave close). ROUTE-AUDIT HARNESS BUILT, NOT BANKED 2026-08-26 (tools/prove_route_numbers.mjs). The CM family asks 'what is this number?' per PAGE; a person meets numbers along a ROUTE, so this walks the worker field loop (index/logbook/pm-scheduler/inventory) and the supervisor triage route (index/alert-hub/analytics/hive) signed in as the real personas and judges every visible figure. HONEST STATUS: after three calibration passes - text-node -> block-context judgement (the platform labels tiles with SIBLING elements, so v1 called every correct KPI tile naked), identifier exclusions (asset tags CR-001, hex serials), one-letter units (0.6d, 6.7h) - the count moved 224 -> 203 -> 202 and spot-checks STILL disagree with the rules. So it is deliberately NOT registered and NO baseline is stored: a ratchet on a number I cannot defend banks a false claim and makes every later run argue with noise. The harness itself (per-route sign-in, block-context judgement, identifier filtering) is the durable part. NEXT: dump the full per-page finding list and read it against the rendered page - the samples, not the total, will calibrate it. || THE CALIBRATION THIS TRAJECTORY ASKED FOR, DONE - AND THE RULE WAS CLIMBING TOO SHORT (2026-08-27). The harness's own NEXT said to read the findings against the rendered page rather than tune the total. Did that on index, which it scores at 20 naked numbers.
