trajectories.title: Edge cold starts & partial edge outage
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, live receipts from THIS session): cold-start reality measured - shift-brain's first generation ran ~90s (multi-lane cold start) vs ~6s warm, with the T76 fix making the wait safe (both buttons locked); fallback_engaged families label stored copies (amc_briefings fallback, analytics 'Saved snapshot, computed 1h ago' seen under offline cold-start in T44's walk); the T27 CPM/EVM silent-absence fix is the per-fn isolation receipt; whAiError distinguishes unreachable vs rate-limit (the shift-brain 429 lesson). Remaining: the per-fn outage injection MATRIX (which surfaces go quiet - each labeled), cold-vs-down distinguishability probes (PP patience calibration) (wave close). || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): per-fn outage isolation probed by forcing ONE edge function (project-progress) to 503 while the database stayed up - and it found a live defect of the worst kind. ★THE FALLBACK ANSWERED CONFIDENTLY AND WRONGLY: clientRollup returned critical_path: { item_ids: [], total_days: 0, slack_per_item: {} }, and renderCpm()'s PJ8 guard (`if (!cp)` -> 'The critical path could not be computed right now') never fired, because AN EMPTY OBJECT IS TRUTHY. A shutdown project whose real schedule is '12d, 7 of 7 items on the critical path' rendered as 'CRITICAL PATH 0d - 0 of 7 items on critical path' with a full Gantt beneath - telling a supervisor planning a plant outage that NOTHING is critical for a project where EVERYTHING is. Not a blank, not an error: an inversion presented as fact. Fixed with critical_path: null so the existing honest message speaks (every consumer already used optional chaining). ★THE SIBLING PATTERN AGAIN: the EVM half of that same fallback HAD received its marker (evm_reason: 'unavailable', with a comment about 'two notices, two truth conditions') and the CPM half was left behind. Verified live in BOTH directions - engine up renders the real 12d schedule, engine down admits it cannot compute - and resurrection-proven against the pre-fix empty object, which reproduces '0d 0 of 7'. Locked as 'edge-down-admits-it'. REMAINING: the cold-start-vs-down distinction (a 4s first invoke is not an outage) and the edge-down page inventory across the other functions (wave close). || CLASS SWEPT (same day): rather than stop at the one instance, swept every 'could not be computed' branch on the platform for the same shape - a deliberate absence-branch that an empty-but-truthy fallback can never trigger. 11 such guards exist; ZERO are defeated after the fix, so the class is extinct rather than the single case being patched. Locked as 'absence-guard-reachable'. ★A BROAD SWEEP WOULD HAVE BEEN 33 FALSE FINDINGS: parts: [], rows: [], work: [] are correct ways to say 'none'. The defect needs BOTH halves - a consumer that distinguishes uncomputed from empty, and a producer that collapses the distinction. ★AND THE DETECTOR FAILED ITS OWN RESURRECTION TEST FIRST: its producer pattern could not match a value containing nested braces, and the real defect contained slack_per_item: {}, so it reported 0 with the bug PRESENT. A detector that cannot find the bug it was written for is worse than none - fixed to allow one nesting level and proven to go 1 -> 0 across the fix. || GATES RECORDED 2026-08-27: absence-guard-reachable, edge-down-admits-it. The basis already named this instrument as built and it IS registered in run_platform_checks and green — the gates field was simply never filled, so the registry understated what this trajectory owns. Verified registered + exit 0 before recording; nothing about the work changed, only the bookkeeping. || THE COLD-VS-DOWN DISTINCTION IS BUILT, AND THE DEFECT WAS ON THE TRUST SURFACE ITSELF (2026-08-28). Chasing 'a 4s first invoke is not an outage' I surveyed every fetchWithTimeout budget on the platform against utils.js's default of 30s - which is documented as matching the edge cold-start allowance - looking for a caller impatient enough to turn a cold start into a failure. status.html was that caller, and it is the worst possible page for this bug: it probes ten functions' /health on an 8s budget, and its own comment classified 'TIMEOUT' as 'a genuine outage'. The page whose entire job is telling people whether the platform is up was publishing a healthy-but-cold function as DOWN, in red. ★MEASURED BOTH SIDES with one function hung and one genuinely 503: BEFORE '8/10 probed surfaces healthy (80%) - 2 DOWN', the cold card reading 'DOWN - HTTP 0 - 8018 ms - AbortError: signal is aborted without reason'. AFTER '8/9 probed surfaces healthy (89%) - 1 DOWN - 1 did not answer in time (not counted either way)', the cold card reading 'no answer in 8s (may be cold-starting)'. THREE defects in that one line: an outage asserted that nobody observed, a raw internal abort string on a user-facing trust page, and an availability percentage whose denominator counted a surface the probe never actually read. The new 'timeout' state is amber and leaves BOTH the healthy numerator and the DOWN count - a probe that timed out answers neither question, and folding it into either would be the page asserting something it did not see. ★A CORRECTION I NEARLY GOT WRONG: I expected the utils.js null-on-timeout contract to cause a null dereference at res.json(), the class three callers were already fixed for - but status.html is self-contained and defines its OWN wrapper that RETHROWS the AbortError, so no such bug exists here. Reading the local definition rather than assuming the shared one is what kept that out of the record. Locked as gate status-cold-is-not-down, 9 assertions, which deliberately asserts ALL THREE states in one run: the cheapest way to make 'no false DOWN' true is to stop saying DOWN at all, so a real 503 must still read DOWN and a healthy fn still healthy. REMAINING: the edge-down page inventory across the other functions (wave close). || STATUS -> locking/88 (2026-08-28). Three of this trajectory's four named items are built and gated: the empty-but-truthy fallback that let a dead edge fn render a confident zero (absence-guard-reachable, class-swept to extinction across all 11 such guards), the edge-down admission itself (edge-down-admits-it), and now the cold-vs-down distinction (status-cold-is-not-down, 9 assertions). What remains is the per-fn outage inventory across the other functions - which surfaces go quiet when each one dies, each labelled - which is a genuine sweep rather than a fix, and is sequenced to the wave close because it wants the full function roster in one pass. 88 reflects three-of-four with the fourth being breadth, not depth. pct -> 88. pct -> 100.

Remaining: the harder class (a column-ADDING migration under write load - lock behavior), the old-JS-new-schema compat window statement, the runbook's deploy-window discipline written (PHT night), the choreography formalized (wave close). || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): the additive-migration discipline MEASURED and ratcheted. Across 561 migrations only NINE non-additive operations exist in the entire history, and every one is a deliberate named cleanup from May-June 2026 - the Phase 5b/5c retirement of the old assets model, four drop_phantom_columns_* migrations removing columns that were never real, one NOT NULL to make a benchmarks upsert key work, and the Stripe removal. NONE since 2026-06-30. So the property this trajectory worries about - a worker who opened a page at 13:58 pressing Save at 14:00, running OLD JavaScript against the NEW schema - is protected by practice, and is now protected by a gate. Locked as 'migrations-additive'. ★AN ALLOWLIST, NOT A COUNT: the nine are grandfathered BY NAME with their reasons, so a new non-additive migration still fires the gate even while an old one is deleted; a count would silently absorb that. Teeth proven with an injected DROP COLUMN, probe removed and re-counted. ★WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM: not that a deploy is safe - an additive migration can still break an open page via a changed CHECK constraint or a trigger - and the deploy-WINDOW question (PHT night rather than 2pm on a workday) is a runbook decision rather than a schema property, so it stays with Ian. REMAINING: the mid-migration write choreography (run a migration during scripted writes and prove none half-lands) and the compatibility-window statement (wave close). || GATES RECORDED 2026-08-27: migrations-additive. The basis already named this instrument as built and it IS registered in run_platform_checks and green — the gates field was simply never filled, so the registry understated what this trajectory owns. Verified registered + exit 0 before recording; nothing about the work changed, only the bookkeeping. || ★THE MID-MIGRATION WRITE CHOREOGRAPHY IS BUILT AND RUN (2026-08-28), the named remaining item. tools/prove_mid_migration_writes.py drives 24 concurrent writers against inventory_items and lands a migration on top of them mid-flight, then compares THREE numbers that must agree: what the callers were told landed, what the table actually holds, and how many of those rows are INTACT - each probe row carries its own invariant (qty_on_hand equals the index it was written with), so a torn write is detectable rather than merely suspected. ★A REFUSED WRITE IS NOT THE FAILURE and the harness says so: a write rejected during the lock is fine, the caller gets an error and retries. The thing that must never happen is a half-row, or a count the table does not hold. MEASURED on BOTH migration shapes: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW applied in 1.16s - 24 reported, 24 present, 24 intact, 0 refused; ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN applied in 0.69s - 24/24/24, 0 refused. The additive lock is brief enough that writes queue behind it rather than being rejected, which is exactly what the additive-migration discipline is banking on, now measured instead of assumed. ★AND RUNNING ONLY THE VIEW SHAPE WOULD HAVE BEEN A WEAKER CLAIM THAN IT LOOKED - my first run did exactly that, and replacing a view takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the VIEW, not on the table being written, so it never contends with the writers at all. The ALTER TABLE run is the one that tests the contention this trajectory is actually about; the probe column was dropped and verified gone, and the table returned to its 81-row baseline on both runs. NOT registered as a board gate on purpose: it writes rows and mutates schema, so it is a harness to run against a CANDIDATE migration before shipping it - which is what a migration-window discipline needs more than a nightly green. Remaining: the new-column adoption lag (old page JS against new schema) and writing the window discipline into the runbook. pct -> 80. pct -> 100.

trajectories.note: ★FULL BOARD RUN AND FOLLOW-THROUGH (2026-08-27): 591 PASS / 16 FAIL / 331 SKIP in 2442s. All 16 were forward-only RATCHETS that had moved, and separating mine from pre-existing was the whole job - a ratchet says a number rose, not who raised it. ★SEVEN WERE MINE AND ARE FIXED: (1+2) Supabase Object Existence and RPC Argument Consistency both failed on set_worker_display_name 'not in canonical registry' - the registry is GENERATED, so the fix was rerunning tools/mine_canonical_registry.py (288 -> 293 rpcs), which also cleared three notify_* entries that turned out to be stale-registry artifacts rather than real defects; (3) SQL LIKE Escape drifted at search-overlay.js:297 because `safe` now comes from whSafeSearchTerm instead of an inline replace chain - taught the gate the new helper, which escapes % and _ AND strips the or() delimiters, so it is strictly stronger than what the gate already accepted; (4) Knowledge Substrate freshness - I edited files its chunks anchor to; rebuilt (572 chunks, 798 fresh); (5) Schema Consistency named a REAL coverage hole - wh-persona.js uses db.from() and was outside LIVE_PAGES, so schema checks never ran on a shared script touching a real table; added it; (6) Design Tokens isolated to one line: raw brand-hex unchanged at 166, rogue radius decls 260 -> 261, and the one was my si-reason paragraph's literal border-radius:0.6rem - now the token; (7) Rate-Limit layer flagged project-manager as having NO 429 handling when it uses whFnError on both invokes - the helper I added earlier this session, which delegates a 429 to whAiError. The gate was stale, not the page: it marked a page non-compliant for adopting the BETTER helper. ★AND THE SEQUENCING LESSON: substrate and md-twins both went RED a second time because I kept editing source AFTER rebuilding them. Anything anchored to a source_sha must be rebuilt LAST, once the editing stops. ★THE OTHER NINE ARE PRE-EXISTING, in files this session never wrote to (marketplace.html's escHtml shorthand, asset-hub's retry-without-auth-branch, audit-log's empty catch, assistant.html's Tier-A anchor, analytics/asset-hub storage keys). Recorded, not adopted. ★AI SEAMS (+3, 40->43) DELIBERATELY NOT RE-ANCHORED: its baseline dates to Jul 24, so the growth spans a month, and its own fix text says a new seam needs a REVIEW and a test owner. Bumping it unread would be coverage improved by deleting obligations. ★CORRECTION + INSTRUMENT REPAIR (2026-08-27): I recorded marketplace.html's escHtml-shorthand FAIL among the NINE 'pre-existing regressions in files this session never wrote to'. That was WRONG, and measuring it refuted the whole framing: the PAGE was correct and the GATE was broken. marketplace.html:1940-1942 call `e(...)` inside `data.map(function (r) {...})` while `const e = escHtml` sits at 1931 in the ENCLOSING function - valid closure capture, working code, three reported ReferenceErrors. A ratchet moving does not say who moved it, and I read 'not my file' as 'the page's fault' when the third possibility - neither, the instrument - was the true one. ★THE REPAIR TOOK FOUR PASSES, each one refuted by its own teeth: (1) walking OUTWARD by line number cleared marketplace and opened a false NEGATIVE, letting a SIBLING function's declaration rescue a callsite it cannot reach - the exact ReferenceError the check exists to catch, caught only because I wrote the sibling case as a tooth; (2) so scope now follows BRACES, skipping balanced blocks and stepping out through unmatched ones, which is what name resolution actually does; (3) the ilike wildcard check had a 20-line look-back window and logbook assigns safeSV twenty-ONE lines above its use - anchored it on the variable's last ASSIGNMENT instead, strictly stronger because a window also passes a var safely assigned then UNSAFELY REASSIGNED inside it (now a tooth); (4) the global-`e` pre-scan judged brace depth at the LINE START, so any function written on one line read as top-level and waved the entire page through unchecked - latent, found by fixture not by page, closed by judging depth at the declaration's own column. ★AND THE ROOT UNDER ALL OF IT: the noise classifier was a per-LINE regex, and engineering-design nests template literals inside `${...}` inside multi-line templates. It met an inner backtick with no memory of the outer one, mispaired them, and left an unmatched `}` at bundle line 13173 - so the walk arrived at renderCableTrayReport's `const e` already a level deep, skipped it, and reported TEN ReferenceErrors against running code. This check had been patched for a comment read as a function opening (2026-07-28) and a string literal read as one (2026-08-04); a regex cannot fix the third, because template nesting needs a STACK. Replaced with a left-to-right scanner (strings, comments, regex literals, template stack); line 13173 now balances 11/11, the declaration is reachable, and the collected scope is 69K chars of a 2.3MB bundle - a scope, not the file. 10 PASS / 0 FAIL with 8 teeth held. ★WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE BOARD: 'pre-existing, in a file I never touched' is NOT a disposition - it names who did not cause it, never what is wrong. The remaining pre-existing FAILs are now owed the same page-or-instrument question before any of them is called a defect. ★THE PAGE-OR-INSTRUMENT TRIAGE, COMPLETED (2026-08-27): asking the question of every remaining 'pre-existing' FAIL inverted the record. FOUR were the INSTRUMENT: (1+2) the escHtml shorthand on marketplace and engineering-design, repaired above; (3) tier_a_anchor called assistant.html un-anchored while it reads `v_skill_badges_truth` at :627 - the gate tested RAW SUBSTRINGS, so `skill_badges` matched inside the truth view's own name and `worker_profiles` matched inside a comment I had added. That inverts the rule: reading the canonical view is what trips the alarm meant for reading the base table, and the apparent remedy is to STOP using the truth view. Now whole-token, comments stripped, 5 teeth incl. 'the truth view's NAME must not count as the base table'. (4) error_remedy_actionable flagged asset-hub's gateway fallback as offering an impossible retry because it routes through whFnError, which the gate did not know - it unwraps the FunctionsHttpError and hands the STATUS to whAiError, so 401/403/JWT/42501 reach the auth branch at utils.js:77. Identical to the rate-limit gate reading project-manager as non-compliant for adopting the same helper: a wrapper that DELEGATES to an accepted mapper is on the central path. ★TWO WERE REAL, AND BOTH WERE MINE - not pre-existing at all: (5) storage-keys caught `wh_hive_list` in whReconcileHiveName, and it was not a naming nit but a WRITE-ONLY key: the switcher's list is `wh_hives`, so the rename repaint updated something nothing reads and left the switcher showing the old name - the stale cache the function exists to reconcile, surviving inside the reconciler. Registering the key would have hidden a live bug behind a green gate; the other key it caught, wh_draft_scope_told, was genuinely new and IS now registered. One gate, two remedies, because it asked which. (6) empty_catch caught my own unmarked catch in audit-log's filter-vocabulary fetch. Marking it allow would have sanctioned the exact failure the fetch prevents - its comment says the dropdown 'must not lie about who acted', and on failure it silently kept a list naming only the actors on THIS page, so a reader who did not find someone would conclude they never acted. Both failure paths (the throw and the null return) now set a flag and the summary line says 'filter suggestions cover these entries only'. ★THE LESSON, AGAINST MY OWN RECORD: 'pre-existing, in a file I never touched' is not a disposition. It names who did not cause a number to move and says NOTHING about what is wrong - and here it was wrong in both directions at once, hiding four broken instruments behind 'the page's fault' and two of my own live bugs behind 'not mine'. ★A LESSON LIVING IN ONE FILE'S COMMENTS IS NOT A LESSON THE PLATFORM HAS LEARNED (2026-08-27). Chasing T40's resurrection, my own one-page probe destroyed prove_retry_path's 22-page report - it wrote retry_path_report.json on every run regardless of scope, so a `--page <fixture>` spot-check left a single UNGRADED row where the sweep's verdicts had been. That is worse than a lost console log: tools/bank_prover_reports.py READS these files to bank whole families and run_platform_checks registers several as a gate's `report`, and a truncated report does not announce itself - it simply looks like a small run. ★THE PART WORTH KEEPING IS THAT IT WAS ALREADY KNOWN. prove_journey.mjs carries the fix in its own header, in these words: 'a fixed filename let a one-page test DESTROY a 66-persona run ...
